title: As LSU chases NFL players, SEC speaks out against it
summary: The current vibe in college football consists of Machiavelli vs. the lingering vestiges of amateurism.
full_text: The current vibe in college football consists of Machiavelli vs. the lingering vestiges of amateurism. With players from the high school class of 2022 securing a fifth year of college eligibility, even if they've signed with NFL teams, some college coaches are pouncing. One major conference is cringing. On Monday, SEC presidents and chancellors sounded off against the practice of former NFL players trying to return to play college football. "College athletes, not former professional athletes, have been at the heart of the Southeastern Conference," they said, via Heather Dinich of ESPN. "Individuals who choose to leave college athletics, sign professional playing contracts, and compete professionally should not then be permitted to return to college competition. "Allowing that to occur will blur the line between college and professional sports, create significant competitive equity concerns, and reduce opportunities for high school and current college athletes. "College sports are for college athletes. The current confusion around national eligibility standards emphasizes the need to advance the Protect College Sports Act." And there it is. Just like the Brendan Sorsby case, those who hope to clear out the chaos from college sports (and in turn pick the pockets of the players), will seize on the unpopularity of the practice to push for the antitrust exemption they covet. The bottom line is that it's always a two-way street. At the core of every sky-is-falling example for college football is a college football program that is helping to pull the sky down. For the Brendan Sorsby situation, it was Texas Tech. For the Thornton Melon situation, it's LSU — and others. "At the end of the day, because of these rulings, they're either going to play for you or they’re going to play for someone else around the country," LSU coach Lane Kiffin told reporters on Monday, via Max Olson of ESPN. "So we've made the decision to recruit them like probably most people are." Kiffin isn't alone. Ohio State coach Ryan Day, while claiming he doesn't like it, is also willing to do it if it means helping Ohio State win. "[I]f there are teams that have some players out there who are cut from NFL rosters that are gonna be on other teams, we have to at least consider it and look at it," Day said Monday, via Alec Lasley of USA Today . "Do I like anything about it? Absolutely not. But we gotta do what’s right for Ohio State . So it’s sort of a day-to-day thing right now. And like anything, we’re just gonna try to adapt." Others are taking a stand against it — probably because they don't see a short-term benefit to their teams by welcoming fifth-year players who have spent time on NFL teams. Oregon coach Dan Lanning, for example, has made it clear that he's against it. " Once you go to the NFL, you’re in the NFL ," Lanning said over the weekend. "You don't get the opportunity to come back. It's unfair to the sport, and it's unfair to the players on current teams for those guys to be coming back." It's easy for Lanning to take that position as to what is, essentially, a one-year glitch given the NCAA's shift to a five-year model moving forward. By next year, it won't be an issue. If there's no NFL player in whom Lanning is interested, it's easy to climb onto a soapbox against the practice. There's also an element of hypocrisy lurking in Lanning's position. Last year, Lanning embraced the opportunity to land receiver Malik Benson, a beneficiary of Diego Pavia’s effort to secure through the court system a fourth year of major college football after playing at the junior-college level for two years. Benson led the Ducks in receiving in 2025. If Lanning could land another Malik Benson this year under the new wave of litigation flowing from the attempt to apply the five-year rule retroactively, Lanning would do it. That's the tension. As it relates to the broader issues in college sports, which flow directly from the chronic antitrust violations committed by college sports by decades, the return of NFL players becomes a solid talking point in the effort to get Congress to wave a magic wand that partially restores order. As it relates to the specific effort to win games, teams that perceive a potential benefit from welcoming players who have spent preseason time with an NFL franchise will roll out the red carpet — even if they feel compelled to feign reluctance to do so.
author: Mike Florio

title: Kellen Moore on Zxavian Harris going from Saints to LSU: There's no regulation to anything
summary: "Hopefully there can be some leadership and some regulations developed," Moore said.
full_text: '' The Saints signed defensive tackle Zxavian Harris as an undrafted rookie on May 1, and he was on the Saints until they waived him on August 8. Now Harris plays for LSU, and Saints head coach Kellen Moore is trying to wrap his head around how that's possible. Harris was one of 16 players who re-gained NCAA eligibility as a result of a Louisiana judge's ruling. Moore, whose brother Kirby Moore is the head coach at Washington State, thinks football needs eligibility rules that are clearly established and don't change every time a player takes the NCAA to court. "I think it's unfortunate that there's no regulation to anything right now. My brother coaches college football so I follow it closely, just watching everything college football is going through," Moore said. Moore said he wants players to have every opportunity but also wants someone to step up and provide some leadership in college football. "I think there's a challenging balancing act to this, and hopefully there can be some leadership and some regulations developed here shortly," Moore said. Asked if he ever thought he'd hear that a player who was in training camp with the Saints would play that season in college, Moore answered, "No. It's a unique college football world we live in right now."
author: Michael David Smith

title: Saints lose cornerback and special teamer Rejzohn Wright to season-ending hip injury
summary: Saints cornerback and special teams contributor Rejzohn Wright will miss the entire 2026 season.
full_text: ''' Saints cornerback and special teams contributor Rejzohn Wright will miss the entire 2026 season. New Orleans head coach Kellen Moore confirmed that Wright is out for the season with a hip injury that will require surgery. Last year Wright played exclusively on special teams for the Saints, but he was competing in training camp for a role on defense as well. Instead, he'll miss the year. The 25-year-old Wright first became known to football fans when he was featured on the Netflix college football documentary series L ast Chance U. He was originally an undrafted free agent with the Panthers out of Oregon State in 2023. He is the brother of Jets cornerback Nahshon Wright. Wright has been with the Saints since 2024 but spent the whole 2024 season on injured reserve and will now spend the whole 2026 season on injured reserve as well.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Police close investigation into death of Ed Oliver's young son
summary: On Saturday, the Bills acknowledged that defensive tackle Ed Oliver's young son died earlier this summer, after a report regarding the tragedy had emerged a day earlier.
full_text: On Saturday, the Bills acknowledged that defensive tackle Ed Oliver's young son died earlier this summer, after a report regarding the tragedy had emerged a day earlier. On Monday, authorities in Houston closed the investigation regarding the situation. "The incident was thoroughly investigated by detectives, and their finding [was] no criminal findings ," the Harris County, Texas, Sheriff's Office said Monday, per the Associated Press. "The case is now closed." Oliver's son, who was nearly two, was found unresponsive in a swimming pool in late June. Quarterback Josh Allen spoke out on Saturday against the decision to publish information about the boy's death, saying he was " very, very sad and angry " that the information had come to light before Oliver was ready to share it. The situation sparked a discussion regarding journalism ethics , with the prevailing view being that the story should not have been shared until Oliver was ready to do so.
author: Mike Florio

title: Justin Jefferson vows to return to NFL preeminence
summary: There was a time, not all that long ago, that Justin Jefferson was regarded as the best receiver in the NFL, without question.
full_text: There was a time, not all that long ago, that Justin Jefferson was regarded as the best receiver in the NFL, without question. After 2025, there are plenty of questions about where he fits among the league's elite pass catchers. He believes that opinions will change in time. “Not yet,” Jefferson recently told Mike Silver of The Athletic . “Not yet. But they will [know] after this year —I’ll tell you that .” It helps that he has a quarterback he fully believes in, both as to what he can do with his legs and as to what he can do with his arm. “What excites me is his ability to just be an athlete,” Jefferson said regarding Kyler Murray. “Everybody knows what he does when the ball is in his hands, running the ball and being able to create time back there in the pocket. When a play might be dead, he’s able to kind of move with his feet and make something happen. So, you’re always alive, and you’re always just expecting that the ball is going to come your way. “But his throwing ability is also something that has really, really surprised me. While he was in Arizona, I didn’t really keep track and pay attention to his arm talent. And seeing the different type of throws he’s making, where he’s throwing the ball, it’s been really, really surprising me.” This year, Jefferson may be in position to repeatedly heap praise on his quarterback. Last year, he conspicuously bit his tongue. Because he knew what the reaction would be. “That one comment that I [might] make about one of my teammates might make headlines and be the trending topic, and that might be a bad look on the team and for me as well," Jefferson told Silver. "So just keeping it in house, communicating with my teammates personally and letting them know what’s going on . . . even talking with J.J. [McCarthy] last season and making sure his head is on right, with all of the negativity. Never will I downplay anybody in the media, no matter how bad it is." Through it all, Jefferson still finished with 1,048 receiving yards — his sixth straight 1,000-yard season. This year, who knows? Maybe he'll turn the clock back to 2022, when he was a first-team All-Pro and the NFL offensive player of the year.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jed York filed for divorce in May 2026
summary: The private lives of the NFL's ultra-rich and famous are never really all that private.
full_text: The private lives of the NFL's ultra-rich and famous are never really all that private. They become less private when their private proclivities become public. With 49ers owner Jed York pleading no contest on Monday to multiple misdemeanor charges in Ohio arising from an alleged effort to engage in prostitution , multiple media outlets are following the publicly available paper trial. Per multiple reports, York filed for divorce from his wife, Danielle Belluomini, on Monday, May 11. He cited irreconcilable differences in connection with the dissolution of a marriage that dates to 2011. The timing of the filing is notable. The couple has two children; York filed for divorce the day after Mother's Day. Fifteen Mondays later, York was involved in a much different court proceeding — one that may have triggered a divorce filing, if a divorce wasn't already pending. It's unclear what if any impact the divorce will have on York's ability to continue owning the 49ers. More immediately, York faces potential discipline from the NFL for violating the Personal Conduct Policy.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jalen Ramsey says "pay Joey Porter"
summary: Steelers defensive back Jalen Ramsey exited the Physically Unable to Perform list and practiced for the first time during 2026 training camp.
full_text: Steelers defensive back Jalen Ramsey exited the Physically Unable to Perform list and practiced for the first time during 2026 training camp. He also had a message, during a session with reporters. "We need the whole secondary out there," Ramsey said. " They’ve got to pay Joey Porter ." Earlier on Monday, coach Mike McCarthy said that the Steelers and Porter, a second-round pick in 2023, are at an " impasse ." Porter remains on the PUP list, the product of an obvious hold in. The question becomes whether he'll take the best offer the Steelers have made on a multi-year deal, play the final year of his rookie contract at less than $4 million, continue to sit out into the regular season, or be traded. Regardless, the clock is ticking. The Steelers, as a matter of policy, don't do new deals once the season begins.
author: Mike Florio

title: Deion Sanders on subpoena: "When you're 'him,' you get sued"
summary: Colorado coach Deion Sanders is under subpoena to testify at a trial involving his son, Shilo.
full_text: Colorado coach Deion Sanders is under subpoena to testify at a trial involving his son, Shilo. The case starts on Monday, August 31 — five days before Colorado's first game of the 2026 season. Deion disputes the notion that the situation will be a distraction. " Do you think that’s my first subpoena? " Sanders told reporters on Monday, via the Associated Press. "When you have 'it,' when you're 'him,' you get sued. You have off-the-field foolishness that if someone really sat down and explained it to you, you would say, 'You've got to be kidding.' But it is what it is. "I don't know anyone that's a game-changer, a way-maker, that is not dealing with some type of lawsuit." He's right, on one level. People with money become targets for litigation. But, at another level, he's wrong; successful persons who don't dance on the line of potential liability don't get sued — unless the claim is truly frivolous. Of course, Deion isn't a defendant in the case for which he has been subpoenaed to testify. He is, however, facing a separate lawsuit regarding the development of his “Prime” logo .
author: Mike Florio

title: Sean Payton: The Riley Moss rib injury is "nothing serious"
summary: On Friday night, Broncos cornerback Riley Moss made an early exit with a rib injury.
full_text: On Friday night, Broncos cornerback Riley Moss made an early exit with a rib injury. After the game, coach Sean Payton didn’t have much to say about Moss's condition. On Monday, Payton didn't have much to add. “He’s doing fine," Payton told reporters regarding Moss. "I would say it’s nothing serious. We’re being smart. We’ll see as the week progresses where he’s at.” Teams don't have the same level of injury-reporting obligations during training camp and the preseason. It's possible not much more will be known about Moss until the Broncos' first Week 1 injury report is released, in advance of their Monday night game against the Chiefs.
author: Mike Florio

title: Allen Robinson announces retirement
summary: Former NFL wide receiver Allen Robinson II announced his retirement on Monday.
full_text: Former NFL wide receiver Allen Robinson II announced his retirement on Monday. Robinson, 33, did not play in the NFL last season. He played for five times in his 11 seasons after the Jaguars drafted him in the second round in 2014. Robinson's best season came in 2014 when he had 1,400 receiving yards and 14 touchdowns, earning his only Pro Bowl honor. Robinson had two 1,000-yard seasons in his four seasons with the Bears. He played for the Rams in 2022, the Steelers in 2023 and the Lions in 2024. Robinson finished his career with 565 catches for 7,058 yards and 43 touchdowns.
author: Charean Williams

title: Report: Saints fear RB Ty Chandler suffered serious knee injury
summary: The Saints made a trade for Zamir White on Monday and injuries in their offensive backfield appear to be the reason why they made the made.
full_text: '' The Saints made a trade for Zamir White on Monday and injuries in their offensive backfield appear to be the reason why they made the made. The list of injured backs grew to include Ty Chandler in Saturday's loss to the Rams. Chandler suffered a knee injury and head coach Kellen Moore said on Monday that Chandler was looking at possibly missing time. A report from Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football suggests it could be quite a bit of time. Underhill reports that the team fears it is a serious injury . Chandler's injury comes at a moment when Alvin Kamara is sidelined by a sprained MCL and Devin Neal is battling a hamstring injury. Kendre Miller also missed extended time with a back injury before returning recently. Miller joins White and Audric Estime as the team's available options behind Travis Etienne at the moment.
author: Josh Alper

title: 49ers sign DE Viliami Fehoko
summary: The 49ers added pass rush help on Monday, signing defensive end Viliami Fehoko, according to the NFL's transaction wire.
full_text: The 49ers added pass rush help on Monday, signing defensive end Viliami Fehoko, according to the NFL's transaction wire. In a corresponding move, the 49ers released tight end Josiah Deguara. Fehoko entered the NFL as a fourth-round pick of the Cowboys in 2023. He spent part of his rookie season with a knee injury that landed him on IR. The Cowboys waived Fehoko before his second season and he signed with the Commanders' practice squad late in the 2024 season. Washington waived him with an injury designation during training camp in 2025. He spent some time on the Colts' practice squad last season. But Fehoko has never played in a regular-season game. The 49ers needed depth at the position with rookie defensive end Romello Height nursing an injury.
author: Charean Williams

title: Texans DE Dylan Horton tore his Achilles at Monday's practice
summary: Texans defensive end Dylan Horton is likely to miss the entire 2026 season after an injury at Monday's practice.
full_text: Texans defensive end Dylan Horton is likely to miss the entire 2026 season after an injury at Monday's practice. Per multiple reports, Horton tore his Achilles during the team's workout. Horton has been with the Texans since being selected in the fourth round of the 2023 draft. Horton missed the end of his rookie season and the start of the 2024 campaign while battling lymphoma. He has been in remission since March 2024. When healthy, Horton has appeared in 39 regular season games for the Texans. He had 55 tackles, a half-sack, a forced fumble and a fumble recovery in that action. He also has two tackles in four playoff games.
author: Josh Alper

title: Lions put RB Raheem Blackshear, WR Cedrick Wilson on injured reserve
summary: The Lions placed a couple of veterans on injured reserve Monday.
full_text: ''' The Lions placed a couple of veterans on injured reserve Monday. Running back Raheem Blackshear and wide receiver Cedrick Wilson both landed on the list. They will not be eligible to play this season unless they are released with injury settlements at some point in the future. Blackshear signed with the team earlier this month and ran 16 times for 62 yards in the team's two preseason games. He appeared in 41 games for the Panthers between 2022 and 2024. Wilson had three catches for 24 yards in his preseason appearances. He's also played for the Dolphins, Saints and Cowboys. The Lions filled the open roster spots by signing defensive back Jason Taylor and running back Roydell Williams.
author: Josh Alper

title: Former Saints rookie Zxavian Harris returns to college, commits to LSU
summary: The Saints waived rookie defensive tackle Zxavian Harris on Aug. 8.
full_text: The Saints waived rookie defensive tackle Zxavian Harris on Aug. 8. Matt Zenitz of CBS Sports reports that Harris has committed to LSU. Harris played for new LSU coach Lane Kiffin at Ole Miss. He just became eligible to return to college football after a court order in Louisiana on Aug. 19 granted Harris and 15 other college football players a temporary restraining order against the NCAA. Harris went undrafted in the spring and signed with the Saints as an undrafted free agent. He totaled 58 tackles, nine tackles for loss and three sacks.
author: Charean Williams

title: NFL adds Tony Boselli to competition committee
summary: Jaguars Executive V.P. of Football Operations Tony Boselli is the newest member of the NFL's competition committee.
full_text: Jaguars Executive V.P. of Football Operations Tony Boselli is the newest member of the NFL's competition committee. Boselli, a Hall of Fame offensive tackle, is one of 12 members of the committee, which reviews issues such as playing rules, roster rules, game-day operations and player safety. The competition committee is very influential within the league, although rule changes are ultimately made by a vote of the owners, and the competition committee's recommendations are not always followed. The co-chairmen of the competition committee are former Falcons CEO Rich McKay and Cowboys CEO Stephen Jones. In addition to Boselli, the other members of the committee are Bengals Executive V.P. Katie Blackburn, Giants owner John Mara, 49ers GM John Lynch, Buccaneers coach Todd Bowles, Rams coach Sean McVay, Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell, Broncos coach Sean Payton, Texans coach DeMeco Ryans and Patriots coach Mike Vrabel.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Aaron Glenn: Breece Hall, Kenyon Sadiq on track for Week 1
summary: Jets running back Breece Hall has missed the last week of work with a groin injury, but the team isn't showing much concern about his status for the season opener.
full_text: Jets running back Breece Hall has missed the last week of work with a groin injury, but the team isn't showing much concern about his status for the season opener. Head coach Aaron Glenn said on Monday, via multiple reporters, that Hall is on track to play against the Titans on September 13. Video from Monday's practice show Hall moving well on a side field as he goes through the rehab process. Glenn said that the team also expects tight end Kenyon Sadiq to play in the opener. The first-round pick has been sidelined after a procedure to address a hernia. Second-round corner DeAngelo Ponds (calf) and running back Isaiah Davis (knee) round out the group of injured players that the team is planning to have in Tennessee.
author: Josh Alper

title: Ty Simpson will "definitely" play preseason finale, Sean McVay undecided on backup QB
summary: The Rams have the reigning MVP at starting quarterback, but their QB2 is still to be determined.
full_text: The Rams have the reigning MVP at starting quarterback, but their QB2 is still to be determined. Head coach Sean McVay told reporters on Monday that he's still undecided as to who will be Matthew Stafford's backup between Stetson Bennett and first-round rookie Ty Simpson. When gathering data to help make that determination, McVay said the Rams will "definitely" play Simpson in this week's preseason finale against the Chargers while Bennett may or may not get on the field. "I’m just truly taking things a day at a time ,” McVay said, via Benjamin Royer of the Southern California News Group. “Today, Stetson took nine of the 15 reps [with the second team]. Ty took six of them. As far as what we’re doing with the game, you know we haven’t even gotten into that.” Bennett is entering his fourth season but has not been in a regular-season game. Jimmy Garoppolo has served as Los Angeles’ backup quarterback for the last two seasons, but he has not been back with the club in 2026 as he contemplates retirement. Bennett was 19-of-31 for 181 yards with a pair of rushing touchdowns in the Rams’ preseason matchup with the Saints on Saturday. Simpson finished that contest 8-of-12 for 73 yards. The Rams will be the “away” team when they play the Chargers at SoFi Stadium on Thursday night.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Cardinals activate Josh Sweat from active/PUP among several moves
summary: The Cardinals activated pass rusher Josh Sweat from the active/physically unable to perform list on Monday, the team announced.
full_text: The Cardinals activated pass rusher Josh Sweat from the active/physically unable to perform list on Monday, the team announced. It gets him back in time for some work in Green Bay later this week. Sweat did not participate in voluntary offseason work, working out on his own, before going on the PUP list at the start of camp. Sweat has needed rehab on his knee since he seriously injured it while in college. He led the team with 12 sacks last season. The Cardinals also announced they waived running back Trey Benson with an injury designation. He has been out with a knee issue. The Cardinals selected Benson in the third round of the 2024 draft, but he played only 17 games. He totaled 451 yards on 92 carries. Arizona also placed wide receiver Xavier Weaver on injured reserve after Weaver hurt his hamstring in the preseason game against the Cowboys on Saturday night. The team signed safeties Hudson Clark and Devyn Bobby, helping with depth going into the final preseason game against the Packers. The secondary took hits in the Cowboys game, with safety Rabbit Taylor-Demerson exiting with an injury to his ribs, and safety Wydett Williams and cornerback Kalen King diagnosed with concussions. The Cardinals have also released tight end Baylor Cupp and wide receiver Bryson Green. All the moves leave the team with a roster spot, which likely will go to a punter. Punter Blake Gillikin injured his groin Saturday, and coach Mike LaFleur said Monday he will not be available this week.
author: Charean Williams

title: Colts' kicking competition remains neck-and-neck between Blake Grupe and Spencer Shrader
summary: Last year the Colts started the season with Spencer Shrader as their kicker and finished the season with Blake Grupe taking Shrader's place after an injury.
full_text: Last year the Colts started the season with Spencer Shrader as their kicker and finished the season with Blake Grupe taking Shrader's place after an injury. This offseason the two kickers have been competing to make the roster, and with less than a week to go before cutdown day, it remains a close competition. "I don't think we could really go wrong," Colts special teams coordinator Brian Mason said, via JJ Stankevitz Colts.com. "I think we have two really good kickers that are talented that can get the job done for us, and I think whichever one we go with is going to be really, really good for us." Grupe has been a little better on the practice field in training camp, but Shrader has been better in the preseason, making a 61-yard field goal against the Patriots and 48- and 53-yard field goals against the Falcons, while Grupe missed a 36-yarder against the Falcons. Mason said kicks under game conditions matter the most, but the Colts will give both kickers some high-pressure situations on the practice field this week before the preseason finale. "We have two really good kickers," Mason said. "We're not going to judge somebody on one day or judge somebody in the first two weeks. We're going to see how do they progress through training camp, and who do we believe can be the best starting kicker for us for 17 regular season games, and then hopefully into the playoffs, right? So, that's not just based on statistics. It's based on hey, who's kicking the best right now that we think can kick the best over the entire regular season." It's a big decision for the Colts, one that needs to be made by Sunday.
author: Michael David Smith

title: John Harbaugh: "Reasonable to assume" Malik Nabers plays in Week 1
summary: Nabers has continued to make progress in his return from a torn ACL.
full_text: '' Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers took another step in his recovery from last year's torn ACL at the team's practice on Monday. Nabers took the field without a red non-contact jersey for the first time this summer. After the session, head coach John Harbaugh said that it was a good practice for Nabers and that the wideout was " probably moving the best we've seen him look" since he returned to the field. That did not result in Harbaugh ruling Nabers in for the season opener against the Cowboys, but the head coach said it was safe to make inferences about the wideout's availability. "I don’t want to make any kind of statements like that," Harbaugh said, via SNY. "It’s reasonable to assume that. Those are all kinds of things you can assume just based on watching the guy practice. The only thing I know more than you guys know is what the docs and the trainers tell me as far as his rehab. And that’s doing well, he’s doing really well with that. He’s strong, he’s in a good place but how he gets through practice, how ready he is to play and protect himself is really based on practice." Getting Nabers back in the lineup would be a big plus for Harbaugh as he starts his time on the Giants' sideline and it may not be long before the answers about Nabers move from assumptions to guarantees.
author: Josh Alper

title: Andy Reid: No predictions on Patrick Mahomes for season opener
summary: Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes avoided the physically unable to perform list to open training camp and he's been practicing without issue all summer, but head coach Andy Reid stopped short of making any pronouncements about his status for Week 1 on Monday.
full_text: ''' Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes avoided the physically unable to perform list to open training camp and he's been practicing without issue all summer, but head coach Andy Reid stopped short of making any pronouncements about his status for Week 1 on Monday. Mahomes did not play in either of the team's first two preseason games, but said during Saturday's game that he wanted to play against the Buccaneers. Reid confirmed that was the case on Monday, but said Mahomes was "probably not cleared enough" for that contest and said he would not look ahead to September 14 against the Broncos at this point. “He’s doing great ,” Reid said, via Pete Sweeney of the Kansas City Star . “We’ll just see. I’m literally taking it day by day. There are no predictions here on anything. But if the doctors and the trainers and everybody that are involved with this give him an OK — and then most of all, if he feels like he can, then we’ll address that when we get there. But other than that, these other guys are playing quarterback and doing a nice job with it.” Barring any news of a medical setback for Mahomes in the coming days, it is hard to imagine anyone else taking the first snaps of the season for the Chiefs but Reid isn't counting any chickens before they've hatched.
author: Josh Alper

title: Carson Beck still dealing with rib injury, TBD if he'll play on Friday
summary: Cardinals rookie quarterback Carson Beck is making progress, but has not fully recovered from the rib injury he suffered in the Hall of Fame Game.
full_text: Cardinals rookie quarterback Carson Beck is making progress, but has not fully recovered from the rib injury he suffered in the Hall of Fame Game. Head coach Mike LaFleur told reporters on Monday that Beck's recent throwing session went well, but it's still to be determined whether or not Beck will be able to play this week's preseason game against the Packers. Beck played well in his one preseason appearance, going 15-of-19 for 188 yards with one touchdown and no picks against the Panthers on Aug. 6. But with the regular season approaching, Beck’s opportunities to get reps are dwindling, which means this injury has affected some of the young quarterback’s development. “I mean, it’s easy to magnify the quarterback position, a rookie, all that stuff. But, yeah, you get better at football by practicing and playing football,” LaFleur said. “So when you’re not out there, it’s hard to get better, right? So, he’s missed some days. But that’s no different than the nose guard, that’s no different than the receiver, that’s no different than the left tackle — particularly for the younger guys. “So, it is what it is. Injuries are part of this thing. He’s a tough dude . Like I said, he battled through it for three or four practices before the discomfort became so real that it just wasn’t worth it — because it wasn’t going to improve until we gave him a little bit of time.” The Cardinals and Packers will have a joint practice this week before playing a preseason game at Lambeau Field on Friday night.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Patriots sign OL Jack Conley, P Matt Haack
summary: The Patriots signed first-year offensive lineman Jack Conley and veteran punter Matt Haack, the team announced Monday.
full_text: The Patriots signed first-year offensive lineman Jack Conley and veteran punter Matt Haack, the team announced Monday. In corresponding moves, the Patriots released rookie cornerback Kenneth Harris and rookie wide receiver Kobe Prentice. Conley, 25, entered the NFL as a rookie free agent with New England on May 9, 2025, out of Boston College. He had two brief stints on the Patriots' practice squad last year. He also spent time on the Detroit and Cleveland practice squads during the 2025 season. Conley went to training camp with Cleveland this past summer, but the Browns released him on Aug. 18. Haack, 32, entered the NFL as a rookie free agent with the Dolphins out of Arizona State in 2017. He spent his first four NFL seasons with the Dolphins (2017-20). He has also played for the Bills (2021), Colts (2022), Browns (2023), Giants (2024) and Cardinals (2025). Haack has also spent time with the Jaguars and the Broncos. He went to training camp with the Commanders this summer but was released on Aug. 18. Haack has appeared in 110 NFL games and has 478 punts for 21,513 yards and a 45.0-yard average. Harris, 24, was signed by New England as a rookie free agent out of Oklahoma State on May 8. Prentice, 22, was claimed off waivers by New England on July 25. He signed with the Panthers as a rookie free agent on May 7.
author: Charean Williams

title: Jeremiyah Love will remain out of practice this week
summary: At least one J.
full_text: At least one J. Love will not be on the field this week. Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur told reporters in his Monday press conference that rookie running back Jeremiyah Love will still be sidelined this week, Arizona heads to Green Bay for a joint practice and Friday preseason game. "He will not be on the field doing any sort of practice or anything like that right now," LaFleur said. Love has been out since suffering a high-ankle sprain during the Cardinals' preseason matchup against the Raiders on Aug. 13. Arizona is reportedly hopeful Love will be able to return by Week 1. Love had 14 touches in that game — 11 rushing attempts, three catches — for a total of 72 yards.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Chiefs sign DE Niles King
summary: The Chiefs announced a pair of transactions on Monday afternoon.
full_text: The Chiefs announced a pair of transactions on Monday afternoon. They have signed defensive end Niles King to the active roster. They cleared a spot for King by waiving wide receiver Jeff Caldwell with an injury designation. King signed with the Chargers after going undrafted out of San Diego State in April, but he was let go by the Chiefs' AFC West rivals a couple of weeks later. He had 30 tackles, 10 tackles for loss and 6.5 sacks in his final college season. Caldwell was also undrafted this year and signed with the Chiefs this spring. He played in their first preseason game, but did not see action against the Bucs on Saturday.
author: Josh Alper

title: Eagles release S J.T. Gray, waive RB Ja'Quinden Jackson
summary: The Eagles dropped a pair of players from their 90-man roster on Monday.
full_text: The Eagles dropped a pair of players from their 90-man roster on Monday. They announced that they have released safety J.T. Gray and waived running back Ja'Quinden Jackson. Jackson was dropped with an injury designation after he was taken to the hospital after being injured on the opening kickoff of Saturday's game in New England. Jackson had full movement in his extremities and traveled home with the Eagles that night. He will revert to injured reserve if he clears waivers. Gray signed with the Eagles in March. He spent seven years as a core special teams player for the Saints before splitting the 2025 season between the Buccaneers and Broncos.
author: Josh Alper

title: Makai Lemon: "For sure" I'll be up to speed for Week 1
summary: Eagles wide receiver Makai Lemon returned to practice last week after an extended absence due to a hamstring injury and the rookie is confident that he'll have enough practice time to be at full speed for the season opener.
full_text: '' Eagles wide receiver Makai Lemon returned to practice last week after an extended absence due to a hamstring injury and the rookie is confident that he'll have enough practice time to be at full speed for the season opener. Lemon said "for sure" to a question about whether there's enough time for him to feel like himself for the Eagles' matchup with the Commanders and said all of the mental reps he took while off the field have served to prepare him for the task at hand. The first-round pick's process will include as much time with quarterback Jalen Hurts as he can get. “Each and every day I feel like that chemistry and that work never stops ," Lemon said. "Each and every day after practice, just talking to him whenever I can. I feel like anytime I can build that chemistry, it's good." Lemon dealt with a hamstring injury in the same leg during the offseason program and said he isn't worried about further issues on that front. "I feel pretty confident," Lemon said. "Just learning from my mistakes from the previous times, working with the trainers, setting a good plan for me, just being a professional off the field." The Eagles picked Lemon as part of their plans for life without A.J. Brown in 2026, so anything he can do to ensure he's on the field and playing at a high level over the next few weeks will be welcome in Philadelphia.
author: Josh Alper

title: Cowboys sign TE Mitch Van Vooren
summary: The Cowboys needed a tight end for depth purposes with injuries to Michael Trigg and D.J.
full_text: '' The Cowboys needed a tight end for depth purposes with injuries to Michael Trigg and D.J. Rogers. To that end, they signed tight end Mitch Van Vooren on Monday, Todd Archer of ESPN reports. In a corresponding move, the Cowboys waived defensive tackle Kelvin Gilliam. Van Vooren spent part of the offseason with the Patriots. Van Vooren, 25, entered the NFL as a rookie free agent in 2025, signing with the Seahawks. Seattle cut him on June 13, 2025, and he signed with the Browns on Aug. 4 before they waived him on Aug. 24. Van Vooren earned first-team All-NACC honors during his final collegiate season at St. Norbert after recording 33 receptions for 510 yards and 10 touchdowns. He began his college career as a track athlete at Marquette, setting the school record in the 400-meter hurdles.
author: Charean Williams

title: Kevin Stefanski: Michael Penix, Tua Tagovailoa to split first-team reps in practice
summary: After being cleared for all football activities, Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. is set to truly enter Atlanta’s quarterback competition.
full_text: '' After being cleared for all football activities, Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. is set to truly enter Atlanta’s quarterback competition. Head coach Kevin Stefanski told reporters on Monday that Penix and Tua Tagovailoa will split reps with the first-team offense on Monday. “[T]he new part for Mike is just being in there in with a full offensive line, a full defensive line, but he's been in walkthrough huddles, he's been in 7-on-7, he's obviously gone through individuals,” Stefanski said in his press conference, via transcript from the team. “So, this is a good — now that Mike is cleared — it’s good that he can start that process of getting back to 11-on-11.” Stefanski, however, said that he “can’t speculate” when asked if it’s realistic that Penix could start Week 1. “Everything we do around this building is competing,” Stefanski said. “I know it's easy to say, ‘position battles,’ and those types of things, but we're constantly competing. That's not the focus for our guys. Our guys are pushing each other by showing up and putting in the work.” Penix is returning from a torn ACL suffered midway through last season. He had been participating in individual drills and 7-on-7 work throughout training camp. While undrafted rookie Jack Strand has impressed in the preseason, Stefanski noted that at this point, Strand is not an option to be the club’s starter. “At this point, Jack's going to work with the twos and threes, but very excited about his development,” Stefanski said. “But it goes back to the earlier point of like all of our young players, we have a plan to bring them along and develop them. And the player development is a huge part of what we do, whether you're talking about quarterback position, the linebacker position, nose tackle, I don't care. Player development is important to us and being intentional about how we bring players along is important to us.” Stefanski said he is planning to play the starters against the Dolphins in Friday’s preseason finale, which could be a chance for Penix to make an impression if he gets through practice cleanly.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Steelers at an 'impasse' with Joey Porter Jr.: Cowboys among possible landing spots for emerging cornerback
summary: Porter has been holding in as he hopes to land a new contract
full_text:
While much of the talk surrounding the Steelers has been backup quarterbacks Will Howard and Drew Allar , the focus on Monday shifted to another player who has been notably absent this summer.
Joey Porter Jr . has been present during Steelers' practices, but the veteran cornerback has yet to practice as he is hoping to land a new contract. Coach Mike McCarthy said that the team is at an "impasse" with Porter, who is also on the team's physically unbale to perform list after aggravating his back during the team's mobility test on the first day of training camp.
Along with Porter, fellow defensive back Jalen Ramsey also missed training camp as he was dealing with a knee injury. Ramsey, who was taken off the team's PUP list on Monday, feels that it's time something got done with regard to Porter's contract. The Steelers' unofficial deadline to get something done with Porter is September 13, when they host the Falcons in Week 1.
"We need the whole secondary out there," Ramsey said, via ESPN. "They got to pay Joey Porter, and we need got some other guys that are out as well. So, the secondary has not been out there together yet, so I can't answer that for you."
At this point, it's more likely that Porter remains in Pittsburgh through 2026. But if that were to change, here's a look at some of the possible landing spots for Porter.
Dallas makes sense on several fronts, starting with the fact that Porter would complement what the Cowboys already have in the secondary. Porter could serve as a mentor of sorts for first-round pick Caleb Downs .
The Cowboys, who have been in spending mode since trading Micah Parsons last summer, have a considerable amount of cap space and could make a move to acquire Porter if they were inclined to do so. Making this even more logical is the fact that Jerry Jones and Steelers GM Omar Khan have a history of working out significant trades .
Speaking of Jones, the Cowboys' 83-year-old owner is desperate to end Dallas' championship drought, which is now at 31 years. That, coupled with the fact that Jones loves making splashy trades, makes this scenario even more logical.
Chicago's pass defense was one of its biggest weaknesses in 2025, and based on how it currently looks, that may well be the case for 2026 unless the Bears do something soon. The Bears spent a high draft pick on safety Dillon Thieneman , but he alone won't help make up for the current injuries the unit is dealing with. Starting safety Coby Bryant (knee) and starting nickelback Kyler Gordon (calf) are currently dealing with injuries.
It goes without saying that Porter's arrival in Chicago would strengthen the team's Super Bowl aspirations. Adding to the likelihood of this scenario is that Khan and Bears GM Ryan Poles have a history of making notable transactions .
The Steelers could trade Porter to a team that also has an interesting situation with one of their cornerbacks. Veteran cornerback Mike Jackson is entering the final year of a two-year, $10.5 million deal. Jackson outperformed his contract last season and is likely looking for a better deal for 2026 and beyond.
In this scenario, it's possible that the two teams could swap cornerbacks. The Steelers would be getting an adequate and cheaper replacement for Porter, while the Panthers would have one of the league's best cornerback duos in Porter and Jaycee Horn , who, like Porter, is the son of a notable former NFL player.
Pittsburgh would also be getting something else (likely a draft pick) in this scenario, given Porter's stature as one of the league's top young cornerbacks.
The Giants ' have heightened expectations this season that are likely buoyed by John Harbaugh's offseason arrival. But if New York really wants to have realistic hopes of competing in 2026, they need to strengthen a few areas of their team, which includes the secondary.
Porter's addition would be a big boost for the Giants, who play in a division that includes opposing quarterbacks Jalen Hurts , Dak Prescott , and Jayden Daniels . Harbaugh, who coached against Porter the previous three seasons, knows firsthand how disruptive Porter can be for an opposing offense.
Like the Panthers and Giants, the Saints are another NFC team that is looking to take the next step in 2026. After a slow start, the Saints enjoyed a strong finish to the 2025 season, including four straight wins under new coach Kelln Moore.
The Saints could use a player of Porter's caliber in their secondary to increase their odds of winning what is the NFL's most wide-open division. With that in mind, it's possible that Saints veteran GM Mickey Loomis could work something out with Khan -- a New Orleans native whose first NFL job was with the Saints -- if he feels that Porter can help the Saints snap their five-year playoff drought.
Yet another NFC team with high expectations that is looking to separate itself from the pack (pun intended). The Packers showed last year that they are willing to swing big when they traded for Parsons. It's worth wondering whether Green Bay is considering a similar move now to add another notable player to its defense.
Like the Steelers, the Packers are a franchise that measures itself only by championships. After falling short in the playoffs once again in 2025, the Packers are desperate to make a serious playoff push in 2026. That's why the Packers should be considered as a legitimate landing spot if Porter ends up on the trading block.
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: Browns name Deshaun Watson starting QB ... yet have 200 million reasons to cut him after the 2026 season
summary: Cleveland is turning to Watson now even though his contract makes it almost impossible for him to remain with the team beyond this year
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns officially have a starting quarterback in Deshaun Watson , and for some reason, they decided to give the job to a player who likely doesn't have a future with the team.
Due to the way Watson's contract is structured, the Browns will almost certainly release him in March, and that just adds another bizarre layer to the team's decision to hand him the starting QB job . The Browns could have given the job to Shedeur Sanders , but instead, they gave it to someone who essentially has no future in Cleveland.
After the Browns traded for Watson in 2022 , they gave him a five-year, $230 million contract that was fully guaranteed. Not only did the Browns make one of the worst trades in NFL history, but they followed it up by handing out one of the worst contracts ever. That's the kind of double whammy that can set your team back for the better part of a decade.
Over the past four years, the Browns have restructured Watson's contract multiple times, mainly so Cleveland could kick the can down the road on his salary cap hits. However, the Browns also included a poison pill when they restructured his contract in December 2024, and the clause pretty much guarantees they will cut Watson by March 13, 2027, so be sure to mark your calendar, Browns fans.
Here's how the clause works, via former NFL agent Joel Corry, who laid out the details in February :
By the time next March rolls around, the Browns will have paid Watson $230 million, and you can go ahead and bet everything you own that they're going to make sure they don't have to pay him another dollar.
If Watson were to somehow lead the Browns to the Super Bowl this year, the team would still be forced to cut him because there's no way they'd be able to afford to keep him with the $200 million salary becoming guaranteed in 2029.
And that's the issue here: If Watson plays well, he has no future with the team. If he doesn't play well, he has no future with the team. Starting Sanders would have made more sense.
Although the Browns will avoid paying Watson $200 million by releasing him, they will have to take a massive $86.2 million dead cap hit, which will go down as the second-largest in NFL history. The NFL record for the largest dead cap hit was set just a few months ago when the Miami Dolphins took on a $99.2 million hit when they released Tua Tagovailoa .
The Dolphins are taking on that dead cap hit over two seasons, and that's almost certainly what the Browns will do once they release Watson. The Browns will be able to designate him as a post-June 1 release, allowing them to divide the cap hit over 2027 and 2028:
The Browns' decision to acquire Watson has been a nightmare since the day it happened, but by 2028, they'll finally be able to put the entire ordeal behind them. Through four seasons, Watson has made $184 million for 19 starts, and he's gone 9-10 in those starts. Yes, that means the Browns have paid him $20.4 million per win. That's good work if you can get it.
The Browns will pay Watson $46 million more in 2026, and that will likely be the last time they give him a single penny.
author: John Breech

title: Kayshon Boutte trade grades: Texans fleece Patriots while filling key roster need
summary: New England strengthened a potential future playoff foe while getting very little in return
full_text:
A day after Mike Vrabel lamented about the state of his roster, the Patriots did something about it. New England traded receiver Kayshon Boutte to the Texans in exchange for safety Jaylen Reed and a draft pick, according to The Ringer . It will be a seventh-round pick, ESPN reports .
Boutte, 24, spent his first three NFL seasons with the Patriots, who selected him in the sixth round of the 2023 draft. After catching just two passes during his rookie season, Boutte developed a bigger role in the Patriots' offense each of the past two seasons. He set career-highs with 43 receptions and 589 yards in 2024 and caught a career-high six touchdowns in 2025.
Like Boutte, Reed was also the 187th overall pick in his respective draft. As a rookie last season, Reed made one regular-season start while appearing in seven games. He finished the regular season with 14 tackles and a fumble recovery. Reed started in each of Houston's two playoff games and had two tackles during Houston's season-ending loss to New England in the divisional round of the playoffs.
Who won the trade? Let's find out.
Rumblings already existed that Boutte would ultimately be traded. With Boutte entering his final year under contract, the Patriots deserve a little credit for getting something in return for him in the form of draft capital and a player who can help them in 2026.
That being said, it's surprising that the Patriots couldn't get more for Boutte, an emerging receiver who is still playing on his rookie contract. This just gives off a vibe that the Patriots simply wanted to get this done and move on.
As noted above, it was less than 48 hours ago when Vrabel expressed concern for his team's lack of depth. And while the Patriots strengthened their secondary by getting Reed (who, like Boutte, is a player who should be on the rise), they weakened their depth at receiver by parting ways with Boutte.
Making this trade even worse is that the Patriots traded Boutte to an AFC competitor (the only worse move would have been trading him to division rival Buffalo). Instead of sending him to the NFC, the Patriots dealt Boutte to a team they may very well face in the 2026 playoffs.
Houston deserves a ton of credit for quickly and emphatically addressing their need at receiver after Jayden Higgins went down with a season-ending ACL injury.
After Higgins went down, the Texans reportedly placed a call to New England about Boutte and another to Baltimore regarding Rashod Bateman . They reportedly weren't interested in a reunion with DeAndre Hopkins , who recently became the assistant receivers coach at Georgia Tech.
Given Bateman's legal issues , Boutte became the clear-cut option for Houston, who ultimately pulled off a very favorable deal with the Patriots. Boutte will now fill Higgins' spot while joining a receiving corps that also includes Nick Collins and Jaylin Noel . His arrival should also aid C.J. Stroud , the Texans' former Pro Bowl quarterback, who is hoping to return to form that saw him win Offensive Rookie of the Year back in 2023.
Higgins' injury could have been a big blow for Houston, which is trying to get beyond the divisional round of the AFC playoffs this year after losing in that round in each of the past three seasons. The trade for Boutte has put them back on track.
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: Latest NFL injury updates: Ashton Jeanty avoids major injury, other running backs uncertain for Week 1
summary: Who will be ready for season openers, and who's trying to get there?
full_text:
The second week of the preseason is over, and that means all preseason action for expected starters is a thing of the past, too. Teams generally treat the final preseason game as a chance to evaluate depth charts, battles for backup roles, roster spots and practice squad spots. Starters, meanwhile, will have their attention fully turned to Week 1 at last.
This training camp and preseason cycle have been particularly busy on the injury front, unfortunately. Hopefully, that's mostly behind us as teams hone in on Week 1 prep. As such, we've turned our injury analysis toward Week 1. As injury news continues to filter in, we'll be tracking not only the bumps and bruises (and sometimes more) but also their impact on season openers' availability.
Aug. 24 -- Lower-body injury. Dan Quinn said Monday that Jacory Croskey-Merritt is dealing with an undisclosed injury, potentially sustained near the end of last week, and reporters said he has a lower-body injury. He could be back next week.
Aug. 24 -- Hamstring. Dave Canales said Monday that Chuba Hubbard is expected to return for Week 1 and that Hubbard and Jonathon Brooks would operate in a committee in that case. Hubbard himself said his hamstring feels good, but the team is protecting him from himself after he returned too early last year.
Aug. 19 -- Calf strain. Oweh, who signed a four-year, $96 million deal with the Commanders this offseason, suffered a calf strain either Aug. 17 or 18 (he did not practice on the 18th), and Quinn announced the injury on the 19th.
Aug. 17 -- Groin. Hall suffered a non-contact groin sprain, but coach Aaron Glenn said it would sideline him for 2 to 3 weeks and not carry over into the regular season. The Jets ' Week 1 opener was nearly four weeks away when Glenn provided the timetable.
Aug. 24 -- Neck injury recovery. Jesse Minter said, "I don't know the answer to that right now," when asked about Madubuike's Week 1 availability. Madubuike suffered the injury -- thought to be career-threatening at one point -- early last season. He has practiced in a limited capacity so far this training camp.
Aug. 23 -- Ankle sprain. Just as soon as it looked like we were done with injury news over the weekend, one more player got added to the list, and it's a big one. Ashton Jeanty went down during a non-contact catching drill and could not put any weight on his leg. Hours later, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported it's an ankle sprain, and the Raiders are unsure how long it will keep last year's No. 6 overall pick out.
Aug. 23 -- Torn Achilles recovery. George Kittle's impressive recovery from a torn Achilles suffered in the playoffs hit a new high Sunday, when the 49ers activated him off the PUP list . A Week 1 appearance against the Rams in Australia is still on the table, though not a certainty by any measure.
Aug. 17 -- Knee hyperextension diagnosis. Kyle Monangai hyperextended his right knee on Aug. 16, and the next day, Ben Johnson described Monangai's status as "week-to-week."
Aug. 20 -- Hip. Dan Campbell said Sam LaPorta's status for Week 1 is up in the air as he deals with a hip issue.
Aug. 19 -- Pectoral injury recovery. Meeting with the media on Wednesday, Eagles defensive coordinator Vic Fangio said there's concern regarding Greenard's availability for Week 1 due to a pec injury. The Eagles acquired Greenard from the Vikings for a third-round pick and gave him a four-year, $98 million contract this offseason.
Aug. 18 -- High ankle sprain. While seeing a surprisingly large role -- 14 touches while playing nearly the entire first half -- in Week 1 of the preseason, Jeremiyah Love suffered a high ankle sprain, leaving his status for Week 1 up in the air. The No. 3 overall pick got bent awkwardly during a tackle on his final touch of the game, and after it took a few days to get a full diagnosis, it was not good news.
Aug. 24 -- Torn patella. Jesse Minter told the media that Pinter is out for the season with a torn patella. He had been working as the Ravens ' first-team center during training camp. Ethan Pocic , coming off a torn Achilles, will likely take his spot.
Aug. 23 -- Broken ankle. Mike Macdonald said Clark, a second-round pick out of TCU, will miss "several months" with a broken ankle suffered in Seattle's preseason Week 2 game against the Titans . Clark was carted off the field with his lower leg, ankle and foot in an air cast.
Aug. 23 -- Placed on IR. Tyler Biadasz suffered a gruesome-looking injury in an Aug. 18 joint practice with the 49ers, and the initial diagnosis of "out indefinitely with ACL damage and other knee damage" wasn't promising. On Aug. 23, the Chargers officially put Biadasz on IR, a difficult blow for a team in need of much better offensive line play this season.
Aug. 23 -- Placed on IR. Alex Wright , who got a three-year extension after a strong 2025, suffered a torn Achilles in an Aug. 20 joint practice with the Bills . The Browns officially placed him on IR on Sunday and signed Derek Barnett in a corresponding move.
Aug. 21 -- Placed on IR. Jayden Higgins tore his ACL in an Aug. 18 joint practice with the Ravens, leaving a considerable hole in the Texans ' wide receiver room behind standout Nico Collins . He officially went on IR on Friday.
Aug. 19 -- MCL sprain diagnosis. Kamara sprained his MCL in a joint practice with the Cowboys on Aug. 18, and one day later, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported he'd miss at least a month. The Saints ' Week 1 matchup with the Lions was less than a month away at the time of Schefter's report.
Aug. 17 -- Hamstring injury diagnosis. Jordyn Tyson will reportedly miss two months after suffering a right hamstring injury on Aug. 13 during a joint practice with the Jaguars . The No. 8 overall pick in April's draft, Tyson has dealt with several hamstring issues, though this one is separate from previous episodes.
author: Zachary Pereles

title: 49ers owner Jed York arrested in Ohio, pleads no contest after prostitution charge amended
summary: York was sentenced to two days in jail and ordered to pay $1,150 in fines
full_text:
San Francisco 49ers owner and CEO Jed York was arrested in East Palestine, Ohio, this weekend and pleaded no contest to misdemeanor charges of disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools, per WKBN . York was sentenced to two days in the Columbiana County Jail with credit for one day served and ordered to pay $1,150 in fines.
Court documents obtained by KRON4 state the disorderly conduct charge was amended from engaging in prostitution.
York was arrested by the local police department, which was assisting the Mahoning Valley Human Trafficking Task Force, at Wheat Hill Mobile Home Community off state Route 170.
The 49ers released a statement on York's arrest, via ESPN , saying: "As this is a legal matter, which has been resolved, we will not be providing any further comment at this time."
York was born and raised in Youngstown, not far from where he was arrested. He became CEO of the 49ers in 2008 while his parents, John and Denise York, assumed roles of co-chairmen. York's grandfather, Edward DeBartolo Sr., bought the franchise in 1977, while York's uncle, Eddie DeBartolo Jr., served as the team's owner from 1977 to 2000.
York could be subject to discipline from the league under the personal conduct policy. According to the 49ers' official website , York currently serves on three NFL committees: Stadium, Media O&O (NFL's owned media businesses), Business Ventures, and Fan Engagement and Major Events.
author: Jordan Dajani

title: Browns starting QB Deshaun Watson issues apology for remarks trashing Cleveland fans
summary: Watson is unpopular among Browns fans but attempted to earn back some goodwill
full_text:
Just two days after he called out Cleveland Browns fans for giving him a less-than-welcome reception in his second preseason game , Deshaun Watson secured the team's starting quarterback role . As the face of the offense once again, one of Watson's first duties on the job was to mend the tense relationship with the Cleveland faithful .
Fans booed Watson off the field after he went 5-for-12 for 36 yards and threw an interception during the 31-7 preseason Week 2 blowout loss to the Buffalo Bills . He called it a "disrespectful thing" for the Browns' supporters to jeer him, considering all that he has been through during his time in the AFC North, including a torn Achilles.
Watson seemingly wants to let bygones be bygones with the fans, but coach Todd Monken's decision to name him the starting quarterback was far from universally well-received . His apology may only go so far in building any bridges he burned in Cleveland.
"Putting a lot of time these last two years to get back and spend time in this facility and the city, meeting a lot of different people in the community, I thought I was going to get a little different response," Watson said Monday of being booed in his latest outing. "But I think my emotions got the best of me. My comments wasn't intended to go at any of the fans around the city, because there's been a lot of great fans that have been supporting me."
Monken said that Watson's comments toward the fanbase would not impact his decision on whether Watson or Shedeur Sanders would secure the No. 1 quarterback job. He was true to his word, as it was a quick turnaround between Watson riling up the fans and winning the position battle.
"I know the frustration," Watson said. "This organization has put a lot of investment in coming to get me back in '22. Things haven't been going the right direction that we thought it was. A lot of injuries. A lot of time off and not putting the best football and my foot forward. Again, I understand the frustration. I understand everything that goes into that. Moving forward, I just want to focus on football and making sure that I'm putting the best product out there and having the best ability."
In three half-seasons since he signed a mega contract with the Browns in 2022, Watson failed to come close to delivering on the value Cleveland placed on him. The five-year, $230 million fully guaranteed contract is the source of immense frustration for Browns backers, as all it got them was one of the lowest-performing quarterbacks in the NFL .
Watson never played more than seven games in his first three years with the franchise, and he threw just 19 touchdowns to 12 interceptions in that span. The three-time Pro Bowler regressed immensely upon his arrival from Houston and, in 2024, ranked last among quarterbacks in numerous statistics.
In order to rekindle some of his early-career success, Watson might need the support of his fanbase. The fans seemingly have little left to give him, though.
"I thrive off the energy," Watson said. "I thrive off the energy of the fans. I thrive off the energy of the community. I thrive off all that stuff. Looking back at my history at Clemson and previously at the Houston organization, I was a big community guy, big city guy, big fan guy. Again, my emotions got the best of me. I'm human. I take full responsibility of that."
author: Carter Bahns

title: Breaking down Browns' bizarre decision to start Deshaun Watson, plus our 2026 NFL All-Breakout team
summary: Plus, the biggest winners and losers from preseason Week 2, rookie QB grades and the latest news from around the NFL
full_text:
Hello football friends, and welcome to the Monday edition of the Pick Six newsletter!
The second week of the preseason is officially in the books, and I have to say, this might go down as the greatest special teams weekend of preseason football in NFL history. We got a 69-YARD FIELD GOAL from Harrison Butker , the 49ers had an 83-yard punt return for a touchdown and a rookie quarterback had to fill in as the punter. Nothing says preseason football like a rookie signal-caller being forced to punt.
Speaking of preseason, the Browns played over the weekend, and the fans in Cleveland spent half the game booing Deshaun Watson . However, it doesn't seem like those boos had any impact on the starting QB battle, which we'll get to below.
As always, here's your daily reminder to tell all your friends to sign up for the newsletter. To get them signed up, all you have to do is click here . Let's get to the rundown.
The Browns QB battle is officially over, and Cleveland fans are getting exactly what they didn't want: Deshaun Watson being named the starter over Shedeur Sanders . This means Watson will be the starting quarterback in Week 1 when the Browns travel to Jacksonville to face the Jaguars , but how much longer will he keep the job after that? Let's break everything down, starting with the boos from Saturday.
Watson didn't see any action until the third quarter, and once he stepped on the field, he got booed pretty much every time he touched the ball. To make matters worse, he actually called out the fans for booing him in his postgame press conference .
"I think the whole world knows it has nothing to do about the performance," Watson said. "It's a little bit more personal than that. So, I think it's a disrespectful thing."
This might be the least self-aware response any NFL player has ever given at a press conference. Before being traded to Cleveland, he was accused of sexual assault by more than two dozen massage therapists.
And on the field, he's been a total bust in Cleveland: He's only played in 19 games over four seasons and hasn't been good. In Saturday's game, he finished 5 of 12 for 36 yards with an interception.
Monken said Watson's postgame comments wouldn't impact his starting QB decision, which ended up being the case.
Although Sanders appeared to have outplayed Watson in Cleveland's two preseason games, Monken was likely swayed by what he saw in training camp. Monken is implementing a new offense in his first year with the Browns, so he was always going to give the job to the QB who's been running it better, and he seems to think that's Watson.
Now let's take a look at what this means for the Browns.
This feels like a situation where the Browns are simply trying to salvage what they can after making the worst trade in NFL history in 2022, when they gave up three first-round picks along with a third-round pick and two fourth-round picks to acquire Watson from Houston.
As part of the deal, the QB landed a fully guaranteed five-year, $230 million contract that expires after this year. The Browns are on the hook to pay Watson $46 million this season whether he plays or not, and that could be why the organization is giving him one more chance.
If you want the full story on the Browns' QB decision, we've got that here .
The second week of the preseason is officially in the books, and like we do every week, we have some winners and losers. Garrett Podell and Zach Pereles teamed up for this week's list.
Here are two winners and two losers from Week 2:
If you want to see our full list of winners and losers, be sure to click here .
Everyone on the internet loves to overreact to things, and that's especially true when we're talking about the NFL. With that in mind, Carter Bahns decided to take a look at several things that happened during the second week of the preseason to decide if we're all overreacting.
A week after he racked up seven catches for 63 yards in San Francisco's preseason opener, Stribling tied with KhaDarel Hodge for the most catches (four) and yards (46) of any 49er in Week 2.
Importantly, three of those catches came on connections with starting quarterback Brock Purdy . The two were on the same page from the get-go in the rout of the Chargers and strung together three completions on the opening drive. Stribling then hauled in a 21-yard grab from Mac Jones on the team's second possession.
Stribling, the No. 33 overall pick in April's draft, saw his Rookie of the Year odds spike. Per DraftKings , his +1100 odds are the fifth-shortest behind only Jeremiyah Love , Jadarian Price , Fernando Mendoza and Carnell Tate .
The Packers' search to find a successor to Mason Crosby since his departure in 2022 has been anything but smooth. It appears that they finally have an answer, however.
They were the only team to use a draft pick on a kicker in 2026, and it looks like an astute move. Sixth-rounder Trey Smack has been a preseason standout.  In Week 1, Smack drilled a 58-yard field goal and matched that distance on a kick that was ultimately waved off for a defensive penalty. He went 3-for-3 in his professional debut.
That was just the start of it. He was even better this week by making all four of his field goal attempts, with two coming from more than 50 yards out. His longest was a 59-yard blast.
Tagovailoa's grasp on the starting QB role is tenuous. The threat to Tagovailoa is twofold. First, he has been underwhelming in camp. Second, Michael Penix Jr . has been cleared for 11-on-11 work and figures to make a run at the job. This always figured to be a two-man battle, and now that Penix is healthy, he has about three weeks to make up ground and potentially leap past his fellow southpaw.
There are plenty more overreactions from the second week of the preseason, and if you want to check those out, you can do that here .
For the second straight week, we're breaking down how each rookie quarterback looked during the preseason.
Carter Bahns was in charge of handing out these grades, so let's check out one good grade, one bad grade and one ugly grade.
Breakdown: After Tommy DeVito played the first half, Morton took all the second-half snaps in the Patriots ' 24-21 win over the Eagles . That timeshare gave him the opportunity to flex his clutch gene. The second of his two touchdown drives decided the game. Trailing 21-17 with about a minute to play, Morton unleashed a 37-yard strike to Nick DeGennaro , who beat his defender to get into the end zone for the game-winner. It put the final touches on a splendid 13-for-17 day for Morton in which he accumulated 129 yards through the air.
NOTE: Morton also served as the team's PUNTER after Patriots starter Bryce Baringer had to leave the game because he wasn't feeling good.
Breakdown: It was always going to be a massive ask for Drew Allar to replicate the kind of magic he displayed in Week 1. He did not come particularly close to repeating that three-touchdown effort. The most positive takeaway from Week 2 was that he was turnover-free; Will Howard, in comparison, threw two interceptions before giving way to his backup. Still, Allar took three sacks and completed fewer than 50% of his 23 throws, and the Steelers gained just six first downs with him under center in the second half.
Breakdown: The No. 1 overall pick threw an 80-yard pick-six on the Raiders ' opening possession, and he finished his first start 8-for-15 for 86 yards. He also took a sack for an 11-yard loss in the Raiders' 22-20 win over the Texans .
