We have an All-Breakout team for offense and a separate one for defense, but today, we're only going to…
author: John Breech

title: Browns name Deshaun Watson starter days after he called out fans: Veteran QB beats out Shedeur Sanders
summary: Cleveland is giving Watson another opportunity in the final year of his contract after he missed the entire 2025 season recovering from Achilles injuries
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns have named Deshaun Watson the starter for the team's season opener at the Jaguars , beating out Shedeur Sanders for the starting role, per CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz. It will be Watson's first game since Oct. 10, 2024, when he tore his Achilles. He re-tore his Achilles in early January 2025, causing him to miss all of last year.
The decision comes just two days after Watson took several shots at Browns fans following his poor performance in preseason Week 2 against the Bills . Watson was just 5 of 12 passing for 35 yards and an interception, playing with (and against) backups in the third and fourth quarters while boos rained down.
"I think the whole world knows it has nothing to do about the performance," Watson said . "It's a little bit more personal than that. So, I think it's a disrespectful thing."
Browns coach Todd Monken insisted Sunday that the comments wouldn't affect his quarterback choice , and they didn't.
"Deshaun is going to start against Jacksonville," Monken told reporters on Monday. "(I) took in the full body of work over the course of offseason to training camp to the games, the joint practice, and ultimately felt like to start the season on the road Deshaun gave us the best chance to move the ball and score points -- I mean that's really what it's about. I felt that way going into last game but wasn't sure, and after we talked as a staff and after we relooked at everything, we're gonna go that direction."
Watson issued an opening-statement apology when he met with the media, shortly after the starting announcement had been made.
"First off, I want to address the comments from Saturday after the game," Watson said. "I think just human nature, just myself being very emotional, putting a lot of time these last two years to get back and spend time in this facility, in the city, meeting a lot of people in the community, I thought I was gonna get a little different response.
"But I think my emotions got the best of me, and my comments wasn't intending to go at any of the fans around in the city, because there's been a lot of great fans that have been supporting me, and I know the frustration. This organization has put a lot of investment in coming to get me back in '22, and things haven't been going the right direction that we thought it was, you know, a lot of injuries, a lot of time off and not putting the best football and my foot forward. Again, I understand the frustration, I understand everything that kind of goes into that, and moving forward, I just want to focus on football, making sure that I'm putting the best product out there, having the best ability."
Monken said he doesn't anticipate the question of starting quarterback being a week-to-week issue, and while Watson won the job, the coach praised Sanders for closing the gap on the veteran through the preseason.
"I think Shedeur has done a great job, come a long ways and we are excited about his future," Monken said.
Watson was regarded as a slight leader for much of the quarterback battle, often earning the first reps with the first team, even if the overall reps with the starters ended up somewhat evenly split. Watson started in preseason Week 1 alongside starters, while Sanders started in preseason Week 2 with mostly backups. Even so, Monken, in his first year as a head coach, said the competition played out in "the best way I thought we could go about it."
Watson, who turns 31 the day after the Browns' season opener, has been a monumental disappointment in Cleveland, and his acquisition has been regarded as one of the worst in major professional sports history. In 2022, the Browns traded 2022, 2023 and 2024 first-round picks, a third-round pick and two fourth-round picks to the Houston Texans for Watson and a sixth-round pick. The Browns then gave Watson an unprecedented, fully guaranteed five-year, $230 million contract.
At the time, Watson faced 22 civil lawsuits related to allegations of sexual misconduct at massage therapy sessions. The number eventually grew to 27. All 27 have been resolved, with at least 24 ending in confidential settlements. The last two were dismissed -- at least one with a settlement -- earlier this year . The Texans also previously reached confidential settlements with 30 women over claims regarding Watson.
Watson did not play at all in his final season in Houston (2021) and was suspended for the first 11 games of 2022 after being traded to Cleveland. In total, he has appeared in just 19 games since the trade, and he was among the NFL's worst quarterbacks when on the field.
The Browns hope an improved supporting cast helps lift Watson. Cleveland overhauled its offensive line, bringing in four new starters, and drafted wide receiver KC Concepcion in the first round and wide receiver Denzel Boston in the second round. Both have impressed in training camp and are expected to start right away. The Browns also return tight end Harold Fannin Jr . and running back Quinshon Judkins after both had impressive rookie years.
This is the final year of Watson's contract.
As Monken said Saturday, the second preseason game was just another data point in a set of hundreds, ranging far past games and even practices. And as he said Sunday, Watson's comments about the fans wouldn't impact his decision. He appears to have held true to both.
Watson had been the front-runner, even if ever so slightly, for quite a bit, according to various reports. His chance to start in the first preseason game, alongside the starters, was an indication of that, even if Monken said both Watson and Sanders would each get a preseason start (something he held true to as well). For as poorly as Watson played Saturday, he held up decently -- nothing special, but nothing disastrous -- the previous week , and Monken described his return to playing football as "awesome."
Watson's experience and ability to function in the offense were also keys; after all, he has been in far more NFL offenses, including those with more parallels to Monken's. Furthermore, Watson impressed this offseason with his approach and work ethic, per "NFL on CBS" sideline reporter Aditi Kinkhabwala.
"In all the years I have been around Deshaun Watson, this is the best that he is mentally," Kinkhabwala told 92.3 The Fan last week. "The space that he is in right now, his focus, the way that he stayed in Cleveland all summer, went to work quietly every day, didn't ask anything of any of the staff in the building at all, was simply focused on living with his wife and working on football and his rehab. Just the conversations I have with him on the side -- different."
It is also worth noting, in light of Watson's most recent comments, that the Browns' first two games -- Week 1 at the Jaguars and Week 2 at the Buccaneers -- are on the road.
"I feel like I get more love on road games than I do home games," Watson said. "If it is my spot and he does makes me the [starter], maybe it's 17 away games then. I don't know."
author: Zachary Pereles

title: Browns fans, keep booing: Todd Monken picking Deshaun Watson over Shedeur Sanders is wrong, even if it's right
summary: The Browns will give the keys to Watson, at least to start the year
full_text:
Maybe Deshaun Watson was always bound to win the job. The signs could have told us as much.
He got the first reps with the first team more often than not. He has more experience across more offenses. He did everything right this summer in terms of work ethic and demeanor. When Todd Monken gave Watson the start in the first preseason game , alongside the starters, it was another sign, this one the biggest of all. When Monken said Watson's incendiary shots at Browns fans after an awful preseason Week 2 showing wouldn't play a role in the choice, it was yet another sign.
So when news leaked Monday that Watson indeed won the quarterback battle over Shedeur Sanders and will start Week 1 against the Jaguars , it was no surprise.
Let me clarify: It was no surprise the Browns made yet another mistake regarding Watson, arguably the worst trade acquisition in pro sports history.
I will not pretend to know one one-hundredth of what Monken has already forgotten about football. There are legitimate football reasons Monken -- a very good offensive coach for a long time -- made this decision. His job is to do what he thinks will make his team better, not appease fans or media or anyone outside the organization, really. Watson has experience with systems and concepts similar to Monken's. This decision was made with hundreds of data points in mind, most of which are unseen by the public, from games to practices to meetings to workouts to everything else in between. I'm not privy to 99% of what went into this decision.
I can still confidently say it's the wrong one, even if it's right in a football sense. Watson's performance on and off the field Saturday is justification enough. After a truly terrible outing that included a rookie-esque interception, several misfires on open opportunities downfield and several moments of sheer panic the moment he felt pressure, Watson decided to lash out at Browns fans about ... everything.
About the booing? "I think the whole world knows it has nothing to do about the performance. It's a little bit more personal than that. So, I think it's a disrespectful thing."
About the injuries? "Last time I played on this field, I tore my Achilles. That same fan base, they cheered when I got hurt. What does that have to do with anything about performance? When a person gets hurt, especially in your home stadium, and they cheer."
He even played victim. "I thought being away for two years and working myself back from two Achilles injuries and putting the time in, being around the facility, being around the city, doing charity work in the city, supporting the Cleveland Browns, hanging out with fans whenever I do see them, being honest, being the type of person I know I am, and the character would help, and I guess it hasn't."
Monken saw and heard that and wanted more of it?
Browns fans boo Watson for reasons bigger than Watson. They boo him for his truly awful play, yes, and for the truly awful things he's been accused of doing to other human beings, but they boo him for more than that.
They boo him because they can't boo Jimmy Haslam -- at least not as a guy who actually plays. The Browns' owner decided, even amid the then-22 civil lawsuits filed against Watson, to not only trade three first-round picks (and more) for Watson in 2022, but to then give him an unprecedented fully guaranteed five-year, $230 million contract.
They boo him because he is the reason the Browns have continued to be among the NFL's worst teams, even with one of the best defenders of all-time, Myles Garrett , on the roster -- and now Garrett is gone, another five years wasted and still no winning future in sight.
They boo him because two-time Coach of the Year Kevin Stefanski is gone, too, and having Watson made it almost impossible for him to build a winner. The two times he did build winners, it was without Watson.
They boo him because they can't escape him or his outrageous contract or his horrible play, and now he's being put front and center again .
Browns fans want to win, as every other fanbase does. But they also want to not be embarrassed. The Watson trade and contract were one thing. The atrocious play since then is another. Watching awful quarterbacking is a weekly tradition in Cleveland. Watching it and feeling trapped, though, is a whole different animal.
In 2024, 39 quarterbacks threw at least 200 passes. Of those 39, Watson ranked ...
We can take it back farther. Since 2010, there have been 581 instances of a player throwing at least 200 passes in a season. Watson's 2024 success rate ranked 572nd out of those 581. Basically, every other player behind him, we never heard from -- at least as a starting quarterback -- again. Jimmy Clausen , Ryan Lindley , Blaine Gabbert , Brady Quinn , Tim Tebow , Mike Glennon . That's the company. Read it and weep.
But Watson just keeps popping back up, like a Whac-A-Mole. Two years later -- and, for Watson, two Achilles tears later -- he is somehow back again. It's a nightmare the Browns can't escape. Those cheers Watson remembers from when he tore his Achilles in 2024? Maybe some fans were cheering for the injury, and I can't say I agree with that. But maybe fans were cheering that they had finally escaped the Deshaun Watson nightmare. Instead, it's back, now with a vengeance.
"It's a mental battle every day," Watson said. "I feel like I get more love on road games than I do home games. If it is my spot and he does makes me the [starter], maybe it's 17 away games then. I don't know."
The Browns open with two road games, but what makes Monken or Watson think Week 3 at home will be any better than Saturday's disaster? Watson will get booed heavily. He won't play well, but that's beside the point. He probably won't react well, either. Is that truly the way Monken wants to build this franchise?
The football is almost irrelevant, though try telling that to Monken. Sanders might indeed be a worse quarterback than Watson, though even I have significant doubts. Again, it's Monken's job to put the players he feels are best on the field. Anything else would be disingenuous. In that regard, his choice is "right." In every other regard, it's wrong.
One day, the Browns will move on. But that day, sadly, isn't today. Watson will play. Sanders will play. The Browns will lose. The world will keep turning, one mistake by the lake at a time.
If you want to be a Sanders optimist -- and don't let me stop you -- we can look at it this way: Sanders will play this year, whether due to Watson injury or ineffectiveness. The best path forward for Sanders will be to continue what he's done. Work hard. Impress with the second team. Be a good teammate. Be prepared the moment he's called upon.
"I thought he did a lot of really good things," Monken said after Saturday's game. "I'm really proud of him and where he's come from. From the moment I got here until now, very impressive."
Similarly, Sanders said he's "improved every aspect of [his] life." He was a beacon of positivity -- and a stark contrast to Watson -- before the quarterback decision; he has to remain so after the decision.
The start to Sanders' career has been a difficult one, some self-inflicted, but much not. Opportunity is still right there. He is not doomed to be a backup, just as he wasn't doomed to be a backup last year; he started seven games.
The Browns aren't going to trade Sanders. He is a young player on a team trying to build, and much of 2026 will be collecting information on who can help that build, even if no player or coach will admit it. That's why Sanders' continued progress, even as a backup, is essential. Maybe it's to be a starter. Maybe it's to be a good backup. Maybe it's for a job elsewhere.
Sanders will get his shot, and what more can he really ask for? It is a disappointment that the shot isn't in Week 1? Sure. Sanders has to keep plugging away regardless.
In the grand scheme of things, the Browns almost certainly don't have their 2027 quarterback on their roster.…
author: Zachary Pereles

title: 2027 NFL Draft: Arch Manning, Dante Moore lead hyped QB class, but history offers a warning
summary: Meet FRED, a historical model that reveals what makes a first-round QB -- and which 2027 prospects could make the next big leap
full_text:
Every few years, we get to November wondering how a quarterback nobody was talking about over the summer suddenly became a first-rounder.
Burrow, Daniels and Jones didn't take the same path to the first round, but their eventual landing spots would've been difficult to predict before their final college seasons. That got me wondering whether we're looking at this the wrong way: Instead of arguing every summer about which well-known name should be QB1, could we identify the quarterbacks most likely to become first-round picks before everyone else catches on?
That's the question I wanted to answer with the 2027 class. I went through every draft class back to 2015 and looked at the quarterbacks who made big late-career jumps, the supposed first-rounders who slipped and the strange cases where the league's evaluation ultimately went somewhere the numbers didn't. Then I went back to my 2027 notes to see where the history matched what I'd seen on tape -- and, maybe more importantly, where it didn't.
For context: Based on my summer scouting, Dante Moore and Arch Manning are my top two quarterbacks, and both carry top-five grades on my overall board. Brendan Sorsby and Julian Sayin round out my current first-round quarterbacks, followed by Jayden Maiava and Darian Mensah early in Round 2. That's the scouting baseline for our purposes here. Now let's see what history thinks.
let's go! pic.twitter.com/N7sdDJ1Y8I
Also: Ran Carthon, my co-host on the "With the First Pick" podcast, and I have already done deep dives on our favorite quarterbacks in the 2027 draft class, and you can check that out below:
I built a model around the question I really wanted to answer: How close is a quarterback to looking like a future first-round pick? The result is the First-Round Readiness Score -- or FRED, for short.
FRED looks at the things that have historically separated first-round quarterbacks -- passing efficiency, touchdown and interception rates, QBR, experience and, importantly, a quarterback's best three- and five-game stretches.
The idea isn't to predict whether he'll succeed in the NFL ; it's to measure how much his college performance, at that point in his career, resembles what we've historically seen from future first-round picks.
The scale is intentionally easy to read: 50 is the historical first-round threshold. But for what we're trying to learn here, when a quarterback gets there may be just as important as whether he gets there at all. The most revealing FRED score turned out to be the one before his final college season because it tells us which quarterbacks had already started playing like future top picks with another season still to go.
And here's where FRED gets interesting: 22 quarterbacks in our historical sample had played enough football to reach a FRED score of 50 before their final seasons. All 22 became first-round picks. That doesn't make 50 a magic draft grade -- and we'll get to the exceptions in a minute -- but the timing matters.
One quarterback in the 2027 class is already there. Ohio State's Julian Sayin leads the way at 55.3, followed by USC's Maiava (43.4), Oklahoma State's Drew Mestemaker (40.4), Miami's Mensah (39.4) and Sorsby (35.4). For perspective, Patrick Mahomes was at 55.7 entering his final season at Texas Tech, Burrow was at 58.6 before his 2019 breakout and Josh Allen was at 51.6 for Wyoming. Most recently, Daniels was at 49.5 before his Heisman campaign.
I'll occasionally use one other number: Historical First-Round Probability, which looks across a quarterback's broader college résumé. Think of it as a second opinion; for identifying who may be on the verge of making the leap, FRED is the headline number.
Tua Tagovailoa (87.1); Jordan Love (61.2); Joe Burrow (58.6)
Kenny Pickett (54.4); Sam Howell (29.2); Matt Corral (17.1)
Caleb Williams (79.5); Drake Maye (78.0); Bo Nix (68.8)
Jaxson Dart (54.7); Dillon Gabriel (39.4); Kyle McCord (38.9)
Fernando Mendoza (55.7); Cade Klubnik (36.4); Carson Beck (21.2)
Julian Sayin (55.3); Jayden Maiava (43.4); Drew Mestemaker (40.4)
That's what makes this class so interesting. The top three QBs have an average FRED score of 46.4, third among the six classes in the table above, and actually ahead of the 2025 and 2026 groups. But there's still a sizable gap between them and the loaded 2020 and 2024 classes, which entered their final college seasons with top-three averages of 68.9 and 75.5. Sayin has already crossed 50, but Maiava and Mestemaker haven't. So this isn't quite 2022, but it isn't 2020 or 2024, either.
There is an important distinction: Ty Simpson isn't missing from the 2026 row because his score was bad; he just hadn't played enough snaps to have a meaningful FRED score. Kyler Murray is an even more extreme example. He entered his final Oklahoma season having attempted just 18 passes over the previous two years, then won the Heisman and went No. 1 overall.
Not enough information isn't the same thing as a low score. That's important when we're trying to figure out young quarterbacks such as CJ Carr , but it's much harder to use as an explanation for experienced players who remain well below 50.
All 22 quarterbacks in the historical sample who reached 50 before their final seasons became first-round picks. But the 22-for-22 finding sounds almost too clean, so I tried to break it.
And ... I found three exceptions, although all three were right on the doorstep. Daniels was at 49.5 before his final season, Zach Wilson was at 48.9 and Josh Rosen was at 48.5. All three became first-round picks, though only one appears to have the makings of a franchise quarterback.
FRED still can't tell us whether NFL teams believe the traits, age, competition, medical history and everything else about a player should put him in the first-round conversation. But it's a pretty good indicator. Daniels, Wilson and Rosen didn't clear 50, but they didn't miss by much. That's a much different starting point than a quarterback entering his final season at 10 or 20 and needing to make the kind of leap Cam Ward eventually did.
Ward is the real reason 50 can't be treated as a magic number.
Ward entered his final college season with a FRED score of 6.8. His Historical First-Round Probability was only 18.3%. Put simply, his body of work to that point looked very little like that of the quarterbacks who historically became first-round picks. Then he transferred from Washington State to Miami, and everything changed.
Ward didn't just put up bigger numbers at Miami. His passing efficiency jumped, his QBR exploded and the offense around him improved dramatically. Bill Connelly's Offensive SP+ ( which measures an offense's efficiency while accounting for the quality of the opponents it faced ) jumped from 31.0 at Washington State to 44.2 at Miami. That moved Ward from an offense well below what we typically see around first-round quarterbacks to one comfortably within that range.
His FRED score jumped, too. And the scouting notes filled in what the numbers couldn't: arm talent, creativity, pocket movement, throws from different platforms and a quarterback whose game appeared to be maturing. Ward never reached 50, but he showed Tennessee enough on tape to make him the No. 1 pick -- and it was absolutely the right decision.
That's the exception worth remembering with this class. A low starting point isn't a death sentence, and Ward is proof that a quarterback doesn't have to reach 50 for the NFL to ultimately see a first-rounder. But he also shows just how much has to change when a quarterback enters his final season nowhere close to it. A quarterback sitting at 5 or 10 doesn't need a nice season. He needs to make us rethink the player we thought we were evaluating in August.
My big board starts with Moore and Manning, but history is much more interested in Maiava. Moore's FRED score is 19.2, while Manning is at 3.2 (you read that right).
Maiava is already at 43.4, second in the class. His 0.38 EPA per dropback is…
author: Ryan Wilson

title: 2026 CBS Sports NFL All-Breakout Team: Caleb Williams, two other Bears headline rising stars on offense
summary: CBS Sports NFL writers and analysts selected the offensive players poised to take the next step in 2026, with Williams leading a strong contingent of Bears
full_text:
NFL breakouts can come from anywhere and anyone. Maybe it's a player coming off a strong close to the previous season. Maybe it's a player finally putting injury woes behind him. Maybe it's the upgraded surroundings that let the player shine. Maybe it's simply a bigger role.
Whatever "it" is, breakouts happen every year, whether it's one step up or a few steps up or an elevator to the top floor, like Drake Maye going from inconsistent-but-promising rookie to MVP runner-up. Average players going to good are breakouts, just like good players going to great are breakouts. They come in all shapes and sizes.
Thirteen voters, made up of CBS Sports NFL writers and analysts, voted on their All-Breakout Team for 2026, and here are the results for the offensive side of the ball.
Voters: JP Acosta, Carter Bahns, John Breech, Doug Clawson, Jordan Dajani, Jared Dubin, Josh Edwards, Zach Pereles, Garrett Podell, Mike Renner, Tyler Sullivan, Ryan Wilson, R.J. White
With four votes, Caleb Williams won a highly competitive vote that featured seven different quarterbacks. The former USC star took a massive jump from a dismal rookie season, especially in avoiding negative play. Williams was also absurdly clutch with an NFL-high six fourth-quarter comebacks. Now, he's the "Madden" cover athlete. Still, there's another level for him to reach, namely in his consistency and accuracy.
Others receiving votes: Tyler Shough (3), Jaxson Dart (2), Bo Nix , Bryce Young , Cam Ward , Malik Willis (1 each)
Eight different running backs got at least one vote, but Bhayshul Tuten garnered the most with four. The second-year Jaguars running back only averaged 3.7 yards per carry last year, but he had a 51.8% rushing success rate, 15th out of 67 players with at least 70 carries, and directly in front of James Cook .
Others receiving votes: Ashton Jeanty (2), Omarion Hampton (2), Blake Corum , Jonathon Brooks , Jordan Mason , Quinshon Judkins , TreVeyon Henderson (1 each)
Voters listened when Ben Johnson spoke at the outset of training camp. "I'm buying Luther Burden stock right now," Johnson said in late July . "Just how he's approached his offseason, it's been electric." Burden flashed major talent in limited talent as a rookie, finishing with 652 receiving yards. He'll have a much larger role with DJ Moore now in Buffalo.
The diminutive Josh Downs went from 72 catches and 803 yards in 2024 to just 58 catches and 566 yards last year, but it's easy to see why a resurgence could be in store. The fourth-year pro is in line to see an expanded role after Indianapolis traded Michael Pittman Jr. to the Steelers . Downs playing in two-receiver sets could lead to his first 1,000-yard season. He received five votes.
De'Zhaun Stribling's spot on this team coincides with his excellent preseason. He has 11 catches for 109 yards and looks ready to step into a significant role immediately as the WR2 opposite Mike Evans . San Francisco received a lot of criticism for drafting Stribling No. 33 overall, but all the Ole Miss product has done since is impress. He received four votes.
Others receiving votes: Marvin Harrison Jr. , Matthew Golden , Parker Washington (3 each), Adonai Mitchell , Jack Bech , Ryan Flournoy (2 each), Darius Cooper , Isaac TeSlaa , Jalen Coker , Jalen McMillan , Rashid Shaheed , Romeo Doubs (1 each)
NFC North rivals Colston Loveland and Tucker Kraft received three votes apiece to lead the way at tight end. Kraft was on his way to a breakout last year -- 30 catches for 469 yards and six touchdowns through Week 8 -- before tearing his ACL in Week 9. The Loveland selection, on the other hand, is based on a strong finish that included a 137-yard performance in Chicago's playoff win over Green Bay.
Others receiving votes: Gunnar Helm , Chigoziem Okonkwo (2 each), Dalton Kincaid , Mitchell Evans , Isaiah Likely (1 each)
Josh Simmons , the No. 32 pick in last year's draft, and Will Campbell , the No. 4 pick in last year's draft, both received four votes. Simmons looked excellent in the eight games he played, but he missed time first due to personal reasons and later due to a season-ending wrist injury. Campbell was having a solid campaign before a late MCL injury, and his early-season work was overshadowed by a tough postseason.
Also receiving votes: Jordan Morgan (2 votes), Aireontae Ersery , Anton Harrison , Troy Fautanu (1 each)
Grey Zabel started all 17 games (and all three playoff games) for the Super Bowl champs last year as a rookie. The No. 18 pick out of North Dakota State earned a spot on the PFWA All-Rookie team for his solid contributions and has all the makings of a Seattle stalwart for years to come. He received five votes.
Others receiving votes: Dylan Fairchild (3 votes), Alec Anderson , Alijah Vera-Tucker , Christian Mahogany , Donovan Jackson , Mason McCormick (1 each)
One could argue Zach Frazier already broke out, as he was Pro Football Focus' sixth-highest-graded center. He allowed just one sack across 598 pass-blocking snaps. title: The eight milestones Aaron Rodgers could reach during his final NFL season
summary: Rodgers can pass several Hall of Fame quarterbacks on the NFL's all-time leaderboards during his farewell season in Pittsburgh
full_text:
As Aaron Rodgers enters the final season of his Hall of Fame career, the question isn't what milestone he can reach in 2026, but rather how many.
The 42-year-old enters his 22nd and final season as the NFL's all-time leader in touchdown/interception ratio (1.4%) and tied with Lamar Jackson for the best career passer rating (102.2). He has also been sacked more than any other quarterback (600 times) in league history.
Rodgers has a chance to reach several other notable milestones during his final season. Barring an injury, Rodgers is a shoo-in to reach a few of the below milestones, while a few others would require another MVP-caliber season from the four-time league MVP.
Barring an insane season, Rodgers' Achilles injury in 2023 deprived him of the chance to pass his former teammate, Brett Favre, on the all-time career passing list. Rodgers still has a good chance, though, to join Favre in a pretty select fraternity of quarterbacks.
Rodgers is 3,726 yards away from joining Favre, Tom Brady , Peyton Manning and Drew Brees as the only quarterbacks to throw for at least 70,000 yards. Rodgers is just one of 10 quarterbacks in history to throw for at least 60,000 yards.
Dan Marino, the first quarterback to reach 60,000 yards, became the NFL's career passing leader during the 1995 season when he broke the mark that previously had been held by Fran Tarkenton, who led the Vikings to three NFC titles during the 1970s. Favre then broke Marino's record during his final season with the Packers.
Favre held the record for eight years before Manning beat him out. Brees eventually passed Manning before Brady then stepped into the top spot.
Last year, Rodgers passed Favre for fourth all-time in career touchdown passes. With 527 career touchdown passes, Rodgers is 13 away from passing Manning, whose 539 career touchdown passes was the NFL record when he retired at the end of the 2015 season.
Ironically, Manning broke the record that was previously held by Favre, who was the all-time leader in both passing yards and touchdown passes when he retired at the end of the 2010 season. Manning has since been passed by Brady and Brees.
Barring injury, Rodgers will undoubtedly pass former Steelers great Ben Roethlisberger for the fifth-most regular-season wins among starting quarterbacks during the early stages of the season. Rodgers is currently just two wins behind Big Ben.
Rodgers is just 10 wins shy of passing Brees, who won the majority of his starts during his prolific run with the New Orleans Saints, which included the franchise's first Super Bowl win at the end of the 2009 season.
Rodgers is just five wins away from passing Roethlisberger and eight wins from passing Brees for fourth on the all-time list. He won't be able to catch Favre, whose 199 wins trail only Brady and Manning. Once again, Brady has a sizable cushion over the field in this department.
It goes without saying that Rodgers has been a consummate winner throughout his NFL career. In addition to his Super Bowl title, Rodgers led the Packers to the playoffs 11 times, which includes eight consecutive trips from 2009-16. Green Bay reached the NFC title game four times with Rodgers under center.
During his first season in Pittsburgh, Rodgers helped the Steelers capture their first division title since 2020. It was Rodgers' ninth division title as a starting quarterback.
Pittsburgh's last playoff win came on January 15, 2017, when the visiting Steelers posted an 18-16 win over the Chiefs on the strength of six Chris Boswell field goals. Along with Boswell, the star for the Steelers that night was Le'Veon Bell , whose 170 yards on the ground broke his one-week-old franchise single-game postseason record.
While not as long as Pittsburgh's drought, Rogers also hasn't won a playoff game in some time. His most recent win in the postseason was Green Bay's 32-18 win over the Los Angeles Rams in the 2020 NFC divisional round. The following week, the Packers were upset at home by the eventual Super Bowl champion Buccaneers .
Rodgers' teams have been on the short end of the final score in each of his last three playoff games, most recently Pittsburgh's 30-6 wild-card loss to the Houston Texans this past January.
Sans 2023 (when he missed virtually the entire season), Rodgers has engineered at least one game-winning drive each year since he became a starting quarterback back in 2008. He had a career-high four game-winning drives in 2022, his final season with the Packers.
Rodgers mounted three game-winning drives each of the past two seasons. Last season, his late-game heroics led the Steelers to early-season wins over the Jets (in Week 1) and the Patriots (in Week 3). His most recent game-winning drive was a memorable one; it culminated in a touchdown pass that ultimately gave the Steelers a division-clinching win over the Ravens in Week 18.
Rodgers can tie Favre for the fourth-most Pro Bowl selections among quarterbacks if he is selected in 2026. He would also join Brady and Favre as the only quarterbacks to earn Pro Bowl nods after turning 40.
Favre, who turned 41 during the 2009 season, earned his final Pro Bowl nod that season after putting together one of the finest seasons of his career. Brady also had one of his best seasons late in his career. In 2021, at age 44, Brady earned his final Pro Bowl nod after throwing for a career-high 5,316 yards and 43 touchdowns. He led the NFL in both departments.
While unlikely, Rodgers still technically has a chance to tie the record for the most league MVP awards in NFL history. In doing so, he would become the oldest league MVP in NFL history. Ironically, the league's oldest MVP is Matthew Stafford, who was 37 when he captured his first league MVP at the end of the 2025 season.

title: Cowboys WR, Patriots TE among undrafted NFL rookies making noise in training camp and the preseason
summary: From coast to coast, these 10 undrafted NFL rookies are turning heads in preseason and fighting for a spot on the 53-man roster
full_text:
Undrafted free agents are still making a big impact on the NFL game. Last season, there were 54 undrafted free agents (UDFAs) on an active roster to open the season. UDFAs contributed over 3,300 offensive snaps and 3,200 defensive snaps in 2025. Teams are able to identify inexpensive youth who can offset larger salary cap hits on the roster.
Who are some of those undrafted free agent rookies to create buzz in their bid to make the active 53-man roster and continue their respective NFL dreams? Surveying the league, there are 10 names to know.
A few years ago, I conducted some research that found defensive backs were the most likely undrafted free agents to make an NFL roster. Safety, specifically, is a position that requires a higher level of cerebral understanding and is not necessarily solely reliant on athleticism. Los Angeles, in particular, has done an excellent job identifying these players through the years: Jaylen McCollough , Tanner Ingle and a handful of other Day 3 selections.
Andersen may be next. In his five collegiate seasons, he amassed eight interceptions. In preseason exposure, he has not been afraid to play downhill and deliver big hits.
Veteran Hunter Henry and rookie Eli Raridon have separated themselves as the top two tight ends on the roster, but injuries have given Arkin a platform to earn more playing time. As tight end usage rises around the league, and teams are keeping more at the position, the Illinois product, via Colorado State, is coming into the league at the right time.
Arkin is not going to be confused for a vertical element of the team's pass attack, but he has played fullback for the Patriots and has been inserted into gaps as a lead blocker.
Offensive tackle has been a concern for Kansas City. Left tackle Josh Simmons stepped away from the team for personal reasons last season, veteran Jawaan Taylor was released and Wanya Morris was traded. Veteran Jaylon Moore flipped to right tackle and has been in competition with Benson.
Benson has cross-trained at both right tackle and right guard for the Chiefs this preseason. If he is not named the starting right tackle, then he is building a portfolio to become one of the primary reserves capable of fulfilling multiple roles.
Benson spent four seasons at Indiana, one season at Colorado and returned to the Hoosiers for one final season in 2025. The Memphis native appeared in 49 games over the course of his collegiate career.
Brown has made some sensational acrobatic catches in both training camp and the preseason. Dallas has a quartet of entrenched pass catchers -- CeeDee Lamb , George Pickens , Ryan Flournoy and Kavontae Turpin -- but Brown is in the mix for one of those remaining one or two spots.
After three years at Auburn, he finished his career at Georgia Southern. He had 26 career receptions before breaking out with 65 receptions for 1,079 yards and 14 touchdowns his senior season. At 6-foot-2-inches and 204 pounds, with good body control, Brown offers the ability to win above the rim down the field.
CAMDEN BROWN WITH A CRAZY ONE-HANDED TD GRAB 😱 DALvsSEA on @nflnetwork Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/sj2vglr6py
Veterans Tyson Campbell and Denzel Ward are the known commodities in the Cleveland secondary. A few others have the inside track on regular playing time, but playing time is at stake every time the unit takes the field. Coats is a player who, by all accounts, has consistently shown up regardless of whether or not it has been practice or the preseason.
The diminutive cornerback had five interceptions with Nevada before transferring to Morgantown and wrapping up his time in college with the Mountaineers. Coats also showed some play-making ability on special teams.
The former Houston running back is a candidate to make the Rams roster as well. Although the team has built a bit more depth in that spot. He was impactful running and catching the football, tallying 51 total yards in his debut. He also made a tackle on special teams.
Connors was impactful in his lone season with the Cougars after transferring up from Rice.
Garnes was the less-heralded member of Arizona's secondary last season. Fans are more familiar with his teammates: defensive backs Treydan Stukes , Genesis Smith , Dalton Johnson and Michael Dansby ; all of whom were drafted in April.
After faltering in his first preseason snap, Garnes rebounded well as a boundary cornerback for Tampa Bay. He missed a few backfield tackles in the opener, but shows the aggressiveness and athletic baseline to grow into a larger role. He jumped a route that broke in front of him and returned the interception for an interception.
The rook Ayden Garnes with the TD 🙌 📺: #TBvsNYJ on WFLA 📻: @98rocktampabay 📲: Now in-market on the Bucs app pic.twitter.com/gsJKXQrlFo
Several cornerbacks associated with the Buccaneers over the years ( Jamel Dean , Carlton Davis and Sean Murphy-Bunting ) have since moved on, which leaves Garnes fighting for a role with the new guard.
Philadelphia is replacing safeties Sydney Brown and Reed Blankenship from last season's roster. The former had been a key contributor on special teams, which is where Pulley has made the biggest impact early in his time with the NFC franchise.
Beyond Andrew Mukuba , Marcus Epps and Cooper DeJean , if Philly elects to play him there, the depth chart is relatively open for Pulley to make the roster.
Stevens has won the kicking competition in our nation's capital. The former Iowa Hawkeye is known for his leg strength. He is no stranger to kicking in weather Washington may see late in the season.
Sturdivant offers a bit more size, physicality and downfield play-making ability than the Packers receivers could offer beyond Christian Watson . However, his greatest contributions may be on special teams. Through two preseason games, he has three receptions for 30 yards, as well as two special teams tackles.
Green Bay has been known for its ability to identify and develop receivers. Time forced them to make decisions and allow the likes of Dontayvion Wicks and Romeo Doubs to seek opportunities elsewhere. How the team chooses to fill those two or three spots on the depth chart behind Matthew Golden , Jayden Reed and Watson is discretionary. Sturdivant is making his case by competing in two phases.
author: Josh Edwards

title: NFL preseason injuries tracker: Updates on Sam LaPorta, Breece Hall, Jeremiyah Love, Alvin Kamara
summary: We track the biggest injury updates and recovery timelines as teams navigate a brutal start to the NFL preseason
full_text:
Through two weeks of the NFL preseason , most teams have felt the wrath of the injury bug. Washington Commanders quarterback Marcus Mariota suffered a sprained MCL that should hold him out for the remainder of the preseason, Minnesota Vikings defensive Swiss Army knife Jamal Adams suffered a season-ending injury in the Meadowlands, Houston Texans backup signal-caller Graham Mertz tore his ACL, and the Arizona Cardinals are dealing with several notable issues.
Winning the war of attrition is important for any Super Bowl contender, and a major injury could derail any team's season. Unfortunately, it happens every year, and sometimes before we even reach the regular season.
Below, we will break down all of the notable injuries from around the league as we enter the third week of the preseason.
Aug. 20: Lions coach Dan Campbell said LaPorta is dealing with a hip injury suffered earlier in the week and is uncertain for Week 1.
"It flared up a little bit, it's a little aggravated," Campbell said Thursday. "But we feel good long-term about him. We'll rest him for a little bit here and letting it calm down."
LaPorta had a season-ending back injury last year.
Aug. 17 : New York Jets star running back Breece Hall will miss two to three weeks -- but is expected to be available for Week 1 -- after suffering a non-contact groin strain after making a catch in practice.
Aug. 16 : The No. 3 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft had an explosive preseason debut, rushing for 58 yards on 11 carries, and turned three receptions into 14 yards. However, he left with what was determined to be a high ankle sprain.
Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur initially said that Jeremiyah Love "could have returned" to action, but two days later said the rookie would not practice this week or play in Week 2 of the preseason. High ankle sprains are issues that can linger, so it's fair to speculate about his status for the season opener on Sept. 13.
Aug. 14 : It turns out the Cardinals' top two picks from this year's draft were injured in the preseason opener, but the news is much worse for No. 34 overall pick Chase Bisontis . The Texas A&M product unfortunately tore his MCL, and will miss his entire rookie season. Bisontis was viewed as one of the top interior linemen in this past class, having played snaps at both guard and center. Now, he is forced to turn his efforts to recovery.
Aug. 19: Higgins tore his ACL in the Texans' joint practice with the Ravens on Tuesday, ESPN reported Wednesday. The 2025 second-round pick was expected to take a step forward after a strong debut season in which he caught 41 passes for 525 yards and a team-high six touchdowns.
Aug. 19: Oweh, who signed a four-year, $96 million deal with the Commanders this offseason, is dealing with a calf strain, per coach Dan Quinn. After breaking out over the second half of last season with the Chargers, Oweh was impressing in training camp, too. Wednesday was a tough day for Washington front-seven injury news, with K'Lavon Chaisson dealing with a knee injury (not expected to be serious) and Johnny Newton seeing a specialist for a pec injury that could be a long-term issue.
Aug. 19: Meeting with the media Wednesday, Eagles defensive coordinator Vic Fangio said there's concern regarding Greenard's availability for Week 1 due to a pec injury. The Eagles acquired Greenard from the Vikings for a third-round pick and gave him a four-year, $98 million contract this offseason.
Aug. 15: Adams suffered a torn quadricep during the Vikings' preseason opener, head coach Kevin O'Connell announced. It's a season-ending injury for Adams, who signed with Minnesota in late July. He's expected to stay around the team during his recovery, O'Connell said. Adams also suffered the same injury during his time with the Seattle Seahawks back in 2022, but this one is to the opposite leg.
Aug. 17: Monangai reportedly suffered a hyperextended knee during a weekend practice. He's expected to miss multiple weeks but the outcome is considered positive, according to ESPN. D'Andre Swift is likely to carry a heavier workload if Monangai has to miss any time during the regular season, but he has around four weeks to recover.
Aug. 17: Tyson is expected to be out approximately two months with a hamstring injury suffered last week and could begin the season on injured reserve. It's a huge blow for the Saints , who took Tyson with the No. 8 overall pick in this year's NFL Draft. Tyson has a history of hamstring injuries, but according to NFL Media, this one is new and considered unrelated to his prior issues.
Aug. 18: Kamara left the Saints' joint practice with the Cowboys early with a knee injury and will miss at least a month with an MCL sprain, per ESPN's Adam Schefter , meaning Kamara will miss Week 1. The five-time Pro Bowler is expected to have a reduced role after the Saints signed Travis Etienne Jr. but still provides strong pass-catching ability. Kendre Miller could see a larger role.
Aug. 18: Biadasz, signed to a three-year, $30 million deal this offseason to fill Los Angeles' major need at center, suffered ACL damage and additional knee injuries and is out indefinitely, per Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport , after a gruesome-looking injury at the Chargers ' joint practice with the 49ers . He was carted off the field and unable to put any weight on his leg per ESPN's Kris Rhim and The Athletic's Daniel Popper . For more analysis on this injury, click here .
Aug. 11: Egbuka suffered a toe sprain, and at the time it wasn't deemed a significant setback. However, on Aug. 18, coach Todd Bowles struck a different tone, calling both Egbuka and his fellow wide receiver Jalen McMillan (knee) "day to day, week to week" and saying he's unsure if the injury will impact Egbuka's availability for Week 1.
Aug. 17: Tennessee Titans backup quarterback Mitch Trubisky was seen holding his throwing arm after a deep pass attempt. Head coach Robert Saleh said he's being evaluated for a biceps injury. Depending on the severity, this could open the door for Will Levis to see more reps.
Aug 23: The Seattle Seahawks will be without their second-round pick for "several months," according to coach Mike Macdonald. Safety Bud Clark , the No. 64 overall pick in the 2026 draft, played just one snap in the Seahawks' second preseason game before sustaining a broken right ankle. He remained on the field for multiple minutes as trainers placed an air cast on his leg and eventually carted him into the locker room. Clark made waves in camp and took numerous reps with the first-team offense as a potential starter or, at the very least, a key member of the defensive backfield rotation. Now he will watch most, if not all, of his rookie year from the sideline.
author: Jordan Dajani

title: NFL preseason Week 2 overreactions: J.J. McCarthy is Vikings' QB3, Jets' defense is fixed
summary: Not everything that unfolded in the second batch of preseason action is worth reading into
full_text:
The NFL preseason is ripe for overreactions. Much of what unfolds on game days should be taken with a grain of salt as teams hold back the "good stuff" from their playbooks and rest their starters. At the same time, some of the offseason's most important decisions come down to these games. Such is the case in Cleveland, where the Browns might have settled their quarterback competition after a preseason Week 2 eyesore from Deshaun Watson and a solid showing from Shedeur Sanders .
Sanders may be the biggest winner from the second set of preseason games . De'Zhaun Stribling could be on his way to a stellar rookie season with the 49ers if Thursday's display of receiving prowess was any indication. And the Jets ' defense actually looks… competitive?
Not all of those takeaways are guaranteed to play out come the regular season. Some of what unfolded in the second week of the preseason will go down as mere exhibition fallout rather than meaningful data.
Let's separate overreactions from reality.
The plan was always for Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders to get one start apiece to open the preseason. Now that Todd Monken has the data points he set out to acquire, a decision on which of the two will open the regular season atop the depth chart is imminent. In fact, i t could come as soon as Monday . And after Watson's disastrous showing on Saturday, it is hard to picture the veteran winning the job.
It is not as if Sanders went out and won the job himself. He threw an interception in each of his first two preseason outings and was underwhelming in Week 1, albeit with a decent bounce-back effort (9-for-11, 74 yards, one touchdown, one interception) in Week 2. The potential pecking order in Cleveland is more a product of Watson looking unplayable on Saturday.
While Watson outplayed Sanders a week ago, he floundered in his most recent appearance with poorly placed throws and a 5-for-12, 35-yard stat line with an interception. Browns fans booed him off the field, and while Monken said Watson's postgame comments toward the Cleveland faithful will not impact the starting quarterback decision, they were a poor look.
It has been difficult to find uplifting storylines from 49ers camp due to their onslaught of injuries, but De'Zhaun Stribling's emergence as a potentially game-changing rookie is as pleasant a development as any in the Bay Area. A week after he racked up seven catches for 63 yards as the leader of San Francisco's receiving unit, Stribling tied with KhaDarel Hodge for the most catches (four) and yards (46) of any 49er on Thursday.
Importantly, three of those catches came on connections with starting quarterback Brock Purdy . The two were on the same page from the get-go in the rout of the Chargers and strung together three completions on the opening drive. Stribling then hauled in a 21-yard grab from Mac Jones on the team's second possession.
Stribling, the No. 33 overall pick in April's draft, saw his Rookie of the Year odds spike. Per DraftKings , his +1100 odds are the fifth-shortest behind only Jeremiyah Love , Jadarian Price , Fernando Mendoza and Carnell Tate . He has been as productive as any of them this preseason, but the sheer volume of contenders for the award (and the fact that Love and Price, at least, figure to hold larger roles) still means he will have to outperform expectations to win the honor .
Verdict: Overreaction… but possible!
Tua Tagovailoa threw just three passes in the first week of the preseason and watched Saturday's 34-6 drubbing of the Colts from the sideline. That is a starter's preseason workload. His grasp on the role is tenuous, though.
Neither Cooper Rush nor Jack Strand will unseat Tagovailoa from the starting job, but the Falcons have to appreciate what they combined to deliver in this week's offensive showcase. Strand, an undrafted rookie, racked up 212 passing yards, 22 rushing yards and a touchdown both through the air and on the ground. Cooper Rush went 10-for-11.
The real threat to Tagovailoa is twofold. First, he has been underwhelming in camp. Second, Michael Penix Jr . is cleared for 11-on-11 work and figures to make a run at the job. This always figured to be a two-man battle, and now that Penix is healthy, he has about three weeks to make up ground and potentially leap past his fellow southpaw. His momentum from 7-on-7 and individual drills gives him a shot to do so.
The Jets' defense infamously went the entire 2025 season without recording an interception. The group secured two takeaways in one game during Week 2 of the preseason. Andre Cisco , who is in the mix for a starting role at one of the safety spots, hauled in the first one while reserve cornerback Samuel Womack III grabbed the second. Both came against Steelers quarterback Will Howard .
Toss in a David Bailey sack, two sacks from Nate Lynn and another from Chase Wilson , and it was a banner day for New York. The starting unit played into the second quarter of a game in which the Steelers went scoreless.
Remember, though, that this came against Pittsburgh's No. 2 offense. And keep in mind that while the Jets overhauled the unit with a plethora of free agent additions, none of them are elite players. Aaron Glenn needs this group to hold its own in 2026, and it may just do that. But this shutout means very little.
When J.J. McCarthy fell short of Kyler Murray in the competition for the Vikings ' starting quarterback duties, the reasonable conclusion was that he would settle in as the No. 2 option in the group. Even that might be a stretch for the third-year pro at this point. He had a rough go of it against the Ravens' defense on Saturday; across 18 snaps, he completed just five of 10 passes, took three hits and fell victim to a sack.
Coach Kevin O'Connell said that McCarthy would have played longer if not for being "banged up" during his limited work. That highlights another issue with the former first-round pick: he simply cannot stay healthy.
While O'Connell said a week ago that McCarthy is Minnesota's No. 2 quarterback, it is increasingly clear that he does not have a long-term future in this offense. Carson Wentz might give the Vikings a better chance of winning games if Murray misses any time.
The search to find a successor to Mason Crosby since his departure in 2022 has been anything but smooth for the Packers . It appears that they finally have an answer, however. They were the only team to use a draft pick on a kicker in 2026, and it looks like an astute move. Sixth-rounder Trey Smack has been a preseason standout.
In Week 1, Smack drilled a 58-yard field goal and matched that distance on a kick that was ultimately waved off for a defensive penalty. He went 3-for-3 in his professional debut. That was just the start of it. He was even better this week and made all four of his field goal attempts , with two coming from more than 50 yards out. His longest was a 59-yard blast.
After a year in which Green Bay missed four extra points and was as reliable as a coin flip on kicks beyond 50 yards, special teams could suddenly be a legitimate weapon.

title: Cardinals roster 2026: Josh Sweat, Gardner Minshew, and Karson Sharar could shock the world
summary: From a competitive standpoint, last year’s Arizona Cardinals were the equivalent of an eighth-grade football superstar who finds himself trying to play on the high school senior varsity team. You’re somehow good enough to exist at this level, but anything more than existence will be swatted down by the behemoths all around you. That reality […]
full_text: From a competitive standpoint, last year’s Arizona Cardinals were the equivalent of an eighth-grade football superstar who finds himself trying to play on the high school senior varsity team. You’re somehow good enough to exist at this level, but anything more than existence will be swatted down by the behemoths all around you. That reality sank in for the Cards pretty quickly. They didn’t have such an opportunity to impress before things fell apart. They started off 2-0 with wins over the New Orleans Saints and Carolina Panthers, and had close losses to the San Francisco 49ers and Seattle Seahawks, but then, attrition started to hit. Hard. I mean, holy crap. The 2025 Cardinals dealt with 179.8 Adjusted Games Lost , the FTN metric which measures games lost by starters and major contributors. That is the second-highest in the metric’s 25-year history, behind only the 2021 Baltimore Ravens. That’s how the 2021 Baltimore Ravens compiled records of 5-1 and 8-3 before crashing into a ditch and losing their last six games . Kyler Murray’s foot injury, which cost him the last 12 games of the season, was the headline malady, but those dings showed up everywhere in every part of the roster. This was no way to go about winning in the NFC West. Arizona’s 3-14 record was brought about to a great extent by the fact that they were playing in Autobahn traffic against the aforementioned 49ers and Seahawks, as well as the Los Angeles Rams. Seattle and L.A. were the NFL’s two best teams last season, and the 49ers still managed a 12-5 record despite their own fairly epic injury issues (they ranked fifth in AGL). The Seahawks are where they were last season. The Rams have loaded up to a ridiculous degree. The 49ers should still be very good, even if they can’t figure out the whole substation thing . Meanwhile, the Cardinals have hired Mike LaFleur to be their head coach, they’ve already caused a “ Did we overwork Jeremiyah Love in the preseason? ” debate, and nobody really knows who the quarterback is going to be. So, it could be a tough slog for this team. For anything else to be the case, everyone on the roster will need to exceed expectations — not just the stars on the roster, but the lesser-known guys whose on-field exploits currently exceed their national name recognition. To that end, I’ve sought out three Hidden Gems for these 2026 Cardinals — one underrated veteran, one underrated free agent, and one underrated draft pick. Underrated veteran: EDGE Josh Sweat One more thing about last season’s injury bug. Let’s put this as simply as possible — if the Cardinals are to accomplish anything of note on defense this season, they’ll need as much of Josh Sweat as they can possibly get. It’s not just that the eight-year veteran compiled 12 sacks and 47 total pressures in just 355 pass-rushing snaps in his first year with the team after signing a four-year, $76.4 million contract with $41 million guaranteed. It was just as much what Arizona’s pass rush did whenever he wasn’t on the field. Which wasn’t much at all. And the defense changed completely when he was unavailable due to any nagging injuries. When Sweat was there, he was good enough to merit Top 100 consideration, whatever you may think of the NFL’s evaluative process with this particular idea. No. 78 on the NFL Top 100 Players of 2026… @AZCardinals LB Josh Sweat! @NFLFilms pic.twitter.com/MpNTm5YFZ7 — NFL (@NFL) July 7, 2026 When Sweat was off the field, the pass rush got itself smushed. Former head coach Jonathan Gannon put it quite simply last October when asked why and how Sweat opens things up for other quarterback disruptors. “Well, they have to pay attention to Josh, and when they’re paying attention to Josh, that’s typically going to create some one-on-ones. Just kind of a numbers game with that. If you’ve got a win rusher, depending how they choose to negate that it’s going to open up some things for other guys.” Anybody who knows anything about football understands that. That’s the easy part. Getting a guy who creates those opportunities at such a high level is the tougher assignment. For the Cardinals, who didn’t do much in the offseason to put more pass rush around Sweat, keeping him on the field should be Job 1. He’s estimated to come off the active/PUP list (knee) and be ready for the start of the regular season, which is obviously big (and good) news. “Everyone is on the same page the entire time,” LaFleur said in July of Sweat’s status. “You guys can believe me or not, but I am not worried about Josh Sweat at all in terms of his health. He’s logged a lot of miles in this league, and I think not only for Josh to peak on Sept. 13 [for the regular-season opener against the Las Vegas Raiders], but for Josh to also get through the rigors of a 17-game season the way that he plays, and the motor he plays with, this is best for him and the Cardinals.” LaFleur had better hope so. Things will be better with a healthy Walter Nolen in 2026, but it’s clear that Sweat leads Arizona’s pass-rush plan — and he’ll continue to do so. Underrated free agent: QB Gardner Minshew Gardner Minshew has seen a lot of things, man. The 2019 sixth-round pick of the Jacksonville Jaguars has been a starter with the Jags in 2019 and 2020, with the Indianapolis Colts in 2023 (he made the Pro Bowl that year), and with the Las Vegas Raiders in 2024. He’s also been a backup with the Philadelphia Eagles in 2021 and 2022, and with the Kansas City Chiefs last season. Now, Minshew’s winding NFL path has taken him to the Valley of the Sun after the Cardinals signed him to a one-year, $5.75 million contract to help clarify a quarterback situation that remains undefined between what veteran Jacoby Brissett can do, and what rookie Carson Beck needs to prove. Could Minshew take the starting job? Perhaps, but LaFleur sees a different point of entry for him. And Minshew is okay with that. Mike LaFleur has said that he wants Gardner Minshew to be "the best backup quarterback of all time." That's not a slam. It's very hard to come in cold at any time without starter's reps. Minshew can do it. pic.twitter.com/WwhuTByXVC — Doug Farrar ✍ (@NFL_DougFarrar) August 20, 2026 “[I’ve had] maybe a little bit of a perspective shift, but not in the way you think,” Minshew recently said . “What do we really have? Each day we have the opportunity to get better. You can just do that over and over. And that’s it. Looking around and wondering what’s around you or who is around you doesn’t serve you at all, and it doesn’t serve the team. All you can do is show up and work.” LaFleur has made it clear what he wants from Minshew this season — be ready at any time to take over, and let the preparation take care of itself. Because starter’s snaps may not be a thing in practice. “We want him to be the best backup quarterback of all time,” LaFleur said. “What is a backup quarterback? You are one snap away at any given time, and you have to be always ready to go. You’re not always going to get the necessary reps.” With all his experience, and with his YOLO playing personality, Minshew can see things going both ways at any time. Against the Dallas Cowboys on Saturday night as the starter, he completed 19 of 23 passes for 177 yards, no touchdowns, one interception, and a passer rating of 80.6. Minshew’s best and worst moments both involved receiver Simi Fehoko. His interception with 7:31 left in the first quarter happened primarily because Fehoko fell down on the play, and he had a banger of a throw on a 37-yard completion to Fehoko with 1:04 left in the first quarter. gardner minshew's lowlight (receiver fell down) and highlight (great deep throw) vs. the cowboys pic.twitter.com/reEjRJz2dY — Doug Farrar ✍ (@NFL_DougFarrar) August 23, 2026 “He kept the ball in play,” LaFleur said of Minshew postgame. “I thought he did a good job. The interception was unfortunate because it wasn’t a ‘PI’ [pass interference], either—it was a zoning ‘backer with incidental contact on Simi.…

title: Falcons QB Michael Penix Jr. participates in full practice Monday
summary: I thought the Falcons would slow-roll Michael Penix into full contact after he was medically cleared to return to football activities over the weekend. And Monday was not a padded practice, so that’s been slow-rolled at least until tomorrow. But Penix did get a lot of work. Cooper Rush and Jack Strand did not get […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GA - AUGUST 14: Atlanta quarterback Michael Penix Jr. (9) warms up prior to the start of the NFL pre-season game between the Denver Broncos and the Atlanta Falcons on August 14th, 2026 at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, GA. (Photo by Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images I thought the Falcons would slow-roll Michael Penix into full contact after he was medically cleared to return to football activities over the weekend. And Monday was not a padded practice, so that’s been slow-rolled at least until tomorrow. But Penix did get a lot of work. Cooper Rush and Jack Strand did not get a lot of work — something Kevin Stefanski noted prior to practice. Since the backups got so much playing time on Saturday against the Colts, the coaching staff took it a bit easy on them today and let the starters get more reps. Here’s my real-time reporting from the day, and check out everything you need to know from today’s practice below. Kevin Stefanski on all things Penix I mentioned in Monday’s Falcons Opening Drive my concern about whether Michael Penix Jr. is mentally recovered from his knee injury and reconstruction. Stefanski addressed it too, saying, “I think bigger picture for me at least right this minute is getting [Penix] in the huddle with all 11.” Some outlets apparently took this Kevin Stefanski quote to mean that Jack Strand is a serious contender at QB1. I’m curious what y’all think: “At this point, Jack’s going to work with the 2s and 3s. We’re very excited about his development … player development is a huge part of what we do. Player development is important to us, and being intentional about the way we bring guys along is important to us,” Stefanski said. The Falcons’ starters will play this week against the Miami Dolphins to close out the preseason. At this point, Stefanski doesn’t have a set plan for workloads for the starters, but I suspect we’ll get more details on Wednesday when he speaks to the media again. On whether or not that includes Penix: “Michael’s had a bunch of reps without the pass rush, he’s more than eager to get out there and practice, and he’s done a great job … I think there are ways to get ready, to prepare yourself” without taking that contact or that risk, and Stefanski said Penix has done a fantastic job with that. Falcons practice notes: There were no pads and there was no contact in Falcons practice today, so I think it’s important to take what we saw with a grain of salt. Both Tua Tagovailoa and Penix had some off-target throws — often a bit high. There was one Drake London might have been able to pull in, but Tua sailed it over his head and out of bounds. Penix also hit London deep, slightly off target, but like Penix said last week — generally, you’ve just got to get the ball in London’s (or Pitts’) vicinity and let them go up and get it. MPJ also looked very comfortable connecting over the middle with Pitts — no shock, but fun to see! Penix was pressured on one rep and used his legs to extend the play. Again, no pads, no contact, but there wasn’t any hesitation there and that was nice to see. Natrone Brooks got some praise from coaches in special teams drills — he was called out for taking a great angle as a gunner and also had a nice little kick return in the next set of drills. On back-to-back plays, Tua Tagovailoa was pressured, escaped contain and ran it. It was fun to watch and makes me nervous as hell about his concussions. Penix hit Drake London on an over-the-middle completion, and the crowd went WILD. The crowd was every single one of Penix’s teammates. He got them so hyped up! I’ve mentioned this a couple of other times in the last few weeks, but I like the approach to teaching we’re seeing from the coaching staff. One thing in particular is IMMEDIATE correction when someone makes a mistake. Saw that quite a bit today. They also did some blocking drills that were walk-through speed, so there’s really not much to report. Both Penix and Tua got reps with the 1s. I can’t make it up here Tuesday (I am heading to New York City Friday to cover the US Open, and I need one day in my office to get some actual season prep done first!) but I will be back on Wednesday with updates on the QB situation, position battles, and whatever else comes out of that practice.

(Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Who plays alongside Divine Deablo is one of the several positional battles this summer. With plenty to be decided across the defensive line, the linebacker to complement one of Atlanta’s most valuable defensive players will play a pivotal role in keeping a defense filled with uncertainty afloat. Three players have emerged as options, though only two are likely viewed as credible potential starters. Harold Perkins Jr. has plenty of intriguing attributes, but he’s still very raw and could use a year learning from the sidelines while contributing on special teams. That leaves the other rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels to compete with Christian Harris for the starting role. Daniels has been one of the training camp standouts. Harris possesses valuable experience despite his limitations as a three-down linebacker. That gives him the slight edge over the 2026 fourth-round pick. It wouldn’t be a total surprise if Daniels earns his place in the starting lineup. His reading of the game, combined with his physical traits, makes him someone who can find himself playing 55-60 snaps a game at some point in 2026. For now, Harris’ downhill attacking ability should mesh with Deablo’s dynamic skill set to ensure the linebacker core doesn’t take much of a step back without Kaden Elliss. title: Falcons news: Michael Penix cleared to play; what does it mean for Atlanta?
summary: It’s a lot more fun to put Monday’s Falcons Opening Drive together after the Falcons absolutely dominated the Colts in preseason action on Saturday afternoon. Below, I’ve got some thoughts on Michael Penix Jr. being medically cleared and what it means for this quarterback depth chart. We’ve also got some fun looks back at Saturday’s […]
full_text: Jun 16, 2026; Atlanta, GA, USA; Atlanta Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. (9) reacts while being interviewed by the media during Minicamp. Mandatory Credit: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect It’s a lot more fun to put Monday’s Falcons Opening Drive together after the Falcons absolutely dominated the Colts in preseason action on Saturday afternoon. Below, I’ve got some thoughts on Michael Penix Jr. being medically cleared and what it means for this quarterback depth chart . We’ve also got some fun looks back at Saturday’s win over the Colts and the state of the roster , a fantastic article on reasons Falcons fans should be excited about this season despite the quarterback depth chart situation , and don’t miss The Falcoholic’s Question of the Day : Should Jack Strand be this team’s QB3? Falcons Opening Drive: What does a healthy Michael Penix Jr. mean for Atlanta? Every single day Kevin Stefanski takes the podium to speak to the media, somebody asks about the timetable for Michael Penix Jr. to be medically cleared. Now we have the answer to that question. But what we don’t know is whether his change in status means there’s a possibility for Penix to start Week 1. During joint practices with the Colts, Penix participated in 1-on-1s and 7-on-7s, and he mentioned to the media after Thursday’s practice that while he feels healthy, his doctor — and Penix — also had to think about the possibility that he’s not healthy enough to withstand full contact. “If I had a rush coming at me and everything, I could get away, but it’s just right now, if I don’t get away, that’s what we think about,” Penix said during joint practices against the Colts last week. Penix has also spoken several times this offseason and preseason about the mental hurdle associated with his recovery. He’s cleared to participate physically, but has he been able to fully overcome that mental hurdle? And if not, does that create additional injury risk? Is it worth taking the chance? Is his head in the right place? And then there’s the matter of Penix’s injury history, and the injury history of the other potential QB1 on the roster, Tua Tagovailoa . Monday kicks off a fundamentally important week of practice for all four quarterbacks on the roster. Tua Tagovailoa will want to prove he should be the starter regardless of Michael Penix Jr’s status. Penix will want to prove the mental reps he’s taken in addition to his limited physical participation in practice have actually prepared him to start Week 1. For Cooper Rush and Jack Strand , they’re each hoping to snag that QB3 spot. Yes, Tagovailoa and Penix are both healthy now, but because of their injury histories, making sure the QB3 is adequate is fundamentally important. I can understand the thought process behind keeping Rush and his experience around, but Strand has truly been exciting to watch this preseason, and his potential is massive. Kevin Stefanski will speak to the media around noon tomorrow, practice will be at 2:35 p.m., and select players (I won’t know who until tomorrow) will speak to the media after practice. I typically can’t be in Flowery Branch on Monday, but I want to see how they manage getting Penix up to full speed, and I know I’m not the only one who wants to know how he’s looking, so I’ll be there to keep y’all posted. All of my reporting from tomorrow’s practice will be in the Feed, and I’ll have a practice report on The Falcoholic afterward. Now let’s move on to everything you need to read, watch, or listen to about the Atlanta Falcons today. Josh Kendall of The Athletic shares his perspective on Saturday’s player performances and what they mean as we inch closer to roster cuts . Daniel Flick of the AJC introduces us to Za’Darius Smith , who didn’t join the Falcons in Indianapolis until Friday, but did immediately embrace being a part of this Falcons team. D. Orlando Ledbetter of Bowtie Sports has Kevin Stefanski’s full postgame press conference transcript from Saturday , in which the Falcons’ head coach discussed the improved performance of the o-line, gap integrity, Tyler Goodson, and more. I always think there’s value in reading the full transcript — if you just catch quotes here and there you may be missing important context. Candace Buckner of The Athletic wrote an outstanding piece after the Falcons’ joint practices last week about the Falcons’ QB1 conundrum , and it may be even more relevant now that Michael Penix Jr. has been medically cleared. ESPN ’s Mark Raimondi explains why the Falcons are so impressed with Jack Strand in the video below. View Link Falcons vs. Colts Preseason Week 2 coverage That Falcons win over the Colts was extremely fun. Relive it here . Dave Choate covers the snap counts from Saturday’s preseason win , right here on The Falcoh0lic. I am 100% in favor of taking cool-ass penalties on purpose in the preseason, like the excessive celebration flag against the Colts on Saturday. Safe to say the guys took it seriously 😂 pic.twitter.com/ka7HSl9CUv — Atlanta Falcons (@AtlantaFalcons) August 22, 2026 From The Falcoholic community On Friday, I asked everyone to write a mission statement for the 2026 Falcons. There were a ton of fun ones — I was especially partial to the thread that perfectly mimicked the cadence and tone of a certain politician’s Truth Social posts. Spot on, and legitimately hilarious! But TrenchesPlease had my absolute favorite: First of all, it’s an iconic line from an iconic Falcon. Secondly, I couldn’t agree more about the reasoning behind it. And I do think seeing the Falcons bounce back so dramatically on Day 2 of joint practices against the Colts and in Week 2 of the preseason after floundering Week 1 — these things should be indicative of better coaching and a better-run organization.
