title: Browns: Deshaun Watson as QB1. How did we get here?
summary: The Cleveland Browns entered the 2021 season full of hope after a playoff run the prior year that included a Wild Card beatdown of the Pittsburgh Steelers and a close loss to the Kansas City Chiefs in the Divisional Round. But the promise of another playoff run quickly evaporated when quarterback Baker Mayfield suffered a […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - AUGUST 22: Deshaun Watson #4 of the Cleveland Browns looks down field during the third quarter of a preseason game against the Buffalo Bills at Huntington Bank Field on August 22, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns entered the 2021 season full of hope after a playoff run the prior year that included a Wild Card beatdown of the Pittsburgh Steelers and a close loss to the Kansas City Chiefs in the Divisional Round. But the promise of another playoff run quickly evaporated when quarterback Baker Mayfield suffered a shoulder injury while making a tackle on an interception return in Week 2 against the Houston Texans. Mayfield and the Browns were never the same as the injury lingered; the team stumbled to an 8-9 record, and ownership decided in the offseason that it was time for an “adult in the room” at quarterback. That ill-fated decision kicked off a chain of events that have left the franchise as far from solving its quarterback situation as it has been since 1999, as the team is poised to enter the 2026 season with the worst quarterback room in the NFL . Here is a brief timeline of how the Browns reached this point. Deshaun Watson has decided he wants to play for the Cleveland Browns in a stunning change of events, per sources. Watson has informed the Houston Texans that he now is willing to waive the no-trade clause in his contract to be dealt to Cleveland. — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) March 18, 2022 2022 Season After closing out the 2021 season with an 8-9 record and missing the playoffs, ownership decides it needs to find “an adult in the room” for the quarterback position. The Browns trade for quarterback Deshaun Watson on March 18 . Watson had sat out the previous season in a contract dispute with the Houston Texans. To acquire Watson, the Browns give the Texans three first-round draft picks as part of the trade package, and sign Watson to a five-year contract with $230 million in guaranteed money. Mayfield is traded to the Carolina Panthers on July 6. Watson is suspended by the NFL for the first 11 games of the 2022 season due to off-field issues from his time with the Texans. Veteran Jacoby Brissett starts at quarterback and proves to be mostly effective, even though the Browns are just 4-7 with Brissett as the starter. Watson makes his Cleveland debut in Week 13 against the Texans . He finishes 12-of-22 for 131 yards with an interception, as the Browns win, 27-14. Cleveland goes 3-3 with Watson as the starter to close out the season at 7-10. Watson finishes his abbreviated season by completing 58.2 percent of his passes and throwing for 1,102 yards, while tossing seven touchdowns, five interceptions, and taking 20 sacks. Deshaun Watson has signature performance in 33-31 come-from-behind victory over the #Ravens to move to within a half game of 1st at 6-3 https://t.co/IOOCve4913 — Mary Kay Cabot (@MaryKayCabot) November 12, 2023 2023 Season Watson opens the 2023 season as the starter and helps the Browns to a Week 1 victory over the Cincinnati Bengals. In Week 3, Watson takes a hit to his shoulder in a win over the Tennessee Titans. That injury would bother him until Week 10, when after leading the Browns to a comeback win over the Baltimore Ravens, Watson is diagnosed with a broken shoulder that requires surgery and ends his season . In Watson’s absence, the Browns rolled with P.J. Walker for two starts and Dorian Thompson-Robinson for three starts before convincing Joe Flacco to join the team. Flacco makes five starts and leads the Browns to a surprising playoff appearance before self-destructing in a Wild Card loss to the Texans . In his second season with the Browns, Watson plays in just six games, completing 61.4 percent of his passes for 1,115 yards, seven touchdowns, four interceptions, and taking 17 sacks. Deshaun Watson underwent successful surgery today to repair his ruptured right Achilles tendon 📰 » https://t.co/Ec8bzKbOVp pic.twitter.com/JOQkP6Y3Ms — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) October 25, 2024 2024 Season After another offseason of rehab, Watson opens the 2024 season as the starter. He has a poor Week 1 by throwing two interceptions and being sacked six times in a loss to the Dallas Cowboys . Watson and the offense never get going and fall to 1-5 on the season following a 20-16 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles. The following week in a home game against the Bengals, Watson tears his Achilles’ tendon and is lost for the season . In Watson’s absence, the Browns turn to the depressing quarterback trio of Jameis Winston (seven starts), Thompson-Robinson (two starts), and the immortal Bailey Zappe (one start) as they finish the season at 3-14. Watson’s third season with the Browns ends after seven games during which he completed 63.4 percent of his passes for 1,148 yards, five touchdowns, three interceptions, and 33 sacks. 2025 Season While rehabbing his injury in January, Watson re-tears his Achilles’ tendon . Watson misses the entire 2025 season. In his place, the Browns go from Joe Flacco (bad for four starts) to Dillon Gabriel (just as bad for six starts) to Shedeur Sanders (just as bad for seven starts) . The Browns finish at 5-12. Four seasons into his Cleveland tenure, Watson has played in a total of 19 games, completing 61.2 percent of his passes for 3,365 yards, 19 touchdowns, 12 interceptions, and has been sacked 70 times. Deshaun's mindset after being named the starter pic.twitter.com/froMMAWdVL — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) August 24, 2026 2026 Season (so far) The Browns fire head coach Kevin Stefanski on January 5 . In his six seasons with the Browns, Stefanski took the team to the playoffs twice and earned two NFL Coach of the Year awards. After a search that included a mix of familiar and new names, the Browns hire Todd Monken as head coach . It is the first NFL head coaching role for the 60-year-old Monken, who is touted for his quarterback experience and is owner Jimmy Haslam’s top choice. Monken opens up training camp by announcing a competition between Watson and Sanders for the starting quarterback role . Watson starts the first preseason game while Sanders gets the starting nod in the second preseason game. Neither plays well enough to instill confidence that they are QB1 material. During Saturday’s preseason game against the Buffalo Bills, Watson is booed by the home fans when he enters the game and while struggling to get anything going on offense. In his post-game press conference, Watson says he believes that the boos are personal , rather than based on his performance. Everyone loses their minds, with calls for the Browns to cut Watson on the spot. That does not happen, in large part, because the cap hits of $40.9 million in 2026 and $86.2 million in 2027 would decimate the roster . On Monday, Monken announced that Watson will open the season as Cleveland’s starting quarterback . Following the news that he will start in Week 1, Watson explained that his post-game comments from Saturday were just a player being emotional after “putting a lot of time these last two years to get back, spend time in this facility, in the city, meeting a lot of different people in the community, I thought I was going to get a little different response.” Coach Monken names Deshaun the starting quarterback pic.twitter.com/OwYTBOQMhf — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) August 24, 2026 So here we are. For the third time in five seasons, Watson will hit the field in Week 1 as the starting quarterback. The previous two times, he made it through six games (2023) and seven games (2024) before suffering a season-ending injury. So how long will he last this time? Barring another injury, there are three ways this is likely going to play out: The Browns play well enough to come into the home opener at 1-1 (or even 0-2 if both losses are close). They beat the Carolina Panthers and then, four nights later, the Steelers at home, and head into the mini-bye week with…

Even though you may not like the fact that Watson is suiting up as the start over Shedeur Sanders in Week 1, the fact of the matter is Monken was handed a less-than-ideal quarterback situation this year. He tried to make it a competition between the two, and neither player ran away with the job. The long-term prospects of the team seem set up for drafting a quarterback in 2027. Our question below asks if Monken naming Watson the start impacts your view of him as a head coach already? Or does he get more leeway, given the circumstances mentioned above, and because he deserves a chance to make whatever stamp he’s trying to make on the team, regardless of fan popularity? full_text: BEREA, OHIO - JULY 29: Head coach Todd Monken of the Cleveland Browns directs a drill during Cleveland Browns Training Camp at CrossCountry Mortgage Campus on July 29, 2026 in Berea, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images After a weekend full of questions about QB Deshaun Watson having any future in the NFL at all , including a look at the salary cap issues if the Cleveland Browns released him, HC Todd Monken will reportedly name Watson the starting quarterback for 2026 over QB Shedeur Sanders . Monken will get up in front of the media on Monday and explain his decision, noting things, as GM Andrew Berry has done previously, about “production” and “giving us the best chance to win.” The Browns head coach will say nice things about Sanders and him making the competition tight throughout the process. The Cleveland beat reporters will try to get Monken to narrow down what specific things led to the decision. Whether the “straight-shooting” coach gives answers that make sense and that we believe will be interesting to find out. Below is a list of potential reasons the Browns picked Watson over Sanders. Some are serious, and some are very much trying to make light of a situation that has most fans ready to pack it up for the season before the third preseason game even kicks off. (Of note to this author, Watson has been, and could be again, the only reason Cleveland fans have stopped caring about the team. Not The Move, the winless season, or the 1-win season, or every other terrible decision- just Watson: acquiring/paying him, his performance, and now him being named the starter). On to the list: Cadence Getting plays in and out of the huddle quickly Unlocking the QB run game Collecting more contract insurance if he’s injured again Tie goes to the veteran Tie goes to the biggest contract They have a good trade offer for Sanders and plan to take it Easier to go from veteran to youngster than vice versa Sanders is lacking/not doing something really important behind the scenes Owner Jimmy Haslam, who went to Watson’s wedding, said so Since The Move, it’s been one big psyop to see how much it would actually take to ruin the greatest fanbase in the world They want to lose as many games as possible, and starting Watson could help and help ruin Sanders’ confidence for when he does get in Rock-bottoming the fans’ hope so that the resurgence feels even bigger in time for opening the dome They don’t care one bit what fans think (Generally, I’m on board with this, but that press conference…) Watson has a stronger arm They want less risky throws, prefer dink-and-dunk They flipped a coin Deion Sanders said something Monken didn’t like when he visited Berea Sunk cost fallacy isn’t a fallacy; it’s a market inefficiency Someone lost a bet “This is all a simulation, nothing really matters, eat at Arby’s” – SB Nation’s Mark Schofield Someone won a bet “There are 50,000 Deshaun Watson bobbleheads in a bunker they need to get rid of” – SB Nation’s James Dator They had already decided when they hired Monken, and maybe it was part of the decision to hire him that he would agree to Watson starting They can’t read the room They don’t believe they should read the room Watson has been great in the meeting room Sanders deferred to Watson to start the season 2 road games to start the season will either lead to Watson’s benching, or he’ll look good enough that fans might cheer in Week 3 NFL stepped in and said, “We want Watson versus Baker in Week 2” They believe Watson is the quarterback who can win games and do not believe Sanders is that close Again, some tongue in cheek, some humor to get through the process, and some actual reasons the Browns might have made this decision. Now it is your turn… Share your ideas about why the Browns picked Watson over Sanders (just don’t forget the community guidelines, please) Join the conversation! title: Where are your former Browns now? QB Milt Plum
summary: The Cleveland Browns have had a ton of starting quarterbacks. But the majority of those are from when the franchise came back in 1999. That number is 42 different starting quarterbacks. But it wasn’t always like that. RELATED: WHERE ARE YOUR FORMER BROWNS NOW? QB PAUL MCDONALD From the maiden season of 1946 and until […]
full_text: Cleveland QB Milt Plum uncorks a 1st-period pass. (Getty Images) The Cleveland Browns have had a ton of starting quarterbacks. But the majority of those are from when the franchise came back in 1999. That number is 42 different starting quarterbacks . But it wasn’t always like that. RELATED: WHERE ARE YOUR FORMER BROWNS NOW? QB PAUL MCDONALD From the maiden season of 1946 and until the final season of 1995, the quarterback position was mostly stable. Otto Graham was the starter for 10 years. Frank Ryan for seven. Bill Nelsen took the reins for five. Brian Sipe was the starter for parts of 10 years. Bernie Kosar took charge for nine seasons. And Milt Plum took control for five seasons. Plum grew up in Westville, New Jersey, just 10 miles south of Philadelphia. His family grew up as diehard Phillies and Eagles fans. He attended Woodbury High School and was a hard-hitting standout catcher on the baseball team. He also played basketball and football. He had an opportunity to play professional baseball, but went to Penn State instead to play football, with a baseball career as a fallback. In football, he was named First Team All-State as a quarterback and kicker. He was also the team’s punter. He led an undefeated football team that won both the Colonial Conference and South Jersey Group III crowns. Plum was also part of baseball and basketball teams that won Colonial Conference titles. Plum played for Penn State from 1954-1956, which ran the ball frequently. In his college career, he played in 27 games as the starter only in his final two seasons. He had 60 completions on 133 attempts for 961 yards, a 53.3% completion ratio, and tossed eight touchdowns with 16 picks. He also rushed 77 times for 174 yards and scored three times. He was the team’s punter and once had a 72-yard kick go out on the three-yard line. In 1956, he was named First Team All-Eastern. Browns QB Otto Graham had retired after the 1954 season. In training camp in 1955, head coach Paul Brown was not satisfied with all of his signal-callers and talked Graham into coming back for one more season. The Browns had won the 1954 NFL Championship, and with Graham under center, they again won the league title for back-to-back championships. But that was it for Graham, who retired for good to concentrate on his multiple businesses. The 1956 season was the first losing season for Paul Brown as a head coach at any level, as Cleveland finished 5-7-0. His quarterback room was a shuffle of musical chairs. Going into the 1957 NFL draft, the Browns had the #6 pick. Coach Brown had his sights on QB John Brodie of Stanford or QB Len Dawson from Purdue. He had to have one or the other. But Brodie went #3 to the San Francisco 49ers, and Dawson was selected by Pittsburgh at #5. Coach Brown then “settled” on fullback Jim Brown out of Syracuse. In the second round, Coach Brown chose Plum. Plum played five seasons with Cleveland before being traded to the Detroit Lions. On March 29, 1962, Cleveland traded Plum, RB Tom Watkins, and LB Dave Lloyd to the Lions in exchange for QB Jim Ninowski (who returned to the Browns), DE Bill Glass, and RB Howard “Hopalong” Cassady. Now in Detroit, Plum started 52 games in seven seasons before finishing out with the Los Angeles Rams and New York Football Giants. For his career, Plum played in 129 games with 103 starts, had 1,306 completions on 2,419 attempts for 17,536 yards, a 54.0 % completion ratio, tossed 122 touchdowns against 127 interceptions, was sacked 116 times, earned a 72.2 QB rating, and rushed 217 attempts for 531 yards with 13 additional scores. Browns QB Milt Plum at the 1961 NFL Pro Bowl. He was traded to the Lions not long after. pic.twitter.com/7U7fM8r0Gp — SportsPaper (@SportsPaperInfo) December 13, 2016 Plum was named to two Pro Bowls, was selected Second Team All-Pro (1960), was the NFL Passer Rating Leader (1960), was a three-time NFL Completion Percentage Leader, and holds the Browns franchise record for the “All-Time Career Regular Season Passer Rating” at 89.9. After his NFL career was over, Plum worked in the wood products industry. After that retirement, he settled in Raleigh, North Carolina. Dawgs by Nature staff writer Barry Shuck was able to connect with Plum, age 91, to find out what Paul Brown was like, what NFL players think about playing on Thanksgiving, and why he was traded to Detroit after being named to consecutive Pro Bowls. Shuck: At Woodbury High School, you were a star athlete in baseball, basketball, and football. You had a chance of playing minor league baseball, your best sport. Why did you choose football instead? Plum: Well, my thinking was if I didn’t make it in football, I could go to baseball playing catcher. I talked to a couple of people, and with baseball you can linger for years in the minor leagues. With football, you either make it or don’t make it. They didn’t draft baseball players out of high school back then like they do now. Shuck: You chose Penn State where your QB coach was Joe Paterno. What was he like? Plum: All football. One offseason he had three of us quarterbacks and three centers in the gym taking snaps. We went from one center to another. Boring as hell. It was ridiculous. Well, that was illegal and the athletic director found out and told Joe, nope, you can’t do that. You could pick 20 days to have spring practice. If Joe had his way we would be practicing all year round. Shuck: You were one of the top quarterback prospects coming out of the 1956 class. Did it occur to you that you could be playing professional football, or did you have going into private business in mind instead? Plum: I know a lot of athletes decided to skip going professional because going into the business world they could make more money. But the Man upstairs guided me and I said I’m going to try football and make it or not. I still had time to go back to baseball after I graduated from Penn State. I could have played for Penn State in baseball, but in my first year, I was told that players make the football team in spring practice and there were two other quarterbacks. So, I focused on playing football. I didn’t want to show up and then never play. But if I wasn’t drafted, or was drafted really low, I still had the opportunity to play professional baseball. Shuck: Paul Brown went into the 1957 NFL draft needing a quarterback. After taking Jim Brown in Round 1, you were taken in Round 2. How did you find out that you had been drafted, and what did Cleveland pay you? Plum: The draft back then was during the season. So, they had me and others come to New York. Lenny Dawson and John Brodie were considered the top quarterbacks. Most people thought that Pittsburgh was going to take me because I went to Penn State, but that didn’t happen. Back then nobody had an agent and I doubt Paul Brown would have dealt with any agents. My first contract was 14-2. That was $14,000 a year and a $2,000 signing bonus for a two-year deal. Shuck: You and Jim Brown were drafted in the same class. What was Jim Brown like in a huddle? Plum: Kind of like everybody else. He was quiet. I always had command of the huddle. It was a different ballgame then. One game I threw 14 passes because Jim Brown was having a real good day. We threw a pass to give him a rest. Shuck: What was your first training camp like? Plum: Early on, Paul Brown came over and told me, “We don’t throw lillypups in this league.” So, he pulled me over to the sideline, and I practiced throwing harder. I was throwing with touch instead of speed. And I had the arm strength; that wasn’t the issue. Training camp was different, but not really hard. One time, Paul Brown had a sore throat. So, he drove his car right out on the field. And when you wanted a play, he would roll his window down and tell you the play. And getting any water was “frowned on.” One practice, there was a guy working on a telephone pole, working on the telephone lines. Paul Brown sent somebody there and got him to climb down and…

title: Giving Browns Deshaun Watson a smidge of understanding after press conference debacle
summary: Sports can be used as an outlet. Personal note: as someone who dealt with their fair share of bullies (from middle school all the way through early high school), the pent-up anger I had towards the individuals who tormented me day in and day out spilled over whenever I played sports (mainly football). Playing football […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OH - AUGUST 22: Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson (4) on the sideline during the second quarter of the National Football League preseason game between the Buffalo Bills and Cleveland Browns on August 22, 2026, at Huntington Bank Field in Cleveland, OH. (Photo by Frank Jansky/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Sports can be used as an outlet. Personal note: as someone who dealt with their fair share of bullies (from middle school all the way through early high school), the pent-up anger I had towards the individuals who tormented me day in and day out spilled over whenever I played sports (mainly football). Playing football taught me a lot of life lessons, but it also allowed me to be physical towards other people in a legal, clean way. In life, you will have people who will doubt your abilities and belittle you, but the only way to overcome it is to prove them wrong and not let it affect you in a negative way. Saturday afternoon, Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson struggled against a Buffalo Bills team that played mainly their second and third stringers . It wasn’t a great look for someone who is desperately trying to save his career, but his postgame press conference did not do him any favors . To anyone reading body language, it seemed obvious that Watson is frustrated; at the same time, he’s feeling a range of other emotions. Anger, sadness, embarrassment, and frustration might top the list. Watson was booed whenever he stepped out on the field. Instead of ignoring it, he chose to use it as an opportunity to antagonize the fanbase. Not a smart move. It’s clear that Watson has tried to connect with the fanbase in the past, but it’s to no avail. As head coach Todd Monken pointed out in his post-game press conference, play well and the fans won’t boo. Browns coach Todd Monken on Deshaun Watson’s play today and the home crowd booing him: “It sucks. I don’t wanna get booed. Comes with the territory. You don’t wanna get booed, play good football. … Because it can turn just like that.” pic.twitter.com/ulH475yzJT — Daniel Oyefusi (@DanielOyefusi) August 22, 2026 Play poorly, and the fans will react accordingly. Watson will say it feels personal because deep down he knows it’s personal. He’s playing for a city that never fully embraced him and has vitriol due to the serious charges off the field. The lackluster play hasn’t done Watson any favors. Watson says he doesn’t care, but at the same time he says it feels personal. Deep down, Watson does care about what people say about him because this press conference shows that, and it’s affecting him. Instead of using that frustration and taking it out on people who do not know him personally, the frustration should be used to motivate his play. Watson seems mentally defeated, and it’s not a good sign for him. Playing for a fanbase that actively dislikes you is hard, but at the same time he has no one to blame but himself for the situation that he’s in. We will find out on Monday whether the team will name Watson the starter, but from the press conference it feels that Watson doesn’t want the job if he’s given it. It’s not that Watson does not care, but it’s more about him not believing in himself anymore. His frustration spilled over, but it wasn’t the way he envisioned it or anything going since his arrival in Cleveland.

title: Cowboys need to monitor this key position over the next weeks
summary: With the California portion of training camp over and two preseason games now in the rearview mirror, we have much more clarity about where things currently stand depth wise at each position for the Dallas Cowboys. For the most part things look pretty encouraging throughout the roster, however, there are a few concerns that need […]
full_text: With the California portion of training camp over and two preseason games now in the rearview mirror, we have much more clarity about where things currently stand depth wise at each position for the Dallas Cowboys. For the most part things look pretty encouraging throughout the roster, however, there are a few concerns that need to be addressed. One is at offensive tackle. From top to bottom, the Cowboys can’t be 100% confident with their current depth at the OT position. Whether it’s the projected starters Tyler Guyton and Terence Steele or the questionable depth behind them, there’s not a single OT they can 100% depend upon as a full-time starter this year. Every single player at the position can be red flagged for one reason or another and could spell trouble this season. A lot is riding on Guyton and Steele as the full-time starter’s this year. The latter has held down the RT position for a few years now, but has never truly been challenged for the starting job. The Cowboys love his ability as a run blocker, but his pass protection leaves much to be desired, so much so, he’s become somewhat of a liability. As for Guyton, his inability to remain healthy for an entire season and his lack of consistency are pretty significant red flags right now. There’s hope he will be able to overcome these two issues this year, however, without a crystal ball there’s no way of telling whether that’s true or not. That means a dependable swing tackle is needed. Nate Thomas is a projected swing tackle right now. He was supposed to be in a head-to-head battle with Guyton for the starting LT job, but never materialized as a serious contender. Instead, he seemed to regress somewhat and may no longer be a dependable option even as a backup. That would be a huge gut punch. Outside of those top three, no other tackle has shown to be starter material yet, or even an injury fill-in for that matter. Ajani Cornelius shows some promise in his second-year, but he may be better on the inside at the guard then at tackle. And so far, this year’s fourth-round pick Drew Shelton looks like a developmental project. Things are less than ideal right now at OT for the Dallas Cowboys. This is a position that could definitely be upgraded from a depth standpoint. The question is how do they go about doing that considering many teams around the league are probably facing the same problem. As far as available free agents are concerned, the options are pretty slim. Considering his starting experience with the Detroit Lions, Taylor Decker is probably the best option. Other than Decker, Jonah Williams could make some sense. He and Klayton Adams have a history with one another due to their short time together with the Arizona Cardinals. He’s a former first-round pick who has played both LT and RT. He could be an upgrade over Nate Thomas as a swing tackle. The fact the Cowboys haven’t shown any interest in either as of yet could be telling though. They may be willing to roll the dice with their current depth at the position, or could possibly have a trade in mind to upgrade things. Either way, they’d be wise to monitor the veteran OT market closely, especially around cutdown day. How much confidence do you have in the Cowboys offensive tackle situation?

title: Cowboys countdown to kickoff: Top 100 iconic games – Day 20
summary: It is Day 20 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like […]
full_text: Football: NFC Championship: Rear view of Dallas Cowboys Tony Dorsett (33) taking field before game vs Minnesota Vikings at Texas Stadium. Cheerleaders on field. Irving, TX 1/1/1978 CREDIT: John Iacono (Photo by John Iacono /Sports Illustrated via Getty Images) (Set Number: X22028 TK1 R9 F16 ) It is Day 20 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like how big the game was for the organization, how memorable the game was, games that had unusual events take place, games that are a part of NFL lore, Cowboys firsts, and games where the Cowboys just plain dominated. Variety is the spice of life and we have all different kind of Cowboys games to review. At the bottom, we’ll link each day of the countdown so you can go back and check out any you missed. We’ve reached Day 20 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff, when we revisit the conference championship victory that sent one of the greatest teams in Cowboys history to Super Bowl XII. Dallas combined a balanced rushing attack with an overpowering defensive performance to defeat the Minnesota Vikings and capture its fourth NFC title. Sunday, January 1, 1978 — 5:00 p.m. ET Texas Stadium, Irving, Texas Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 23, Minnesota Vikings 6 The Cowboys had finished the regular season 12-2 and demolished Chicago 37-7 in the Divisional Round. Minnesota arrived after beating the Los Angeles Rams in the rain-soaked “Mud Bowl,” but the Vikings were without starting quarterback Fran Tarkenton and again turned to Bob Lee. Dallas immediately placed Minnesota under pressure. Vikings running back Robert Miller fumbled on the third play of the game, with Harvey Martin recovering at the Minnesota 39-yard line. Roger Staubach soon found Golden Richards for a 32-yard touchdown, although Efrén Herrera’s extra point was blocked, leaving the Cowboys ahead 6-0. The Doomsday Defense produced another takeaway later in the opening quarter. Ed “Too Tall” Jones broke into the backfield and forced Chuck Foreman to fumble, allowing Martin to make his second recovery of the game. Dallas created separation during the second quarter. Danny White ran 14 yards on a fake punt to keep an eight-play drive alive before Robert Newhouse scored from five yards out, extending the advantage to 13-0. Newhouse repeatedly punished Minnesota between the tackles and finished as Dallas’ leading rusher. The Vikings responded through two Fred Cox field goals, from 32 and 37 yards, to reduce the deficit to 13-6. Dallas answered before halftime when Staubach connected with Preston Pearson for 32 yards, setting up Herrera’s 21-yard field goal and sending the Cowboys into the break ahead 16-6. Neither team scored during the third quarter. Dallas drove inside the Minnesota 15-yard line, but Tony Dorsett lost a fumble and prevented the Cowboys from increasing their lead. The defense ensured the mistake caused no damage, keeping the Vikings out of scoring range throughout the period. The clinching score arrived in the fourth quarter after Thomas “Hollywood” Henderson forced punt returner Manfred Moore to fumble and Jay Saldi recovered for Dallas. Five plays later, Dorsett scored on an 11-yard run, completing the scoring and securing the Cowboys’ trip to New Orleans. This game belongs on the countdown because it represented championship-level execution from a complete Cowboys team. Dallas scored following turnovers, controlled the line of scrimmage and prevented Minnesota from reaching the end zone. There was little late drama because the Cowboys never allowed the Vikings to seriously threaten their lead. #Cowboys vs #Vikings 1977 NFC Championship Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 23, Minnesota Vikings 6 #DallasCowboys #NFL (📽️: @nfl ) pic.twitter.com/iqUaQtL2IL — Mike Poland (@kenfigkowboy) August 24, 2026 Interesting Facts About the Game The Cowboys held Minnesota without a touchdown. That meant across two playoff appearances , the Cowboys had allowed only one touchdown. title: Updated Dallas Cowboys 53-man roster projection after preseason Week 2
summary: Things have a way of changing quickly in the NFL and that certainly true with the Dallas Cowboys. Nearly two weeks ago we attempted to predict their final 53-man roster at the halfway point of training camp, but the signing of the Von Miller and the emergence of several other players have changed things. Because […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - AUGUST 22: Von Miller #40 of the Dallas Cowboys poses for a selfie before the preseason NFL game against the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) | Getty Images Things have a way of changing quickly in the NFL and that certainly true with the Dallas Cowboys. Nearly two weeks ago we attempted to predict their final 53-man roster at the halfway point of training camp, but the signing of the Von Miller and the emergence of several other players have changed things. Because of that, we decided to bring things up to date with an update. Check it out below. Quarterback (2) Dak Prescott, Joe Milton The QB2 competition is over. Milton has persevered and won the right to be Prescott’s primary backup once again in 2026. Running back (4) Javonte Williams, Malik Davis, Jaydon Blue, Hunter Luepke Should’ve known better than to count out No. 20. He not only replaces Phil Mafah, who will hopefully be retained on the practice squad, but has surpassed Blue as the favored RB2 to backup Williams again this year. Wide receiver (6) CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens, Ryan Flournoy, KaVontae Turpin, Jonathan Mingo, Camden Brown We have the Cowboys going a little deeper here than before with Jonathan Mingo and Camden Brown making the cut, replacing Anthony Smith. Smith hopefully slips through waivers and re-signs to the practice squad. We still really like his potential. Tight end (3) Jake Ferguson, Brevyn Spann-Ford, Michael Trigg Trigg missing time with an injury hurts his case a little, but we believe he’s already on a pretty even playing field with Luke Schoonmaker. Because of that, and due to his upside, we don’t believe Dallas will risk him to waivers. Offensive line (9) Tyler Guyton, Tyler Smith, Cooper Beebe, Tyler Booker, Terence Steele, TJ Bass, Nate Thomas, Nick Leverett, Ajani Cornelius Drew Shelton out, Nick Leverett in. Even as a developmental project so that is nowhere close to contributing. Hopefully he can be re-signed to the practice squad. Leverett replaces him backup center/guard. Keep an eye out for another vet OT joining the mix to solidify things. Defensive tackle (5) Quinnen Williams, Kenny Clark, Otito Ogbonnia, Jonathan Bullard, LT Overton We don’t foresee any changes here. Undrafted rookies Tommy Dunn and DJ Withers show promise, but not enough to earn a roster spot. Both will hopefully be re-signed to the practice squad if they clear waivers. Outside linebacker/Edge (6) Rashan Gary, Donovan Ezeiruaku, Malachi Lawrence, James Houston, Von Miller, Marist Liufau Miller’s addition is the biggest change from our previous projection. The sixth and final spot is still up in the air with Liufau, Sam Williams, Isaiah Land, and Tyrus Wheat all vying for the job. We’ll stick with No. 35 for now, he’ll really need to step up his game to beat out his competition. Inside linebacker (5) DeMarvion Overshown, Dee Winters, Jaishawn Barham, Justin Barron, Shemar James Curtis Robinson out, Justin Barron in. Last year’s undrafted free agent out of Clemson has been playing well, so much so, we believe he’s surpassed Robinson on the depth chart. A vet addition via the waiver wire or trade could potentially replace him though. Cornerback (6) DaRon Bland, Cobie Durant, Shavon Revel, Caelen Carson, Devin Moore, Reddy Stewart For now, we’ll stick with our previous prediction at CB, but believe changes are coming on the backend of the depth chart. Whether it’s the rumored signing of Adoree Jackson , a waiver wire pick up, or potential trade only Bland, Durant, and Revel should feel safe. Safety (4) Caleb Downs , Malik Hooker, Jalen Thompson, P.J. Locke We really wanted to replace Markquese Bell with Julius Wood and still carry five safeties, but was forced to go a little shorter to carry an extra WR. Hopefully the Cowboys can find some way to bring back Wood. He’s played well enough to earn a roster spot. Special teams (3) Brandon Aubrey, Bryan Anger, Trent Sieg Nothing new here. There’s no questioning these three are roster locks.

title: Cowboys backup offensive line evaluation after two preseason games
summary: The roster of the 2026 Dallas Cowboys is slowly taking shape as certain players show out and continue to make a case for their spot on the team. Some position battles are revealing themselves, but there are others that still remain a mystery. One group that still has a lot of questions is the offensive […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TX - DECEMBER 14: Dallas Cowboys offensive tackle Nate Thomas (71) waits for the play to begin during the game between the Dallas Cowboys and the Minnesota Vikings on December 14, 2025 at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Matthew Pearce/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The roster of the 2026 Dallas Cowboys is slowly taking shape as certain players show out and continue to make a case for their spot on the team. Some position battles are revealing themselves, but there are others that still remain a mystery. One group that still has a lot of questions is the offensive line. In the second preseason game, all the starters again sat out, as did their top reserve, T.J. Bass. That left five guys fighting it out for just a handful of remaining spots. How did these guys perform? And how does this impact the team’s decisions when it comes to choosing this group? Today, we’ll run through each player using game film notes and how the game changes their roster outlook. Nate Thomas Currently holding the Cowboys’ swing tackle position, the third-year tackle swung over to the right side after playing on the left side last week. He’s a big guy with good athleticism, but he struggles with consistency. Game notes for Thomas: popped out of his stance well used length to keep defenders from getting to his chest hands were a little wild; defenders could finesse around him at times shuffled his feet well to maintain position didn’t move well in space, wandered around looking to engage Roster outlook: 100%. His play has shown to be serviceable for the position, and he remains the team’s top backup tackle option, so his job is safe. Nick Leverett A free agent signing, this veteran interior blocker is a flexible piece, playing both guard and center. He holds his own with leverage and core strength, and despite being an afterthought a few weeks ago, he has played himself into the conversation. Game notes for Leverett: popped up quickly, hands spread out, assessing the situation moved well, put himself in a good position and set a wide base executed combo blocks well, strikes the shoulder then quickly moves on got under the shoulder pads, moved bodies he was pesky, played through the whistle and was always seen shoving someone after the play Roster outlook: 70%. It’s hard to watch him play and not believe the Cowboys coaches won’t want to keep him around. His ability to handle the center position means he could essentially replace Brock Hoffman and allow T.J. Bass to only have to worry about the guard spots. Ajani Cornelius A draft pick stash from last year, Cornelius has found a new home sliding inside to guard, and it seems to suit him well. He’s a physical player who is still finding his way, but there have definitely been positive signs from him of late. Game notes for Cornelius: set his target and attacked, seemed to always have a plan hands were always ready solid positioning, did a good job securing block anchored well, but strength was hit or miss; sometimes it held up, sometimes he got walked back a bit struggled with balance sometimes, occasionally seen on the ground Roster outlook: 60%. If the play was to keep someone around hoping they would develop and he develops, it seems like hanging on to him would be the right move. It could come down to the wire, but the second-year blocker is showing good progress. Trevor Keegan Poached from the Eagles, the coaches are kicking the tires on this former Michigan stud. He has good strength and can overpower defenders at times, but he’s not the most agile of players. Game notes for Keegan: footwork was a little jittery, slushed around hands were inconsistent, used his length well at times, other times it was wasted moved surprisingly well for a guy his size, effective pulling drove defenders sometimes, but his blocks have a shelf life as they eventually shed him too upright at moments, got walked back despite squaring up, just lost the leverage battle Roster outlook: 40%. There are some consistency issues with him, and he’s looked okay at times, but the emergence of Leverett and sliding Cornelius inside has really hurt his chances. Drew Shelton The team’s top offensive investment has been struggling. Last week he got worked over on the right side, and things didn’t change much switching over to the left side. It’s evident he’s a development project who has a lot of development to do. Game notes for Shelton: footwork was rigid, like he was stuck in mud, way too easy to get around too much of a forward lean ineffective hands, more inclined to just throw his shoulder didn’t know who to block sometimes; processing was on delay willing traveler in space and sealed off lanes a couple times Roster outlook: 100%. A fourth-round draft investment doesn’t promise anyone a roster spot, but it does tell you they want to give this guy a chance, and he has shown enough to at least see where this goes. Fans won’t like this because of how he’s played, but it’s too early to give up on him. What does this mean? The team essentially has seven roster locks – all five starters and their top two reserves, Bass and Thomas. Hanging on to Shelton puts them at eight players. That doesn’t leave much room for others, as the Cowboys are likely to carry nine or ten spots, depending on how they feel about these bottom roster guys. Leverett looks like the player in the best position to secure one of the final spots, with Cornelius right behind him if they go deep, leaving Keegan as the odd man out. And who is to say they don’t still add another outside player the closer they get to the regular season, if they aren’t happy with their tackle depth? That could throw another wrench into things, bumping off yet another player. How do you see the Cowboys’ offensive line group shaping out?

title: Dallas camp standouts are in: Meet the two 2026 camp MVPs
summary: Head coach Brian Schottenheimer kicked off the camp MVP countdown when he was asked about players that have exceeded his expectations coming into training camp and read off 10 names from his roster list. Jon Machota of The Athletic followed suit with his own 10-name list. Not to be outdone, the staff at DallasCowboys.com put […]
full_text: OXNARD, CALIFORNIA - JULY 27 Dallas Cowboy players huddle during training camp at River Ridge Playing Fields on July 27, 2023 in Oxnard, California. (Photo by Jayne Kamin-Oncea/Getty Images) | Getty Images Head coach Brian Schottenheimer kicked off the camp MVP countdown when he was asked about players that have exceeded his expectations coming into training camp and read off 10 names from his roster list . Jon Machota of The Athletic followed suit with his own 10-name list . Not to be outdone, the staff at DallasCowboys.com put together an 18-player list . Nick Harris of The Star-Telegram came up with perhaps the most creative list, coming up with eight award categories featuring eight winners and seven honorable mentions . And finally, Joseph Hoyt from the DMN , feeling pressure because “ all the cool kids are doing it ”, provided us with five standouts and three honorable mentions . Taken together, that gives us five sources for this year’s Camp MVP vote. For the purposes of this vote, every player named by a source counts as one vote, including honorable mentions. 61 votes were cast in total for 28 different players, and only two players were unanimous picks: Shavon Revel and Rashan Gary tied with five votes apiece, but they got there in different ways. Revel was named among the primary standouts by all five sources, while Gary appeared on three primary lists and received honorable mentions from two others. 2026 Camp MVP: CB Shavon Revel “The Cowboys looked at Revel as a rookie heading into this training camp. He missed all of last year’s training camp as he recovered from an ACL injury. The third-round pick didn’t play until mid-November. When he did, he looked like a rookie who was still recovering in a defense that didn’t always suit him.“ “By the end of training camp, the Cowboys had to raise their expectations of Revel. The second-year corner took a major step in training camp. The Cowboys were last in the NFL in pass breakups last season. Unofficially, Revel had the most in training camp. He looked the part of a defensive playmaker that scouts believed could’ve been a first-round pick before his knee injury.“ “There’s still room to go with Revel. There undoubtedly will be up-and-down moments for him in his second season. That shouldn’t be a surprise. But it shouldn’t be a surprise when he impresses, either…” – (Joseph Hoyt, DMN) “I wasn’t sure what to expect entering camp, but he absolutely looked the part of a quality starting cornerback. He’s physical and quick. Most importantly, he’s healthy. The play of Revel, DaRon Bland and Cobie Durant have the Cowboys looking like they will have a quality trio of corners.” – (Nick Harris, Star-Telegram) 2026 Camp MVP: OLB Rashan Gary “Rashan Gary’s leadership has jumped out at me.” – (Brian Schottenheimer) “Even though he’s one of the newcomers who should be able to take this defense to another level, Gary still gets overshadowed some because of Christian Parker or Caleb Downs and now even Von Miller. But make no mistake, Gary is going to be a handful for opposing tackles and he also seems to be someone who can immediately help stop the run. We know that can be a lethal combination for defensive ends.” – (Nick Eatman, DC.com) Four players garnered four votes each, and three of them are very unexpected but also very welcome surprises. 2026 Camp MVP Runner up: DB Caleb Downs The expectations for rookie first-round pick Caleb Downs were already sky-high going into training camp, and the Cowboys [braintrust] feels as though he has already exceeded what they laid out for him going into Oxnard. From playing as the first-team nickel cornerback to getting a heavy dose of work as a deep safety in one-high, two-high and three-high looks, Downs has been tasked with being Christian Parker’s defensive chess piece as a rookie, and it looks like it’s well within his capabilities. Battling against CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens, Jake Ferguson and KaVontae Turpin, Downs always looked like he belonged. While he did suffer some learning moments in the joint practice with the Saints working against Chris Olave, the expectations for Downs in his rookie season continue to drive confidence on the defensive side of the ball. (Nick Harris, Star-Telegram) 2026 Camp MVP Runner up: DT Otito Ogbonnia “And as a player, you guys know that. (Otito Ogbonnia), I mean, you talk about a guy that we thought we were getting maybe a run stopper. This guy’s a good football player, damn good football player, massive, really strong with his hands.” – (Brian Schottenheimer) “The first-year Cowboy arrived at training camp expected to be a rotational body that gets snaps whenever the starting duo needs a breather, but Ogbonnia has proven a lot more value. He can line up anywhere from nose tackle to the 5-Technique spot, he’s proven to have knacks in the run game, and he’s pushed the pocket back in pass rush as well. Ogbonnia may not have been a player that was firmly on the radar as one of the reasons for a potential defensive improvement in 2026, but keep an eye on big No. 91 when the season begins. He may just continue to surprise”. (Nick Harris, Star-Telegram) 2026 Camp MVP Runner up: WR Camden Brown “Pretty much every practice he made a highlight grab. That obviously carried over into the preseason. Brown was not expected to make the roster entering camp. He seems like a lock now.” – (Jon Machota, The Athletic) “How did Brown go from roster afterthought to the cusp of making the team? By consistently making plays, that’s how. Brown has been a consistent standout since the beginning of training camp. He set a school record last season at Georgia Southern with 14 touchdown catches. He flashed that ability in practice then showed it on the big stage against the Seattle Seahawks in the preseason opener with two highlight-reel touchdown catches. There’s still work to be done for Brown if he wants to make the roster. He’s competing with Jonathan Mingo and seventh-round pick Anthony Smith for one or two spots. But the fact that Brown is in the conversation is impressive.“ – (Joseph Hoyt, DMN) 2026 Camp MVP Runner up: OT Tyler Guyton Left tackle was one of the biggest areas of concern entering camp. Guyton has been solid, quieting that noise. As long as he can stay healthy, Guyton should be fine. Leaving California, right tackle seems like a bigger concern. – (Jon Machota, The Athletic) For the first time in his career, Guyton was able to get through an entire training camp healthy, minus a sore elbow that he got taped up but was still able to play through. That experience paid off, as Guyton was consistently solid on the left side of the line and continued to improve over the course of his time in Oxnard. – (Tommy Yarrish, DC.com) Overall, this is how the “voting” played out over the 28 players: body .sbnu-legacy-content-table td, body .sbnu-legacy-content-table th, body .sbnu-legacy-content-table { border: 1px solid #000 !important; border-collapse: collapse !important; } body .sbnu-legacy-content-table td, body .sbnu-legacy-content-table th { padding: 0px 6px !important; } 2026 Cowboys Camp MVP “voting” Status Votes Players 2026 Camp MVPs 5 Shavon Revel, Rashan Gary 2026 Runner Ups 4 Caleb Downs, Otito Ogbonnia, Camden Brown, Tyler Guyton Honorable Mention – 3 votes 3 Quinnen Williams, George Pickens, Malik Davis Honorable Mention – 2 votes 2 Dak Prescott, DeMarvion Overshown, Jaishawn Barham, Ryan Flournoy, Julius Wood, Joe Milton, Javonte Williams Honorable Mention – 1 vote 1 CeeDee Lamb, Jonathan Mingo, Tyler Smith, Tyler Booker, Jake Ferguson, Brevyn Spann-Ford, Michael Trigg, Israel Abanikanda, Bryan Anger, Donovan Ezeiruaku, Kenny Clark, Cobie Durant Interestingly, the consensus isn’t merely “the obvious stars played well.” Ogbonnia and Brown in particular, but also players expected to have a tough camp like Guyton, Milton, or Mingo, emerge from the aggregation as genuine camp surprises. full_text: Dallas once again impressed in their second preseason game, headlined by a strong showing from Joe Milton. Milton may have cemented himself as the QB2 heading into the season, while names like Camden Brown and Jonathan Mingo are making the WR decision even more difficult. With football inching closer, the final 53-man roster is looking a little clearer. A look at the news. 4 winners and 1 loser from Cowboys’ preseason rout of the Cardinals – Marcus Mosher, The Landry Hat The Cowboys’ backup units looked good on Saturday night, and there are a lot of positives to take away from this game. Dallas now has a decent idea of who their QB2 will be, and both Camden Brown and Jonathan Mingo look poised to make the final 53-man roster. Winner: Joe Milton – QB Milton got the start in Week 2 after backing up Sam Howell in Week 1, as the two have been in a quarterback battle all camp. While we can’t say for sure that Milton won the job on Saturday, it sure feels like he is in pole position. Updated Dallas Cowboys 53-Man Roster Prediction – Mark Heaney, Inside The Star Cuts are on the horizon, and there are a decent number of roster spots still up in the air. While most may have an idea of the hierarchy of the names at each position, it will all come down to the depth Dallas chooses to keep at the various spots. 6 WRs: CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens, Ryan Flournoy, KaVontae Turpin, Jonathan Mingo, Camden Brown. – In the wide receiver room, Mingo and UDFA Camden Brown have forced Dallas’s hand: they must go heavy at WR on the 53-man roster to keep both players. 2nd preseason game snap counts reveal Cowboys plans for roster cutdown – Todd Brock, Cowboys Wire Snap counts, especially in the second preseason game, tend to be very telling. Players like Drew Shelton, Jaydon Blue, and Jaishwan Barham got the opportunity to impress Saturday night. On defense, rookie Jaishawn Barham finally took the field, logging over a third of the unit’s snaps and looking good doing it. Cornerback Devin Moore also made his Cowboys debut with 20 snaps and was targeted early by the Arizona passing attack (notably beaten once by former Cowboys WR Simi Fehoko). Top 4 Dallas Cowboys Trade Candidates Entering Preseason Week 3 – Randy Gurzi, Sports Illustrated Dallas has room to make a few splash moves if they choose, and they have the talent to make a trade. Shipping a player like Liufau or Mingo for a backup offensive lineman could add safety. Marist Liufau, EDGE As soon as the Cowboys added Von Miller, Marist Liufau’s spot on the roster became incredibly shaky. That’s why Cowboys On SI’s Josh Sanchez named Liufau the most obvious trade candidate following the Miller signing. Mailbag: Will the run defense be improved?- Patrik Walker & Tommy Yarrish, DallasCowboys.com Granted, there was not a lot of positives for the Cowboys defense in 2025, but the run defense was especially porous. If Dallas is expecting improvement under Christian Parker, it starts with stopping the run. A full offseason of work together for Quinnen Williams and Kenny Clark is going to be big. I think that already in training camp we’ve seen the two of them contribute to making it very difficult to run on the Cowboys when they’re on the field together, although training camp practices and joint practices can be tricky to test just how good a team can run the ball/stop the run. Daily discussion question: Which defensive rookie are you most excited about? Downs or Barham?

title: Sean Payton on the signing of safety Taylor Rapp: ‘It was more availability than necessity’
summary: The Broncos announced that they signed veteran safety Taylor Rapp last week ahead of their Week 2 preseason matchup vs. the Green Bay Packers to add some depth to their safety room. Today, Denver Broncos Head Coach Sean Payton met with the media and explained their reasoning behind signing the veteran safety. He was basically […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CA - DECEMBER 08: Buffalo Bills safety Taylor Rapp (9), wearing a Guardian Cap helmet, during pregame warmups before an NFL football game between the Buffalo Bills and Los Angeles Rams at SoFi Stadium, December 8, 2024, in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Tony Ding/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Broncos announced that they signed veteran safety Taylor Rapp last week ahead of their Week 2 preseason matchup vs. the Green Bay Packers to add some depth to their safety room. Today, Denver Broncos Head Coach Sean Payton met with the media and explained their reasoning behind signing the veteran safety. He was basically too good for them to pass up. The Broncos signed Taylor Rapp because they like his game and what he brings, per Sean Payton: “More talent at that position” — Zac Stevens (@ZacStevens) August 24, 2026 Payton told reporters that Raoo is a veteran player that they liked, had good grades on, and simply wanted to add more talent to the safety position. He added, they weren’t pounding the table to add a safety, but it was more Hey, this player’s available,’ and ‘Let’s work him out and sign him if possible. “Yes, [he’s a] veteran player we liked, had good grades on and just more talent at that position. It was really more… It wasn’t like us pounding the table, ‘We need a safety.’ It was, ‘Hey, this player’s available,’ and ‘Let’s work him out and sign him if possible.’ So I’m glad he’s here. We’ve had experience playing against him. He has real good football instincts and awareness that serves you well at that position. So I think it was more availability than necessity, if that makes sense.” Rapp is a talented football player who brings a ton of experience and playoff/Super Bowl experience to this roster. Throughout his career, the former second-round selection has appeared in 93 games while starting in 72 of those games. Last season, he appeared in six games for the Buffalo Bills before a knee injury ended his season, and he was placed on the injured reserve. During his career, Rapp has totaled 488 tackles, 11 tackles for a loss, 2 sacks, 12 interceptions, 31 pass deflections, and 2 forced fumbles. While Payton says they were not banging the table, saying they needed a safety, they needed to add some depth to that room. They lost versatile/former starter P.J. Locke, who was their third safety last season to free agency, and did not really bring anyone in to replace that role. They allowed their in-house depth to compete for that role throughout the offseason and into training camp. However, All-Pro special teams player Devon Key, JL Skinner, Tycen Anderson, and rookies Miles Scott and Parker Robertson were never able to fully lock down that role. So, it made sense to bring in a talented veteran with experience like Rapp at this point in the summer to fill the Broncos’ one big glaring need heading into the season. At the end of the day, I really like this signing for the Broncos. Adds some much-needed depth and gives the team some insurance in case safeties Talanoa Hufanga and/or Brandon Jones end up missing some time this season. Safety depth was their one glaring hole on the team on paper, and they filled that with his signing.

title: Cut day looms for 2026 Broncos
summary: We interrupt all this preseason fun to remind you that the Broncos roster will need to be trimmed to 53 no later than 4:00pm MT, Sunday, August 30. That means that today is the last Monday that dozens of players will ever clock into work for the Denver Broncos. Sure, there is one last preseason […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - AUGUST 14: Darnay Holmes #30 of the Atlanta Falcons defends Joseph Manjack IV #86 of the Denver Broncos during the second quarter in an NFL preseason game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on August 14, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images) | Getty Images We interrupt all this preseason fun to remind you that the Broncos roster will need to be trimmed to 53 no later than 4:00pm MT, Sunday, August 30. That means that today is the last Monday that dozens of players will ever clock into work for the Denver Broncos. Sure, there is one last preseason game in Denver against Minnesota, but this game is just as disposable as every other last preseason game that has come before it. It has always amazed me that by the time the game re-airs on NFL Network, the vast majority playing in the finale will already be out on the street. This year will likely be no different with cuts due less than 48-hours after the preseason comes to a close. The drama on cut down day in Denver will come on the offensive side of the ball, with decisions at running back, wide receiver, and tight end. At running back, J.K. Dobbins, Jonah Coleman, and R.J. Harvey will surely make it, leaving Jaleel McLaughlin, Tyler Badie, and Cody Schrader vying for the final spot. I would like there to be more intrigue regarding the likely 5 wide receiver spots with Waddle, Sutton, Mims, Bryant, and Troy Franklin, but it’s doubtful that one will be whacked in favor of Lil’Jordan Humphrey, Kobe Katsis, Dane Key, Joseph Manjack, Kyrese Rowan, Kyre Duplessis, or Hakeem Butler. At tight end, Evan Engram, Justin Joly, Lucas Krull, Adam Trautman, Dallen Brentley and the injured Caleb Lohner are fighting for likely 4 spots. Expect the names you know to be the names that make it. Sorry Caleb. Will a player or players be traded before the cut deadline? With the Broncos returning so many of their players from 2025, there is a good chance that George Paton strikes a pre-deadline deal like he did in 2023 when he sent Albert Okwuegbunam (and a 7th rounder) to the Eagles for a 6th round pick. So, stay tuned if you are a fan of late round pick exchanges. With less than a week of the preseason left to play, players that aren’t locks for the 53-man roster are doing everything they can to stick around, either on the practice squad or possibly catching on with another club after cuts. Who will make it and whose NFL dream will come to an end? The NFL Grim Reaper comes for every player eventually. Just who will he come for this Sunday and who will he let stay?

title: Detroit Lions place 2 players on IR; sign injury replacements
summary: In a pair of roster moves from Monday afternoon following their preseason win over the Washington Commanders, the Detroit Lions have placed two players on the Reserve/Injured list: running back Raheem Blackshear and wide receiver Cedrick Wilson. In response to those moves and to fill out their 90-man roster for the rest of training camp, […]
full_text: In a pair of roster moves from Monday afternoon following their preseason win over the Washington Commanders, the Detroit Lions have placed two players on the Reserve/Injured list: running back Raheem Blackshear and wide receiver Cedrick Wilson. In response to those moves and to fill out their 90-man roster for the rest of training camp, they made two corresponding moves with the additions of defensive back Jason Taylor II and running back Roydell Williams. With no addition at wide receiver, it feels like the team is comfortable with their current makeup of that room moving forward. At defensive back and running back, both Taylor and Williams will be entering highly competitive battles where they will have little time to make their presence felt. Taylor was a seventh-round selection in the 2023 NFL Draft after playing at Oklahoma State through college. He has some versatility to his game, having spent time as a professional both in the slot and at safety. On the other side of the ball, Williams went undrafted this year after finishing his college career at Florida State University. Prior to landing in Detroit, Williams signed with the Indianapolis Colts before recently being waived. In the grand scheme of things, both of these players are likely considered to be longshots to make the final 53-man roster. However, the Lions want to ensure that they have enough players to get through the rest of training camp and one more preseason game without having to rush players back from injury. Or overload players who will be fighting for jobs with too many reps. And from a player’s perspective, both will have a chance to put some things on film for the Lions and the 31 other teams that will be looking to fill out their active rosters and practice squads.

title: Report: Detroit Lions to sign rookie RB Roydell Williams
summary: The Detroit Lions running back room has been hit hard by the injury bug, and according to NFL Insider Jordan Schultz, the team is reportedly signing UDFA rookie Roydell Williams to help support the room during the final week of training camp. Williams began his college career at Alabama, where he played four seasons as […]
full_text: WESTFIELD, INDIANA - AUGUST 04: Roydell Williams #36 of the Indianapolis Colts runs a drill during the Indianapolis Colts Training Camp at Grand Park Sports Campus on August 04, 2026 in Westfield, Indiana. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Detroit Lions running back room has been hit hard by the injury bug, and according to NFL Insider Jordan Schultz , the team is reportedly signing UDFA rookie Roydell Williams to help support the room during the final week of training camp. Williams began his college career at Alabama, where he played four seasons as a reserve, before transferring to Florida State to finish off his college career. With just five college starts under his belt, Williams went undrafted and signed with the Indianapolis Colts following the draft but was released five days ago in order to make room for veteran wide receiver Keenan Allen. The Lions’ running backs have looked very solid throughout training camp and are arguably coming off a game where every back who played performed above expectations. But while the talent has been noticeably present, they’ve also been dealing with a string of absences. Starter Jahmyr Gibbs missed the start of camp, waiting on a new contract extension. His direct backup, Isiah Pacheco, is currently dealing with an MCL sprain that has kept him out the last two weeks. RB3 Sione Vaki missed time after suffering an eye injury and broken nose, and after returning to a heavy workload in practice, he dealt with back spasms that kept him out of the Lions’ last preseason game. Jacob Saylors has steadily been RB4, but he only returned from an ankle injury less than a week ago. Jabari Small, his most direct challenger, has been an ascending player, but he suffered a concussion in Saturday’s game, which has the potential to keep him out of this week’s practices. While Gibbs is practicing in full, Pacheco, Vaki, and Small remain question marks for practice and the final preseason game. With Gibbs unlikely to play in that game, that leaves Saylors, Trayvon Williams ( last game’s Player of the Game ), and Raheem Blackshear to finish out the preseason. The addition of Roydell Williams gives the Lions more depth so they don’t have to rush players back from injury, while also giving the rookie the chance to impress enough in the final week to try and earn a spot on the practice squad—something we saw quarterback Jake Fromm do a few preseasons ago.

title: Detroit Lions among teams most likely to improve in 2026, per ESPN
summary: After the Detroit Lions’ 2025 disappointing season—a playoff-less 9-8 year—analysts have gone one of two ways with the future in Detroit. Some believe their Super Bowl window is closing or closed. Others believe it was a temporary step back, and they’ll be back in contention in 2026. Well, you can count ESPN’s Bill Barnwell as […]
full_text: Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell watches practice during training camp at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Wednesday, July 29, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co After the Detroit Lions’ 2025 disappointing season—a playoff-less 9-8 year—analysts have gone one of two ways with the future in Detroit. Some believe their Super Bowl window is closing or closed. Others believe it was a temporary step back, and they’ll be back in contention in 2026. Well, you can count ESPN’s Bill Barnwell as one of the people in the latter category. On Monday, Barnwell put together his annual list of NFL teams most likely to improve in 2026 , and the Lions were one of five teams listed. Barnwell’s methodology for these list typically involves a set of statistics that tend to regress (positively or negatively) to the mean each year. That includes strength of schedule, records in close games, turnover margin, and point differential. When it comes to the Lions, Barnwell pointed to several metrics that indicate Detroit could be in for a bounce-back season. One odd one was Detroit’s terrible recovery rate on fumbles. Per Barnwell, Detroit recovered just 29 percent of fumbles last year, which not only was last in the league, but it was “just the fifth time since 1990 that any team has failed to recover at least 30% of fumbles in a season.” Barnwell also points to injuries as something that should (hopefully) regress to the mean in the Lions’ favor in 2026. “Detroit was last in adjusted games lost on defense , where the only starters who suited up for all 17 games were Derrick Barnes, Jack Campbell, Aidan Hutchinson and DJ Reader,” Barnwell wrote. Though Barnwell was quick to point out Detroit is already dealing with some 2026 injuries, including Cade Mays, Isiah Pacheco, Brian Branch, and Kerby Joseph. Finally, Barnwell points to Detroit’s schedule as another reason for a big 2026 season. “What should make life easier in 2026, though, is the conference’s easiest schedule ,” Barnwell wrote. “Though the NFC North might be a slugfest, the Lions get four games against the NFC South, and that makes anyone’s life easier. Everyone else in the division gets a game against a playoff team from the NFC West, but the Lions get to face the Cardinals.” Barnwell’s 2025 list of five teams most likely to improve included three teams that saw massive success (Bears, 49ers, Jaguars), one that regressed (Raiders), and one that just improved by a single win (Giants). To read Barnwell’s entire column and see the other four teams he predicted to improve, check it out here.

Running back: Assumed in: Jahmyr Gibbs, Isiah Pacheco Sione Vaki: 11 votes (no change) Jacob Saylors: 11 votes (no change) Jabari Small: 0 votes I briefly considered putting Trayveon Williams on the bubble after an impressive preseason debut for the Lions, but Detroit’s running back situation looks as figured out as possible. Small and Saylors were jockeying for the RB4 job, but Small’s concussion in the second preseason game may be the unfortunate death blow to his roster chances. I know many Lions fans are frustrated with Sione Vaki’s continued battles through injuries, but the coaching staff has made it pretty clear how much they value him and how much they are not concerned about the injuries. Wide receiver: Assumed in: Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams, Isaac TeSlaa, Greg Dortch Tay Martin: 8 votes (up 4) Dominic Lovett: 1 votes (down 2) Cedrick Wilson Jr.: 0 votes (down 8) Tom Kennedy: 0 vote (no change) The big move here is Cedrick Wilson dropping eight votes after suffering a knee injury in Saturday’s preseason game. While we don’t yet have confirmation that it’s a serious injury, coach Dan Campbell said after the game that he’s “worried” about it being long-term . Most of those votes went to Tay Martin, who continues to get high praise from the coaching staff, continues to rep high with the offense and get a ton of work on special teams. Interestingly, a few of our staffers have the Lions only keeping four wide receivers. That would be a surprise given how much praise Campbell has given this group, but it’s also pretty hard to point to specific standouts beyond the top four. The rest of Wilson’s votes went to… Tight end: Assumed in: Sam LaPorta, Brock Wright OFF BUBBLE WATCH: Miles Kitselman (IR), Anthony Firkser (IR) Tyler Conklin: 11 “IN” votes (no change) Jackson Meeks: 9 votes (up 7) Thomas Gordon: 0 votes (no change) … Jackson Meeks. After an incredibly strong preseason performance, Meeks jump to the top of the line for the TE4 job, should the Lions opt to keep four. Given how much the Lions have been playing 12 and 13 personnel this offseason, it certainly would make sense to have the extra bodies here. Campbell continues to praise Meeks publicly, while also reminding the media that he’s still learning the tight end position: “He continues to grow, and this tight end thing is still kind of new, so the good news for Meeks is he’s strong – you know, the athleticism. I mean, he was in the receiving room, and he was really a big X – so I think we all kind of know what that is. But he’s strong and he’s willing. And he’s smart. So, it’s just time on task. He’s another one, but you see how he attacks special teams. He gives our guys fits and special teams, too.” Potential plus special teams value could be enough to vault him onto the 53-man roster, but there’s still a week of work to do. Offensive tackle: Assumed in: Penei Sewell, Blake Miller, Larry Borom Colby Sorsdal: 0 votes (no change) Devin Cochran: 0 votes (no change) Offensive tackle continues to stay stable here. But it’s at least worth noting that Devin Cochran is back practicing and playing again, which could give him a chance to make the practice squad. Interior offensive line: Assumed in: Tate Ratledge, Christian Mahogany, Miles Frazier Assumed on IR: Cade Mays Juice Scruggs: 11 votes (up 0) Ben Bartch: 10 votes (down 1) Seth McLaughlin: 8 votes (down 3) Michael Niese: 0 votes (no change) Juice Scruggs may as well be considered a lock at this point, as he’s pretty much nailed down the starting center job while Cade Mays recovers from his broken wrist. The question is interior depth. Bartch has not been able to stay on the field and is now in concussion protocol. With the Lions trying out a couple of veteran guards last week , Detroit may be looking to move on for a more dependable player with loads of experience. Additionally, Seth McLaughlin had a tough afternoon against the Commanders, which has led to a few staffers getting rid of Detroit’s primary backup center. That may be tough to manage should a mid-game injury hit Scruggs, but perhaps that’s why the Lions were cross training starting right guard Tate Ratledge at center. Or the Lions could get McLaughlin on the practice squad and elevate him early in the season. That said, Michael Niese’s preseason injury may give the Lions no choice but to roster an additional center, be it on the practice squad, the 53-man roster, or both.
