title: Let’s Argue: Travis Kelce will have the best year of his career
summary: In our “Let’s Argue” series, Mark Gunnels considers the hot takes, wacky predictions and unpopular opinions of Kansas City Chiefs fans from all over the world. This week, we gathered your hot takes from The Feed! Kansas Chiefs says: Kelce has the best season of his career. The league leading running game and talented receivers […]
full_text: TAMPA, FL - AUGUST 22: Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce (87) runs ahead before a game between the Kansas City Chiefs and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, Saturday, August 22, 2026 at Raymond James Stadium in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Ricky Bowden/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images In our “Let’s Argue” series, Mark Gunnels considers the hot takes, wacky predictions and unpopular opinions of Kansas City Chiefs fans from all over the world. This week, we gathered your hot takes from The Feed ! Kansas Chiefs says : Kelce has the best season of his career. The league leading running game and talented receivers around him will create opportunities like never before. I’m not ready to go that far, but I understand the logic behind it. Even at this stage of his career, I still think Travis Kelce is comfortably a top-10 tight end in football, and you can make a legitimate argument that he’s still top five. The addition of running back Kenneth Walker should only help him. If Kansas City can establish a more consistent running game, defenses won’t be able to key in on Mahomes and the passing attack quite as aggressively, which should create more favorable looks for Kelce over the middle. I absolutely expect Kelce to have a productive season. I just can’t predict the best season of his career when we’ve already seen what prime Kelce looked like. In 2020, he was virtually unstoppable, and 2022 was another ridiculous season where he was still clearly the centerpiece of the Chiefs’ passing game. Those are incredibly high bars to clear, especially at his age. Could the improved running game and more talent around him make Kelce more efficient and keep him fresh for the entire season? Absolutely. But a career year? I’ll believe that when I see it. Prime Kelce set the standard way too high. DynastyMode2024 says : The duo of Delane and Williams will get talk as the best CB tandem in the league 10 or so games into the season and the talk will build steam throughout the playoff run. I can absolutely see this happening. In the time Nohl Williams was on the field last season, he flashed in a major way. There were stretches where he legitimately looked like one of the better corners in football, and if he can build on that over a full season, the Chiefs could have something special. Then you add rookie Mansoor Delane to the mix. Kansas City obviously believes in him, considering the front office traded all the way up to pick No. 6 to get him, and based on what we’ve seen, he already looks like the best corner from this rookie class. That’s why this take doesn’t feel crazy to me at all. The Chiefs may have found their next version of the L’Jarius Sneed and Trent McDuffie duo — two physical, versatile corners who can make life miserable for opposing quarterbacks. Calling them the best cornerback tandem in football by Week 10 is a high bar, but if Williams stays healthy and Delane keeps developing the way the Chiefs expect, I wouldn’t be surprised if that conversation starts getting very real. TheSovereign1587 says : Rice finishes with 100+ catches and 1200 rec yards I’m with this one. If you look at what Rashee Rice was doing last season, he was already on pace to flirt with these numbers over a full 17-game schedule. Now you add the extra motivation of a contract year — and we all know the saying: the contract year is undefeated. If Rice stays healthy, I think he’s in line for a monster season. With his chemistry with Mahomes and his ability to rack up catches and yards after the catch, 100+ receptions and 1,200+ yards are absolutely within reach.

title: Chiefs fan guide: Ranking the road trips on the 2026 schedule
summary: The days are getting shorter, the morning air is crisper, kids are returning to school, and Halloween decorations smack you in the face when you enter stores. This can only mean one thing. Fall is near, and with it, a new season of Kansas City Chiefs football. Part of the fun of preparing for a […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 2: Patrick Mahomes #15 of the Kansas City Chiefs talks to teammates in a huddle prior to the game against the Buffalo Bills at Highmark Stadium on November 2, 2025 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The days are getting shorter, the morning air is crisper, kids are returning to school, and Halloween decorations smack you in the face when you enter stores. This can only mean one thing. Fall is near, and with it, a new season of Kansas City Chiefs football. Part of the fun of preparing for a new football season is planning road trips to support your favorite team in a different city, to go wear red in the “Black Hole.” It’s a great way to spend a weekend during the NFL season. Ranking road trips for the football season takes three main factors into account: Uniqueness of the matchup: How often do the Chiefs play this opponent? While Allegiant Stadium is a great place to watch a football game, the Kansas City Chiefs play the Raiders twice a year. This road trip could be punted to a future season in favor of a road trip to see a team harder to come by. The stadium and city quality: Next, how highly ranked is the stadium, and what fun extracurriculars are there in the city to fill out a weekend? A stadium with poor views, infrastructure, or a lackluster fan experience won’t make for as fun a road trip. Likewise, an NFL game is only three hours of your weekend. What else can the city offer? How is the food and beverage scene? What other local attractions are there? The matchup: The Chiefs have some heavy hitters on their 2026 road slate. The schedule features matchups against several Super Bowl hopefuls, along with rising bitter rivals. A high-stakes game in late November or December against a highly ranked opponent or rival will carry more weight and be higher in these rankings than an early-season tilt against an NFL bottom-feeder. A matchup is even more enticing in primetime. With these factors in mind, and to help you plan your football road trips, let’s rank the Chiefs road games in 2026. Tier 3: Consider staying home No. 9: Miami Dolphins — Hard Rock Stadium Week 3: Sunday, September 27. Noon Just when it’s getting cooler in Kansas City, you could make the trip to South Florida if you’re looking to immerse yourself once again in thick humidity. A Sunday September afternoon in Miami figures to be steamy, and there’s no guarantee this game will be worth the miles to get there. The Dolphins are in the midst of another rebuild and are projected to be one of the worst teams in the NFL in 2026, so the matchup isn’t enticing on paper. There are no major storylines to look forward to in this one either. The Tyreek Hill factor is out of the equation, so this one lacks juice. However, if you want to relive the memories of Super Bowl LIV at Hard Rock Stadium — I wouldn’t blame you. No. 8: Las Vegas Raiders — Allegiant Stadium Week 4: Sunday, October 4. 3:25 PM As already mentioned, the Chiefs and Raiders are a matchup we’ve seen —literally, over 100 times. Allegiant Stadium is a fantastic place to watch a football game, but the Raiders aren’t projected to make a major leap forward in 2026. The Raiders haven’t named a starter yet, but it’s expected that 2026 first-overall pick quarterback Fernando Mendoza will not be the starter. There are just other games on the road schedule that are more exciting. But Vegas is a cheap destination and a fun place to spend a weekend. So no one will fault you for wanting to see the Chiefs continue their winning ways in Vegas. No. 7: Atlanta Falcons — Mercedes-Benz Stadium Week 10: Sunday, November 15. Noon This one barely edges out the Raiders game, strictly due to the uniqueness of the matchup. As an AFC team, the Chiefs do not play the NFC Falcons often, let alone travel to Atlanta. The Falcons are not expected to be a good team in 2026 either, with their quarterback situation potentially being the worst in the league. But this game could pose more playoff ramifications, being in mid-November. Mercedes-Benz Stadium is also well known as having some of the most affordable concessions in the NFL. Tier 2: Solid matchups and road trips No. 6: Los Angeles Chargers — SoFi Stadium Week 17: TBD Chiefs-Chargers games are almost always fantastic. This mid-tier ranking isn’t about the quality of the matchup or of the stadium. SoFi is a fantastic football venue. It’s bumped down in the rankings because it’s a common opponent for the Chiefs, and because another trip to SoFi appears later in the rankings. No. 5: Denver Broncos — Empower Field at Mile High Week 8: Sunday, November 1. 3:25 PM A great divisional matchup, which could be higher in the rankings if it were later in the year. The consequences of this game won’t be felt as highly as if it were played in late November or December. Mile High is another great stadium to watch a game, against the AFC West defending champs. Bad blood is beginning to brew once again between these two teams—which makes for a great rivalry. The Chiefs will be on a mission to reclaim the West crown. Denver is a fantastic city to visit with countless recreational opportunities and attractions to make for a fun weekend. No. 4: Cincinnati Bengals — Paycor Stadium Week 14: Sunday, December 13. 3:25 PM A game that may have been top-ranked a few years ago, this Bengals-Chiefs game in mid-December has the chance to renew this rivalry. The hatred between these teams has seemed to cool off a bit in recent memory. The teams have not met since September 2024, and we are three years removed from their last playoff matchup. Both franchises are looking for a bounce-back campaign. The stadium is nothing exciting, and no one wants chili on spaghetti — but this one will feel like the playoffs and have postseason ramifications. Tier 1: The S-Tier No. 3: Seattle Seahawks — Lumen Field Week 7: Sunday, October 25. 7:20 PM This is a great football game to only be ranked third on this list. The Chiefs will visit the defending Super Bowl champs on Sunday Night Football in late October. We’ll know the general trajectory of these teams by then. New Chiefs’ running back Kenneth Walker III will make his first appearance against his original team — after winning Super Bowl MVP the last time he was in a Seahawks jersey. Head coach Andy Reid will undoubtedly have some special plays dialed up just for him. Seattle is also an amazing city, and a great place to watch a football game. Lumen Field comes in second after Arrowhead in terms of crowd noise. Chiefs Kingdom will feel right at home. No. 2: Los Angeles Rams —SoFi Stadium Week 13: Thursday, December 3. 7:15 PM I flipped the second and third spots in this ranking a few times. SoFi is a common destination for the Chiefs, and despite making two trips there in 2026, this matchup is too good to be ranked lower. The Rams are the offseason darlings of the NFL, currently the betting favorite to win the Super Bowl. Not only is this game a great matchup, but cornerback Trent McDuffie will be making his first appearance against his former team following the April trade. Thursday Night Football in primetime—everyone will be seated for this one. No. 1: Buffalo Bills — Highmark Stadium Week 12: Thursday, November 26. 7:20 PM We all knew this would be at the top of the rankings. Every game between these teams turns into an instant classic. The Bills have owned the regular-season matchups, while the Chiefs own the postseason. Everything is working in this game’s favor. Bitter rivalry? Check. Great quarterbacks? Check. New stadium? Check. Fun city to visit? Check. And to top it all off — Thanksgiving football in primetime. Chiefs-Bills will be a fantastic way to cap off Turkey Day. There will be no tryptophan-induced comas in this one. This isn’t the right opinion; it’s just my opinion. Do you agree with these rankings of the road trips in 2026 for Chiefs fans? Give us your own rankings in the comments below.
author: Dakota Watson

title: Chiefs News: Who will be the right tackle for Patrick Mahomes Week 1?
summary: The latest We are learning more and more about the Kansas City Chiefs with each preseason snap. Two exhibitions have provided plenty of snaps to evaluate, and one question stands above the rest in terms of significance right now. It has to do with the starting offensive line and who will be protecting the right […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - NOVEMBER 10: Patrick Mahomes #15 of the Kansas City Chiefs looks to pass in the fourth quarter of a game against the Denver Broncos at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium on November 10, 2024 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images) | Getty Images The latest We are learning more and more about the Kansas City Chiefs with each preseason snap. Two exhibitions have provided plenty of snaps to evaluate, and one question stands above the rest in terms of significance right now. It has to do with the starting offensive line and who will be protecting the right edge of the pocket for quarterback Patrick Mahomes against the Denver Broncos defense on “Monday Night Football” in Week 1. 2026 NFL preseason Week 2: Game takeaways, analysis | ESPN Chiefs: Who will be the right tackle for Patrick Mahomes on opening night? The team invested most of training camp in preparing Kahlil Benson, the undrafted rookie from Indiana. Benson’s performance Saturday, however, was quite disappointing. He struggled in pass protection, surrendering quick pressure to rookie Rueben Bain Jr. and a strip-sack to outside linebacker Anthony Nelson. At this point, the Chiefs likely move Benson to guard, where he played much better against the Los Angeles Rams last week. Jaylon Moore, a five-year veteran, hasn’t been impressive, either. But Moore is likely the Chiefs’ most ideal option. The only other possibility is Esa Pole, a second-year player who took snaps Saturday at left tackle with the second-team offense. — Nate Taylor Biggest Winners and Losers From Chiefs’ Preseason Week 2 Loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers | Sports Illustrated Losers Jared Wiley, Tight End Tight end Jared Wiley was technically third on the team with two catches and 15 receiving yards, but he was targeted four times and had a drop. He looks smooth catching passes in open space, but Travis Kelce and Noah Gray already fill that role. What the Chiefs need from a third tight end is someone willing to do the dirty work, and Wiley has not shown that. Kansas City Chiefs Preseason Week 2 Snap Counts: Jalen Royals settling in, Mansoor Delane shuts it down in debut | A to Z Sports Mansoor Delane gets nearly a dozen shutdown cornerback snaps in his debut The No. 6 overall pick by the Chiefs in the 2026 NFL Draft, Mansoor Delane, made his NFL debut on Saturday. He only played during the first quarter, but that’s all it took for him to impress. Through three drives, he played 11 snaps at outside cornerback. He wasn’t targeted once by Baker Mayfield or Jake Browning. Typically, seasoned quarterbacks will test rookie cornerbacks, but they didn’t even think to look his way in his first NFL action. Delane also had a beautiful downhill trigger on a screen pass that disrupted the play for a loss. He very much so looks capable of playing opposite Nohl Williams early for Kansas City. Longtime Chiefs RB Named Candidate to Replace Ashton Jeanty After Injury | Heavy Sports Kareem Hunt Could Fill in for Ashton Jeanty NFL analyst Nathan Jahnke of Pro Football Focus broke down the potential replacements for the Raiders if they lose Jeanty for an extended period. He noted a pair of trade candidates alongside Hunt. “If the Ashton Jeanty injury is serious, they should try to trade for Tyrone Tracy or James Conner. Kareem Hunt might be their best free agent option,” Jahnke wrote in a post on X. Chiefs’ Jalen Royals, Emmett Johnson make preseason matter in loss to Buccaneers | The Kansas City Star “It was great to see Royals step up and have a couple nice catches and then the yards after the catch,” Chiefs head coach Andy Reid said after the game. “He did a nice job there.” The play from Nussmeier to Royals helped set up a third-and-6 deep shot to wide receiver Andrew Armstrong down the left sideline. Bucs cornerback Roman Parodie was called for pass interference on the play, bringing the Chiefs inside the Tampa Bay red zone. Around the NFL Dae’Quan Wright to LSU? What we know after Browns waive former Ole Miss TE | The Athletic “Man, ain’t that s— crazy?” Monken told reporters. “I wondered why Lane Kiffin reached out a week ago. Now I know.” The team source who confirmed Wright had been waived spoke on condition of anonymity because the move has not been finalized. Wright is part of a lawsuit challenging new NCAA eligibility rules that give athletes a five-year window to compete in college sports. Raiders’ Ashton Jeanty injured after landing awkwardly, has sprained ankle according to reports | CBS Sports The second-year rusher had been having a strong practice when he landed awkwardly diving for a catch thrown by Kirk Cousins during 11-on-11 drills. His teammates immediately froze as he lay on the ground. Trainers tended to him, then helped him up and aided him off the field. As he left, the entire team got down on a knee and stayed silent for a while before finishing practice. The team did not immediately provide information on Jeanty’s injury following practice. Niners activate TE George Kittle off Phyiscally Unable to Perform list | NFL.com The 49ers activated Kittle from the physically unable to perform list on Sunday, the team announced. Kittle, who has been rehabbing from an Achilles tear he suffered in San Francisco’s wild-card playoff game last season, can now begin practicing and getting into true football shape for the regular season. Regardless of his contagious optimism, Kittle coming off the PUP list is by no means a guarantee he’ll suit up for Week 1. In case you missed it on Arrowhead Pride Chiefs Preseason Week 2 snap count analysis: Jalen Royals leads offense Rookie, second-round edge rusher R Mason Thomas was not among the first out on the field for the Chiefs’ starting defense, but he was a factor for the first-team unit. On an early third-and-11, Thomas flew up the field with his head and hands up, batting down a pass that was nearly lateral and staying with it through the whistle. It was just one play that showed off his pass-rushing prowess, but there were a number of chances for Thomas to rush the passer. In fact, all 15 of Thomas’ defensive snaps in Tampa were against a pass play, and he did not drop into coverage on any of those reps. PFF marked Thomas with four pressures over the 15 opportunities, including a quarterback hit. title: Chargers roster 2026: Donte Jackson, Alec Ingold, and Brenen Thompson are underrated
summary: It’s probably fair to say that Jim Harbaugh found his usually relentless optimism (Alex Smith recently told me that Harbaugh is the real-life Ted Lasso) a bit tested through the 2025 season. Harbaugh’s Chargers finished the regular season with an 11-6 record despite the leakiest offensive line in the NFL, but the injuries to tackles […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - DECEMBER 27: Donte Jackson #26 of the Los Angeles Chargers takes the field prior to a game against the Houston Texans at SoFi Stadium on December 27, 2025 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Katelyn Mulcahy/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s probably fair to say that Jim Harbaugh found his usually relentless optimism ( Alex Smith recently told me that Harbaugh is the real-life Ted Lasso ) a bit tested through the 2025 season. Harbaugh’s Chargers finished the regular season with an 11-6 record despite the leakiest offensive line in the NFL, but the injuries to tackles Rashawn Slater and Joe Alt, and other issues inside, really came home to roost in the playoffs. In the 16-3 Wild Card loss to the New England Patriots, Justin Herbert was pressured on 25 of his 44 dropbacks, completing eight of 14 passes for 84 yards under duress, and that was that for the season. Now, Harbaugh has decided to weaponize Herbert’s efforts as never before with Mike McDaniel, the offensive wunderkind who absolutely tore through opposing defenses as the Miami Dolphins’ head coach when things were on the right track. When he has the personnel to attack the ways he would prefer, McDaniel is miles ahead of Joe Lombardi and Greg Roman, Herbert’s last two OCs, who treated Herbert like the Lamborghini you never took out of the garage. McDaniel sees a different outcome, and Herbert is all in. “That’s kind of his big emphasis in getting the ball out and getting the ball in the receivers’ hands at a time where they can go up field and make something happen,” Herbert said over the summer regarding McDaniel’s passing game vision. “We turned on the tape of Miami the last few years, and how many plays they had with YAC — guys catching the ball, and breaking for a touchdown. The better I can do at getting the ball quicker in their hands and into a position they can run with it, I think the better our offense will be.” Which is a good thing, because the offensive line isn’t quite ready for prime time just yet. Left tackle Rashawn Slater is still dealing with the aftereffects of the torn patellar tendon that cost him the entire 2025 season. Center Tyler Biadasz, signed this offseason to be the rock of the front five, was carted off the field this week with a lower leg injury during practice , and he’s now out indefinitely with an ACL thing . Still, McDaniel should finally give Herbert the schematic godliness he’s always deserved. Because from a pure tools perspective, there aren’t five other NFL quarterbacks to match him — pressured ceaselessly or not. Justin Herbert making big-time throws under pressure. It shouldn't ALWAYS have to be this way. pic.twitter.com/JR8F6geI2T — Doug Farrar ✍ (@NFL_DougFarrar) June 10, 2026 In the grand scheme of things, if these Chargers are to exceed what has happened before them, they’ll need all kinds of help from everyone on the roster — not just the major stars, but also (and especially) the guys whose on-field performances have not yet etched their names in the court of public opinion. To that end, I’ve identified three Hidden Gems for the 2026 Chargers — one underrated veteran, one underrated free agent, and one underrated draft pick. Underrated veteran: CB Donte Jackson Losing defensive coordinator Jesse Minter to the Ravens as Baltimore’s new head coach was an inevitable and unpleasant reality, as Minter is one of the finest defensive minds at any level of football. Now, it’s up to 2024 Chargers safeties coach and 2025 Western Michigan defensive coordinator Chris O’Leary to replace Minter — not an easy task. O’Leary’s Chargers do have a lot of talent on that side of the ball, and cornerback Donte Jackson may be the player whose 2025 season most outstripped his name recognition. L.A. signed the 5’10”, 180-pound veteran to a two-year, $13 million contract before the 2025 season with $7 million guaranteed. That was a very smart move, as under Minter, Jackson had his best season to date. The 2018 second-round pick of the Carolina Panthers allowed just 23 catches on 46 targets for 323 yards, 112 yards after the catch, three touchdowns, four interceptions, seven pass breakups, and an opponent passer rating of 58.5. It went under the radar, but @chargers CB Donte Jackson had his best season to date in 2025. Dude was erasing all over the place, and he's excited about Year 2 with the team. pic.twitter.com/zLeYFcXw0Y — Doug Farrar ✍ (@NFL_DougFarrar) August 19, 2026 The good news for O’Leary is that he has a returning secondary of Jackson, Derwin James, Tarheeb Still, Tony Jefferson, and Elijah Molden, and Jackson is pretty amped about what the new season will bring. “First year here doing it, I was kind of like the new guy still feeling my way around,” Jackson said in June . “I was a vet, but still had that energy of a young guy because I was new. Still learning the guys, still learning everything, the building, the city, stuff like that. “These days, it’s smooth sailing. You come back in, have the same guys you went to war with last year, and the confidence and everything has been high. It’s been awesome.” Hopefully, the awesomeness continues. Underrated free agent: FB Alec Ingold As much as Mike McDaniel is known for his high-flying passing game (more on that in a minute), it should come as no surprise that a guy who was Kyle Shanahan’s run game specialist in 2017, and run game coordinator from 2018-2020, would also have a highly diverse ground game with heavy doses of variable fullback action. Last season, McDaniel’s Dolphins ranked third in the NFL in the rate of 21 personnel (two backs, one tight end, and two receivers) at 25%. Only the Pittsburgh Steelers (36%) and the Chargers (26%) had a higher rate in 2025. Scott Matlock was the primary fullback last season, and McDaniel added to that depth by bringing one of his favorite Dolphins — Alec Ingold — over on a two-year, $7.5 million contract with just $3.75 million guaranteed. Ingold was with McDaniel all four seasons he was the Dolphins’ head coach, and when you watch how Ingold facilitated so many of McDaniel’s run game concepts, it’s easy to see why he’s now a Charger. When the Dolphins gave running back De’Von Achane a four-year, $64 million contract extension this offseason with $27.378 million guaranteed, one of the first things I wondered was, “They didn’t have the extra bucks to bring back the guy who helped make so many of Achane’s biggest plays happen?” Interesting thing about the massive De'Von Achane contract: 20 of Achane's 40 explosive plays last season came with FB Alec Ingold as a key blocker. Ingold signed a two-year, $7.5 million contract with the Chargers. Good news for Omarion Hampton, Keaton Mitchell, and Kimani… pic.twitter.com/DtuYITauj2 — Doug Farrar ✍ (@NFL_DougFarrar) August 19, 2026 Well, that’s Miami’s problem now, and it’s to McDaniel’s, and the Chargers’ great benefit. Whether he’s displacing linebackers in I-formation runs, or pulling with authority to take out a defensive end on an outside zone concept, Ingold has a rare ability to know where he’s going, and who he needs to take out. Each of the Chargers’ backs — Omarion Hampton, Keaton Mitchell, and Kimani Vidal — should reap the rewards of Ingold’s blocking acumen. “I run and hit,” Ingold said over the summer, when asked what he brings to his new team. “I think that’s like, you know, something I do. Tone set when I need to. I think previous years, I’ve nerded out on leadership, sports psychology, all of that, and trying to build really good relationships with guys. Not just in the locker room, but in the meal room, in the weight room… constantly trying to be a positive voice of change, of effort, of intensity. “Probably wore some people out after four years of hearing my shit, but excited to learn from that and grow from it. This past offseason I’ve learned a heck of a lot on different ways to build relationships, different sports psych and different literature that I’ve studied. So I’m nerding out…

title: Don’t get too attached to Wesley Bailey
summary: Wesley Bailey had one of the best defensive performances of the 2026 preseason yet. The UDFA out of Louisville earned 10 pressures in Saturday afternoon’s contest between the Los Angeles Rams and New Orleans Saints. But a breakout game doesn’t necessarily translate to security on the 53-man roster. We’ve seen other Bailey’s with the Rams […]
full_text: Inglewood, - August 22: Linebacker Wesley Bailey (47) of the Los Angeles Rams reacts after a New Orleans Saints fumble in the second half of a NFL preseason football game at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood on Saturday, August 22, 2026. (Photo by Keith Birmingham/MediaNews Group/Pasadena Star-News via Getty Images) | MediaNews Group via Getty Images Wesley Bailey had one of the best defensive performances of the 2026 preseason yet. The UDFA out of Louisville earned 10 pressures in Saturday afternoon’s contest between the Los Angeles Rams and New Orleans Saints. But a breakout game doesn’t necessarily translate to security on the 53-man roster. We’ve seen other Bailey’s with the Rams before. 2021 brought Chris Garrett’s breakout—and Garrett was drafted by the team whereas Bailey wasn’t. Pass-rush productivity comparison for Chris Garrett and Wesley Bailey Player Season Height Weight PRSH Grade PRSH Snaps Pressures Breakdown Pressure Rate Chris Garrett Arizona Cardinals · ED 2021 6’4″ 245 lb 78.2 42 7 2 SK · 1 HIT · 4 HUR 16.7% Wesley Bailey Los Angeles Rams · ED 2026 6’5″ 265 lb 68.6 59 10 1 SK · 3 HIT · 6 HUR 16.9% Source: Chris Garrett PFF page and Wesley Bailey PFF page . Pressure rate equals total pressures divided by PRSH snaps. To Bailey’s credit, he’s roughly an inch taller and 20 pounds heavier than Garrett. Garrett never posted 10 pressures in a single game—he posted seven in the totality of his rookie preseason. Both players boast roughly the same pressure rate. Bailey edges out in terms of total pressures with more snaps. Garrett earned a notably better pass rushing grade from Pro Football Focus (PFF). The roster math is still the same. EDGE is a position that requires incredible measurables and athletic traits. Very few human beings on earth can way 250 lbs. while displaying bend and explosiveness. There is a reason why the NFL’s elite pass rushers are usually drafted at the top of the first round. While the Rams have found success later with the likes of Byron Young and Josaiah Stewart, it’s rare that unheralded prospects develop into bonafide pass rushers. In short, don’t be surprised if Bailey falls victim to the looming roster cuts following LA’s preseason finale on Thursday. The Rams’ EDGE rotation is mostly set: Myles Garrett, Young, Stewart, and Desjuan Johnson. There will be room on the practice squad if Bailey clears waivers, and he probably will because he doesn’t clear the athleticism bar that a difficult position requires. When the most telling thing the Rams can tell you about the preseason is who isn’t on the field, don’t risk falling in love with standout players who are mostly auditioning for their next role. Don’t get too attached to Wesley Bailey. We’ve seen this story before.
author: JB Scott

title: Stetson Bennett’s performance against Saints was overhyped
summary: Here are a few headlines coming out of the Los Angeles Rams’ preseason win over the New Orleans Saints led by quarterback Stetson Bennett: Bennett seems ready to serve as Matthew Stafford’s understudy – PFT Bennett gets moxie back, strengthens backup case – The Athletic They mostly get it wrong. Bennett filled up the stat […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 22: Stetson Bennett IV #13 of the Los Angeles Rams celebrates his touchdown with Max Klare #86, to take a 17-0 lead over the New Orleans Saints, during the first half in a preseason game between the New Orleans Saints and the Los Angeles Rams at SoFi Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images Here are a few headlines coming out of the Los Angeles Rams’ preseason win over the New Orleans Saints led by quarterback Stetson Bennett: Bennett seems ready to serve as Matthew Stafford’s understudy – PFT Bennett gets moxie back, strengthens backup case – The Athletic They mostly get it wrong. Bennett filled up the stat sheet. Box score watchers came away impressed, which happens often in the preseason. Watching the game portrays a much different story. Bennett did not look like an efficient thrower of the football. In the last two weeks he’s demonstrated a concerning trend of often throwing behind moving receivers. Against New Orleans specifically, the ball often sailed on Bennett and he left several big plays on the field. I will say…sometimes Bennett can make the easy look hard and the hard look easy. The Rams QB had a few get away from him yesterday. Threw behind Daniels on the slant and he did the same last week. pic.twitter.com/flPhMrJHDz — Blaine Grisak 💭 (@BGMediaOnSI) August 24, 2026 In no way would a regular season offense led by Bennett be efficient. His running ability gives him a high floor—that is a positive. But starting defenses will almost certainly play tighter coverage than we are seeing in the exhibition games. Bennett isn’t making a lot of tight window throws. He’s missing the hard passes more often than not. This isn’t to say that rookie Ty Simpson has been convincingly better. He hasn’t. Simpson’s second appearance was a continuation of the first. The same questions from the preseason opener—primarily surrounding competence in the deep area of the field—remain as Thursday’s finale approaches. The truth is that the Rams probably don’t have a reliable backup quarterback right now. Bennett isn’t Jimmy Garoppolo. Simpson may surpass that bar one day—he’s simply not there right now. Max Klare has WD-40 on his hands in the middle of Inglewood, CA…. pic.twitter.com/QpaFTkXy2E — Rams Tapes 🇵🇷 (@RamsTapes) August 22, 2026 Could LA get by for a game or two with either Bennett or Simpson? Possibly. But if Stafford misses a month of the season and someone needs to keep the team afloat—it’s difficult to imagine either player rising to the occasion. Simpson is probably the safer bet at this point. And the NFC West figures to be ultra-competitive again in 2026. Dropping a game to a team you shouldn’t could reasonably be the difference between raising the division crown or traveling on the road into the playoffs. In an offseason where the Rams added loads of talent across the roster, they may not have done enough at football’s most important position: quarterback.

title: 4 Rams who just missed the roster bubble
summary: The two most contentious positions on the L.A. Rams roster heading into final cuts on Sunday are at running back and offensive line, which is why at this point Ronnie Rivers and Austin Blaske are two of the most controversial decisions that Sean McVay could end up making next weekend. In a survey of Rams […]
full_text: Inglewood, - August 22: Running back Jarquez Hunter (27) of the Los Angeles Rams reacts after running for a touchdown against the New Orleans Saints in the second half of a NFL preseason football game at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood on Saturday, August 22, 2026. (Photo by Keith Birmingham/MediaNews Group/Pasadena Star-News via Getty Images) | MediaNews Group via Getty Images The two most contentious positions on the L.A. Rams roster heading into final cuts on Sunday are at running back and offensive line, which is why at this point Ronnie Rivers and Austin Blaske are two of the most controversial decisions that Sean McVay could end up making next weekend. In a survey of Rams fans asking for their final 53-man rosters , the top-four players who have failed to make the cut so far are two running backs and two offensive lineman. Rivers and Dean Connors are on 47-percent and 39-percent of rosters thus far, while Blaske and A.J. Arcuri are both on 34-percent. Will one or all four end up making McVay’s final roster? If you want to help change the results, you still have time to submit your own Rams 53-man roster before we make a final consensus edition . McVay indicating Rivers is on the roster Through 2 preseason games, Rivers is getting the “protected player” treatment that McVay always gives to guys he thinks are important to the regular season roster. He hasn’t played at all. If Rivers makes the roster, the reason for it should be obvious: He’s the team’s kick returner . Now if Rivers does not make the cut, it must be because numbers didn’t work in his favor after the team liked what they saw from Jarquez Hunter, Connors, or even Jordan Waters. Even in the case, for McVay to give Hunter so much preseason playing time, including in the fourth quarter, would be completely opposite of his typical treatment of NFL regular season players. He just hasn’t done that in the past, like at all. But Hunter is on 79-percent of rosters right now and it’s not surprising. Hunter was a fourth-round pick last year, so he’s not a camp body. He also disappeared and wasn’t heard from for his entire rookie season. Not that surprising given the team’s respect for Kyren Williams and Blake Corum, we get it. But Hunter hasn’t returned kicks. Rivers has. This could be the difference. Meanwhile, Dean Connors would be a major surprise relative to his presumed value a month ago. He was undrafted, he could probably clear waivers, and he’s not a threat to steal anyone’s job on offense. Connors played just six snaps against New Orleans. A.J. Arcuri still playing preseason Despite playing in his fifth NFL season, the former seventh-round pick is still a preseason and practice squad type on the Rams. He played 51 snaps against the Saints on Saturday. Blaske played the entire game. David Quessenberry, who is maybe a bland player in the eyes of most (but not a bland last name, to be fair) is still on 76-percent of your rosters. The widely held expectation is that Quessenberry will be on the roster over Blaske and Arcuri, and sure enough he is sitting out the preseason. Will Arcuri or Blaske get enough support to reach the consensus roster?
author: Kenneth Arthur

title: LA Rams roster 2026: Byron Young, Jaylen Watson, Tim Keenan III are underrated
summary: Four points. Four freakin’ points. That’s what separated the 2025 Los Angeles Rams from an appearance in Super Bowl LX, as the Seattle Seahawks beat them, 31-27, in the NFC Championship game. The Rams had every reason to believe that they could have beaten, and subsequently become, the defending champs, because Sean McVay’s offense was […]
full_text: WOODLAND HILLS, CALIFORNIA - MAY 26: Jaylen Watson #35 of the Los Angeles Rams walks off the field after an OTA offseason workout at Rams Village at Warner Center on May 26, 2026 in Woodland Hills, California. (Photo by Ric Tapia/Getty Images) | Getty Images Four points. Four freakin’ points. That’s what separated the 2025 Los Angeles Rams from an appearance in Super Bowl LX, as the Seattle Seahawks beat them, 31-27, in the NFC Championship game. The Rams had every reason to believe that they could have beaten, and subsequently become, the defending champs, because Sean McVay’s offense was the only one that consistently beat up on Mike Macdonald’s defense . In three games last season, Seattle went 2-1 in the series, with a point total of 88-85 in their favor. Les Snead’s and Mr. McVay’s response was eminently predictable for anybody who has followed these guys and what they do over the last decade. Build slowly to come up on Seattle from the back over time? Yeah, no. Instead… well, if you’re reading this, you know what they did. They traded for Kansas City Chiefs cornerback Trent McDuffie, signed McDuffie bookend Jaylen Watson in free agency, nabbed Myles Garrett away from the Cleveland Browns, and may have Aaron Donald coming back from retirement to possibly destroy every quarterback he faces. Now, these Rams are as loaded as any Super Bowl contender we’ve ever seen — as long as everything clicks the right way. They have F’d Them Picks, and the rest of the NFL may have to suffer as a result. “I’m really excited about our team coming together, because that’s what every single year is about,” McVay said on June 2, during the press conference announcing the Garrett trade. “That happens one day at a time. We’ll finish up this offseason program where it’s this week, the following week, and then we’ll come back for training camp and we’ve got to be ready to rock. Then, the goal will be to be able to peak when we start in Australia [for the regular-season opener]. Hopefully, we’re fortunate to stay healthy, and continue to build and adjust and adapt as we go but it’s a long journey. We’ve got to be able to handle it, but most important is the caliber of people. “How do we come together? How do we establish what this team really looks like? We are fortunate to have a lot of continuity, and there’s excitement being able to add a player like [Garrett]. It’s one day at a time. We’re not going to let the outside narratives affect our ability to be courageous every single day, and go swing, and see what the hell happens.” Well, the Rams have certainly swung this offseason. The effects of all that activity remains to be seen, but it’s also true that the Rams wouldn’t be as good as they are without finding a lot of lesser-known guys to fill their roster with excellence. So, while it’s easy to focus on the bigger names, I wanted to point out three Hidden Gems for the Rams — one underrated veteran, one underrated free agent, and one underrated draft pick. Underrated veteran: EDGE Byron Young Byron Young is used to living under the radar. Nobody thought much of him when he came out of Carvers Bay High School in Hemingway, South Carolina, and he worked at Dollar General for 18 months to make money before walking on at Georgia Military College in 2020. That led to Young’s status as a highly-ranked junior college prospect, and his acceptance of Tennessee’s recruiting efforts. In 2021 and 2022 for the Vols, the 6’2”, 250-pound Young totaled 16 sacks and 74 pressures, which led to the Rams taking him with the 77th overall pick in the third round of the 2023 draft. Young was unusual in that he was immediately more productive at the NFL level than he was in college. He jumped from 8 sacks and 51 pressures in his rookie season, to 11 sacks and 54 pressures in 2024, to a team-high 13 sacks in 2025; only Jared Verse (100) had more pressures than Young’s 74. Moreover, Young can get to the quarterback any which way he chooses — this is no one-trick pony. Who led the @RamsNFL 's loaded line in sacks last season? That would be Byron Young. He can jump gaps, go around you, move inside your reach, or bull you right into Mr. Quarterback. The hidden force on Chris Shula's defense. pic.twitter.com/kMo2xYFF00 — Doug Farrar ✍ (@NFL_DougFarrar) August 22, 2026 “I think what’s been great for B.Y. is he’s just gotten better every single year,” McVay said on August 13. “And when you know his backstory, what an incredible human being. You want to talk about a guy that’s mentally and physically tough. I thought his best practice of camp was against the Cowboys. We’ve obviously been smart with what his workload looks like. He felt good. I thought he had some good quick wins, being able to counter inside. I thought he was stout against the run. He did a really good job with everything that was asked of him the other day. He had another good day today. “If you don’t love ‘B.Y.’, something is wrong with you. He’s a special human. His story’s incredible. I love everything he’s about.” McVay may love everything ‘B.Y.’ is about even more when Young is on the other side of Myles Garrett, and dealing with the one-on-ones that will invariably generate. Not that Young needs them. The next step for Young will be to grab a second contract in line with his productivity . That should happen sooner than later. Underrated free agent: CB Jaylen Watson Wait. What? Why are you featuring a cornerback who just signed a three-year, $51 million contract with $34 million in total guarantees? That’s not underrated! Well, my counter to that would be that Jaylen Watson received below market value for his work to date — he’s currently 21st in Average Annual Value among cornerbacks , behind such luminaries as Deommodore Lenoir, Tyson Campbell, and DaRon Bland. Chump change for a guy who, last season for the Chiefs, allowed 35 catches on 59 targets for 447 yards, 173 yards after the catch, no touchdowns, two interceptions, four pass breakups, and an opponent passer rating of 69.0. It was the 2022 seventh-round draft pick out of Washington State’s best NFL season to date, and it exceeded even McDuffie’s efforts — the more well-known McDuffie, who scored a four-year, $124 million contract extension with $100 million guaranteed after the trade. Last season, McDuffie allowed 37 catches on 55 targets for 342 yards, 130 yards after the catch, three touchdowns, one interception, six pass breakups, and an opponent passer rating of 94.7. Watson and McDuffie do have different responsibilities, as Watson has noted. He’s more of an outside cornerback, while McDuffie is the movable chess piece. It got a bit lost in the Chiefs' disappointing season, but CB Jaylen Watson became All That against some of the NFL's better receivers in 2025. That should play out wherever he goes in 2026 and beyond. pic.twitter.com/JkBIAOEqhj — Doug Farrar ✍ (@NFL_DougFarrar) March 4, 2026 “To be honest, I think that’s my strength,” Watson said in March about his ability to defend bigger receivers at 6’2” and 197 pounds. “That’s why I think me and Trent complement each other so well. His strengths are the short area, quick game and the smaller, shiftier guys. My strengths are the big receivers. We should be pretty diverse. We should be able to match up pretty well against a lot of different looks that we get.” Not that Watson can’t erase other receivers with authority — check out what he did to the 6’0”, 200-pound Malik Nabers last season. Nabers is more quick and shifty than big and nasty, and Watson was all over it from step one. One target, one pass breakup, one interception. Boom. New @RamsNFL CB Jaylen Watson has said that guarding bigger receivers is a primary strength of his. True, but here's what he did to Malik Nabers last season. pic.twitter.com/GyG1pXYRiQ — Doug Farrar ✍ (@NFL_DougFarrar) August 22, 2026 Another reason it’s good to remember that Jaylen Watson will be just as responsible for fixing last year’s cornerback issues as McDuffie will.…

author: Kenneth Arthur

title: 6 teams that could have trade interest in Stetson Bennett
summary: As the Los Angeles Rams continue to evaluate their quarterback depth heading into the regular season, Stetson Bennett could become an intriguing name on the trade market. While Bennett may not be viewed as a long-term starter, his experience in Sean McVay’s offense, familiarity with the Rams’ system and potential upside could make him appealing […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 22: Stetson Bennett IV #13 of the Los Angeles Rams celebrates his touchdown with Sean McVay, to take a 17-0 lead over the New Orleans Saints, during the first half in a preseason game between the New Orleans Saints and the Los Angeles Rams at SoFi Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images As the Los Angeles Rams continue to evaluate their quarterback depth heading into the regular season, Stetson Bennett could become an intriguing name on the trade market . While Bennett may not be viewed as a long-term starter , his experience in Sean McVay’s offense, familiarity with the Rams’ system and potential upside could make him appealing to teams dealing with uncertainty at quarterback. With injuries, roster decisions and unexpected developments always capable of changing the quarterback landscape, there could be franchises willing to explore a trade rather than enter the season without a reliable insurance option. For Los Angeles, that could create an interesting decision: keep Bennett as valuable depth behind Matthew Stafford, or capitalize on his potential trade value if another team comes calling. The Rams would not receive anything beyond a Day 3 draft pick but maybe that is worth it for a team that is always wheeling and dealing. Here are 6 teams that could trade for Stetson Bennett. Atlanta Falcons The Falcons moved on from Kirk Cousins so that they could watch Tua Tagovailoa and Michael Penix Jr have a cat fight for the quarterback position. With both quarterbacks having an extensive injury history, it may just be a matter of time before the Falcons make a call. The @AtlantaFalcons should try and trade a late pick for Stetson Bennett — Dan Orlovsky (@danorlovsky7) August 23, 2026 Arizona Cardinals Mike LaFleur was just with the Los Angeles Rams for the past three seasons. title: Rams final cuts due in 6 days; can anyone change their minds?
summary: All NFL teams must cut their rosters down to 53 players by August 30, giving the Los Angeles Rams less than one week to figure out who will make their final roster and who will be released. It’s a nerve-racking time for any player on the roster bubble, and it’s exciting as well. Some players […]
full_text: LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA - JULY 26: Les Snead of the Los Angeles Rams on the field during training camp at Loyola Marymount University on July 26, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Ric Tapia/Getty Images) | Getty Images All NFL teams must cut their rosters down to 53 players by August 30, giving the Los Angeles Rams less than one week to figure out who will make their final roster and who will be released . It’s a nerve-racking time for any player on the roster bubble, and it’s exciting as well. Some players are going to be disappointed as they won’t make their team, other players will have their dreams come true. The Rams have plenty of work to do to figure out their backup quarterback situation , they need to determine the look of their running back room , and more! So much to do, never enough time in the NFL. To this point, the Rams are 2-0 and are having a nice preseason with Ty Simpson looking solid against the Kansas City Chiefs, and then Stetson Bennett looking confident against the New Orleans Saints. You could make the case that preseason is going exactly as it should for the Rams as their quarterbacks look serviceable, and their depth overall looks like a strength. Take that all with a grain of salt. It’s only preseason, and the Rams want to look good in the regular season, not just the preseason. That aside, take it for what it is. The Rams have looked good in August, and that’s all they can do right now. 2026 Los Angeles Rams: Projecting final 53-man roster (espn) “LOS ANGELES — The Rams open the 2026 NFL regular season against the San Francisco 49ers on Sept. 10 at Melbourne Cricket Ground. But first, they play one more preseason game Thursday against the Los Angeles Chargers and then must cut their roster to 53 players by 6 p.m. ET on Sunday. Who will make the team? Which positions have tough decisions on deck? And where might the lineup be deepest and thinnest this season? This roster projection doesn’t include Aaron Donald , who is currently going through a “regimented” process to determine whether he wants to come out of retirement. This is an offensive-heavy projection, in part because it includes six receivers, five tight ends and 10 offensive linemen.“ No one is talking about these heroes of Rams preseason thus far (ramblinfan) “Some have called out the offensive line for a lack of depth. But rewatching preseason games to focus on the performance, you’ll see a different story. LA may lack a stable of backup linemen with draft-day pedigrees, but they come to play. So who are these overachievers? Rams’ preseason offensive line: C Dylan McMahon, G Beaux Limmer, LT AJ Arcuri, G Bill Murray, G Wyatt Bowles, G Austin Blaske, T Blake Hance (T Keagen Trost – injured) In the two games, this anonymous group helped LA put up 726 yards of offense: 482 passing yards, 244 rushing yards, two passing touchdowns, and three rushing scores. For a preseason unit that has been stitched together on the fly, that’s a noteworthy performance.“ Stetson Bennett layers it over the defense Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Dvb3NBR5jd — NFL (@NFL) August 22, 2026 Rams 53-man roster prediction entering Week 3 of the preseason (ramblinfan) “ Matthew Stafford, Stetson Bennett, Ty Simpson Not much to say here … well, actually there might be a little. Stafford is the reigning MVP. Bennett will be the backup unless head coach Sean McVay tells us otherwise. Simpson will continue developing. The main question is whether Stafford can stay healthy, and after that, is there another quarterback on the roster who can capably handle a series or a drive – or heaven help us, a whole game – if QB1 gets dinged?“ Ty Simpson’s preseason shows he’s right on track with his development (ramswire) “Going 21-for-25 for 190 yards and two touchdowns on his debut, Simpson avoided committing big mistakes while guiding the Rams up-and-down the field. What really impressed was his targeting of tight ends and running backs. He found running back Dean Connors for both his touchdowns, while Max Klare and Mark Redman had massive performances.” Two Wisconsin alumni headline Los Angeles Rams preseason standouts (badgerswire) “As part of a 34-0 shutout against the New Orleans Saints, the Rams improved to 2-0 in preseason action. Former Badgers Nyzier Fourqurean and Darryl Peterson III both have a chip on their shoulder , and each did their part to contribute to a defensive masterclass. Fourqurean recorded four tackles, three of which were solo, but most importantly, he added a pass deflection and forced a fumble.“ ‘ Loudmouth,’ ‘He’s 10! What Does He Know?’ — Chiefs Fans Take Offense at Rams QB Ty Simpson’s Shot at Arrowhead Stadium (sports.yahoo) “One fan reacted on social media by playing into the fact that Simpson is as green as it gets by NFL standards. “ He’s 10! What does he know? “ Another urged Simpson against making up his mind so quickly, pointing out the major differences between a preseason and regular season matchup at Arrowhead. “ Haven’t experienced Arrowhead during the regular season . Loud mouth [expletive].” Meanwhile, one commenter was quick to note that Simpson will get a chance to see how passionate Chiefs fans can be when Andy Reid, Patrick Mahomes and Co. travel to SoFi on Dec. 3.“ Ty Simpson said playing at Arrowhead Stadium was a big difference to playing at SoFi. Simpson said playing at Arrowhead felt like a college stadium, while SoFi felt like an NFL Stadium. pic.twitter.com/rSVoS9t1DJ — Eric Williams (@edubnfl22) August 22, 2026 Sean McVay’s victory speech after preseason win vs. Saints “HOW ABOUT THE DEFENSE FOR THE SHUTOUT?!” (therams.com) “Watch Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay’s victory speech after Saturday’s preseason win against the New Orleans Saints.“ This angle of Stetson Bennett’s 4th-down dime is a must-see (ramswire) “Flat-footed, he threw a sidearm dime to Tyler Scott, who was running a crosser route against man coverage with a linebacker also dropping into that area. The ball was layered perfectly over the corner and linebacker where only Scott could get it. The end zone angle of the throw shows just how impressive it was.“ Send apologies to Les Snead pic.twitter.com/vBQ19lJ9CV — Steve Palazzolo (@StevePalazzolo_) August 23, 2026 5 notable players the Rams held out vs. Saints (and what it means) (Ramswire) “Interestingly, several other players who may have been flirting with the roster bubble were also kept on the sidelines after playing in the first game last week against the Chiefs. For some, it’s a sign that they’ve all but secured a roster spot, but it’s not guaranteed that all five will make the team. WR Xavier Smith Smith played a lot in the preseason opener, and he stood out as both a receiver and returner. It may have been enough for the coaching staff to feel good about him as their punt returner and backup receiver. It’s likely that the team held him out to avoid any potential injury, given the role he’s expected to play this season.“ Los Angeles Rams Get Apparent Answer From Aaron Donald (heavy.com) “Donald, 35, has been away from the Rams and the NFL since the end of the 2023 season. He has teased a comeback this offseason amid the Rams’ trade for Garrett, who is also keen on the idea of teaming up with the 10-time Pro Bowler. “‘Locked in for season,’” one fan posted in the replies. “Do not play with our emotions [laughing face emoji].” Another fan said, “You just leaked the script gang [crying face emojis].” Comment of the Day: Food for thought, some nice points made below. Though I think Jimmy Garoppolo could make a lot of sense for the Rams. I also think we don’t know how ready Bennett or Simpson are for the regular season, but the Rams should have a decent idea. I’ll trust the Rams. “Really what good would the preseason reps be for Simpson? Bennett has being getting preseason reps nearly all his years with the Rams. The reps Simpson needs are the practice reps. That’s what matters. But if Simpson can’t beat out Bennett…

title: The Year 2 bar for Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty
summary: A complete bell cow-type back that handles 300-plus carries and close to 60 receptions per season all the while racking up 1,500-plus yards from scrimmage. That’s a mighty high bar for any running back in the NFL, but for the Las Vegas Raiders’ Ashton Jeanty, that’s the expectation his head coach — Klint Kubiak — […]
full_text: Dec 28, 2025; Paradise, Nevada, USA; Las Vegas Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty (2) enters the field before the game against the New York Giants at Allegiant Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect A complete bell cow-type back that handles 300-plus carries and close to 60 receptions per season all the while racking up 1,500-plus yards from scrimmage. That’s a mighty high bar for any running back in the NFL, but for the Las Vegas Raiders’ Ashton Jeanty, that’s the expectation his head coach — Klint Kubiak — has for the No. 6 overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft. And said high aspirations came to a screeching halt during the Raiders Sunday practice. According to reports, Jeanty dove for a low pass, landed awkwardly before remaining on the turf and being helped up by trainers as he was unable to put any weight on his right leg. With players and coaches taking a knee, the injury appeared quite serious in nature. And, Sunday evening, both Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport provided a reprieve — the ailment is believed to be a sprained ankle and not one of a season-ending variety. No joke: When the injury news started spreading, I stopped typing this piece. But while Las Vegas wades through the length of recovery for Jeanty, the Year 2 bar piece remains valid, albeit, potentially truncated with how many games the Raiders starting running back misses at the onset of the 2026 regular season. The type of ankle sprain is key, too. If it’s the high variant, that can result in longer recovery time and for a running back, zap them of the ability to thoroughly cut, plant, and create explosion from said ankle. By The Numbers Ashton Jeanty, Running Back, 2nd Year 2025: 17 games (17 starts), 266 attempts, 975 yards, 4 touchdowns; 73 targets, 55 receptions, 346 yards, 5 touchdowns Career: See above. #Raiders RB Ashton Jeanty, who had to be helped off the practice field today, is believed to have sprained his ankle, sources tell @AdamSchefter and me. Las Vegas still are unsure how long he will be out, but it is not considered a long-term injury and the organization is… pic.twitter.com/NchDFQDSdw — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) August 24, 2026 Schematic Sync Missing the initial slate of games (we’re assuming three to four, once the type of sprain is brought to light as is the recovery timeframe) is likely the case for Las Vegas’ workhorse back and that’ll put the spotlight on promising 2026 draft pick Mike Washington Jr. (fourth round, 122nd overall). A bigger tailback at 6-foot-2 and 228 pounds, the Arkansas product physical stature, running style, and speed are very reminiscent of another former Razorback and Raider: Darren McFadden. Washington showcased the vision, power, and ability to breakaway from defenders in the two preseason games thus far and it’ll be intriguing to see the New York native fare Week 1 and beyond. We’ll see if the electric running back can take advantage of one of the reasons Jeanty’s bar in Year 2 is so high: The offensive line revamp. With Jeanty generating a pedestrian 3.7 yards per carry as a rookie as he was met by defenders often at the or behind the line of scrimmage — meaning at a meager 1.26 yards before contact, the majority of the Boise State product’s rushing yards he created on his own after contact — the Raiders spent big coin on free-agent center Tyler Linderbaum to anchor the offensive line. Left tackle Kolton Miller is back healthy and there’s fiery competition to fill the rest of the interior group. That front five is set to be the heartbeat of Kubiak’s offense and fortunately for the Raiders head coach and offensive play caller, the running backs on the roster are a schematic fit for the heavy zone concepts being installed in the desert. The vision, one-cut decisiveness, tackle-breaking ability, alongside route running and soft hands as a receiver Jeanty has are a tailormade fit for Kubiak’s run game which relies on patient runners who read blocks and burst through cutback lanes to gore opposing defenses. Washington can do much of the same, hence why the Raiders are excited about the 1-2 punch Jeanty and the rookie bring to the table. ASHTON JEANTY ALL THE WAY! LVvsHOU on CBS/Paramount+ https://t.co/HkKw7uXnxV pic.twitter.com/szuynuAtqu — NFL (@NFL) December 22, 2025 Statistical Signficance Kubiak didn’t stutter when he broadcast his plan of using Jeanty in a Christian McCaffrey-type high-volume role that sees the RB1 get a majority of carries and be both an asset and weapon in the passing game. As a rookie, Jeanty received his fair share of totes (266 carries) and targets (73)and the tailback produced despite often getting battered and bruised — 1,321 yards from scrimmage with 10 touchdowns (five on the ground, five more through the air). Behind a much more accomplished play caller — who in turn, hired a veteran offensive line coach Rick Dennison — the needle is trending upwards in Las Vegas. We saw glimpses of what the offense can be and do in preseason action and watching a lead-blocking fullback in the run game is a welcome sight. That all noted, with improved play in the trenches alongside veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins (or rookie and No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza — Kubiak hasn’t officially named QB1 for Week 1) under center, and Kubiak orchestrating the offense, improved play is expected. That said, Jeanty producing a total of 1,500 yards from scrimmage (1,100 yards rushing, 4oo more receiving) in 2026 is the Year 2 bar, statistically. Getting Jeanty to be the all-around weapon in the Raiders’ offense is mission critical as Kubiak is old-school in his philosophy of a team’s run game being the engine of the attack. And the 5-foot-8 and 208-pound tailback has the skillset and production to become the type of chess piece running back Thurman Thomas was in the famed Buffalo Bills K-Gun offense in the late 1980s/1990s. The 5-foot-10 and 200-pound Oklahoma State product and hall of famer was equal parts dazzling and punishing runner and receiver. Both Jeanty and Thomas have the elite contact balance and low center of gravity that makes them difficult to tackle and the processing and vision to exploit openings. 2 receiving TDs 3 total TDs Ashton Jeanty is having a breakout game 🤩 CHIvsLV on CBS/Paramount+ https://t.co/HkKw7uXnxV pic.twitter.com/8w5xLiEmXZ — NFL (@NFL) September 28, 2025 Workload Balance While Kubiak has high expectations for Jeanty, he’s well aware even the workhorse needs a breather and having a big and fast spell back in Washington provides quite the jolt of a hammer. Believe it or not, at 22, Jeanty is younger than Washington (23) and having two young halfbacks in the room is a boon for Las Vegas. The Raiders can find themselves in a similar situation like the 2008-11 seasons when the team had both McFadden and bruising back Michael Bush. The pair complemented each other’s running styles culminating in an impressive 2010 season where McFadden ran for 1,157 yards and seven touchdowns along with 47 receptions for 507 yards and three more end zone visits. Bush, meanwhile, had 655 yards and eight touchdowns rushing and 18 catches for 194 yards. The following season, Bush paced the Raiders ground game with 977 yards and seven touchdowns along with 37 receptions for 418 yards and a score. McFadden, on the other hand, had 614 yards and four touchdowns rushing and 19 catches for 154 yards and a score. With Washington likely to earn the RB1 role with Jeanty missing any games, the rookie gets to set the tone and it’ll be interesting to see both their usage when the sixth overall pick from the 2025 draft gets a clean bill of health.

title: Could Las Vegas Raiders use Darien Porter or Hezekiah Masses at nickelback?
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders have a problem at the cornerback position during training camp, but it’s a good problem to have… Rookie fifth-round pick Hezekiah Masses has been generating plenty of buzz and is, surprisingly, expected to compete with second-year pro Darien Porter for the starting spot opposite Eric Stokes in free agency. That’s on […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - NOVEMBER 23: Darien Porter #26 of the Las Vegas Raiders warms up prior to an NFL football game against the Cleveland Browns at Allegiant Stadium on November 23, 2025 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders have a problem at the cornerback position during training camp , but it’s a good problem to have… Rookie fifth-round pick Hezekiah Masses has been generating plenty of buzz and is, surprisingly, expected to compete with second-year pro Darien Porter for the starting spot opposite Eric Stokes in free agency. That’s on top of having rookie fourth-rounder Jermod McCoy in the mix, and a solid start to camp from third-year pro Decamerion Richardson. Between Stokes (27), Porter (25), Masses (22), McCoy (21 on Aug. 16) and Richardson (25), the Raiders have a stable of young talent and promising outside cornerbacks on the roster. The problem is only two can be on the field at a time, so the coaching staff will have to get creative to maximize and get the most out of the position group’s collective potential. It sounds like that’s already in the mix, as ESPN’s Ryan McFadden posted on X/Twitter that the Raiders were experimenting with having Stokes and Porter on the perimeter while Masses was covering the slot at one point during practice on Monday, Aug. 10. This tells me while Porter isn’t getting as much love as Masses, the coaching staff likes what they’ve seen from Porter so far in camp Seems like they’re experimenting with ways to get him, Masses and Stokes on the field at the same time https://t.co/8fkdQfXyy4 — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) August 10, 2026 That tells me while Masses is getting most of the attention publicly, the coaching staff is just as pleased with Porter’s performance in camp. To be fair, there have been plenty of notes that the latter has been playing well. There’s just more buzz around the former because he’s new, performing better than expected and has emerged as a starting candidate despite being a fifth-round pick. For what it’s worth, the Raiders’ first unofficial depth chart has the second-year pro above the rookie. So, it seems like the coaching staff is looking for ways that they can get Stokes, Porter and Masses on the field at the same time. This is something they’ll find out for certain with a trial-and-error period in practice, but it does beg the question: Are Masses and/or Porter capable of handling nickelback duties? Part of where the ambiguity lies is that neither of them has much experience covering the slot. According to Pro Football Focus , the 2025 third-round pick took a total of 16 snaps as an inside cornerback during his college career at Iowa State, and was only targeted one time (an incompletion) while in slot coverage. Granted, it’s worth the reminder that he was originally a wide receiver and didn’t get much playing time at corner in general until his last season in Ames. But even as a rookie in the NFL, Porter took just two snaps at nickel . Meanwhile, Masses experience covering the slot is about the same, with 29 career snaps from that alignment over four seasons of College Football. He drew four targets and allowed three catches for 36 yards and a touchdown on those opportunities, per PFF . The lone score accounted for one of the four he surrendered last year. Traits-wise, slot corners are typically on the shorter side and have good short-area quickness to be able to stick with shifty slot receivers. For example, Taron Johnson, who the Raiders traded for in the offseason and was a 2023 second-team All-Pro nickelback, is a shade over 5-foot-11, per MockDraftable . Porter is one of the taller cornerbacks in the league at nearly 6-foot-3 , and Masses is fairly long too at 6-foot-1 . In other words, neither of them fits the typical size profile for the position. It’s often difficult for taller corners to make quick transitions because their center of gravity is higher and their strides are longer, so it takes them longer to get in and out of cuts. It requires more effort to sink their hips and cut their stride length down versus someone who’s closer to the ground and already has shorter strides, relatively speaking. The height difference is likely why Masses was viewed as the better initial candidate to cover the slot than Porter. Neither player has particularly great short-area quickness, but the Cal product has more potential to improve in that area. Another significant factor for playing nickelback is being physical enough to get involved in run fits. Especially since nickel personnel typically means a linebacker is coming out of the game, the defense needs the extra defensive back to bring some juice as a run defender since they’re going to be lined up near the box. A defensive coordinator can hide a bad run defender on the perimeter, but that isn’t the case on the inside. Despite his lack of size, that’s one of Johnson’s strengths. He’s feisty, willing to stick his nose in the running game to take on blocks and is a good tackler. That doesn’t describe Masses or Porter, though. That isn’t to say the latter two shy away from run defense, but they don’t bring the same level of physicality a typical nickelback would. Part of that is chalked up to how they’re built. As mentioned above, both Masses and Porter are significantly taller than Johnson/the typical physical profile for an inside corner. However, Porter is only three pounds heavier than Johnson, while Johnson has seven pounds on Masses, according to the Raiders’ roster . That’s going to limit the two young defensive backs’ ability to contribute against the run because they aren’t very dense. To summarize, the coaching staff is giving Masses (and maybe Porter down the line) an opportunity to see what he can do at slot corner rather than just assuming the rookie can’t get the job done. Maybe the Cal product can hold up in coverage at that spot. But right now, it seems like that might be trying to fit a square peg in a round hole. Of course, this is the time of year to experiment with these types of lineups, so there’s no shame in at least giving it a try.

title: What’s next for Raiders and Ashton Jeanty?
summary: The exact nature and timeline for Ashton Jeanty’s recovery from a Sunday practice injury will still develop, however, it appears the Las Vegas Raiders’ standout second-year starting running back has avoided a major injury. ESPN reported Sunday night that it appears Jeanty has a sprained ankle and it is not considered to be a long-term […]
full_text: HENDERSON, NEVADA - AUGUST 03: Ashton Jeanty #2 of the Las Vegas Raiders laughs after Kirk Cousins #8 reacted to a fan yelling his "You like that?!" celebration as they stretch during the team's training camp at the Las Vegas Raiders Headquarters/Intermountain Health Performance Center on August 03, 2026 in Henderson, Nevada. (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images)r | Getty Images The exact nature and timeline for Ashton Jeanty’s recovery from a Sunday practice injury will still develop, however, it appears the Las Vegas Raiders’ standout second-year starting running back has avoided a major injury. ESPN reported Sunday night that it appears Jeanty has a sprained ankle and it is not considered to be a long-term injury. That was refreshing news because there was major concerns when the No. 6 overall pick in the 2025 draft went down diving for a pass Sunday afternoon. He reportedly couldn’t put weight on his right leg and the team was stunned, kneeling and praying in silence. So, this news is really a best-case scenario. There are remaining questions, though. The Raiders open the regular season in 20 days at home against the Miami Dolphins. Sprained ankles can take between 1-6 weeks to heal depending on severity. So, if Jeanty has a high-ankle sprain, it could linger into the season. The worst-case scenario is he misses 3-4 games. The season opener could be in jeopardy even if it is a moderate sprain. If Jeanty isn’t ready to go for the opener, rookie Mike Washington will likely take the load with Dylan Laube and Dare Ogunbowale behind him. The team could add veteran, perhaps bringing back free agent Raheem Mostert. But there is less urgency for help with Jeanty being out for the short term. In the end, this could have been an offense-altering injury, but it seems like it will be just a temporary issue and that is a huge relief for Las Vegas.

Bell joins an unproven wide receiver room that includes two other rookies — third-round pick Caleb Douglas from Texas Tech and fifth-round pick Kevin Coleman Jr., most recently from Missouri. One player who has missed a week of work returned to action today. Quinn Ewers — Miami’s second-string quarterback who sat out last Saturday’s game against the New York Giants due to injury — returned to practice for the Dolphins on Monday. Ewers suffered a groin injury during Miami’s first preseason contest — a 20-7 loss against the Washington Commanders in which Ewers completed just one of eight passes for 27 yards, zero touchdowns and one interception. He earned a dismal 1.6 passer rating for his efforts. Cam Miller and Mark Gronowski handled Miami’s quarterback duties against the Giants on Saturday — with Miller finishing the game with six completions on 11 attempts, for 60 yards and no touchdowns, while Gronowski threw five passes, completing two of them for a single passing yard and no touchdowns. Neither quarterback threw an interception. Behind starter, Malik Willis, the Dolphins are trying to sort out who would best serve the team in the backup quarterback role, but through two preseason tilts, no man has separated himself from the bunch. As such, the team may look outside of the organization for a second-string passer once cut-down day takes place this Sunday.

title: J.J. McCarthy’s Painful Preseason: Regression, Edge Depth, and Flores’ Future
summary: The Minnesota Vikings’ preseason has gone from bad to painful, with backup quarterback J.J. McCarthy showing regression, edge rusher depth looking dangerously thin, and Brian Flores’ stalled lawsuit keeping him in purple. Darren Campbell and Dave Stefano break it all down on Two Old Bloggers. McCarthy, the highest-drafted quarterback in franchise history, has fans wincing. […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - AUGUST 22: J.J. McCarthy #9 of the Minnesota Vikings passes the ball against the Baltimore Ravens during the first quarter of the preseason game at U.S. Bank Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings’ preseason has gone from bad to painful, with backup quarterback J.J. McCarthy showing regression, edge rusher depth looking dangerously thin, and Brian Flores’ stalled lawsuit keeping him in purple. Darren Campbell and Dave Stefano break it all down on Two Old Bloggers . McCarthy, the highest-drafted quarterback in franchise history, has fans wincing. After a 13-3 loss to the Ravens, Dave didn’t mince words: “I think he’s regressed.” Darren agreed, noting “the ruthless consistency that you need to be an NFL quarterback… is just not there with J.J. McCarthy at this point in time.” The same issues that plagued McCarthy in 2025 — inaccuracy, poor ball placement, shaky pocket presence — were on full display again. Dave admitted, “He flashes at times and that gets you all excited, and then he reverts,” before delivering the gut punch: “I’m off his train.” Darren went further: “I feel more confident in Carson Wentz being the backup quarterback than I do in J.J. McCarthy.” Dave even floated trading McCarthy to the Colts one-for-one for Anthony Richardson, giving both former first-rounders a fresh start. The edge rusher situation is equally unsettling. Starters Dallas Turner and Andrew Van Ginkel are solid — Turner “was killing it” in joint practices — but the depth behind them is a giant question mark. Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins, Tyler Batty, Bo Richter, and Chaz Chambliss combined for just over 110 defensive snaps last season. Darren’s concern was palpable: “I don’t know if they can be really an effective guy.” Meanwhile, veteran edge rushers are disappearing — Za’Darius Smith signed with Atlanta, Von Miller with Dallas, Derek Barnett with Cleveland. Haason Reddick, Kyle Van Noy, Joey Bosa, and Leonard Floyd remain available, but time is running out. Dave suggested GM Nolan Teasley might wait for cut-down day on August 30th to scavenge reinforcements. One silver lining? Brian Flores’ discrimination lawsuit against the NFL continues with no end in sight, keeping him from head coaching opportunities. “The longer it drags on, the longer he gets to stay,” Dave noted. Darren added that when the Vikings offense finally catches up to Flores’ defense, “that’s when the Vikings are gonna be… a Super Bowl contender.” Key Points: J.J. McCarthy appears to be regressing, with the same accuracy and pocket presence issues persisting into Year 3 Dave Stefano is “off the train” on McCarthy; Darren feels more confident in Carson Wentz as the backup Edge rusher depth is a major concern behind starters Dallas Turner and Andrew Van Ginkel Veteran free-agent edge rushers are signing elsewhere, thinning the available pool Brian Flores’ ongoing lawsuit keeps him in Minnesota, which benefits the Vikings defense Win projections have the Vikings at 8.7 wins, lowest in the NFC North Kyler Murray has been inconsistent in training camp and joint practices Kevin O’Connell’s preseason approach mirrors other NFL coaches — starters barely play Roster battles: Tai Felton and Myles Price appear to lock up WR4/5; TE3 remains unsettled Final preseason game Friday in Denver, with cut-down day Saturday August 30th Listen: Or on your favorite podcast aggregator.
