title: 4 performances of note from the Patriots’ 21st training camp practice
summary: Before the Kayshon Boutte demanded our attention, the New England Patriots made their return to the practice fields behind Gillette Stadium. Their 21st session this summer was held in full pads, with multiple players sidelined, and star cornerback Christian Gonzalez making his return. To recap the action, please visit our Patriots training camp notebook. In […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MA - AUGUST 06: Quintayvious Hutchins #45 of the New England Patriots arrives to New England Patriots training camp on August 6, 2026 at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Summer Lamont/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Before the Kayshon Boutte demanded our attention, the New England Patriots made their return to the practice fields behind Gillette Stadium. Their 21st session this summer was held in full pads, with multiple players sidelined, and star cornerback Christian Gonzalez making his return. To recap the action, please visit our Patriots training camp notebook . In the meantime, here is who caught our eye during the two-hour session. Standout of the day RB Rhamondre Stevenson: With TreVeyon Henderson leaving practice during an early 11-on-11 period, the Patriots could have moved one of their available backup running backs — Hassan Haskins or JaMycal Hasty — up to work with the starting offense. They opted to go a different route, and simply upped Stevenson’s workload. Despite taking virtually every meaningful rep, the veteran looked very good. Stevenson was at his best during the simulated end-of-game situation to close out practice. He caught two passes during the series, including an impressive over-the-shoulder touchdown grab on a wheel route while covered tightly by linebacker Robert Spillane. The 15ish-yard reception was one of multiple touchdowns scored by the sixth-year runner on the day, and showed how he can be a factor both as a ball-carrier and a receiving option. Other performances of note OL Greg Van Roten: With Ben Brown unavailable for the time being, the Patriots brought in Van Roten in free agency. On Monday, he showed the value the team sees in him by lining up at all three interior line spots. Starting out at right guard, he also saw action on the left and at center — all as part of the first-team offense. His chances of making the team continue to look good. The rookie edges: The Patriots selected two outside linebackers in this year’s draft, and both performed well on Monday. Lining up as the starters on the second-team defense, Gabe Jacas and Quintayvious Hutchins were disruptive for much of the day. Jacas registered three hurries and a stuffed run, while Hutchins worked his way into the backfield on a couple of occasions. John Saunders Jr: His outlook is uncertain with the Patriots bringing in Jaylen Reed as part of the Kayshon Boutte trade, but Saunders Jr. continues to do his thing nonetheless. And this thing in 2026 is making splash plays: on Monday, the second-year man registered his fifth takeaway this summer when he hauled in a Tommy DeVito pass for an interception. Other players worth highlighting include tight ends Hunter Henry and Tanner Arkin. The former was actively involved during team drills, at one point catching a touchdown in an end-of-game setting, while the latter spent time with the starters as both a tight end and fullback. James Hudson, meanwhile, looked more comfortable moving back from guard to safety. The Patriots will hold their 22nd and final practice of this year’s training camp on Tuesday. The session, which will be closed to the public but open to the media, will kick off at 2:30 p.m. ET. As always, Pats Pulpit will be present to cover it.

title: What Kayshon Boutte trade to Texans means for the Patriots
summary: Kayshon Boutte’s time in New England has come to an end. As was reported on Monday afternoon, the Patriots have decided to trade the fourth-year wide receiver to the Houston Texans in return for safety Jaylen Reed and a seventh-round draft choice in 2028. Boutte is leaving Foxborough after back-to-back productive seasons as the team’s […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - JANUARY 18: Kayshon Boutte #9 of the New England Patriots runs with the ball during an NFC Divisional Playoff game against the Houston Texans at Gillette Stadium on January 18, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Kayshon Boutte’s time in New England has come to an end. As was reported on Monday afternoon, the Patriots have decided to trade the fourth-year wide receiver to the Houston Texans in return for safety Jaylen Reed and a seventh-round draft choice in 2028. Boutte is leaving Foxborough after back-to-back productive seasons as the team’s primary outside receiver and one of Drake Maye’s favorite targets. While never a top-tier producer, whose Patriots career ends with 87 passes for 1,327 yards and 10 touchdowns in 38 games, the 24-year-old has been a reliable deep target for quarterback Drake Maye — one that will now be wearing a different team’s colors. Let’s dissect what the move means for the Patriots from a big-picture perspective. Expected outcome The writing for a Boutte trade has been on the wall for a while now. There already was speculation last year and it took off again this offseason, especially after the Patriots signed Romeo Doubs to a multi-year free agency deal and acquired A.J. Brown in a trade with the Eagles. The Brown move in particular changed his outlook in New England. While not necessarily making him redundant, it added an established X-receiver whose career track record and potential in the Patriots offense both surpass Boutte’s — to a point where a trade started to feel inevitable. Boutte still had value to New England as a rotational WR4 with serious deep-field ability and an established chemistry with Drake Maye, but training camp showed that both Brown and Doubs have the former while also developing nicely in the latter. Add the fact that Boutte had requested a trade himself in the spring, and the Texans lost Jayden Higgins to a torn ACL last week, and the pieces were simply all falling into place. Trickle-down effect Entering Monday, the Patriots had 12 wide receivers on their roster. Among those, seven — the aforementioned A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs as well as Boutte, DeMario Douglas, Mack Hollins, Kyle Williams and Efton Chism — were in the realistic roster conversation. This, in turn, sparked questions about how many wideouts the team would actually be willing to keep on the 53-man team. It turns out, six might be the magic number. With Boutte no longer part of the conversation, after all, the team could keep a relatively standard quantity of receivers in the fold. Accounting for the Boutte trade as well as Kobe Prentice getting release on Monday, the depth chart at the position now looks like this: Wide receiver (10): A.J. Brown (1), Romeo Doubs (87), DeMario Douglas (3), Mack Hollins (13), Kyle Williams (18), Efton Chism III (86), Cameron Dorner (88), Kyle Dixon (83), Nick DeGennaro (23), Tejhaun Palmer (80) IR (2): Jimmy Kibble, Jeremiah Webb With Brown, Doubs, Douglas, Hollins, Williams and Chism now all relatively safe bets to make the team, the other wideouts will be fighting for practice squad spots. Cameron Dorner has looked like the frontrunner in that race throughout training camp, but fellow undrafted rookie Kyle Dixon received a shoutout from head coach Mike Vrabel after Saturday’s preseason game against the Eagles. Perception meeting reality Boutte was a productive wide receiver in New England who managed to make multiple big plays en route to a 15.3-yard average per catch over his three years with the club. He also showcased some maturity off the field and in light of the trade speculation surrounding him was praised by his position coach, Todd Downing. “It’s an example I will use for the rest of my coaching career, the way that he has just been a pro and shown up every day,” Downing said earlier this month . “He is an absolute joy to coach and I’m really glad he’s here.” Given all that, Boutte looked like a player who should be able to generate quite a bit of trade buzz. But while the rumors never stopped, the competition to get him seemingly did not drive the price up: all it took was a second-year safety with nine in-game appearances on his résumé as well as a seventh-round draft pick two years in the future. The reasons why remain hidden behind closed doors, but it is clear there was a disconnect in perception of Boutte’s value between the public and the NFL. Depth-for-depth trade Coming out of the Patriots’ preseason win over the Philadelphia Eagles on Saturday, head coach Mike Vrabel stated that “I don’t think we have a very deep team.” One position where the team was deeper than the norm was wide receiver, which in turn gave Vrabel and company the confidence to eventually move on from Boutte. The Patriots therefore used their depth at one position to help bolster it elsewhere on the roster. And while the safety position might not have looked like the biggest concern , it also was still unsettled behind starters Craig Woodson and Kevin Byard: Dell Pettus seemingly was on the inside track for the third role, while John Saunders Jr. made some strides as well. However, the Reed acquisition shows that New England — which is trying to implement more three-safety looks this year — was still looking for upgrades. As a consequence, the room now looks like this: Safety (9): Craig Woodson (4), Kevin Byard (31), Jaylen Reed (—), Dell Pettus (24), Mike Brown (33), Brenden Schooler (41), John Saunders Jr. (23), Peter Manuma (34), Eric Butler (30) The question for the Patriots will now be how many safeties, or defensive backs in general, to keep. Woodson and Byard are locks, and one would assume that Reed is as well. With core special teamer Brenden Schooler also a theoretical part of the mix as soon as he returns from the non-football injury list, no more than one spot might be open. Versatility and stability Jaylen Reed entered the league as a sixth-round pick by the Texans last year, and in his rookie season played nine games with three starts — including both of Houston’s playoff games. The 6-foot-1, 212-pound safety showed quite a bit of versatility along the way. Mostly lining up as a free safety, he also played closer to the box and in the slot. In addition, he was used on up to five special teams units. He still totaled only 173 snaps on defense and 113 in the kicking game, but that was mainly the result of injury rather than ability: Reed started the season on the physically unable to perform list due to a knee issue and was not activated until late-October; he later also missed time on injured reserve because of a forearm issue, but did return in time for the postseason. Had he not gotten banged up, there is a chance he would have been more regularly involved particularly as a defender. That did not happen, but the talent is clearly there. To quote Dan Brugler’s 2025 draft guide , The Beast : With his enforcer mentality, Reed is a blur working downhill, especially as a blitzer, and doesn’t have a passive bone in his body. His tackling technique looks different from play to play, however, and the misses add up. He has the range to cover ground and explodes into the catch point in coverage, but his streaky angles and eye discipline can leave him out of position. Overall, Reed has the athletic traits and competitive urgency NFL teams want on their rosters, but he might be stuck as a backup and special-teamer until he cuts down on costly. mistakes. He has starting potential in the post if he finds better consistency. What Reed also brings, at least theoretically, is stability. Signed through 2028 just like Craig Woodson, he is one of the few safeties under team control beyond this season. Kevin Byard and Mike Brown will both enter unrestricted free agency next year, while Dell Pettus is a restricted FA and John Saunders Jr. carrying the exclusive-rights label. Capital gains The Patriots trading Boutte for Reed also…

full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MN - AUGUST 16: New England Patriots guard Jack Conley (74) warms up before the NFL preseason game between the New England Patriots and Minnesota Vikings on August 16th, 2025, in Minneapolis, MN. (Photo by Bailey Hillesheim/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Update 8/24/2026: Patriots sign punter, O-lineman after suffering preseason injuries While news about the Kayshon Boutte trade to the Texans made headlines, the New England Patriots announced a series of roster moves. Besides making the previously-reported signings of offensive lineman Jack Conley and punter Matt Haack official, they also announced a pair of follow-up moves. To create space on the roster for Conley and Haack, the team released wide receiver Kobe Prentice and cornerback Kenneth Harris. Prentice, 22, split his college career between Alabama and Baylor. He did not hear his name called in this year’s draft, but quickly agreed to a rookie free agent deal with the Panthers. He lasted only three months in Carolina before getting waived in late July and subsequently claimed by the Patriots. The 5-foot-10, 184-pounder saw action in both preseason games and caught four of seven targets for 47. Harris, 24, came to New England as a rookie free agent in May. The Oklahoma State product, who started his college career at Arkansas State, appeared in both preseason games and was on the field for a combined 43 snaps between defense and special teams. Original story 8/24/2026: Patriots sign punter, O-lineman after suffering preseason injuries The New England Patriots welcomed two new faces to practice on Monday. Gearing up for their preseason finale against the Cleveland Browns, the team brought back offensive lineman Jack Conley and signed punter Matt Haack. No follow-up moves have been announced yet. Conley, 25, originally entered the NFL as an undrafted free agent out of Boston College last spring. The 6-foot-7, 333-pound lineman was picked up by the Patriots, who used him at both tackle and guard before signing him to their initial practice squad. Less than a month into the season, however, we was released again. Following stints with the Lions and Browns, Conley has now found his way back to Foxborough. Haack, 32, joined the league as a rookie free agent in 2017. The Arizona State product has since spent time with nine different franchises, including the Dolphins, Bills, Colts, Cardinals, Browns, Giants, Jaguars, and Broncos. Most recently, he participated in training camp with the Commanders, for whom he punted six times with an average of 44.7 yards during the preseason opener. The moves come in response to the Patriots suffering some injuries during Saturday’s preseason game against the Philadelphia Eagles. Offensive tackle Marcus Bryant exited the game after injuring his ankle in the first quarter, while punter Bryce Baringer was limited to holding duties after his second punt of the day; rookie quarterback Behren Morton took over as punter in his place. The Patriots will close out their preseason on Thursday against the Browns. Kickoff at Cleveland’s Huntington Bank Field is scheduled for 8 p.m. ET. The NFL’s roster cutdown deadline will come up three days later, on Aug. 30.

title: Instant grade for Patriots trading Kayshon Boutte to Texans
summary: The New England Patriots have traded wide receiver Kayshon Boutte, putting an end to an offseason full of rumors. The fourth-year man is headed to the Houston Texans for safety Jaylen Reed and a 2028 seventh-round draft selection. Let’s put a grade on the move. Patriots’ Kayshon Boutte trade to Texans, graded Bernd Buchmasser: Boutte […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - AUGUST 13: Kayshon Boutte #9 of the New England Patriots looks on prior to an NFL preseason football game against the Indianapolis Colts at Gillette Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New England Patriots have traded wide receiver Kayshon Boutte , putting an end to an offseason full of rumors. The fourth-year man is headed to the Houston Texans for safety Jaylen Reed and a 2028 seventh-round draft selection. Let’s put a grade on the move. Patriots’ Kayshon Boutte trade to Texans, graded Bernd Buchmasser: Boutte not making it to the end of his rookie contract with the Patriots seemed like a realistic possibility for a while now, and trading him at this point in time makes sense as well. That said, the return does look a bit underwhelming and is probably not what fans had in mind. On the other hand, Reed is an interesting if somewhat unproven prospect who is a good athlete and versatile player in the safety room. He should be an upgrade over Dell Pettus and possibly get a shot at a starting role — one Boutte would not have had in a crowded receiver room — next season. | Grade: C+ Matt St. Jean: Kayshon Boutte had big moments in New England, but the writing was on the wall about his future with the team with the additions of Romeo Doubs and A.J. Brown this offseason. Getting both a young player and a pick of any kind is a great return for a player who was likely going to be a depth receiver for one season before departing in free agency, and Kyle Williams playing the way he has in the preseason makes it a lot easier to pull the trigger on a move like this. Jaylen Reed was seen as a borderline top-150 prospect in the 2025 class, and the Patriots badly needed to bolster their depth up the middle on defense. Reed is a versatile player who fits well alongside Byard and Woodson and who allows the defense to play a variety of three-safety looks, and having him under contract for three more seasons makes him a possible starter in 2027 with Byard on a one-year deal. The 2028 seventh is a nice added sweetener as well. | Grade: A Pat Lane: The Patriots probably needed to move on from Boutte, but I don’t love the return here. In desperate need of linebacker and edge depth help, and they trade for a safety, when they have someone who has played extremely well in camp in John Saunders Jr. Maybe Reed comes in and helps out, but I don’t have high hopes. I’m also extremely concerned that the Patriots are going to see the Texans in the playoffs and this trade might come back to haunt them. I hope I’m wrong, but I was hoping they’d get more for Boutte. | Grade: C- Andrew Guindon: Drake Maye established strong chemistry with Kayshon Boutte as a downfield target. Maye had a 143.8 passer rating when targeting Boutte last season, and the pair connected on 12 of 20 deep targets during the regular season, totaling six touchdowns and 340 yards. Jaylen Reed is a fine developmental piece, especially with the recent injury to Craig Woodson, but that may come at the expense of the growth seen from John Saunders Jr. this offseason. If Boutte’s trade value in terms of draft capital was that low, it might’ve been better to hold onto him. That said, however, the receiver room grew crowded, and this should help Kyle Williams see more opportunities. Reed may also consistently be used in the box as a rotational piece with his athletic and physical player profile. | Grade: C + What do you think about the Kayshon Boutte trade? Do you like it? Do you not? Please participate in our poll and head to the comment section to discuss.

title: Patriots trade Kayshon Boutte to Texans
summary: After months of speculation, the New England Patriots have finally pulled the trigger: wide receiver Kayshon Boutte has been traded. The reigning AFC champions are sending Boutte to the Houston Texans, as first reported by The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero and since confirmed through the NFL transactions wire. In return, they are receiving safety Jaylen Reed […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - AUGUST 22: Kayshon Boutte #9 of the New England Patriots runs against the Philadelphia Eagles prior to an NFL preseason football game at Gillette Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images After months of speculation, the New England Patriots have finally pulled the trigger: wide receiver Kayshon Boutte has been traded. The reigning AFC champions are sending Boutte to the Houston Texans, as first reported by The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero and since confirmed through the NFL transactions wire. In return, they are receiving safety Jaylen Reed and a seventh-round selection in the 2028 NFL Draft. Boutte, 24, originally joined the Patriots as a sixth-round pick in 2023 out of LSU. Following a quiet rookie season with the team that saw him mostly serve as a healthy scratch, he showed some significant progress the next two seasons and developed in one of quarterback Drake Maye’s favorite receivers. In total, he ends his Patriots career having appeared in a combined 38 regular season and playoff games. Along the way, he caught 87 passes for 1,327 yards — an average of 15.3 yards per catch — and 10 touchdowns. Despite his growth and role in the offense, Boutte had been the subject of trade rumors for two straight offseasons. No trade materialized in 2025, but the circumstances changed in 2026 following the Patriots’ acquisitions of fellow wide receivers A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs. Boutte requested a trade in the spring, and now has gotten his wish. With him out of the picture, the top of the Patriots’ wide receiver group now consists of Brown, Doubs, DeMario Douglas, Mack Hollins, Kyle Williams and Efton Chism.

title: Patriots training camp recap: Injuries continue to pile up
summary: Following an off-day on Sunday after their second preseason game, the New England Patriots returned to the practice field on Monday. Here’s what went down on lower practice field in front of the New Balance Athletics Center. Setting Attire: Full pads Duration: ca. 2 hours (10:30 a.m.-12:30 p.m. ET) Conditions: Sunny, temperatures in the high 70s The Patriots […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MA - AUGUST 01: New England Patriots running back Treveyon Henderson (32) participate in drills during training camp on August 1, 2026, at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, MA. (Photo by M. Anthony Nesmith/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Following an off-day on Sunday after their second preseason game, the New England Patriots returned to the practice field on Monday. Here’s what went down on lower practice field in front of the New Balance Athletics Center. Setting Attire: Full pads Duration: ca. 2 hours (10:30 a.m.-12:30 p.m. ET) Conditions: Sunny, temperatures in the high 70s The Patriots returned to wearing full pads as work transitioned back into the red zone. Inside the 20 remains an area of focus for the team after struggling their last season — while Mike Vrabel also noted their red zone performance in the second joint practice against the Eagles was not their best. Working on the lower practice field for the first time this summer, the grass playing surface and footing was an issue for many players. “We haven’t practice there in a minute,” Rhamondre Stevenson said. “I know we were all slipping. We need to find our footing down there.” Attendance Absent: S Craig Woodson, P Bryce Baringer, WR Kobe Prentice, RB Jam Miller, RB Lan Larison, CB Kenneth Harris, OT Marcus Bryant, ED Xavier Holmes, LB Khalil Jacobs, OL Mehki Butler, OT Lorenz Metz, OL Ben Brown, DL Cory Durden Injured: RB TreVeyon Henderson Returnee: CB Christian Gonzalez, CB Channing Canada (red non-contact jersey) PUP/NFI: ED Harold Landry III, S Brenden Schooler As Mike Vrabel noted, the Patriots had a “good list of guys” working through injuries after their second preseason game. That included safety Craig Woodson, who left Thursday’s last practice early, and punter Bryce Baringer who suffered an injury in the preseason game — leading to the team signing veteran Matt Haack . With the team also adding offensive lineman Jack Conley, two corresponding moves will need to be made. With the bad footing on the field, running back TreVeyon Henderson spent time with the training staff looking at his right foot/ankle after slipping on a cut. Henderson did not return to practice. In a positive development, cornerback Christian Gonzalez returned on Monday and was a full participant. Takeaways Mondre’s minute: Ending practice with 55 seconds on the clock and the ball at the 35-yard line, it was the Rhamondre Stevenson show for the top offense. After catching a pass in the flat to beat a blitz, Drake Maye’s next pass went right back to the running back on a wheel route down the left sideline — which he hauled in over his shoulder in the back corner of the end zone with linebacker Robert Spillane tight in coverage. Even before Henderson’s injury, Stevenson continues to operate as the team’s top running back and has had an overall impressive summer. “I feel great. Probably one of my healthier training camps. My body feels fresh,” Stevenson said. Van Roten’s ramp up: After signing last week, veteran lineman Greg Van Roten did not take part of team periods in joint practices with the Eagles. On Monday, the Patriots upped Van Roten’s workload as he mixed in at both guard spots and center with the first-team offense. He impressed in 1-on-1s and also saw plays at center with Tommy DeVito’s unit, where had one low snap. Van Roten projects as New England’s top interior backup next to Ben Brown once he returns from injury. With injuries impacting the backup offensive line, the second unit largely featured: James Hudson, Darrian Dalcourt, Jacob Rizy, Joe Michalski, and Caleb Lomu from left to right. Saunders’ strong summer: Safety John Saunders Jr. added another interception to his summer total on Monday as he picked off Tommy DeVito to end the quarterback’s end-of-game drive. The pick marked Saunders fifth of the summer (four on the practice fields). Saunders’ play style is a strong fit for what the Patriots look for at the safety position and he is trending towards a 53-man roster spot. “John definitely has the most turnovers this camp. He’s been balling out of control,” fellow safety Kevin Byard said. “He’s a ballhawk.” Other notes: Eli Raridon and Kevin Byard were full participants after not being present for Saturday’s preseason game. After spending the last several weeks at guard, James Hudson was back at tackle on Monday. Hudson’s preseason tape from Saturday was better than live viewing at guard. A.J. Brown was active in the red zone and scored on a got-to-have-it play to end the day. Quintayvious Hutchins was notably in the backfield on two occasions with the second-team defense. Hutchins then was on the first-team defense side during scout team work. Preview The Patriots will hold their final training camp practice on Tuesday ahead of their preseason finale on Thursday in Cleveland. Practice will begin at 2:30 p.m. ET with executive vice president of player personnel Eliot Wolf set to speak beforehand for his annual training camp press conference.

title: Christian Gonzalez returns to Patriots practice on Monday
summary: The New England Patriots were back on the practice fields behind Gillette Stadium on Monday, and one of their most important players took part in the action. Christian Gonzalez, who had missed seven practices and both preseason games so far, made his return after a two-week injury absence. Gonzalez, 24, was last spotted at practice […]
full_text: Foxborough, MA - August 1: New England Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez at training camp at Gillette Stadium on August 1, 2026. (Photo by Jonathan Wiggs/The Boston Globe via Getty Images) | Boston Globe via Getty Images The New England Patriots were back on the practice fields behind Gillette Stadium on Monday, and one of their most important players took part in the action. Christian Gonzalez, who had missed seven practices and both preseason games so far, made his return after a two-week injury absence. Gonzalez, 24, was last spotted at practice on August 10 . Covering wide receiver Romeo Doubs 1-on-1 in an end-of-game situation, he came down hard. While he did not require immediate medical attention, he sat out the next day’s joint session with the Indianapolis Colts . Christian Gonzalez was back at practice today. A full participant in team periods. pic.twitter.com/0DOkgqoIWO — Brian Hines (@iambrianhines) August 24, 2026 While speculation arose whether or not his ongoing contract negotiations played a part in his absence, head coach Mike Vrabel repeatedly iterated that Gonzalez was not doing on-field work for physical reasons. Speaking to the media on Monday, however, Vrabel mentioned that a return was on the horizon. “I think we’re hopeful that he’ll be able to do some stuff,” he said about the Pro Bowl cornerback before practice. “He was working before the game and trying to work through the return-to-play, so we’ll see how it feels this morning.” Vrabel also was asked about Gonzalez’s readiness for the upcoming regular season opener against the Seattle Seahawks, but offered little insight. “I’m going to focus on today. I’m not ready to talk about Week 1,” he said. “We have to do everything we can to get guys ready. Each guy has to be ready individually, and then I have to find a way to make sure that the football team is ready, and that we’re conditioned and ready to go.” The Patriots’ first-round draft pick in 2023, Gonzalez has been one of the best cornerbacks in football over the last two seasons. This prompted the organization to exercise the fifth-year option in his rookie deal earlier this offseason, even though both sides continue working toward a multi-year extension that will likely best Devon Witherspoon’s new deal with the Seahawks to make him the highest-paid cornerback in NFL history.

title: 5 Patriots players highlighted by Mike Vrabel after Eagles preseason game
summary: For the second time in two preseason contests this summer, the New England Patriots decided to rest their starters against the Philadelphia Eagles on Saturday night. This, in turn, gave the depth players on the team another opportunity to showcase themselves in a game setting. Not all of them were up to the task, but […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - AUGUST 22: Kyle Dixon #83 of the New England Patriots signals as he lines up against the Philadelphia Eagles during an NFL preseason football game at Gillette Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images For the second time in two preseason contests this summer, the New England Patriots decided to rest their starters against the Philadelphia Eagles on Saturday night. This, in turn, gave the depth players on the team another opportunity to showcase themselves in a game setting. Not all of them were up to the task, but the Patriots did get some positive contributions from players who may have flown under the radar in training camp. Speaking to reporters on Monday, head coach Mike Vrabel highlighted five of those: wide receivers Efton Chism and Kyle Dixon, offensive tackle Dametrious Crownover, defensive tackle Leonard Taylor, and cornerback Kindle Vildor. “Kindle, obviously, had some very competitive snaps,” Vrabel said about the veteran defender. “Crownover, I thought, played well and tried to finish, and tried to use his length in pass protection. I thought Lenny T played well and factored and showed up. “Offensively, even just down the line, I thought Chizz did a great job when the ball found him making the plays, but also his ability to go and block force and finish. Kyle Dixon hadn’t been out there for a while. A guy that’s relatively new to the receiver position. That was really cool to see him show up in some big moments. We’re throwing the ball to Kyle Dixon — he was a baseball player not too long ago — on fourth down and he’s making a play. And then he’s trying to find the right guys to block in the run game. Those were all really interesting things.” Out of those five players, four appear to have at least somewhat realistic shots at making the 53-man roster come next week’s cutdown deadline. Vildor is competing for the fifth cornerback spot and showed some promising play over the last week-plus; Crownover would probably have projected more as a practice squad option, but might benefit from fellow backup tackle Marcus Bryant leaving the Eagles game with an injury in the first quarter; Taylor is in the mix for a rotational spot behind starting interior D-linemen Milton Williams and Christian Barmore; Efton Chism is fighting for the last spot in a deep wide receiver room. That very same room, meanwhile, will likely not feature Dixon. Despite his efforts and catching two passes for 10 yards against Philadelphia, the depth ahead of him at the position is likely to prevent him from earning a spot on the active roster come the start of the regular season. He and the rest of the players pointed out by Vrabel, as well as their other teammates, will get more chances to prove themselves this week. The Patriots will practice two times before their preseason finale in Cleveland on Thursday.

title: Patriots News: Preseason spotlights Vrabel’s fight to the depth
summary: Preseason Week 2 was entertaining. Fans tune in with the underlying questions being, “How does my team look?” and “Does this roster look like it can win enough games to get to the playoffs?” Watching a game with backups vs. backups isn’t the ideal way to answer either of those questions, to assess positional depth, […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - AUGUST 13: Tanner Arkin #84 of the New England Patriots runs with the ball prior to an NFL preseason football game against the Indianapolis Colts at Gillette Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Preseason Week 2 was entertaining. Fans tune in with the underlying questions being, “How does my team look?” and “Does this roster look like it can win enough games to get to the playoffs?” Watching a game with backups vs. backups isn’t the ideal way to answer either of those questions, to assess positional depth, or even get an overall feeling of confidence that concerns have been addressed. But here we are, assessing the team anyway and trying to extrapolate from what we saw to Week 1 and the entire season ahead. It’s what we do. Mike Vrabel knows what he’s looking for, and needs to see, from each player on the field. He knows who’s banged up already, and the Marcus Bryant injury Saturday night didn’t help. title: Who was the Saints’ breakout player vs. the Rams?
summary: The New Orleans Saints had very little to celebrate in their second preseason game of the 2026 season, suffering a 34-0 loss to the Los Angeles Rams. Still, even in a game where the offense struggled to find any rhythm, one player made the most of his limited opportunity. This week’s breakout player capitalized on […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CA - AUGUST 22: Moliki Matavao #80 of the New Orleans Saints carries the ball during an NFL preseason game between the New Orleans Saints and the Los Angeles Rams on August 22, 2026, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Greg Fiore/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The New Orleans Saints had very little to celebrate in their second preseason game of the 2026 season, suffering a 34-0 loss to the Los Angeles Rams. Still, even in a game where the offense struggled to find any rhythm, one player made the most of his limited opportunity. This week’s breakout player capitalized on his opportunity amid an uphill climb in a crowded position group: TE Moliki Matavao . The second-year tight end out of UCLA entered this past matchup with plenty to prove, and he delivered almost immediately. Matavao finished with three receptions for 34 yards, including first down conversions and a contested catch. What makes his performance even more impressive is how little time he actually spent on the field. The 23-year-old played just eight total snaps, yet he finished with a team-high 93.8 overall grade from Pro Football Focus, along with a 93.1 receiving grade. For a player competing for a roster spot in a tight end room featuring Juwan Johnson, Noah Fant and Oscar Delp, this was exactly the kind of performance Matavao needed. The Saints have plenty of experience and talent ahead of him, making opportunities difficult to come by. Unfortunately, the biggest concern coming out of the performance is Matavao’s health. He exited the game with a knee injury after making his impact felt, putting a halt to what otherwise would have been an encouraging night. The Saints will now have to wait and see whether the injury is significant. That is the most important development surrounding Matavao heading into the final preseason game. His performance against the Rams showed that he can contribute, but he needs the opportunity to continue building on it. In a preseason game filled with negatives, Matavao provided one of the few reasons for optimism. If the injury is minor, he could have another chance to make his case before roster decisions are made.

title: Saints sign former Raiders kicker Daniel Carlson
summary: The New Orleans Saints are signing kicker Daniel Carlson, per Mike Garafolo. Carlson, 31, has spent eight seasons in the NFL, earning two All-Pro honors. After being drafted in the fifth-round by the Minnesota Vikings in 2018 Carlson was released by the Vikings after two games before signing with the then Oakland Raiders and staying […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - JANUARY 04: Daniel Carlson #8 of the Las Vegas Raiders makes a field goal to take the lead in the fourth quarter of the game against the Kansas City Chiefs at Allegiant Stadium on January 04, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Ian Maule/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New Orleans Saints are signing kicker Daniel Carlson, per Mike Garafolo. The #Saints are signing two-time All-Pro K Daniel Carlson, his agents at @RangeSportsRMP tell me and @RapSheet . The former #Raiders kicker brings experience to New Orleans, which had been holding a competition between Tanner Brown and Charlie Smyth. pic.twitter.com/bTL7entvEH — Mike Garafolo (@MikeGarafolo) August 24, 2026 Carlson, 31, has spent eight seasons in the NFL, earning two All-Pro honors. After being drafted in the fifth-round by the Minnesota Vikings in 2018 Carlson was released by the Vikings after two games before signing with the then Oakland Raiders and staying with the franchise until 2025. Throughout his career, Carlson has accumulated an 86.9 field goal conversion rate along with making 95.7 percent of his PAT attempts. The signing comes after each of the Saints’ young kickers, Charlie Smyth and Tanner Brown, has been able to find consistency in training camp and preseason. Smyth has attempted just one field goal through two preseason games, missing from 52 yards. Brown went 2/2 against the Jacksonville Jaguars, with a long of 49 yards, but missed on Saturday against the Los Angeles Rams from 39 yards out. New Orleans addition of Carlson adds another leg to the battle, but also a veteran presence. The Saints have opted to go younger in all their recent kicker battles, opting for Blake Grupe over Wil Lutz, then going with Smyth over Grupe last season. With the signing of Carlson, New Orleans may be going with an established kicker rather than betting on young talent. Carlson was released from Las Vegas after the 2025 NFL season after his third season of making less than 87% of his attempts, with a poor 81.5% conversion rate in 2025. Despite his recent struggles, the veteran kicker could turn over a new leaf with a change of scenery.

title: Saints vs. Rams: Preseason Matchup Review
summary: The New Orleans Saints played their first road game of the preseason when they paid a visit to the Los Angeles Rams at SoFi Stadium on Saturday afternoon. Here’s a quick review of what was a disappointing day for the black and gold. First Quarter Stetson Bennett started the game at quarterback for LA, though […]
full_text: The New Orleans Saints played their first road game of the preseason when they paid a visit to the Los Angeles Rams at SoFi Stadium on Saturday afternoon. Here’s a quick review of what was a disappointing day for the black and gold. First Quarter Stetson Bennett started the game at quarterback for LA, though the Saints were able to force the Rams into a quick punt on the opening drive. Zach Wilson and the Saints offense didn’t fare much better, however, with an unnecessary roughness penalty against rookie guard Jeremiah Wright forcing New Orleans into a 3rd-and-long and then a punt of their own. Bennett returned and put a longer possession together, including a 4th-down conversion to Tyler Scott for 16 yards. After the Saints defense was able to halt the drive in the red zone, Harrison Mevis converted from 26 yards for the opening field goal. Trailing 3-0, a number of penalties hurt the Saints on the ensuing drive as they sought to respond. Second Quarter Facing 3rd-and-11, Wilson was intercepted by Al’Zillion Hamilton on the first play of the quarter. The Rams took advantage of the short field, with Bennett eventually running in himself for a 1-yard touchdown and a 10-0 lead. Wilson returned and converted a 3rd down with a pass to Moliki Matavao near midfield, but the black and gold were once again unable to get into scoring position. A throw intended for Kevin Austin Jr was incomplete on 4th down, forcing a Saints turnover. Bennett returned and put together an 11-play, 56-yard touchdown drive, once again running it in himself for the score and a 17-0 lead. New Orleans was fruitless on the ensuing drive, with another quick punt giving the Rams just under two minutes before the half. But Bennett took advantage yet again, with four consecutive completions for 59 yards getting LA into field goal range. Mevis converted once more from 26 yards to give the Rams a 20-0 halftime lead. Third Quarter Spencer Rattler entered the game at QB for the black and gold and started the half on an encouraging note. Rattler converted his first three throws, including a 25-yard connection with Jalen Moreno-Cropper as New Orleans drove into Rams territory. But a 78-yard drive ended in the worst fashion. Alex Cook intercepted Rattler on the goal line and returned the ball 100 yards to the house for a Rams touchdown. Both teams then went three-and-out before the Saints offense returned to the field. Rattler continued to move the ball, including a 32-yard pass to CJ Donaldson to get New Orleans into the red zone. But Ty Chandler fumbled near the goal line as he looked to find the end zone. Ty Simpson entered the game at QB for the Rams, who began their drive on their own 1-yard line. Fourth Quarter Simpson delivered a decent drive, including completions for 14 and 15 yards. But the Rams turned it over on downs near the red zone with an incomplete pass on 4th-and-2. The Saints went three-and-out again before the Rams returned and put together yet another touchdown drive. This one went 66 yards in just over five minutes, capped off with a 12-yard touchdown run by Jarquez Hunter. With under four minutes to play, Rattler moved the ball quickly as the Saints sought to avoid a shutout. But Tanner Brown missed his 39-yard field goal attempt, summing up a frustrating afternoon for New Orleans. The Rams knelt out the clock to secure a 34-0 victory. The Saints will close out the preseason on Friday in Dallas.

summary: Good morning, New York Giants fans! The Giants head into the last week of training camp with the traditional preseason matchup against the New York Jets set for Friday night. Deonte Banks opens up to The Post on making his Giants ‘reset’ count with strong preseason | New York Post He was more aggressive playing […]
full_text: Good morning, New York Giants fans! The Giants head into the last week of training camp with the traditional preseason matchup against the New York Jets set for Friday night. Deonte Banks opens up to The Post on making his Giants ‘reset’ count with strong preseason | New York Post He was more aggressive playing for defensive coordinator Wink Martindale but regressed under Shane Bowen. He seems reenergized with his new defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson. “This is fun,” Banks said. “I’m having a great time with it. I wouldn’t say I’m more confident because I feel I’m always a confident dude. I guess you can see it in my play more.” The new coaching staff “gave me a reset,’’ he said, and “let me be me.’’ Asked what that means, Banks said, “Let me go out there and play my game. Let me go out there and do what I do best.” This means increased usage as an aggressive press corner in man coverage. Which NFL Teams Have The Best Skill Position Players? Ranking All 32 Groups | FOX Sports 23. New York Giants. If the Giants are sure that both WR Malik Nabers and RB Cam Skattebo will be ready for the start of the season, this group could be ranked higher. But Nabers is still in the process of returning from a torn ACL and Skattebo is dealing with an ankle injury, so while the early reports are encouraging, the longer-term prospects are at least a little murky. Nabers is the real key because he’s far and away the Giants’ most dangerous weapon. They’ll piece together the rest of the receiving corps with Darius Slayton, Darnell Mooney, Calvin Austin and rookie Malachi Fields, and maybe what’s left of Odell Beckham Jr. New York is also hoping for a leap from TE Isaiah Likely, a John Harbaugh transport from Baltimore who often thrived in limited action behind Mark Andrews. 2026 NFL Preseason Week 2 Winners and Losers | Bleacher Report Loser: Tyrone Tracy Jr., RB, New York Giants. Over the last two weeks, Tyrone Tracy Jr.’s stock has plummeted. In the New York Giants’ preseason opener, he missed a block that allowed Minnesota Vikings safety Jay Ward to crush quarterback Jaxson Dart on a sack. In this week’s game against the Miami Dolphins, Tracy lost a fumble before halftime. He finished with six carries for 26 yards. Devin Singletary outperformed him, logging eight carries for 40 yards and a touchdown. While this may seem like an overreaction, it wouldn’t be a surprise to see the Giants move on from Tracy. Big Blue signed Narris Harris, a 6’1″, 232-pound ball-carrier who can split early-down touches with Cam Skattebo. Singletary may have played his way into the No. 3 spot. Tracy is the most dynamic pass-catcher of the group, but if the Giants believe he’s a liability in pass protection, they may cut or trade him. Feels like Arvell Reese will get a weekly #BaldyBreakdown this year . @Giants @arvxll "Step up; Blow it up". It's his mantra….just follow the red wing tip shoes. Violent and Swift. #BaldysBreakdowns pic.twitter.com/XcAG9tfxp0 — Brian Baldinger (@BaldyNFL) August 23, 2026 Projecting NY Giants’ 53-man roster entering final week of preseason | The Record Defensive line (6). Starters: D.J. Reader, Shelby Harris, Chauncey Golston. Backups: Darius Alexander, Bobby Jamison-Travis, Leki Fotu What we have seen: This is going to be the priority of the personnel department and coaching staff over the next two weeks. We’re including Golston here because he has flashed at 5-technique. Could he legit hold up as a starter in the base run defense? That’s a tough ask. I think the Giants will be looking for depth at this position. There are questions about Alexander against the run that have emerged, so until he firms up there, the Giants have more work to do. The waiver wire and/or trade market should factor here. Giants roster projection: Has Odell Beckham Jr. done enough to secure a spot? | The Athletic In: Malik Nabers, Darius Slayton, Darnell Mooney, Malachi Fields, Calvin Austin III, Braxton Berrios Out: Odell Beckham Jr., Isaiah Hodgins, Beaux Collins, Dalen Cambre, Jalin Hyatt, Xavier Gipson, Ryan Miller, Gunner Olszewski (IR) It may feel wrong to not see Beckham on the 53-man, and I don’t make the choice lightly. The fan favorite has looked sharp in camp and still clearly has something left. He made a couple Dolphins defensive backs look silly in one-on-ones and showed off some wiggle after the catch on his first reception Saturday. However, he also dropped what would have been a touchdown reception. It’s a mistake a player fighting for a spot can’t make. Berrios has made a ton of catches during camp and offers more special teams flexibility, so I ultimately decided to give him the final spot. Predicting NFL teams most likely to improve in 2026 season | ESPN.com That’s six losses that could have gone the other way against teams with winning records. The Giants held fourth-quarter leads in five of the six — and final-minute leads in three. They lost four games where they held a win probability of at least 90% in the fourth quarter. The rest of the league lost just 15 such games combined. The Giants are just the fourth team to lose four of those games in a season, joining the 2013 Buccaneers, 2009 Steelers and … 2015 Giants, who also got their head coach fired (or forced out), with Tom Coughlin’s tenure ending. Dennard Wilson’s defense will be tested to begin the campaign, as the Giants start their season against the Cowboys and Rams before the schedule briefly softens. Over the full season, the Giants project to face the league’s eighth-toughest schedule by the FPI’s algorithm, which could dampen their chances of making it to the postseason. I believe they have a legitimate shot at surprising the league and becoming a last-place team that jumps into the playoffs in 2026, but so much will depend on whether the offensive standouts stay healthy for much (or all) of the year. title: Fantasy Football 2026: Red Light! Players I’m avoiding in my drafts
summary: Welcome to Part II of my Red light/Green light series for 2026. The Green light: Players to target column dropped the other day and today I’m giving you some tough love – the players I’m trying to avoid. Draft season for redraft leagues is here at last, and if you decide to read anything to […]
full_text: Can Lamar bounce baclk? | Getty Images Welcome to Part II of my Red light/Green light series for 2026. The Green light: Players to target column dropped the other day and today I’m giving you some tough love – the players I’m trying to avoid. Draft season for redraft leagues is here at last, and if you decide to read anything to help you prep for your fantasy drafts, make it these two columns. Follow this link for my other preseason fantasy football content here at Big Blue View, including the Sleepers column: Fantasy Football Hub . Here’s what this column is all about. I’m not advocating that you cross off the players discussed. Rather, I’m trying to identify players whose current Average Draft Position (ADP) for redraft leagues is not offering good value. You’ll notice that my rankings on players listed in this column are mostly below market. This isn’t a “busts” column. It’s a listing of players who I think will underperform their current draft price, and who I probably won’t have much exposure to in redraft because I’ll pass on them at ADP. Would I draft some of them a round (or more) later than ADP? Sure, I would, although that varies by player. Sound fantasy drafting is all about value and getting good returns on your investment. Avoiding costly mistakes is part of the exercise. When you decide to click on Player X, you’re passing on others in the same range. NOTE: I’m mainly focusing on players going inside the first 130 picks (roughly, the first 11 rounds of a 12-team draft). Once you get past that point, overpaying doesn’t hurt you so much, because you’re taking players as depth and/or for potential upside if things break right, and you’re less likely to pass on difference-making players. For those who play in auction leagues, I’m looking to avoid the same players at average draft cost in that format, because I think they’ll be overpriced. ADPs listed are as of Aug. 24, 2026, are a consensus of several sites, and are for Half PPR scoring. Prior year rankings reflect Half PPR scoring, on a points per game basis, with Week 18 excluded. ADPs are a little all over the place right now – your mileage may vary. Red light players, 2026 Quarterback Lamar Jackson (ADP 33, my rank 41), Drake Maye (ADP 51, my rank 57), and Joe Burrow (ADP 54, my rank 56) are ranked as quarterbacks 2, 3, and 4, and while they’re all studs, I’m not likely to pay up for them. Each could realistically challenge to be the QB1 when this season wraps up. I get that. Maye was a strong BUY and breakout candidate for me last season, at his much lower price. That was then, this is now. I’m not willing to burn a third rounder on Jackson, and the other two are fades for me in the first five rounds. Here’s why: This is about value, supply and demand, and whatever other Econ 101 terms I can throw at you. I’m tired of talking about how deep quarterback is this season. It’s like the ocean. The opportunity cost (another econ term, sorry) is just too great in the part of the draft where these guys are going, plus quarterbacks are the biggest names in the game and the top ones almost always end up getting pushed up and taken well ahead of ADP. Meanwhile, none of these three is a sure thing to finish as a Top-4 quarterback. Lamar ran a lot less last season, even when he was healthy, and he’s missed an average of three starts to injury across the last five seasons. While I love the A.J. Brown addition, Maye faces a tougher schedule this year plus his O-line is a question mark. Burrow has played 10 games or less in half of his six seasons. Pass, at cost. I like way too many quarterbacks with ADPs from late in Round 6 through Round 11 (see the Green Light column for more on that), and I’m happy to load up on backs and receivers while these three come off the board. Others: In 2-QB leagues, it’s easy to get two decent starters this year. Again, the depth of quality at the position is nuts and I’m good with most of the QBs ranked in the Top-24. Some of the lower-ranked QBs that I like less than others ranked near them are Patrick Mahomes (coming off a torn ACL which will surely limit his scrambling), Baker Mayfield , C.J. Stroud , Cam Ward , and Bryce Young . Running Back Here’s a flex for you: I CRUSHED my red light running backs last year: Ashton Jeanty (who had an ADP around the 1-2 turn), Breece Hall, Alvin Kamara, R.J. Harvey, and Joe Mixon. Only Harvey was a value, thanks to 12 touchdowns. But don’t worry, I’m running him back for good measure. The 2026 list: Christian McCaffrey (ADP 5, my rank 8) is the headliner here, and it’s a tough call. I have CMC ranked a little behind where he’s going, and if my pick is in the middle of Round 1, I’ll probably fade him for a safer player. I don’t like taking on that much risk with my first pick, and no player offers a wider range of outcomes. McCaffrey finished as the RB1 in two of the last three seasons, sandwiched around a lost year. If he’s on the field, he’s an absolute fantasy destroyer, because he’s so devastating in the passing game. But there are legit concerns, and they go way beyond the substation and the 49ers’ ridiculous injury history. He led the NFL in touches last year (we saw how that worked out for Saquon Barkley after his league-leading 2024 workload), he’s 30, his efficiency declined in each of the last three seasons, and it wasn’t long ago that we wondered if his calf issues were going to end his career. I realize that passing on him can be costly. De’Von Achane (ADP 14, my rank 18). Achane might be my favorite player in the NFL. He’s absolutely electric and so fun to watch, and I’m a Miami fan. So this one pains me. Concerns about the change in ecosystem and the overall state of the Dolphins make it hard for me to click him at the top of Round 2. He led all backs in receptions over the last two seasons. Malik Willis is a running quarterback with a big arm and I’m assuming the receptions will fall off, as will the overall efficiency of the offense without Mike McDaniel. I hate fading him, but Achane is a little too risky for me at ADP. I don’t love Jeremiyah Love for this season. His ADP is now 26 (my rank, 37) which reflects a drop due to the high ankle sprain but it’s still way too high for me. He’s a pass at ADP for many of the same reasons I faded Jeanty last season. I love the talent, but I just don’t see him getting enough work and scoring chances (on what’s going to be a truly terrible team) for him to deliver on an ADP that’s likely to creep back up into Round 2 as the season approaches. The Cardinals still have a big crowd at running back. They paid Tyler Allgeier a lot of money and surely plan to give him a good chunk of the work. Love was a draft pick for Arizona’s future. Let someone else deal with him and an injury that could linger into September. Breece Hall (ADP 34, my rank 39). I’ll fade Hall again. I’m not taking him in Round 3 because I’m not taking ANY Jets player that high. I know he’s talented as both a runner and pass-catcher, and their O-line could be very good. I just don’t trust them to score enough TDs with a washed-up Geno Smith running the show (for now, it could get worse) and Aaron Glenn on borrowed time. I also think he’ll share the work more than you’d like. Bhayshul Tuten (ADP 54, my rank 62) and TreVeyon Henderson (ADP 51, my rank 55) are back-to-back fades for me at cost. They’re both in major timeshares and that’s not what I want in Round 4 or 5. Sure, an injury could open a pathway to an RB1 finish but that’s hard to bank on. Rhamondre Stevenson is still going to get his and is trusted by the coaching staff in big situations, and I can’t help but worry that Chris Rodriguez, who played for Liam Coen for a season at Kentucky, is going to be a season-long annoyance for those hoping Tuten is this year’s massive breakout. Others: I’m OK with most running back values in the Round 6-10 range, other than the Steelers’ duo who I’m happy to avoid, and R.J. Harvey . I’m all-in on Jonah Coleman…
author: David Hartman

title: NY Giants trade rumors: Daniel Faalele trade could be followed by more moves
summary: EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — The New York Giants are open to making trades to acquire draft capital in exchange for some surplus assets, head coach John Harbaugh said on Monday. “If we could, we’d do as much as we possibly could,” Harbaugh said. “We’d like to take advantage of the opportunities if they come up as […]
full_text: Darnell Mooney | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — The New York Giants are open to making trades to acquire draft capital in exchange for some surplus assets, head coach John Harbaugh said on Monday. “If we could, we’d do as much as we possibly could,” Harbaugh said. “We’d like to take advantage of the opportunities if they come up as much as we can.” The Giants were surprisingly able to trade guard Daniel Faalele to the Jacksonville Jaguars recently in exchange for a sixth-round pick. “It’s not too often you can trade a player for a sixth-round pick in the middle of training camp,” Harbaugh said. “But sometimes teams have needs. And Daniel’s started many games in the National Football League. So they felt like that was valuable for them. With us, Daniel was doing well for the role he was going to be playing. And yet, we have other guys that were doing well, too. “So it was a luxury for us.” The idea that the Giants had the “luxury” of trading a surplus player because they had the depth to fill in behind him is not something a Giants coach has been able to say often over the past few seasons. The Giants currently have seven selections in the 2027 NFL Draft. They are as follows, per Tankathon: Round 1 Round 2 Round 3 Round 4 (projected compensatory) Round 5 Round 6 Round 6 (from Jacksonville) With rosters needing to be trimmed from 90 to 53 players by Sunday, Aug. 30 at 6 p.m. ET, teams will be looking to fill holes with experienced players. Do the Giants have any other players they might be willing to part with? ‘We do have some guys’ “We do have some guys,” Harbaugh said. “We’re kind of deep in a few positions, and maybe that’ll happen. It doesn’t happen that often, but maybe it will.” The Baltimore Ravens, Harbaugh’s former employer, are well-known for collecting draft picks via trade or by manipulating the compensatory pick formula. That is something Harbaugh would like the Giants to copy. “Anytime you can add picks, it’s a valuable thing,” Harbaugh said. “It’s a future thing. It doesn’t seem like much now, but it’ll matter day three of the draft. It’ll be something that we’ll be happy we’ve got.” Who could those guys be? BBV’s Chris Pflum took a look at this last week after the Faalele trade. Here are some updated thoughts on players the Giants might be willing to move. WR Darnell Mooney The Giants have a logjam at wide receiver. If everyone remains healthy, it would be difficult to find roster spots for Odell Beckham Jr. and/or Dalen Cambre. Mooney, who has 309 catches in a six-year NFL career, and Darius Slayton are similar receivers who would occupy a similar role in the Giants’ offense. Slayton carries a $12.25 million base salary, while Mooney has a guaranteed base salary of just $1.215 million, making Mooney much easier to trade. RB Tyrone Tracy The view here is that the Giants should keep Tracy on their 53-man roster, regardless of the miscues he made in the two preseason games this summer. He is the closest thing the Giants have to a game-breaking running back. Still, the Giants do have Cam Skattebo, Najee Harris, and Devin Singletary. Could Tracy be deemed expendable for the right price? PK Ben Sauls/CB Paulson Adebo I put these guys together as they were the others mentioned last week by Chris. I don’t believe Sauls, who has missed far more kicks this summer than Dominic Zvada, has enough of an NFL resume to make teams want to give up assets for him. Adebo, after a slow start this summer, has been playing better and appears likely to be a starter. I don’t believe the Giants would trade him unless they received an overwhelming offer.
author: Ed Valentine

title: NY Giants’ WR Malik Nabers sheds the red jersey, takes step toward Week 1
summary: EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — After wide receiver Malik Nabers took another step forward on Monday in his recovery from a torn ACL, New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh said it is “reasonable” to think Nabers has a chance to play in the Giants’ Sept. 13 season-opener against the Dallas Cowboys. In a shells practice […]
full_text: Malik Nabers | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — After wide receiver Malik Nabers took another step forward on Monday in his recovery from a torn ACL, New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh said it is “reasonable” to think Nabers has a chance to play in the Giants’ Sept. 13 season-opener against the Dallas Cowboys. In a shells practice with little contact, Nabers was on the field participating in team drills without a red, non-contact jersey for the first time. Unofficially, Nabers took 13 reps, some in 11-on-11 and some in 7-on-7. He caught six passes from Jaxson Dart, Jameis Winston, and Brandon Allen. Nabers’ best catch was a diving play on a comeback route from Allen in front of cornerback Art Green. Nabers was barely touched during any of his 13 reps. Harbaugh stopped short of predicting that Nabers would be ready for Week 1. “I just don’t want to make any kind of statements like that. I think it’s reasonable to assume that, those are all kind of things that you can assume; it’s just based on watching the guy practice,” Harbaugh said. “The only thing I know more than you guys know is what the docs and trainers tell me as far as his rehab, and that’s doing well, he’s doing really well with that. “He’s strong, he’s in a good place, but how he gets through practice, how ready he is to play and protect himself is really based on practice, so you’re watching practice, too, and you can see it. Here are a few more takeaways from Monday. Injury updates: Theo Johnson leaves practice Tight end Theo Johnson left practice after a collision with Kayvon Thibodeaux. “I think he’s okay, didn’t get a report back that it was serious, but they’ll look at it. I haven’t talked to him since,” Harbaugh said. Starting right tackle Jermaine Eluemunor missed practice. Harbaugh said Eluemunor should return on Tuesday. Marcus Mbow took first-team reps in Eluemunor’s absence. Starting right guard Francis Mauigoa (stinger) did not practice. Mauigoa did come outside to watch part of practice. Harbaugh said Mauigoa should return to practice on Tuesday. Aaron Stinnie took first-team reps at right guard. Rookie cornerback Colton Hood returned to practice. Linebacker Jack Kelly left the field with a trainer, but returned after a few minutes to watch. He did not return to action. Leadership council pow-wow The Giants’ leadership council met on the field for quite a while after practice. That group included Jaxson Dart, Andrew Thomas, Chris Manhertz, Jordan Stout, Jameis Winston, Brian Burns, Tremaine Edmunds, and Jevon Holland. Harbaugh said that group was elected by player vote. Harbaugh said the meeting was about “in-house stuff, it really isn’t anything that I want to share.” Harbaugh said jokingly that the players had asked him for a pool table. “I told them, hey, we win games? … We might get a golf simulator if we win enough games,” Harbaugh said.

title: NY Giants facing roster cuts, regular season focus in week ahead
summary: The New York Giants enter a different phase of preseason preparations this week. Rosters have to be trimmed to the regular-season limit of 53 players by Sunday, Aug. 30 at 6 p.m. ET. With the regular season now less than three full weeks away, practices will also take on a different tone. There won’t be […]
full_text: John Harbaugh | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The New York Giants enter a different phase of preseason preparations this week. Rosters have to be trimmed to the regular-season limit of 53 players by Sunday, Aug. 30 at 6 p.m. ET. With the regular season now less than three full weeks away, practices will also take on a different tone. There won’t be any 2½-hour padded practices this week as the Giants look toward their final preseason game. Practices will be two hours in length this week, and head coach John Harbaugh said on Sunday that none will be fully padded. Healthy Giants starters played in the Aug. 15 preseason opener against the Minnesota Vikings. Those who the coaching felt needed the work played Saturday, Aug. 22 against the Miami Dolphins. The Giants have had a grueling — by modern NFL standards — training camp. Edge defender Brian Burns said last week that was part of why the team performed as well as it did in scorching heat during last Thursday’s joint practice with the Dolphins. “I ain’t gonna lie, if we didn’t practice as hard as we do, I don’t know if we would have made it through this heat,” Burns said. “And the level of competition that we practiced with today. But I feel like us practicing as hard as we do, definitely prepared us for all of this.” The last thing the Giants want to do between now and the Sept. 13 season-opener against the Dallas Cowboys is dull that competitive edge. I asked Harbaugh on Sunday about whether the idea that players could go three weeks to a month before that game without live competition will factor into the team’s decision-making. We did not directly discuss playing time in Friday’s preseason finale against the New York Jets. “Most definitely. Most definitely. You have to factor that in and consider that,” Harbaugh said. “Playing together in a game, communicating together in a game, those things are valuable things that it’s better to have some experience with before you get into the game that counts, so to speak. “So, yeah, that’s part of it, even the way we practice, what we work on, how we set up our practices. We set up our practices for the week this afternoon and what we needed to work on. That’s definitely a big part of that mindset in terms of how we organize the plays and what we work on. So, big yes to what you asked.” Harbaugh also acknowledged, in a lengthy answer, how this is a difficult week for players competing for roster spots. In his 19th season as a head coach, he said there is “a human aspect to this whole thing.” “We tell them your best dream is not too big, matter of fact it might not even be big enough,” Harbaugh said. “And you have the right to go ahead and feel free to hope for all the things that inside you might not even want to tell anybody because for fear that someone might – but if they’re not laughing at your dream then it’s not big enough either, so say it, speak it and go for it. “And these guys have really done that. I feel like they’ve really put that out there and they’ve talked to each other, they’ve committed to helping one another achieve each other’s dreams, those kinds of things we talk about in our meetings and I know they talk about amongst themselves as a group of guys.” Trimming a roster from 90 players to 53 is never a fun part of the job. “This week, to your point, is a very challenging week because there will be guys that won’t be here after this week. Now, maybe they’ll come back,” Harbaugh said. “We brought (defensive lineman) Ben (Barten) back, the defensive lineman who just got released by the Jets and came back to us again here this week. And so, I told him, I said, “Hey, we had this conversation man, I told you you’d be back here.” And I don’t know why I thought he would, but he is. So, maybe you go back to what (Former Giants owner) Wellington Mara famously said, ‘Once a Giant, always a Giant.’ I think that holds true as well. So, you become part of the team, part of the organization, part of the fabric of what it means to be a Giant, and I do think that those guys, they treasure it. “I know I’m getting a little long-winded, but how many of us that played football wouldn’t have loved to have had an opportunity to be in a football camp in the National Football League? To be invited, to get a try out even? All the not-so-good players like me would have loved that, and I tell these guys, ‘You are the very best. Every single player here in this room is a great football player.’ There is not one football player in an NFL camp who’s not a great football player. You talk about the top .0001 percent of football players, even athletes, in the world that are going to be in a football camp. But then there’s levels to that too, just like there’s levels to anything else, so within that striving to be the best you can be. But I would say everybody, every one of our guys, whether they’re here the next week or they’re not, will look back and say they did their very best, they put their best foot forward, and it’s something that they can look back on really for the rest of their life proudly.”

title: NY Giants 53-man roster projection: Tough decisions loom everywhere
summary: Up until now, our looks at the New York Giants’ potential season-opening 53-man roster have included “locks, bubble players, and long shots.” With only one preseason game remaining, we now move to a true roster projection. There will be a final projection after the third preseason game, which will be Thursday against the New York […]
full_text: Up until now, our looks at the New York Giants’ potential season-opening 53-man roster have included “locks, bubble players, and long shots.” With only one preseason game remaining, we now move to a true roster projection. There will be a final projection after the third preseason game, which will be Thursday against the New York Jets. Teams must be at the 53-man regular-season roster limit by 6 p.m. ET on Sunday, Aug. 30. OFFENSE (27) Quarterback (2) IN: Jaxson Dart, Jameis Winston Out: Brandon Allen, Jake Haener The question here is which of Allen and the recently-signed Haener the Giants choose to keep on their practice squad. Running back (4) IN: Cam Skattebo, Tyrone Tracy, Devin Singletary, Najee Harris Out: Eric Gray, Damon Bankston Yes, I am keeping Tracy despite the mistakes he made in each of the first two preseason games. Unless a running back-needy team buzzes GM Joe Schoen’s phone and offers draft capital worth accepting, I think the Giants would regret letting Tracy go. Head coach John Harbaugh was asked about Tracy during his Sunday call with New York media. “I don’t think you say, hey, a bad play or even two bad plays nullifies a whole career body of work, so to speak,” Harbaugh said. “And even in the game, he played well. He had numerous good runs, catches, pass protection pickups were good, but he had the one play that’s the one thing you don’t want to have as a running back. And in the last two games, he’s had two things you don’t want to have. “So, nobody feels worse about it than he does. I mean, he’s very conscientious, very determined guy. It matters a lot to him, so he’s beating himself up. But the rest of the plays were all good. They were all pluses. So, you don’t hold it against him. At the same time, you understand how valuable and important those things are to your football team, and he knows as well. So, it’s just a balancing act that way.” Pass protection reps from Tyrone Tracy Jr. vs. Miami in preseason Week 2. pic.twitter.com/y6ISvs0DDy — Nick Falato (@nickfalato) August 23, 2026 Fullback (1) IN: Patrick Ricard Out: Grant Finley Nothing to see here. I wonder if the Giants will keep the 6-foot-4, 281-pound Finley, like Ricard a player with defensive tackle experience, on the practice squad in hopes of turning him into Ricard 2.0. Tight end (3) IN: Isaiah Likely, Theo Johnson, Chris Manhertz Out: Tanner Conner, Thomas Fidone I really would like to keep Fidone on the roster. With Ricard able to line up at times as a blocking tight end, though, I just don’t see how to make it happen. Wide receiver (7) IN: Malik Nabers, Darius Slayton, Calvin Austin, Darnell Mooney, Malachi Fields, Braxton Berrios, Dalen Cambre Out: Odell Beckham Jr., Ryan Miller, Xavier Gipson, Isaiah Hodgins, Jalin Hyatt The decision here is between Beckham and Cambre. Today, I am choosing Cambre for his special teams ability. In my final roster prediction? Unknown. I do believe there is a scenario in which the Giants could make a trade to open a spot for Beckham. Such a deal would likely involve Mooney or Slayton — probably Mooney based on Slayton carrying a $12.25 million base salary in 2026. I also believe there is a scenario where the Giants keep six wide receivers, and neither Beckham nor Cambre makes the 53. Or, even one where they keep six, Mooney gets dealt, and Beckham gets the last spot with the Giants hoping to slide Cambre to the practice squad. Offensive line (10) IN: Andrew Thomas, Jon Runyan, John Michael Schmitz, Francis Mauigoa, Jermaine Eluemunor, Marcus Mbow, Josh Ezeudu, Aaron Stinnie, J.C. Davis, Lucas Patrick Out: Bryan Hudson, Evan Neal, Ryan Schernecke, Jake Kubas, Jarrod Gray (International Exemption), Brendan Jaimes I think 10 offensive linemen is heavy, but after the way he played on Saturday I doubt there is any chance the Giants can get Davis through waivers to the practice squad. The only way to ensure keeping him is to have him on the 53-man roster. I don’t know you justify cutting any of the other guys. Patrick has been the No. 2 center since the spring, and there is zero indication the Giants want to change that. Mbow is the swing tackle. Ezeudu offers them guard/tackle flexibility on the right side, and has earned a spot. Stinnie is a plug-and-play veteran who can step in at either guard. DEFENSE (23) Defensive line (6) IN: D.J. Reader, Darius Alexander, Shelby Harris, Chauncey Golston, Leki Fotu, Josh Tupou Out: Bobby Jamison-Travis, Zacch Pickens, Anquin Barnes Jr., Marlon Davidson I don’t like the idea of exposing Jamison-Travis to waivers. I do think there is a better chance Jamison-Travis gets through waivers to the practice squad than Davis, simply based on the amount of NFL film available on both players. Still, I have Tupou making the roster ahead of Jamison-Travis, but I could be convinced to flip that. Off-ball linebacker (4) IN: Arvell Reese, Tremaine Edmunds, Micah McFadden, Jack Kelly Out : Darius Muasau, Zaire Barnes, Chandler Martin, Anfernee Orji I do wonder if the Giants will find space for one of Martin, Barnes, or Muasau as a special teams player. Here, I did not. You can certainly make an argument that I should have. Edge defender (3) IN: Brian Burns, Abdul Carter, Kayvon Thibodeaux Out : Khalid Kareem, Trace Ford, Caleb Murphy Golston might end up starting on the defensive line. I have considered him as the fourth edge defender. If he is taking a heavy load of defensive line snaps, perhaps there is a spot open for one of Kareem, Ford, or Murphy. If that happens, I don’t know who would lose a job at another position. Cornerback (6) IN: Paulson Adebo, Greg Newsome II, Colton Hood, Dru Phillips, Deonte Banks, Art Green Out: Korie Black, Nic Jones, Ugo Amadi I considered keeping Black, but seven cornerbacks just seems like one too many. Especially since Ar’Darius Washington can drop down and play cornerback if needed. Safety (4) IN: Jevon Holland, Tyler Nubin, Ar’Darius Washington, Jason Pinnock Out : Elijah Campbell, Beau Brade, Raheem Layne, J.T. Woods I would like to keep Campbell, a veteran special teams player, I just don’t know how. SPECIAL TEAMS (3) IN: Jordan Stout (punter) , Dominic Zvada (placekicker) , Ben Mann (long-snapper) Out: Ben Sauls (placekicker) No surprises here. Zvada over Sauls has been the call for a while. Final thoughts First of all, yes, I know that 27 offensive and 23 defensive players is an imbalance. I don’t like it, but that is how it worked out. My final projection will probably be slightly different. As of today, though, I am not willing to drop Cambre or any of the reserve offensive linemen. Many things can happpen. Injuries, trades, players shining against the New York Jets on Friday and winning spots. Me being wrong. There are a lot of possibilities. This exercise has been hard. Really hard. And decisions across the roster can be questioned. That is actually a good thing. It indicates that there are NFL-caliber players who won’t make the team.
