title: 3rd preseason game ‘will be a big, important game’ for 49ers 2nd year player
summary: The San Francisco 49ers are slowly starting to see some of their players come back, with the running back position finally getting healthy again. The returns of Christian McCaffrey, Kaelon Black, and Jordan James allowed for Sunday night’s trade with the New Orleans Saints, where the 49ers sent running back Zamir White for linebacker Deion […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WA - JANUARY 17: Jordan James #29 of the San Francisco 49ers rushes during the NFC Divisional Playoff game against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field on January 17, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. The Seahawks defeated the 49ers 41-6. (Photo by Michael Zagaris/San Francisco 49ers/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers are slowly starting to see some of their players come back, with the running back position finally getting healthy again. The returns of Christian McCaffrey, Kaelon Black, and Jordan James allowed for Sunday night’s trade with the New Orleans Saints, where the 49ers sent running back Zamir White for linebacker Deion Jones. This past Thursday, we got an early look at Black in action, and he impressed in a multitude of ways. While he only had 33 yards on eight carries, Black had several impressive runs with his vision and ability to find holes, while also holding up very well in pass protection. We have yet to see his running mate, Jordan James, in the preseason, as a rib injury on the first day of training camp held him out for the past few weeks. But, the 2025 fifth-round pick finally returned to practice on Saturday, and is now set up for a big role in San Francisco’s third preseason game against the Las Vegas Raiders, according to offensive coordinator Klay Kubiak. “Really happy to see Jordan back out there,” Kubiak said on Sunday. “We’ve loved Jordan. We’ve been excited about him. It’s just been unfortunate not having him on the field as much, but he looks good. He’s in really good shape. I think seeing other young players get out there and have success makes him hungry. He knows, ‘I’ve got to get out there. I’ve got to show what I can do.’ Following Black’s strong performance in Week 2 of the preseason, James is ready for his moment to shine. “Seeing Kaelon get some of those reps, he’s stepped up,” Kubiak continued about James. “He’s had two really good practices, in my opinion. So, we’re excited about his future. I’m going to say the same thing I said about Kaelon, though. He’s got to keep getting better. He’s got to keep going out there and practicing. Stay healthy. This will be a big, important game for him. He’s going to get a lot of reps. I want to see how he looks in the game and just keep going.” While the 49ers have a couple of unproven guys behind Christian McCaffrey in their running back room, they’re in a much better shape than they were last week with all of the injuries. “Yeah, I don’t want to slight the guys who were out there at all. The guys who were out there were battling, competing, and did a heck of a job,” Kubiak said about the running back room with injuries. “But we drafted these guys for a reason, these young backs who we’re real excited about. It’s good to have them out there healthy. I was really pleased with the guys who were out there too and who were working and getting the most out of those guys. But these are the guys we wanted here from the draft that we think have a lot of ability. And so, just got to keep stacking days with those guys.” James should get a ton of opportunity in the final preseason game, although Black’s availability and play seems to have catapulted him up the depth chart.

title: Jed York reportedly responded to an ad on a known prostitution site
summary: San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York was arrested in East Palestine, Ohio, over the weekend and found guilty of two misdemeanor charges. He was arrested sometime Sunday in East Palestine before posting a $5,000 bond. […]
full_text: Jed York, principal owner and chief executive officer of the San Francisco 49ers at Celtic Park, Glasgow. Picture date: Sunday May 10, 2026. (Photo by Andrew Milligan/PA Images via Getty Images) | PA Images via Getty Images San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York was arrested in East Palestine, Ohio, over the weekend and found guilty of two misdemeanor charges. According to WKBN News, York pleaded no contest Monday morning to misdemeanor charges of disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools. He was arrested sometime Sunday in East Palestine before posting a $5,000 bond. 49ers owner arrested in East Palestine https://t.co/TZehJeTb4X — WKBN 27 First News (@WKBN) August 24, 2026 According to court records, York was sentenced to two days in the Columbiana County Jail, which he’d serve concurrently with a credit for a day served. York was also ordered to pay $1,150 in fines. Court orders show that $160 seized will be forfeited to the Mahoning Valley Human Trafficking Task Force as part of the agreement. He did get his phone back. Kyle’s update, 11:00 a.m. PT: This story isn’t going anywhere. According to The California Post , York responded to an ad on a known “prostitution website in Columbiana County, Ohio, and arranged to have sexual activity with the female in exchange for $140. The location was a trailer park in East Palestine, Ohio. From there, York was taken into custody after law enforcement from the Mahoning Valley Human Trafficking Task Force determined that York had in his possession his cellular device, which was used to arrange the criminal act.” So, York’s cell phone was his criminal tool in this case. Without trying to speculate, the fact that authorities donated the money to a Human Trafficking Task Force cannot be good. This news channel says it’s prostitution-related : The State of Ohio amended the one count of engaging in prostitution to a disorderly conduct charge before York pleaded no contest on Monday. He was also convicted of possessing criminal tools. ABC Chicago said the same, saying the original arrest was for engaging in prostitution. York could have spent up to two months in jail had he been convicted of that charge. Because of the amendment, York only has to serve a couple of days in jail. If you’re wondering why York was in the area, he went to Cardinal Mooney High School in the Youngstown area. York was specifically arrested at the “Wheat Hill Mobile Home Community.” Here’s the Ohio state definition of possessing criminal tools : (A) No person shall possess or have under the person’s control any substance, device, instrument, or article, with purpose to use it criminally. (B) Each of the following constitutes prima-facie evidence of criminal purpose: (1) Possession or control of any dangerous ordnance, or the materials or parts for making dangerous ordnance, in the absence of circumstances indicating the dangerous ordnance, materials, or parts are intended for legitimate use; (2) Possession or control of any substance, device, instrument, or article designed or specially adapted for criminal use; (3) Possession or control of any substance, device, instrument, or article commonly used for criminal purposes, under circumstances indicating the item is intended for criminal use. (C) Whoever violates this section is guilty of possessing criminal tools. Except as otherwise provided in this division, possessing criminal tools is a misdemeanor of the first degree. If the circumstances indicate that the substance, device, instrument, or article involved in the offense was intended for use in the commission of a felony, possessing criminal tools is a felony of the fifth degree. Don’t be surprised if the NFL steps in and disciplines York. The NFL’s personal conduct policy applies to all league personnel, not just the players. We’ll continue to update this story as more information is released.

title: Projecting the 49ers’ practice squad: Which players will the team keep around?
summary: The San Francisco 49ers need to have their roster cut down to 53 players by Sunday, August 30, at 3:00 p.m. PT. It’s a big week of practice with one final preseason game to go to determine whether players are good enough to make the roster, have flashed enough to keep on the practice squad, […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 13: Larry Worth III #47 of the San Francisco 49ers celebrates after completing a sack during the fourth quarter of a preseason NFL football game against the Tennessee Titans at Levi's Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers need to have their roster cut down to 53 players by Sunday, August 30, at 3:00 p.m. PT. It’s a big week of practice with one final preseason game to go to determine whether players are good enough to make the roster, have flashed enough to keep on the practice squad, or aren’t worthy of keeping around. A practice squad has 16 spots, plus an additional spot reserved for an International Player Pathway Program. Rookies or second-year players can hold ten spots. An additional six can have unlimited accrued NFL experience. Offense I think the 49ers end up keeping three quarterbacks, so there’s no need to keep one on the practice squad. Kurtis Rourke will serve as the scout team quarterback. I doubt the team risks losing him on waivers, given how important the position is and that Rourke will be Brock Purdy’s backup after this season. Running back is a bit trickier. Isaac Guerendo doesn’t make this guessing game any easier. Sincere McCormick sticks on the practice squad, but that could change, depending on Guerendo’s health. No need to keep a fullback. That’s what tight ends are for. I’m projecting Brayden Willis and Khalil Dinkins to make the practice squad. Willis has lined up at fullback 10 times through three preseason games. Wide receiver is tricky. Jordan Watkins is not guaranteed to make the roster. Neither is Christian Kirk. As of today, I’m listing Watkins on the practice squad, with Malik Turner and Wesley Grimes. The team is giving Kirk the benefit of the doubt and is unwilling to risk losing him, since he would immediately become an unrestricted free agent. You’ll need a scout team offensive line to go along with the skill players. Some of the backups can play, but not all of them. Don’t be surprised if this list includes multiple players who aren’t on the roster today. For now, I think it’ll be Enrique Cruz Jr., Drake Nugent, and Connor Colby. Isaac Alarcon sticks as the International player. Defense Defense always gets the short end of the stick. Here, the 49ers believe in a pair of young defensive tackles, as well as a veteran pass rusher — who will be elevated until Mykel Williams is activated. At linebacker, keeping Larry Worth around and continuing to develop him should be part of the plan. It’s not as easy to pick a name in the secondary. But we’ll roll with Jakob Robinson at nickel and bring Darrell Luter Jr. back once he clears waivers. Lastly, Jalen Stroman sticks at safety. Here’s the projected practice squad: Sincere McCormick Brayden Willis Khalil Dinkins Jordan Watkins Malik Turner Wesley Grimes Enrique Cruz Jr. Drake Nugent Connor Colby Sebastian Valdez Bryson Eason Ogbo Okoronkwo Larry Worth III Jakob Robinson Darrell Luter Jr. Jalen Stroman Isaac Alarcon

title: Klay Kubiak highlights where Kaelon Black was ‘impressive’ in preseason debut
summary: San Francisco 49ers offensive coordinator Klay Kubiak spoke about rookie running back Kaelon Black’s performance last Thursday. Black left enough of an impression in pass protection for Brock Purdy to mention it to the media. Kubiak said, “That was just as impressive. He was on it from the second snap of the game. They brought […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CA - AUGUST 20: Kaelon Black #26 of the San Francisco 49ers rushes during the game against the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium on August 20, 2026 in Inglewood, California. The 49ers defeated the Chargers 41-17. (Photo by Michael Zagaris/San Francisco 49ers/Getty Images) | Getty Images San Francisco 49ers offensive coordinator Klay Kubiak spoke about rookie running back Kaelon Black’s performance last Thursday. Black left enough of an impression in pass protection for Brock Purdy to mention it to the media. Kubiak said, “That was just as impressive. He was on it from the second snap of the game. They brought a blitz, and he was on it, and he was stout. Not surprising, though. He’s a sharp young man. He’s in his playbook. He’s very coachable. Bobby T[urner] got him on the right page. He’s just got to keep going, keep getting better.” The eye test looked different with Black running the football compared to what we saw from the runners in Week 1. Black created on his own and was elusive enough to work his way back to the line of scrimmage despite multiple linemen missing their blocks. He showed plenty of promise. Kubiak said, “I loved how he ran. He really brought kind of a spark to our offense. He’s a guy who you don’t have to block it perfect every time. He’s going to muscle his way through for five, six yards, but he’s got good speed to burst and get some explosive runs. I thought he did a really good job. His first time in NFL action, the moment wasn’t big for him. He didn’t blink. He was ready to go. Love his development. Love where he’s at, but he needs to keep getting better, too, and stacking days. I think we’re going to have a good player on our hands down the road, but he’s got to keep pushing himself every day.” Black made an impact in the passing game without catching a pass. During OTAs and the early parts of training camp, Black was active as a wide receiver. The 49ers would attempt to isolate him against linebackers, using Black’s speed as a weapon. According to Kubiak, that’s the next step in Black’s development: “Yeah, we’re definitely trying to get him involved, definitely trying to get him some of those reps whether it’s choice routes, option routes, things out of the backfield that we ask our backs to do consistently. That’s a big part of his development, for sure, and getting the comfort and timing with the quarterback. I thought he’s done a nice job here in these couple practices in that area. But again, it’s the same thing. It’s just more reps, more growth, but he takes that jump and continues developing the pass game. We’re excited about him.” Kubiak also mentioned how he was excited to have Jordan James back in the fold. He didn’t want to slight the other running backs who have been out there, but Kubiak said, “we drafted these guys for a reason.” The battle for RB2 is a competition that’s unlikely to be solved by Week 1. That rotation will continue throughout the year.

It’s just a matter of how soon he’s ready to play in a game after not playing football for more than seven months.” 49ers OC Klay Kubiak […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CA - DECEMBER 14: George Kittle #85 of the San Francisco 49ers celebrates a touchdown with Christian McCaffrey #23 of the San Francisco 49ers during a NFL game against the Tennessee Titans on December 14, 2025 at Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara, CA. (Photo by Matthew Huang/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images 49ers activate Kittle from PUP list; McCaffrey returns to practice “Sunday’s move means Kittle will, barring a setback, definitely be back at some point in the first four weeks. It’s just a matter of how soon he’s ready to play in a game after not playing football for more than seven months.” 49ers OC Klay Kubiak shares key updates ahead of Raiders preseason game “San Francisco 49ers offensive coordinator Klay Kubiak spoke with reporters after Sunday’s training camp practice. Here’s everything he had to say.” Christian McCaffrey, George Kittle provide ‘energy’ in return to 49ers practice “Obviously, when you don’t practice, the way the media works now is, (it’s a) firestorm,” McCaffrey said. “But this was kind of part of the plan from the jump, to ramp up pretty big, get nine, 10 practices in. Then, come back down and then ramp back up so we’re fresh for the duration.” 49ers’ George Kittle practices Sunday for first time since Achilles injury (paywall) “The five-time All-Pro and seven-time Pro Bowler worked through individual drills but did not play any snaps during the team 11-on-11 periods as he eased back in Sunday.” 49ers’ Christian McCaffrey returns to practice after 2-week absence: ‘I feel fresh’ (paywall) “Both McCaffrey and tight end George Kittle were in uniform for Sunday’s practice, Kittle’s first since tearing an Achilles tendon Jan. 11. Though he’s easing back in and was held out of everything but individual drills, McCaffrey took part in a handful of 11-on-11 snaps and carried the ball three times. He broke one of those carries to the right for a roughly 25-yard gain. “I feel fresh,” he said. “It’s good to be back out there.”…Black had another impressive practice, breaking at least two big runs. His hard-charging style, however, also created a friendly fire moment when he plowed into the back of center Jake Brendel, knocking the 300-pounder face-first to the ground. Brendel got up and took part in the next play…..All eyes were on Kittle on Sunday, but fellow tight end Jake Tonges was prolific for the second straight day. That included back-to-back sideline catches on throws from Purdy. If Kittle couldn’t take part in the Week 1 opener, Tonges likely would start at tight end.” 49ers trade for veteran linebacker who played under Kyle Shanahan and Raheem Morris “He spent his rookie season in Atlanta under offensive coordinator Kyle Shanahan. Raheem Morris was coaching on the offensive side of the ball for the majority of his tenure when Jones was there. However, there was overlap in 2020, when Morris was the defensive coordinator alongside the interim coach. That was in 2020. So Shanahan and Morris have both seen Jones during 100+ tackle seasons…With Martin suffering a hamstring injury late Thursday, it could also be the team telling us that Martin’s injury is severe. If you’re on the roster bubble, the last thing you want to see is your team trade for the position you play. One of Jones’ calling cards has been as a pass rusher. As we’ve seen, that is something Raheem Morris is going to do early and often with his inside linebackers. Jones pressured the quarterback on 23.1% of his rushes last season with Tampa Bay. No matter where he’s been, Jones’ pressure percentage has been above league average. And even as he’s gotten longer in the tooth, Jones has still recorded multiple “hustle stops,” which is when a defender makes a tackle from 20 yards away. He had two last season in 20 snaps. That’s a sign that his speed remains above average.” 49ers training camp practice 16: Quick hits “Jacob Cowing also drew some attention during Sunday’s practice. “Jacob Cowing looking sharp in 1-on-1 drills. Finishing camp strong,” Tafur reported. Cowing is competing for a spot in a crowded wide receiver room, so strong practices at this point in camp can only help his case. Mike Evans was another player to watch. The veteran wide receiver left practice and took off his pads, appearing frustrated. Jennifer Lee Chan reported that the situation could be injury-related, although there was no immediate indication of the severity.” The Good and Not So Good from Day 16 of 49ers Camp: Kittle and McCaffrey Return “Black isn’t a hybrid slot receiver like McCaffrey, but he can catch passes, and the 49ers will throw to him. He’s a three-down player. But the best thing he does is run the ball, particularly between the tackles. He has the speed to get to the perimeter, but he wants to run downhill. He hits holes between the tackles with zero hesitation, and can squirt through the tiniest of creases. In that sense, he reminds me of Frank Gore. At one point, he took a helmet-to-helmet hit from Fred Warner on a pass over the middle, stayed down for a second, shook his head, ran back to the huddle, lined up in the backfield, took the handoff and exploded around the left side for a 20-yard gain. He’s so tough….[James Thompson Jr] is probably the second-best defensive tackle on the team after Osa Odighizuwa. Thompson Jr. is a terrific run defender who actually can rush the passer as well. Today, he lined up with the starters and beat Carver Willis to “sack” Purdy. Whoever scouted this guy deserves a promotion….[Raheem Morris] is trying to install so many new things, and he doesn’t currently have the personnel to pull off any of them. To be fair, his players do a good job aggressively breaking on intermediate passes over the middle, but they can’t seem to stop anything else. Today, Morris kept using a defense with five defensive linemen, one linebacker and five defensive backs. And it couldn’t stop anything — not the run or the pass. On third down, he wants to be aggressive and blitz. This just leaves his subpar safeties one on one against superior players. And if the blitz doesn’t get to the quarterback right away, which it usually doesn’t, the defense gives up huge catches.”

title: Cam Ward showed marginal growth vs. Seahawks in preseason Week 2
summary: The Tennessee Titans defeated the Seattle Seahawks 19-16 in Week 2 of the NFL preseason, but it wasn’t exactly a convincing performance. The Titans’ first-team offense only managed three points versus the Seahawks’ backups, and the starting defense was dismantled for two explosive touchdowns by Seattle’s second-team offense. We’re measuring Cam Ward’s progress during the […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 13: Cam Ward #1 of the Tennessee Titans looks to pass against the San Francisco 49ers in the first half at Levi's Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Tennessee Titans defeated the Seattle Seahawks 19-16 in Week 2 of the NFL preseason, but it wasn’t exactly a convincing performance . The Titans’ first-team offense only managed three points versus the Seahawks’ backups, and the starting defense was dismantled for two explosive touchdowns by Seattle’s second-team offense. We’re measuring Cam Ward’s progress during the preseason. The sophomore No. 1 overall pick played an improved game compared to his preseason debut against the San Francisco 49ers last weekend. Ward’s marginal growth could have been significantly more obvious had his teammates capitalized on some missed opportunities. Ward completed 8-of-12 passing attempts for 69 yards. He was sacked once. His completion percentage was much better than the below 50% he was versus the 49ers, and two drops could have had him finish his night 10-of-12 instead. First, Carnell Tate dropped a pass near the sideline. It was a fade route that would have been a difficult catch, but Tate got his hands on the ball. More glaring, tight end Gunnar Helm totally wasted a beautiful off-script throw by Ward by failing to get his feet in-bounds despite having enough room to do so. That’s not to indicate Ward was perfect. An issue of inaccuracy arose when he airmailed a ball for Tate that had enough open space to be a completion. He also carelessly fumbled the ball near the sideline and was fortunate to see it roll out of bounds. Ward’s performance won’t draw much attention. He didn’t throw any touchdowns, lead any touchdown drives, nor did he commit any turnovers. Still, had Tate and Helm come up with receptions they should have made, the box score and narrative could have looked very different, and maybe the Titans get into the end zone during one of those possessions. Ward was better versus the Seahawks than he was versus the 49ers, and that’s how progress is measured.

full_text: The Daily Slop – 25 August 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links Articles Cover 4 Quarters Sonny Styles is already proving the hype in Washington is real This play from Styles drew the ire of fans everywhere, who immediately clamored, “Bust!” “Played like a fiddle”, and other pejorative statements. All of this outcry proved the maxim “It’s better to stay silent and be thought a fool than to speak and remove all doubts” is as true as it was when the statement was first introduced in Proverbs 17:28. On the 50-yard Joshua Dobbs TD, just a complete defensive breakdown by the #Commanders The rookie Joshua Josephs gets faked amongst other defenders. Great play by Lions. Also, Will Harris wasn’t on the same page as well. pic.twitter.com/qtnYCWGRby — brandon (@JayDanielsMVP) August 23, 2026 As the MIKE linebacker, Styles is fitting the C-gap here as his responsibility. View Link you can see he keeps his eyes on his gap responsibility until he realizes that the defensive end (#48) has completely blown his responsibility here too. It’s a read option. The defensive end is supposed to keep his eyes on the ball. #48 simply doesn’t, and Dobbs makes him pay for the mental lapse. Ideally, #48 should “squeeze and pop”, where he shuffles down the line of scrimmage to discourage the give to the running back (squeeze) before “popping” back to the quarterback by flattening out his path to interfere with his pathing. [I]t’s not a scrape exchange because nobody is filling in for Styles’ fit on this play. If there were another safety in the box, I could theoretically buy it, provided he filled in the C-gap for Styles. This play is from a 2-high shell, so the safety is deep and isn’t in the primary run fit. For my money, this touchdown lies squarely on the defensive end and the safety. The defensive end is a fifth-round rookie, so I expect some mistakes like that. The safety #3 is 30-year-old veteran Will Harris, who…I’m going to be honest: I’m not sure what he’s doing. [Styles] doesn’t give any ground to the tight end and is in prime position in his gap to take on the rusher. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Bullock’s Film Room (subscription) Commanders give glimpse of Daronte Jones’ defensive scheme vs Lions [ F rom BiB : The excerpt below describes the defensive play you can see in the tweet from Bullock at the bottom ] [I]t’s important to remember that in preseason, nobody wants to show anything resembling their actual schemes. However, I felt that we got a little more of a hint as to what the schemes might look like in the regular season, especially on defense. It happened early on too. On just the second snap of the game, we got a glimpse of what might be to come from Daronte Jones and his defense this year. Normally when a cornerback blitzes, you see multiple other defenders on the line of scrimmage bail out to make up the numbers in coverage, but not here. The Commanders rush their entire front five, including the three interior defensive lineman and the two edge rushers at outside linebacker. With Robertson joining them, that gives Washington six defenders blitzing, leaving just five in coverage. Having five defenders in coverage is rare, but what’s even more unique is that they don’t play man coverage behind the six-man blitz. Most offenses will associate a blitz with man coverage, because zone coverages typically rely on multiple extra defenders to cover every area on the field effectively. But the Commanders still play what appears to be zone coverage here. The safeties rotate post-snap, with Jeremy Reaves working to a deep outside third, replacing Robertson’s role in coverage. Nick Cross rotates to the deep middle of the field to play the middle third. Cornerback Mike Sainristil on the other side of the field acts like he’s playing man coverage but is actually responsible for the deep third on his side of the field. Having three deep zone defenders isn’t unusual, but typically you have four underneath defenders as part of a Cover-3 zone, or at least three underneath defenders as part of a fire zone blitz scheme. But here, Washington has just two underneath defenders in linebackers Sonny Styles and Frankie Luvu. This is a tough blitz on them because they have a huge amount of ground to try and cover underneath. But the Commanders will argue that the pressure is actually the coverage. By sending six rushers, the offense has to keep at least one eligible receiver in to protect, or they’ll be overrun. You can see on this play that both tight ends stay in to chip while the running back is slow to release as he checks protection inside. With three eligible receivers helping in protection before releasing underneath, that leaves just two receivers running routes down the field. That buys time for those six rushers to try and get to the quarterback. Rookie outside linebacker Joshua Josephs does a great job darting inside the left tackle and creating immediate pressure, which actually forced a holding call from the left tackle to prevent the sack. The quarterback feels that pressure and has to try and scramble away from it, but he has no idea Robertson is there. He runs to his left and hits a brick wall as Robertson is there to make the sack and knock the ball out. From there, it’s a fight of effort and desire to see who can jump on the ball and recover the fumble. Josephs shows great effort as he’s the one that sticks with it and fights hardest to win the ball, recovering it in the end zone for a touchdown. That was just a glimpse of what Daronte Jones has in mind for this defense. Remember, nobody wants to show anything significant at this point in the year, especially the Commanders with two new coordinators that have an advantage of opponents not knowing what schemes they’re about to face. So for Jones to show this blitz tells you it’s a very vanilla blitz for them. While the Commanders were looking to stay vanilla as possible, I felt like we got to see a small glimpse of what defensive coordinator Daronte Jones has planned for Washington's defense this year. I broke it down: https://t.co/aJbDglmEyN pic.twitter.com/hmdkGgxUew — Mark Bullock (@MarkBullockNFL) August 24, 2026 Last Man Standig Dan Quinn didn’t like the ‘disarray’ in preseason Game 2. Now the Commanders get back to work Jacory Croskey-Merritt was not formally declared out of the preseason game because of injury, but he seemed to pull up at the end of a catch-and-run in Thursday’s open practice. The groin injury isn’t considered significant, I’m told, but “Bill” is the latest player the Commanders aren’t rushing back into action after an injury. Quinn said Croskey-Merritt joins a “number of guys that we hope to get into practices next week,” following a Saturday evaluation. Croskey-Merritt, Rachaad White (hamstring) and Jeremy McNichols (quad), Washington’s top three experienced backs, are all working through some form of injury. White went through individual drills Monday after sitting out practices last week. That leaves two rookies, sixth-round pick Kaytron Allen and UDFA Robert Henry Jr., along with recent signee Craig Reynolds, as the known available options against Baltimore. For more from Ben Standig, click here Sports Illustrated 3 Things We Learned From Commanders’ Added Day 15 Training Camp Practice 3. Injuries Are Still Reshaping Position Battles More than anything, Washington is still evaluating several positions while key players remain unavailable or limited. Center is the perfect example and a glaring weakness now as well . Quinn said Nick Allegretti is still not ready , while Matt Gulbin will move back exclusively to center this week after getting some work at guard. Hearing Quinn say Washington still has work to do moving forward feels like someone telling me…

full_text: DETROIT, MI - AUGUST 22: Washington Commanders wide receiver Jaden Bradley (86) stretches to try to catch a pass against Detroit Lions corner back Keith Abney II (28) during the third quarter of an NFL preseason football game between the Washington Commanders and the Detroit Lions on August 22, 2026 at Ford Field in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Scott W. Grau/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The preseason is almost over, with one more joint practice and game to go against the Baltimore Ravens this week. The Washington Commanders visited the Detroit Lions for the second game, and we got a one-series look at Jayden Daniels, then some extended time with the backups. There were some bottom of the roster guys that stood out like WRs Jaden Bradley and Nick Nash. Sixth-round pick Kaytron “Fatman” Allen takes the lead as top preseason back. Is there really a competition for QB3? Two defenders make some noise at the bottom of the depth chart. Mason/Brennan Preseason Hype! Award History Former Washington Redskins 6th-round draft pick Colt Brennan was a star in college at the University of Hawaii and brought that hype with him to Washington in 2008. Brennan was a cult sensation during his brief time here, and was the inspiration for the annual Mason/Brennan Preseason Hype! Awards here at Hogs Haven. Brennan passed away at the way-too-young age of 37 five years ago . This was started as a tongue-in-cheek tribute to players that fans push to the moon before they play a snap, or after one great performance in the preseason. But it also puts the focus on some of the unheralded players who fans hype up and have a fighter’s chance at making Washington’s roster. Colt Brennan was a great college player that lit up the preseason, but injuries and other issues saw him flame out in the NFL early. RIP Colt and thanks for the inspiration. The Rules: 1. Player must have been drafted late or signed by the Redskins as an undrafted free agent. Players that have only been on other teams practice squads that are signed by the team are also eligible. 2. A player that has been on the team for several years is still eligible if most of that time has been spent on the practice squad, inactive, or with very limited productivity/time The Keenan “the Barbarian” Robinson Amendment: only 6th-round draft picks or later for their first two years in the league. The Nominees: Jaden Bradley, WR – UDFA (2026) – Jaden Bradley was an early camp hype favorite, getting talking about by coaches, reporters, and fans. He had a decent first game, but Bradley got national attention with a great one-handed catch with his other arm locked up for a DPI penalty. If you get Baldy saying you had the catch of the week, you’ve got the right kind of preseason hype! what a catch 😱 pic.twitter.com/fFklIWffKZ — NFL (@NFL) August 22, 2026 come for the catch, stay for the reactions pic.twitter.com/KxKAtDf2wb — Washington Commanders (@Commanders) August 24, 2026 . @Commanders @Lions UDFA Jaden Bradley with the best catch of week 2 in preseason. Great way to get noticed pic.twitter.com/sNxIVH0r2A — Brian Baldinger (@BaldyNFL) August 23, 2026 Nick Nash, WR – FA (2026) – Who the heck is Nick Nash, and where did he come from? That was the question a lot of people were asking when Athan Kaliakmanis threw a bomb to him down the sideline for 55 yards. He had another catch for 7 yards on the same drive, but Nash’s big catch got him on the hype radar. Nick Nash making plays ‼️ 📺 #WASvsDET @wusa9 pic.twitter.com/Vz5jtyKZis — Washington Commanders (@Commanders) August 22, 2026 Kaytron “Fatman” Allen, RB – 6th round (2026) – It looked like rookies Kaytron Allen and Robert Henry Jr. were in a competition for a roster spot last week, but Fatman stepped up while Henry disappeared. The Commanders didn’t run much vs the Lions, but Allen was the lead back and was the only one who could find some room to run against Detroit’s defense. Give Kaytron Allen an inch and he'll take a mile pic.twitter.com/36UJUETk8H — Martenzie Johnson (@10zJohnson) August 23, 2026 Kaytron Allen's numbers weren't big today — 10 carries for 30 yards. But those were tough yards; escaped issues in the backfield; good vision. And his blitz pickup on the deep pass to Jalen Bradley was textbook. — John Keim (@john_keim) August 22, 2026 Athan Kaliakmanis, QB – 7th round (2026) – Jayden Daniels was only in for a 3-play series, and Marcus Mariota is out for the rest of the preseason with an MCL sprain. That leaves a lot of playing time for Athan Kaliakmanis and Sam Hartman, who were rotating series against the Lions. Kaliakmanis once again showed he’s got the better arm, hitting Nick Nash on the biggest play of the day. #Commanders QB Athan Kaliakmanis (The Greek Rifle) All-22 vs the Lions • 11 for 14 passing (79%) • 162 pass yds • 114.9 RTG • 92.4 PFF grade #RaiseHail pic.twitter.com/j0tXnFAMNT — brandon (@JayDanielsMVP) August 23, 2026 On the money 💰 pic.twitter.com/icEedW4v3m — Washington Commanders (@Commanders) August 23, 2026 How about Athan Kaliakmanis stepping up in the pocket and pushing the ball down the field? title: Mark Tyler’s Washington Commanders 53-man roster projection
summary: With just one remaining preseason game left to play, coaches are going to have some tough decisions to make as to who will round out the Commanders 53-man roster. There are still some very tight position battles going on, including QB3, WR5-6, RB3-4, center, safety and the final cornerbacks. There may be plenty to glean […]
full_text: With just one remaining preseason game left to play, coaches are going to have some tough decisions to make as to who will round out the Commanders 53-man roster. There are still some very tight position battles going on, including QB3, WR5-6, RB3-4, center, safety and the final cornerbacks. There may be plenty to glean from this week’s joint practice with the Ravens , so that may be even bigger than the game itself in determining the final roster. Below is my 53-man roster projections following preseason Week 2, with some notes and some potential practice squad candidates. Offense QB (3): Jayden Daniels Marcus Mariota Athan Kaliakmanis Athan Kaliakmanis has shown me enough to feel comfortable letting Sam Hartman get an early start on his modeling career. RB (4): Bill Croskey-Merritt Rachaad White Kaytron Allen Jeremy McNichols The top three guys here are set. What has yet to be determined is how bad Jeremy McNichols ‘soft-tissue injury is. If his injury is more severe and prevents him from starting the season, a move to injured reserve could be in the cards opening the way for Robert Henry Jr. WR (6): Terry McLaurin Stefon Diggs Antonio Williams Treylon Burks Luke McCaffrey Jaylin Lane This is a tough one. Terry McLaurin, Stefon Diggs and Antonio Williams are all roster locks. Both Jaylin Lane and Luke McCaffrey have special teams value where Dyami Brown and Van Jefferson really don’t. That’s why I have both making it over Dyami. If it were me making the decision, I would probably have Brown in over Lane, but I feel GM Adam Peters won’t want to give up on Jaylin that quickly. TE (4): Chig Okonkwo John Bates Ben Sinnott Colson Yankoff This group has the potential to be sneaky-good. If Ben Sinnott can find his way as more of a receiving threat, this unit should flourish in David Blough’s offense. OL (9): Brandon Coleman Josh Conerly Trent Scott Andrew Wylie Sam Cosmi Chris Paul Nick Allegretti Matt Gulbin Julian Good-Jones I do not think this one is over. Julian Good-Jones is only on here until Peters can either swing a trade for a veteran center, sign a free agent or claim one who is released on cut-down day. I’m not at all comfortable with either Trent Scott or Andrew Wylie coming into the game should something happen to Brandon Coleman or Josh Conerly, so I’d have a close eye on cuts at tackle too. Defense DL (5): Daron Payne Javon Kinlaw Tim Settle Charles Omenihu Shy Tuttle The versatility of this group is what stands out. Each player can play multiple techniques in Daronte Jones’ new defense. There is a case to be made for Ricky Barber, but I have Shy Tuttle getting the nod over him. EDGE (5): Odafe Oweh K’Lavon Chaisson Dorance Armstrong Joshua Josephs Javontae Jean-Baptiste This is a young, fast, explosive group with great upside. Odafe Oweh and K’Lavon Chaisson are both great athletes who can rush the passer and even drop into coverage when asked. Joshua Josephs boasts great length and developmental upside as a rookie. There is also a good chance we’ll see Leo Chenal walked up here in the under front. LB (4): Sonny Styles Leo Chenal Frankie Luvu Jordan Magee I was originally going to go with five linebackers, but I see Jones using Tyler Owens as the Big Nickel a lot, so he fills this hole. This may sound like the staff is giving up on 2025 draft pick Kain Medrano, but I feel he may benefit from some time on the practice squad. CB (5): Amik Robertson Mike Sainristil Trey Amos Rasul Douglas Fabian Moreau I have Fabian Moreau as my final corner, making the team over the likes of Antonio Hamilton, Car’lin Vigers and Fred Davis II because of his familiarity with Jones secondary during his time with Minnesota. S (5): Nick Cross Quan Martin Jeremy Reaves Tyler Owens Percy Butler In a bit of a surprise, I have Will Harris getting cut. The big decision I have is between Percy Butler and Malik Spencer. I think there is a better shot of sneaking Spencer on the practice squad, so I have Butler making the 53. Maguranyanga (EDGE) Ricky Barber (DT) Jeffrey M’ba (DT) Kain Medrano (LB) Ale Kaho (LB) Fred Davis II (CB) Car’lin Vigers (CB) Malik Spencer (S) Qwuantrezz Knight (S)

(Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Daily Slop – 24 August 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Commanders links only a few more weeks 🫣 pic.twitter.com/r8w6IrfnK0 — Washington Commanders (@Commanders) August 23, 2026 Articles Sports Illustrated Quan Martin is starting to answer Commanders’ safety questions At the end of the day, [Quan] Martin entered camp this year running out of time to show whether he was a reliable answer at safety, and after two preseason games, he is finally beginning to make that answer easier to see. Martin has been…ranging from the back end, [getting] ball production, and making plays capable of changing possessions. None of this frees Martin from his tackling issues from a year ago, as we haven’t seen enough evidence to confirm or deny an improvement in that situation. Quinn sounded extremely confident in Martin’s skills after the Lions game: “He’s always somebody that has good ball skills, and he’s got the speed to get to the locations for that. So, I’m not surprised,” Quinn said. “He’s usually at his best when he’s got, as a high safety, to come and make some plays.” Quinn ended the conversation by saying, “He’s off to a great start,” which shows he’s still paying close attention to Martin’s progress. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Sports Illustrated Washington’s Turnover Emphasis Keeps Showing Up in Preseason The Washington Commanders spent their entire offseason program and training camp preaching takeaways and, through two preseason games, are producing results. The team now has six total takeaways after adding two more on Saturday night . Both takeaways came from the starting defense, as Amik Robertson got the early strip-sack that Joshua Josephs was able to recover in the end zone for a touchdown. Safety Quan Martin had the other takeaway after adding his second interception in as many games. This defense has a plan to take the ball away, not just talk of playing more aggressively. Martin’s two interceptions and Robertson’s strip-sack show how the defense is generating more possessions for the offense. Mix in the five sacks against Detroit, despite several of the team’s top pass rushers not playing , and Quinn has more evidence that the disruptive style the staff has stressed wanting is now showing up in games. Those six preseason takeaways are lovely to see, but if Washington wants that to continue into the regular season, the habits creating them need to survive and thrive once the games begin counting. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE A to Z Sports Antonio Williams and Jaden Bradley are making noise Antonio Williams was my player of the game for Washington. He finished the matchup with three catches for 41 yards on three targets and his best play was a catch where he confidently secured a ball over the middle. title: Playing Commanders GM: KEEP or CUT, you make the call – 5 O’Clock Club
summary: It’s 5 o’clock somewhere… The 5 o’clock club aims to provide a forum for reader-driven discussion at a time of day when there isn’t much NFL news being published. Feel free to introduce topics that interest you in the comments below. The Commanders have had surprising play from some players this offseason, both good and […]
full_text: It’s 5 o’clock somewhere… The 5 o’clock club aims to provide a forum for reader-driven discussion at a time of day when there isn’t much NFL news being published. Feel free to introduce topics that interest you in the comments below. The Commanders have had surprising play from some players this offseason, both good and bad. We all know that, come Sunday, finalizing the roster is a numbers game. Around 1,200 players league-wide will get their walking papers at the end of the week. Players “on the bubble” have to find a way to shine in camp and in preseason games, despite the fact that whatever they do comes with the caveat that it was done against the other team’s second- & third-string players, so somehow, it doesn’t seem to mean as much. Still, players like receiver Jaden Bradley and defensive lineman Ricky Barber have been able to grab the attention of Dan Quinn and his staff from OTAs to training camp by “making plays”, and we still have one more preseason game left for players to make an impression. Hustle, hard work, intelligence all count. Making big plays — a lot of big plays — trumps the rest. In the end, though, if you’re a player, all that counts is what the coaching staff and the general manager think of you. Today, I invite you to enter the world of “suppose”. Suppose you are the GM of the Commanders. All but one roster spot has been decided, and you have to make the final choice. Who do you keep? Who do you cut? (Man, as a former English teacher, it really hurts me to NOT write “ Whom do you keep?”, but it just sounds too pretentious for a sports blog). I’ve put five different poll questions below, but I’d invite you to answer each poll question individually, independent from the others. In other words, for each poll question, assume that all other decisions have been made, and all you have to decide is: Between the players listed in that poll question, who do you keep, and who do you cut? NOTE : Some poll questions say KEEP, and some say CUT . They are not all the same. If you want to add some different choices than the ones I’ve proffered and explain your thinking in the comments, feel free. Today, you’re in charge of Commanders personnel. You decide who is on the roster that lines up against the Eagles in three weeks.
