title: 2026 Arizona Cardinals: Projecting final 53-man roster
summary: The Cardinals have depth at running back and wide receiver. Too much? Tough decisions loom.
full_text:
TEMPE, Ariz. -- The Arizona Cardinals open the 2026 NFL regular season at the Los Angeles Chargers on Sept. 13 at SoFi Stadium. But first, they play one more preseason game Friday against the Green Bay Packers and then must cut their roster to 53 players by 6 p.m. ET on Sunday.

 Who will make the team? Which positions have tough decisions on deck? And where might the lineup be deepest and thinnest this season?

 The Cardinals have a handful of a major decisions to make, especially at two positions. Figuring out who to keep at wide receiver and running back won't be easy because of how deep both rooms are and how well the bottom of the depth chart at both positions have played. Then there is the Josh Sweat decision. Sweat has been on the PUP list since reporting for training camp in July with an apparent knee injury after skipping the voluntary portion of the Cardinals' offseason program to train on his own. If the Cardinals move Sweat to the reserve/PUP list before cut-down day, he'll have to miss the first four games but can practice after the first two.

 Here is our projection for the final 53-man roster for the Cardinals.

 

 Quarterbacks (3) 
 Jacoby Brissett , Gardner Minshew II , Carson Beck 

 At some point, the Cardinals will need to see what they have in Beck, but they can't put him on the practice squad because he'll be poached within seconds. Minshew is the backup for now, unless Beck can outplay him in practice, but after dealing with sore ribs and unlikely to get many snaps during regular season practices, that's somewhat unlikely. 

 
 Running backs (4) 
 Jeremiyah Love , Tyler Allgeier , Bam Knight , James Conner 

 Figuring out who to keep in this room will be one of the Cardinals' toughest decisions. Knight continued to look consistent and reliable during camp and the preseason, but Conner did not take a single 11-on-11 snap during camp. There's always a chance that Conner gets moved before the season, but if not, he'll be part of the running back committee.

 

 
 Wide receivers (7) 
 Marvin Harrison Jr ., Michael Wilson , Kendrick Bourne , Devin Duvernay , Simi Fehoko , Jalen Brooks , Reggie Virgil 

 The biggest decision for the Cardinals will be whether to keep six or seven receivers. Besides the obvious roster spots in Harrison, Wilson, Bourne and Duvernay, Arizona has seen productive play from Fehoko, who also doubles as a special-teams ace, Brooks, Virgil and Ihmir Smith-Marsette , who was a standout of camp. If the Cardinals keep six receivers, Smith-Marsette and either Virgil or Brooks are likely to be the odd-men out, but both, along with Xavier Weaver , could be practice squad possibilities.

 
 Tight ends (3) 
 Trey McBride , Elijah Higgins , Teagan Quitoriano 

 Tip Reiman will reinsert himself into the tight end rotation whenever he's healthy, but Arizona will have to make a tough decision with him in whether to put him on the reserve/PUP list, which will keep him out of the first four games.

 
 Offensive linemen (9) 
 Paris Johnson Jr ., Isaac Seumalo , Hjalte Froholdt , Isaiah Adams , Elijah Wilkinson , Hayden Conner , Jon Gaines II , Jayden Williams , Josh Fryar 

 There are a couple of tough decisions at the bottom of the offensive line depth chart that could impact how the initial group on the 53 looks. Matt Pryor has looked good in camp and Demontrey Jacobs could also make a case. However, both could be practice squad possibilities.

 
 Defensive linemen (7) 
 Walter Nolen III , Darius Robinson , Roy Lopez , Dante Stills , Jonah Williams , L.J. Collier , Andrew Billings 

 If the Cardinals keep eight defensive linemen, then Zachary Carter could make the roster, but Arizona will have a deep, experienced room to start the season.

 
 Linebackers (8) 
 Zaven Collins , Jordan Burch , Baron Browning , Mack Wilson Sr ., Cody Simon , Jack Gibbens , Karson Sharar , Owen Pappoe 

 Sweat's situation will dictate a bit of how the room ends up, and an inside linebacker could be the odd-man out.

 
 Cornerbacks (5) 
 Garrett Williams , Max Melton , Will Johnson , Denzel Burke , Sean Murphy-Bunting 
 With Williams back from the physically unable to perform list, the Cardinals cornerback room has come into shape. Kei'Trel Clark could end up making the roster if Arizona doesn't keep as many defensive linemen or linebackers, but the depth at cornerback isn't something to sweat about, for now.

 
 Safeties (4) 
 Budda Baker , Dadrion Taylor-Demerson , Andrew Wingard , Kitan Crawford 

 Crawford has been a standout in camp and the way Arizona utilizes Taylor-Demerson in the slot, Arizona's safety room will be steady this season.

 
 Special teams (3) 
 Chad Ryland  (K), Blake Gillikin  (P), Casey Kreiter  (LS) 

 It's the status quo, for now, for the Cardinals' special teams room.

title: 2026 NFL preseason Week 2: Game takeaways, analysis
summary: NFL Nation reporters tackle the biggest looming roster questions coming off each NFL Week 2 preseason game.
full_text:
Week 2 of the  2026 NFL preseason kicked off Thursday, giving us more insight into position battles and the push to make 53-man rosters before the cut-down deadline Aug. 30. Action began with two games Thursday before Friday's three contests, with severe weather rolling through Jacksonville late in the fourth quarter -- causing league and team officials to end the game there because of lightning at the two-minute warning.

 Things continued Saturday with 10 games, including  Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson 's first home game since tearing his right Achilles tendon in October 2024 and him being greeted with loud boos, and Minnesota Vikings signal-caller  J.J. McCarthy getting "banged up" during a rough first quarter in a loss to the Ravens.

 And Sunday's game wrapped up the weekend with the  Tennessee Titans  beating the defending Super Bowl champion  Seattle Seahawks .

 Our NFL Nation reporters picked out what you need to know about big roster decisions and more coming off Week 2 of the preseason.

 
 Quick links: 
 Full NFL schedule | Where to watch 
 Depth charts  | Sign up to play fantasy 

 

 

 Sunday's results 
 Titans 19, Seahawks  16 
 

 Should there be concern about the Titans' revamped secondary?  The secondary had a good showing against the Seahawks in joint practice, but the unit remains a concern. Starting cornerback Cor'Dale Flott was called for pass interference, which negated an interception by Kevin Winston Jr.  A bad coverage breakdown resulted in one of Seattle's two explosive touchdowns. Seahawks tight end Elijah Arroyo got wide open when Winston and cornerback Alontae Taylor locked in on an outbreaking route by the running back. --  Turron Davenport 

 Next game:  vs. Chicago Bears (Saturday, 8 p.m. ET, NFL Network)

 

 Can Bud Clark return at some point this season? The rookie safety is expected to miss "multiple months" after breaking his right ankle Sunday, coach Mike Macdonald said. Clark, Seattle's second-round pick, had been working with the No. 2 defense, but the team's hope was that he'd start to push Ty Okada for the starting job at some point. The Seahawks have more NFL-caliber safeties than they'd be able to keep if everyone was healthy. With Clark sidelined, AJ Finley' s chances of making the team increase. Rodney Thomas II , who's also fighting for a roster spot, didn't play Sunday after surgery this past week to repair a right hand fracture. -- Brady Henderson 

 Next game:  at Kansas City Chiefs (Friday, 8 p.m. ET, ESPN Unlimited)

 

 Saturday's results 

 Cowboys 34, Cardinals 13 
 

 Cowboys: Has Joe Milton III separated himself in the No. 2 quarterback battle? Milton's command of the offense is so much greater than it was in 2025, and the results have been telling. In two games, he has completed 21 of 28 passes for 286 yards and three touchdowns. He also ran for a score. He has made the big plays -- a TD of 56 yards and a completion of 70 yards vs. the Cardinals -- but more importantly, he avoided mistakes.

 Milton's arm strength is unquestioned, but his poise and decision-making have impressed the coaches. Sam Howell has done nothing to lose the job (though that late-game pick with the Cowboys in the red zone against Arizona didn't help), but the roster gymnastics required by keeping three quarterbacks on the 53-man roster could be too costly when the Cowboys look to fill their spots at wide receiver, linebacker and cornerback. -- Todd Archer 

 Next game: vs New Orleans Saints (Thursday, 8 p.m. ET, ESPN Unlimited)

 

 Cardinals: What does the bottom of the wide receiver room look like? There are a few guarantees to make the roster: Marvin Harrison Jr ., Michael Wilson , Kendrick Bourne and Devin Duvernay . After that, there are two questions: How many receivers will Arizona keep and who will the rest of them be?

 There are essentially three options for the last two (possibly three) spots: Simi Fehoko , Reggie Virgil and Jalen Brooks . Brooks has played great this preseason, and Wilson called Fehoko one of the best preseason receivers of all time. He plays a big role on special teams, so that will factor in. Virgil is a rookie who's quick and has shown promise. If Arizona keeps six WRs, Brooks might be the odd man out but won't last long on the practice squad, and if Virgil gets cut, Brooks could last a little longer. -- Josh Weinfuss 

 Next game: at Green Bay Packers (Friday, 8 p.m. ET)

 
 Patriots 24, Eagles 21 
 

 Patriots: Did veteran cornerback Kindle Vildor play his way onto the roster? The Patriots' top three at the position are solidified --  Christian Gonzalez , Carlton Davis III and  Marcus Jones  -- and coaches seem committed to third-year player Charles Woods as the fourth option. Vildor (seventh year) would be competing for a fifth or possibly sixth spot, and he made a case with tight coverage and two pass breakups Saturday. He also had a would-be interception nullified by an unnecessary roughness penalty on OLB Gabe Jacas . Vildor (5-11, 190) had an INT in Week 1.

 Other questions of note: Did Lan Larison 's strong performance give him the edge at RB3 and did Behren Morton 's poise in the second half force the Patriots' hand to keep him on the active roster as QB3? -- Mike Reiss 

 Next game : at Cleveland Browns (Thursday, 8 p.m. ET, Prime Video)

 

 

 Eagles : Who will back up QB Jalen Hurts this season? Andy Dalton has started both preseason games -- seemingly an indication that he is ahead in the competition with Tanner McKee  to be Hurts' backup, despite the two splitting practice reps with the second team this summer. Dalton has not fared well in those games, however, going 3-of-10 for 44 yards against the Patriots and 3-of-6 for 20 yards versus the Baltimore Ravens .

 McKee tossed two touchdown passes against New England and was more efficient overall. But neither QB has clearly separated from the other, making for an interesting decision as the time nears to trim the roster to 53. -- Tim McManus 

 Next game : at Cincinnati Bengals (Friday, 8 p.m. ET, CBS)

 

 Bucs 16, Chiefs 15 
 

 Bucs: Has Jalon Daniels worked his way into the QB2 role behind Baker Mayfield ? Every time the undrafted free agent rookie out of Kansas has entered games, he has given the offense a jolt. He went 9-for-14 for 71 passing yards, including a 2-yard touchdown pass across his body to tight end Ko Kieft . Daniels also rushed for 23 yards and led a second scoring drive after Roman Parodie 's interception that was capped by a 1-yard Sean Tucker touchdown run. Then, Daniels went with a hard count on third-and-1 and lured the Chiefs offsides. His play on the move really stood out during a night when Jake Browning was pressured on 58% of his dropbacks and was sacked three times. -- Jenna Laine 

 Next game : at  Jacksonville Jaguars  (Friday, 7:30 p.m. ET)

 

 

 Chiefs: Who will be the right tackle for Patrick Mahomes on opening night? The team invested most of training camp in preparing Kahlil Benson , the undrafted rookie from Indiana. Benson's performance Saturday, however, was quite disappointing. He struggled in pass protection, surrendering quick pressure to rookie Rueben Bain Jr . and a strip-sack to outside linebacker Anthony Nelson . At this point, the Chiefs likely move Benson to guard, where he played much better against the Los Angeles Rams last week. Jaylon Moore , a five-year veteran, hasn't been impressive, either. But Moore is likely the Chiefs' most ideal option. The only other possibility is Esa Pole , a second-year player who took snaps Saturday at left tackle with the second-team offense. -- Nate Taylor 

 Next game : at Seattle Seahawks  (Friday, 8 p.m. ET, ESPN Unlimited)

 

 Bengals 27, Bears 9 

 

 Bears : Who will be the Bears' left tackle? The Bears are still searching for their starting left tackle and got an extended look at Braxton Jones and Theo Benedet in Cincinnati. After missing more than a week because of injury, Jones got back in the mix, and it…

title: 2026 NFL offseason trade grades: Kayshon Boutte, Myles Garrett
summary: We're sizing up post-June 1 deals, including the blockbuster A.J. Brown and Myles Garrett trades along with Kayshon Boutte going to Houston.
full_text:
The main transaction window of the 2026 NFL offseason is over, with free agency and the draft long behind us. But teams are still leaning on trades to improve their rosters between now and Week 1. And we're grading the biggest swaps around the league, putting each deal into perspective for teams.

 The post-June 1 deals started with a bang. The Browns are  trading  edge rusher  Myles Garrett to the Rams for multiple draft picks -- including a 2027 first-rounder -- and edge rusher Jared Verse . The Patriots finally made their move to bring in Eagles wide receiver  A.J. Brown , giving up two draft picks. Did the Rams overpay in a massive return for Cleveland? Does Brown complete New England's offense? And how do we feel about the Falcons acquiring offensive tackle Wanya Morris from the Chiefs and Monday's deal , in which the Texans got wide receiver  Kayshon Boutte  from the Patriots for safety  Jaylen Reed  and a draft pick?

 To determine each grade, I am looking at multiple factors, including on-field impact, salary cap implications, compensation, player value/age and the context of a team's short- and long-term outlooks. How large is the effect of this decision, and how sure are we that it's a good or bad choice? How does this affect a team's chance to win the Super Bowl, this season or in the future?

 Let's get into our grades, and check back throughout training camp and the preseason for more trade evaluations.

 
 See more: 
 Tracking trades over the summer 
 Grades from earlier in the offseason 

 
 

 

 Patriots send WR Boutte to Texans for S Reed, draft pick 
 Date: Aug. 24

 Texans get: WR Kayshon Boutte 
 Patriots get: S Jaylen Reed , 2028 seventh-round pick

 Texans grade: A 
 Patriots grade: C

 Jayden Higgins ' season-ending torn ACL created a major need for the Texans. Houston had to add an outside wide receiver who could produce opposite Nico Collins , particularly one who could execute Higgins' route profile. They found a pretty ideal replacement in Boutte -- a short-term solution available for cheap, but one who should step in and help right away.

 Higgins ran a go route or deep fade on 18% of his routes last season, the 10th-highest rate among all receivers with at least 300 routes run. Boutte was No. 1 in that category by a mile at 31%, so he should have no problem assuming those deep routes along with slants, a route both Higgins and Boutte ran frequently last season.

 

 While not a star, Boutte is solid at what he does. He recorded 1.6 yards per route run during a mini-breakout season in 2025. Having a receiver with his route tree gives Collins help while allowing Houston to see how Jaylin Noel develops and how Tank Dell recovers from injury without them having to be impact players right away. Getting Boutte at this point of the offseason for as little as they did is good business.

 I can understand why the Patriots made Boutte available -- he had been bumped down the depth chart after the team had acquired both A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs this offseason -- but that doesn't he should have been, at least for this price. The Patriots are trying to win now and having a deep receiving group for Drake Maye to throw to seems like a worthwhile endeavor. New England's ticket back to the Super Bowl is through an elite passing game. And even if Boutte had left in free agency in a year, there's a chance the Patriots could have earned a compensatory pick in exchange.

 In addition to the future draft pick, the Patriots acquired Reed, a 2025 sixth-round pick. Reed played 73 defensive snaps in seven games last season, aligning as a box safety or nickel roughly two-thirds of the time. He should provide depth for the Patriots.

 

 

 Chiefs deal OT Morris to Falcons 
 Date: June 11

 Falcons get: OT Wanya Morris , 2027 seventh-round pick 
 Chiefs get: 2027 sixth-round pick

 Falcons grade: B+ 
 Chiefs grade: B-

 Two days after the Chiefs decided to explore trade options for Morris, who was hoping for a better path to playing time, they found a partner. Coincidentally, Morris will likely find himself competing for playing time with former Chiefs teammate  Jawaan Taylor  in Atlanta.

 A 2023 third-round pick, Morris played only 1,085 snaps and started 16 games over three seasons with the Chiefs, including one start in 2025 before suffering a season-ending knee injury on the opening snap of that game.

 

 His numbers have been solid when he's on the field, though. Morris has a career 89.3% pass block win rate and 73.5% run block win rate at tackle, which are both a shade below average for a starter. That said, win rates for Chiefs players have often been a bit better than expected, so those figures should come with a small grain of salt. And he had recently fallen down the depth chart, according to ESPN's Nate Taylor .

 The Falcons have veteran Jake Matthews entrenched at left tackle. But Jawaan Taylor is atop the depth chart at right tackle after his disappointing tenure in Kansas City as the Falcons try to fill the void from Kaleb McGary's retirement . Taylor signed a one-year, $5 million deal with Atlanta this offseason, which suggests that he's not entrenched as the starter -- especially since he's missed OTAs for undisclosed reasons . Morris is on the final year of his rookie contract.

 With Morris gone, the Chiefs suddenly lack proven depth at tackle, and coach Andy Reid has said the right tackle spot is a competition rather than  Jaylon Moore 's job to lose.

 

 

 Eagles trade WR Brown to the Patriots 
 Date: June 1

 Patriots get:  WR  A.J. Brown 
 Eagles get: 2027 fifth-round pick, 2028 first-round pick

 Patriots grade: B- 
 Eagles grade: A-

 The inevitable trade finally happened: Brown is headed to the Patriots. With the Eagles and Brown long headed for a split, the wide receiver is reuniting with his old head coach, Mike Vrabel. The hope is clear that Brown can augment an already-strong passing offense with Drake Maye at the helm to give New England a good shot to get back to the Super Bowl.

 I have long been bullish on Brown relative to consensus. Even though he has widely been considered one of the better NFL receivers over the past six seasons, I've always believed that evaluation still underrated his skill.

 

 Brown has only surpassed 1,100 receiving yards twice in his career (2022 and 2023) -- though both times he nearly reached 1,500 yards. Of course, it's important to consider that he has almost exclusively caught passes from Ryan Tannehill and Jalen Hurts . That's not the worst combination, but it's not the best, either. Maye will undoubtedly be the best quarterback Brown has played with in the NFL.

 And looking at Brown's performance on a per route basis tells a different story. Over the past six years -- starting with his second season in the league -- Brown ranks second in yards per route run (2.7) behind Puka Nacua . He has three of the top 20 individual seasons in the metric, too. And even that might not fully capture the degree of his ability.

 Brown once hung a sign that said "Always Open" at his locker. And according to ESPN's open score -- which measures a receiver's ability to get open on all routes, regardless of target, relative to expectations -- that was an accurate description. Brown recorded a 99 open score in 2021, first in the league and the highest possible score. That kicked off a four-year streak of him finishing at least in the top five in the metric, including a tie for first place in 2024. Brown was so consistent at getting open that we used him as our prime example when explaining how open score works .

 But Brown is coming off a down year. He managed just 1,003 receiving yards over 15 games with the Eagles and became publicly rankled at the offense as his production dropped in the middle of the year. Still, he ended up with a strong 2.3 yards per route run at the end of the season. His open score dipped to a 76 -- his lowest since 2020 but still in the top 10.

 Ultimately, the…

title: 2026 Atlanta Falcons: Projecting final 53-man roster
summary: It may take a while for a QB1 to emerge as Tua Tagovailoa and Michael Penix Jr. battle, so will Atlanta keep 3 QBs?
full_text:
ATLANTA -- The Falcons open the 2026 NFL regular season at the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sept. 13 at 1 p.m. ET at Acrisure Stadium. But first, they play one more preseason game Friday at the Miami Dolphins and then must cut their roster to 53 players by 6 p.m. ET on Sunday.

 Who will make the team? Which positions have tough decisions on deck? And where might the lineup be deepest and thinnest this season?

 New Falcons general manager Ian Cunningham said in the offseason it was his goal to elevate the team's floor, which meant getting deeper at as many positions as possible. Largely that was a success, even if the only high-profile signing Atlanta had was quarterback Tua Tagovailoa . There has been plenty of competition to make the team in training camp.

 Here is our projection for the 53-man roster for the Falcons.

 

 Quarterbacks (2) 
 Tua Tagovailoa , Michael Penix Jr . 

 The starting quarterback decision is still up in the air, but with Penix (knee) yet to be cleared for full practices it sure seems like Tagovailoa's job to lose. Once Penix is able to do 11-on-11s, though, he could re-enter the competition. The Falcons also have veteran  Cooper Rush and undrafted rookie Jack Strand  in camp, but probably don't have the luxury of keeping three quarterbacks on the 53-man roster.

 

 
 Running backs (3) 
 Bijan Robinson , Brian Robinson Jr ., Tyler Goodson 

 The big and physical Robinson Jr. should be a nice complement to his fellow B. Robinson after the Falcons lost  Tyler Allgeier  to free agency. Goodson has so far held off  Nathan Carter and Cash Jones  for the third running back role. Both Robinson Jr. and Goodson could see some time as returners, as well.

 
 Wide receivers (5) 
 Drake London , Jahan Dotson , Olamide Zaccheaus , Zachariah Branch , Chris Blair 

 This is a completely revamped room behind London, one which was mired by injuries and inexperience last season. Zaccheaus, in his second stint with Atlanta, has quickly regained his role as a mentor to London. Branch, a third-round pick, can make a real impact with his speed and yards-after-catch ability.

 
 Tight ends (3) 
 Kyle Pitts Sr ., Austin Hooper , Charlie Woerner 

 Look for this offense to utilize plenty of two- and three-tight-end formations under new head coach Kevin Stefanski and new offensive coordinator Tommy Rees. Pitts will likely be second in line for targets after London. Woerner is a consummate pro and hard-nosed blocker, while Hooper is a reliable pass catcher.

 
 Offensive linemen (9) 
 Jake Matthews , Matthew Bergeron , Ryan Neuzil , Chris Lindstrom , Jawaan Taylor , Michael Jerrell , Wanya Morris , Kyle Hinton , Corey Levin 

 With the exception of right tackle, this group has been together longer than most in the NFL. As of early training camp, Taylor was still working his way back from elbow surgery last season with the Chiefs. He'll be needed at right tackle to cover the blindside of whichever lefty quarterback is under center. Matthews has 195 consecutive starts, the longest active streak in the league.

 

 Defensive linemen (6) 

 Da'Shawn Hand , Maason Smith , Brandon Dorlus , Chris Williams , LaCale London , Zach Harrison 

 Stopping the run is a priority for the new regime, which necessitated the acquisitions of Hand and Smith to get bigger up front. Harrison was on his way to a career season before injuries in 2025. Dorlus had 8.5 sacks last season and will see some time on the edge, as well.

 
 Edge rushers (6) 
 Za'Darius Smith , Samson Ebukam , Cameron Thomas , Azeez Ojulari , Bralen Trice , Cameron Sample 

 James Pearce Jr . will play this season following his eight-game suspension for violating the league's personal conduct policy with a domestic violence arrest in February. Jalon Walker will not, courtesy of a torn ACL . That leaves a host of veterans to try and make up the 16 combined sacks that Pearce and Walker had last season as rookies.

 
 Linebackers (5) 
 Divine Deablo , Christian Harris , Harold Perkins Jr ., Kendal Daniels , JD Bertrand 

 Deablo was the sneaky most valuable player on the Falcons defense last season. Some combination of Harris, Perkins and Daniels will try to replace Kaden Elliss , one of the most underrated inside linebackers in the league who left in free agency. Daniels, a rookie like Perkins, has already impressed after being given the green dot in the first preseason game.

 
 Cornerbacks (6) 
 AJ Terrell Jr ., Mike Hughes , Darnay Holmes , Clark Phillips III ,  C.J. Henderson , Avieon Terrell 

 The Falcons got deeper at cornerback in the offseason with the signing of Holmes and the selection of Avieon Terrell in the second round of the draft. AJ and Avieon are brothers who hail from Atlanta. Avieon could push Holmes for the starting role at nickel corner until  Billy Bowman Jr . ( Achilles ) returns.

 
 Safeties (5) 
 Jessie Bates III , Xavier Watts , DeMarcco Hellams , Natrone Brooks , Sydney Brown 

 Bates and Watts make up one of the best safety duos in the league. Watts had five interceptions last season as a rookie and Bates is a three-time second-team All-Pro selection. Brooks and Brown can both also play cornerback, adding some versatility to the secondary.

 
 Special teams (3) 
 Nick Folk (K), Jake Bailey (P), Liam McCullough (LS) 

 The Falcons went through three kickers last season and actually lost games due to the ineptitude of the kicking game. The 41-year-old Folk is as steady as it gets and has actually gotten better with age. Bailey, another free-agent signing, is a plus punter who has experience with Folk in New England.

title: How Jesse Minter has motivated Lamar Jackson, Ravens to 'Be The Best'
summary: Competitive drive. Player connection. Cool demeanor. All these are why the Ravens believe the 43-year-old can elevate Baltimore to a championship level.
full_text:
AT THE END of one of the Baltimore Ravens ' offseason workouts, first-year coach Jesse Minter rolled out two 16-pound medicine balls onto the practice field to get his point across.

 In an impromptu battle between the offense and defense, rookie guard Olaivavega Ioane used all his strength to throw the medicine ball farther than outside linebacker Zion Young . All of the defensive players were forced to do pushups. The offensive players' celebration was capped by rookie wide receiver Ja'Kobi Lane doing a cartwheel into a backflip.

 Throughout spring practices and training camp, the 43-year-old Minter has sprung on his players what he calls "At our best, when our best is needed" periods. The contests, which are kept secret until announced to the players at the end of practice, have included a relay featuring rookies carrying weights in both hands, a competition of one-handed catches and a race in which players push blocking sleds.

 "You never know what play is going to be the biggest play of the game," Minter told his players. "Every situation, you've got to be ready. When your number is called, you step up and make the play."

 Minter's mantra -- "Be The Best" -- is displayed in massive silver lettering next to the doors that lead to the Ravens' practice field. It's a variation of a saying by basketball coaching legend John Wooden, and it has become the foundation for this new era in Baltimore.

 Minter was hired to replace John Harbaugh, who was fired after 18 seasons, because the Ravens have struggled over the past decade to be their best when their best was needed. In eight seasons with quarterback Lamar Jackson , Baltimore dominated in the regular season but repeatedly underachieved in the playoffs because of critical mistakes and turnovers. 

 

 The Ravens believe Minter can elevate Baltimore to a championship level because of his competitive drive, his ability to connect with players and his cool demeanor.

 Unlike Harbaugh's intense, alpha-type leadership, Minter's coaching style has been described by Ravens players as calm and collected. His father, Rick, and his best friend, Ravens safeties coach P.J. Volker, can't remember a time when Minter has lost his temper.

 Throughout the spring workouts and training camp, no one has heard Minter raise his voice to the players. When Minter is unhappy with how practice is going, he huddles up the team so everyone can hear his message. Minter believes NFL teams win when there is a partnership between players and coaches.

 "He's very [focused on] connecting the team right now," wide receiver Rashod Bateman said. "I think that's something that we needed."

 One of Minter's biggest changes was how Baltimore conducted training camp. Instead of sticking with Harbaugh's scorching afternoon practices, Minter moved the start of practices to the morning to avoid the heat and players wearing down.

 Minter has also regularly cut practices short, something that rarely occurred under Harbaugh. During a practice in the middle of training camp, Minter ended practice 30 minutes early because the team had reached its goal of 100 snaps that day. This is a major shift in philosophy from Harbaugh, who wanted his players to take pride in being one of the NFL's hardest-working teams and would run as many reps as possible during the allotted practice time.

 The Ravens' players say the positive vibes stem from Minter's encouraging words. When there is a mistake, he is known to put his arm around the player to address the correction and then urge him to move on to the next snap. In discussing the changes under Minter, some in the organization have noticed less anxiety around the team.

 "It's kind of a pressure cooker that we live in on a daily basis, and he tries to take a lot of that out of it by maximizing our opportunities when we're out there -- understanding that we have to work hard, but at the same time, he takes care of us and puts us in positions to be successful and does not put everything on our plate every single day," Ravens safety Kyle Hamilton said. "It's little things each time, and I can see us slowly crescendoing throughout the season."

 

 THOSE CLOSE TO  Minter believe others mistake his mild-mannered temperament for not being competitive. Their suggestion: Ask Minter about the toughest moment of his football career.

 As the defensive coordinator for Georgia State in 2014, he watched his defense allow 69 points to rival Georgia Southern. Georgia State gave up 613 rushing yards and 10 rushing touchdowns in a game that still bothers Minter.

 "I've always felt like you can come up with answers and solutions," Minter said. "And it was just what we were trying to get accomplished wasn't translating to the players. And that was a major 'Come to Jesus' moment, I would say."

 

 Volker, who has known Minter since they were college teammates at Mount St. Joseph University, knew Minter couldn't wait for another shot at Georgia Southern.

 "We went into the lab in the offseason," Volker said. "And I'll never forget, he circled the date on the calendar. It was Dec. 5, and we were going to have the guys ready to play. And we were."

 Minter spent that offseason devising a defense that would shut down Georgia Southern's triple-option offense. He also recruited players to fit that scheme.

 That next season, Minter enjoyed one of his most satisfying wins as Georgia State defeated Georgia Southern, 34-7. Minter's defense held Georgia Southern to a season-low 203 yards of total offense. Georgia Southern coach Willie Fritz acknowledged after the game he was "outcoached."

 "That's a day I'll never forget," Minter said.

 

 IN WHAT WOULD later become a full-circle moment, Minter's first NFL coaching job came compliments of Harbaugh.

 In 2017, the Ravens had an opening for a defensive assistant. Rick Minter, Jesse's father, called Harbaugh, who had been Rick's special teams coordinator at the University of Cincinnati 20 years earlier.

 Rick Minter told Harbaugh: "He's smart, he's good looking. He can communicate. He sees the big picture."

 

 As Rick Minter put it, "I sold him on him being like John."

 But Jesse Minter quickly stood out to players by how much he listened. He often sat next to safety Eric Weddle in meetings and picked his brain about schematics and other ideas.

 "Early on, you knew he was a bright coach," Weddle said. "He thought outside the box. I just drew a great appreciation of him, his personality, his demeanor."

 In 2018, Minter was part of the staff, which included defensive coordinator Wink Martindale and linebackers coach Mike Macdonald, to overhaul Baltimore's scheme. It was during this time that Minter gives Martindale credit for valuing his input and empowering him to build more confidence in himself.

 "I just think he was very thorough and thinking things through strategically as well as breaking down opponents," Martindale said.

 Eight years later, after being defensive coordinator at Michigan and with the Los Angeles Chargers , Minter is back with the Ravens as the fourth head coach in their history. He takes over in Baltimore just months after Macdonald became the first defensive playcalling head coach to win a Super Bowl .

 Weddle believes Minter and Macdonald are "cut from the same cloth."

 "They're just very, very similar in a lot of ways," Weddle said. "And I expect to have the same impact in Baltimore as Mike has had in Seattle."

 

 IN MINTER'S INITIAL videoconference interview for the Ravens' head coaching job, he laid out his vision for the team's franchise QB to team officials.

 "Creating a partnership with Lamar as myself as a head coach is the very first priority," Minter told them. "Creating an environment where he feels like the system is helping him become the best player he can be. That he's learning a system of offense and not a collaboration of plays."

 Minter will be judged on whether he can help Jackson, one of the top players in the NFL, advance…

title: Predicting NFL teams most likely to improve in 2026 season
summary: Can the Giants and Jets improve on their awful 2025 records? Will the Chiefs, Lions and Ravens all make it back to the playoffs?
full_text:
Even by NFL standards, 2025 was a topsy-turvy season. Seven teams saw their records improve or decline by at least six wins, the most in any campaign since 2008. And though that's a little more feasible in a 17-game season than it was in the 16-game era, the 10-game improvement by the Patriots, who improved from 4-13 to 14-3, was the largest by any team since 1999, when the Colts pulled that off in Peyton Manning's second season.

 Teams hoping to emulate the Patriots might find a difficult path forward. The Pats made a major coaching upgrade by hiring Mike Vrabel, who had been one of the league's best coaches during his time with the Titans before losing a power struggle in Nashville. New England relied as heavily on free agency as any team in recent memory, with 13 of its 25 most-used players on offense and defense acquired as free agents over the previous two offseasons. And the Patriots notably had what was one of the easiest schedules in league history, facing just two teams that posted a winning record all season.

 The Patriots' path toward the Super Bowl was off my radar, and they weren't included in my annual look at teams most likely to improve at this time last year . The other six teams to jump by at least six wins, though, are all featured in one of the two columns you'll see this week. Today, we start on the rosy side and focus on the teams that are most likely to improve in 2026. And on Tuesday, we'll talk about the ones that are most likely to decline.

 
 Subscribe: 'The Bill Barnwell Show' 

 
 Last year's column featured the Raiders, who declined by a game, and the Giants, who improved by one win. The other three teams were much bigger successes. The Bears rode the Ben Johnson effect and a flood of takeaways on defense to an 11-6 mark after going from 5-11 in 2024. The 49ers jumped from 6-11 to 12-5. And the Jaguars made the biggest leap, going from 4-13 to 13-4 in Liam Coen's first season at the helm. All three teams made the playoffs after finishing well below .500 the previous season.

 Since 2017, this annual column has gone 35-8 (.813) in picking teams to improve on the previous season's record. The average team has gotten 3½ games better after adjusting for the 17-game schedule. And if we include our picks for teams that will decline, the back-to-back columns are a combined 69-17 (.802) in accuracy, while going 50-36 (.581) against the preseason over-under totals preserved on Pro-Football-Reference.com.

 So, recent history suggests four of the five teams listed in this year's column should get better. There's a fun mix of teams that just took a step back in 2025 and long-frustrating organizations that might exceed expectations in 2026. Let's start with the headliners from last year's decline column  who might be the most obvious pick of the bunch ...

 Note: Schedule strength is via ESPN's Football Power Index (FPI) . 

 

 
 Jump to: 
 BAL | DET | KC | NYG | NYJ 

 
 

 

 Kansas City Chiefs 
 Record in 2025: 6-11 (1-9 in games decided by seven or fewer points) 
 Point differential in 2025: plus-34 
 Projected strength of schedule:  14th easiest

 You could have suspected things would start here. Twelve months ago, the Chiefs were coming off a 15-2 regular season and led my column on teams most likely to decline in 2025. Andy Reid's squad had gone 10-0 in games decided by seven points or fewer in 2024, an NFL record. And though anyone who has read this column annually is already familiar with the idea that teams struggle to win a significant proportion of their close games year after year, I wouldn't have blamed anyone who believed the Chiefs were an outlier.

 The 10-0 mark took Patrick Mahomes  to 43-17 in one-score contests. We've seen other generational quarterbacks -- with Tom Brady as a notable example -- win more of their one-score games than you might expect. It would have been foolish to count on the Chiefs to win every one of their one-score games again, but expecting Mahomes and the Chiefs to fall to even .500 in close games also seemed to be a bad bet.

 

 Then, the Chiefs started their 2025 season with a six-point loss to the Chargers . Kansas City lost by three to the Eagles in Week 2. The Jags ' late charge led to a Chiefs loss in Week 5. They were winning big, but when things were close, a team that had always found a way to win the close ones in 2024 found ways to lose them in 2025. The Chiefs went from 10-0 to 1-9 in one-score games between 2024 and 2025, including a 1-7 record with Mahomes under center before the star quarterback tore his left ACL .

 As you probably guessed, the 18-game swing between 2024 and 2025 is the biggest of one-score victories in league history. The previous record was 13 games by the 2022-23 Vikings, who fell from 9-0 to 4-8 in one-score games. Minnesota then followed with an 8-1 mark in 2024 before regressing to the mean and landing at 4-3 in 2025.

 The Vikings were cycling through quarterbacks for most of that time, though, and the Chiefs had Mahomes for most of last season. Most of the stars who helped the Chiefs to three consecutive Super Bowl appearances were back in 2025, too. And though the Chiefs were down to third-stringers at QB and left tackle by the end of the season, they were about average in terms of season-long health on offense and even had the league's healthiest defense, per the FTN Football Almanac 's adjusted games lost metric.

 Did the Chiefs just play significantly worse? By advanced metrics, the answer to that question is ... not really. The 2024 Chiefs finished the regular season eighth in DVOA, pointing to a good team that had remarkable luck in one-score games. And though the 2025 Chiefs understandably faded after Mahomes gave way to  Gardner Minshew II  and Chris Oladokun at quarterback, they ranked eighth in DVOA through the game against the Chargers in Week 15, when Mahomes suffered his ACL injury.

 The 2024 Chiefs outscored their opponents by 59 points, or roughly 3.5 points per game. And if we don't include the post-Mahomes games, the 2025 Chiefs outscored their opponents by 60 points, which is just under 4.3 points per game. Point differential suggests those teams should roughly expect to get about the same number of wins over a full season with an average amount of luck and timing.

 To put that into context over 17 games, let's look at teams that outscored their opponents by a margin between three and five points per game in a season. Since 1990, 117 teams have fit into that window. The best record produced by any of those teams is 15-2, which matches the Chiefs' 2024 record. The Chiefs were 6-8 with Mahomes in the lineup, and that would have been a .428 winning percentage over a full season. That would be the worst winning percentage produced by any of those three-to-five-point-differential teams over a full campaign. In other words, the 2024 Chiefs got the best recorded results out of being a pretty good team since 1990, and the 2025 Chiefs -- even with Mahomes -- were getting the worst results of any team at that level in recent history before his injury.

 Even if the Chiefs produce average results with that sort of point differential in 2026, they should be back in the postseason. Are there reasons to be concerned that they won't match up to that underlying level of play? Maybe. To start, Mahomes is returning from the torn ACL. Though the soon-to-be 31-year-old quarterback is still in contention to start the season on the active roster, it's difficult to imagine that he won't feel some sort of disruption or struggle coming back from his first significant injury as a pro. At the very least, Mahomes' legendary ability to scramble and extend plays might be limited early in 2026.

 

 The defense has also lost key players in the secondary, with Trent McDuffie dealt to the Rams, Jaylen Watson joining the Rams in free agency and starting safety Bryan Cook inking a deal with the Bengals. The Chiefs used a top-10 pick on cornerback Mansoor…

title: 2026 Baltimore Ravens: Projecting final 53-man roster
summary: The most high-profile decision is whether Baltimore will place DT Nnamdi Madubuike on injured reserve.
full_text:
BALTIMORE -- The Baltimore Ravens open the 2026 regular season at the Indianapolis Colts on Sept. 13 ( 1 p.m. ET, CBS ) at Lucas Oil Stadium. But first, they play one more preseason game Friday against the Washington Commanders  ( 6 p.m. ET, NFL Network ) and then must cut their roster to 53 players by 6 p.m. ET on Sunday.

 Who will make the team? Which positions have tough decisions on deck? And where might the lineup be deepest and thinnest this season?

 The most high-profile decision is whether Baltimore will place Pro Bowl defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike on injured reserve to start the season. Coming back from neck surgery, Madubuike has yet to participate in team drills this summer, which means time is running out for him to be ready for Week 1. The Ravens also have to figure out how many players they can carry at cornerback, which is their deepest position, and at inside linebacker, which is their thinnest.

 Here is our projection for the 53-man roster for the Ravens.

 

 Quarterbacks (2) 
 Lamar Jackson , Tyler Huntley 

 The Ravens re-signed Huntley this offseason to be Jackson's primary backup for a fifth season. Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano looks like he has earned a spot on the practice squad after two impressive outings in the preseason.

 
 

 Running backs (4) 
 Derrick Henry , Justice Hill , Rasheen Ali , Adam Randall 

 There are some question marks on the depth chart after Henry and Hill. After a solid training camp, Ali has missed a chunk of time due to an undisclosed injury, which could lead him to start the season on injured reserve. Randall, who was owner Steve Bisciotti's hand-picked selection in the fifth round this year, is on the bubble but he could land one of the last spots available with his special teams play.

 
 Wide receivers (6) 
 Zay Flowers , Rashod Bateman , Ja'Kobi Lane , Elijah Sarratt , Devontez Walker ,  LaJohntay Wester 

 Bateman could face a suspension under the personal conduct policy after being arrested on family violence charges, which would open up a roster spot. Flowers and Lane have been the Ravens' top receivers in training camp. Sarratt and Walker, a pair of fourth-round picks, are considered safe. Wester has secured the final receiver spot because he's the top punt returner and has received increased reps on offense this summer.

 
 Tight ends (4) 
 Mark Andrews , Durham Smythe , Matthew Hibner , Josh Cuevas 

 Andrews is the Ravens' only returning tight end, but Smythe is the most familiar with new offensive coordinator Declan Doyle's system after playing for him in Chicago last season. Hibner is the favorite to become Baltimore's No. 3 tight end over Cuevas after a strong debut in the preseason opener.

 
 Offensive linemen (9) 
 Ronnie Stanley , John Simpson , Ethan Pocic , Olaivavega Ioane , Roger Rosengarten , Andrew Vorhees , Jovaughn Gwyn , Emery Jones Jr ., Carson Vinson 

 There was a shakeup on the offensive line last week, when first-team center Danny Pinter injured his right leg at a joint practice in Minnesota. Pinter is out for an extended period, which opens up the competition at center. Pocic is the favorite to take the job because of his experience, but he has to prove he is fully recovered from an Achilles injury that he suffered eight months ago. Vorhees, a former starting guard, improved his chances of making the team by taking a $2.2 million paycut.

 
 Defensive linemen (5) 
 Travis Jones , Calais Campbell , John Jenkins ,  Broderick Washington Jr ., Aeneas Peebles 

 One of the biggest questions at the start of training camp - Madubuike's status for Week 1 - still has not been answered. Along with Jones and Campbell, the other defensive lineman who is guaranteed a spot is Washington, who is guaranteed $2 million after taking a $2 million paycut. If the Ravens want to free up another roster spot, they could cut Jenkins and sign him to the practice squad, where he could be elevated for the first couple weeks of the season. Rayshaun Benny and CJ Okoye are on the bubble.

 
 Outside linebackers (5) 
 Trey Hendrickson , Tavius Robinson , Mike Green , Zion Young , Adisa Isaac 

 The Ravens have a good blend of youth and experience with their top four outside linebackers in Hendrickson, Robinson, Green and Young. Isaac, a 2024 third-round pick who has struggled with injuries, has to show he can make an impact on special teams in order to make the 53-man roster. Undrafted rookie Ethan Burke should land on the practice squad after making plays in the preseason.

 
 Inside linebackers (4) 
 Roquan Smith , Teddye Buchanan , Trenton Simpson , Jay Higgins IV 

 Buchanan was activated off the physically unable to perform list after tearing an ACL in December, but it's unknown whether he can be the top weakside linebacker at the start of the season. Given the Ravens' questionable depth at this position, it wouldn't be a surprise if Baltimore added an experienced inside linebacker after other teams make their major cuts.

 
 

 Cornerbacks (7) 
 Nate Wiggins , Marlon Humphrey , Chidobe Awuzie , T.J. Tampa , Chandler Rivers , Keyon Martin , Bilhal Kone 

 The big question here: How many cornerbacks can the Ravens keep? There are five who are locks to make the team: Wiggins, Humphrey, Awuzie, Tampa and Rivers. The Ravens likely have to make room for Martin and Kone because it's difficult to think two talented young cornerbacks will pass through waivers and land on the practice squad. This puts Robert Longerbeam , a sixth-round pick from a year ago, squarely on the bubble.

 
 Safeties (4) 
 Kyle Hamilton , Malaki Starks , Jaylinn Hawkins , Keondre Jackson 

 The Ravens essentially start three safeties in Hamilton, Starks and Hawkins. Jackson has earned a spot with splash plays on defense in the spring and summer. Baltimore can free up a roster spot by moving veteran backup K'Von Wallace to the practice squad for the first couple weeks of the season because he doesn't have to clear waivers.

 
 Special teams (3) 
 Tyler Loop (K), Ryan Eckley (P), Nick Moore (LS) 

 The Ravens put a lot of faith in Loop after not bringing in competition in training camp after his 44-yard missed field goal in the season finale ended Baltimore's season. Eckley has shown a strong leg in camp after being the first punter drafted this year. The Ravens consider Moore to be the top long-snapper in the game.

title: 2026 Buffalo Bills: Projecting final 53-man roster
summary: New coordinator Jim Leonhard will have some difficult decisions to make at inside linebacker and cornerback.
full_text:
ORCHARD PARK, N.Y. -- The Buffalo Bills open the 2026 NFL regular season at the Houston Texans on Sept. 13 ( 1 p.m. ET, CBS ) at Reliant Stadium. But first, they play one more preseason game Thursday against the Pittsburgh Steelers  ( 7 p.m. ET, NFL Network ) and then must cut their roster to 53 players by 6 p.m. ET on Sunday.
 Who will make the team? Which positions have tough decisions on deck? And where might the lineup be deepest and thinnest this season?

 While this roster largely carries over familiar faces on the offensive side of the ball, some tough decisions will have to be made on defense. This is the first year of transitioning to coordinator Jim Leonhard's new scheme, and the players who fit it best will translate to roster decisions that could look different than previous seasons. There are close calls to be made at multiple groups, including inside linebacker, outside cornerback and offensive line.

 Here is our projection for the 53-man roster for the Bills.

 

 Quarterbacks (2) 
 Josh Allen , Kyle Allen 

 It's the all-Allen lineup once again. The goal here for the Bills will be to bring back quarterback Shane Buechele to the practice squad.

 
 Running backs (3) 
 James Cook III , Ray Davis , Ty Johnson 

 The only question at the position is Johnson's health. He is dealing with a lower-body injury, per coach Joe Brady, and hasn't practiced since Aug. 8. Otherwise, this group is solid.

 
 Fullbacks (1) 
 Ben VanSumeren 

 The veteran became the only fullback on the roster when rookie undrafted free agent Jackson Acker was cut. There, however, is a huge question mark if the Bills will keep a fullback on the roster, especially with Brady's comments on Thursday that the team is evaluating if fullback is "a position and a role that we'll be able to have on our football team." This one is close.

 
 

 Wide receivers (6) 
 DJ Moore , Khalil Shakir , Keon Coleman , Joshua Palmer , Skyler Bell , Mecole Hardman Jr . 

 To keep a punt returner or not? That's the question. The Bills showed they are wondering about it themselves by trying out Ray Davis , who is the primary kickoff returner, at punt returner to start both preseason games. Hardman has played behind other receivers, and if the Bills can go Davis at both returner spots, that opens a space elsewhere. Injuries could end up forcing the Bills to keep a six, so Hardman is on for now as he serves multiple roles, but that could easily change.

 
 Tight ends (3) 
 Dalton Kincaid , Dawson Knox , Jackson Hawes 

 This is another group that is relatively locked in. Keleki Latu has certainly stood out this camp, and if there were more roster spots, it would certainly make sense for the Bills to keep him. Otherwise, the biggest question at tight end is if Kincaid can stay healthy.

 
 Offensive linemen (9) 
 Dion Dawkins , Alec Anderson , Connor McGovern , O'Cyrus Torrence , Spencer Brown , Austin Corbett , Jude Bowry ,  Lloyd Cushenberry III , Tylan Grable 

 The Bills have shown just how they feel about Cushenberry, as he has taken over as first-team center in McGovern's absence because of a right leg injury. There is a tough decision to be made for the final spot. Sedrick Van Pran-Granger has an argument to be rostered, but the nod will go to Grable, who provides depth at tackle.

 
 Defensive linemen (11) 
 Bradley Chubb , Greg Rousseau , Michael Hoecht , TJ Parker , Javon Solomon , Ed Oliver , Deone Walker , Landon Jackson , T.J. Sanders , Zane Durant , Greg Gaines 

 This group appeared to have solidified itself when Phidarian Mathis was suspended for three games, but then the Bills signed veteran DT Greg Gaines . This week will be a crucial one for DeWayne Carter to prove a roster spot should be his. There could be a conversation about OLB Mike Danna as well, but the nod here will go to the 2024 fifth-round draft pick in Solomon.

 
 Linebackers (4) 
 Terrel Bernard , Dorian Williams , Kaleb Elarms-Orr , Keonta Jenkins 

 This position makes for one of the toughest decisions. Losing Buffalo legend Joe Andreessen is tough, and there's a good chance he ends up on the roster over Jenkins or that the Bills decide to keep five inside linebackers. This is a coin flip, but Jenkins has had played strong of late.

 
 

 Cornerbacks (6) 
 Christian Benford , Maxwell Hairston , Davison Igbinosun , Kani Walker , Dee Alford , Jordan Hancock 

 Walker is the only question mark here. If the team decides to add at outside corner, Walker would be the person to lose his spot. But as the roster currently stands, more bodies are needed at a position general manager Brandon Beane values investing in and the rookie undrafted free agent has impressed.

 
 Safeties (5) 
 Cole Bishop , C.J. Gardner-Johnson , Damar Hamlin , Jalon Kilgore ,  Sam Franklin Jr . 

 Hamlin has put together a solid camp. As he has done in years past, Hamlin's availability and reliability in the summer have shown his value. He has been a most consistent backup with Gardner-Johnson missing time. This could be a close decision with veteran Geno Stone , while the special teams capabilities of Kilgore and Franklin are important.

 
 Special teams (3) 
 Tyler Bass  (K), Tommy Doman Jr . (P), Reid Ferguson  (LS) 

 The only slight question here was punter, but it was Doman's job to lose, and he secured it over veteran Mitch Wishnowsky early on. No training camp competition was ever brought in for Bass, showing the team's confidence in the kicker.

title: Bills star DT Ed Oliver mourning tragic death of son

title: 2026 Carolina Panthers training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Catch up on our updates from Panthers training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. Panthers writer Mike Kaye will have the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Panthers camp. Will QB Bryce Young and the Panthers take another step forward after making the playoffs in 2025? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Catch up on all the updates, concluding with the Panthers' top camp performer and biggest lingering question.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 Monday, Aug. 24 

 The Panthers won't see wide receiver Xavier Legette again in the preseason. He also won't take part in joint practice against the Houston Texans on Wednesday as he will wear a walking boot on his right foot through Thursday, according to coach Dave Canales .

 Rookie quarterback Haynes King (hamstring) will also be sidelined through the week as well, Canales said. King, like running back Chuba Hubbard (hamstring), is targeting a post-cut-deadline return to the field.

 Tight end Darren Waller , who made his practice debut on Monday, will probably be held out of Friday's preseason finale. The recent addition will be peppered into team drills -- similar to his work to begin the week -- against the visiting AFC South squad.

 The Panthers will cut their roster from 91 players -- including an international exemption -- to 53 players by 6 p.m. on Sunday. Check out our Panthers' 53-man roster projection from Monday morning.

 

 More observations: 

 
 Safety Lathan Ransom (undisclosed) and nose tackle Cam Jackson (concussion protocol) practiced in red non-contact jerseys. 
 Cornerbacks Will Lee III and Akayleb Evans , wide receiver Ja'seem Reed , outside linebacker Jaelan Phillips all returned to practice after missing last week's matchup with the Jacksonville Jaguars due to minor injuries. 
 Linebacker Devin Lloyd (knee) was held out of practice after dealing with soreness following joint practice with the Jaguars on Wednesday. Per Canales, the team doesn't view the injury as something major, but he did undergo treatment. 
 Tight end Feleipe Franks made an excellent over-the-shoulder catch for a big gain off a throw from depth QB Kyle Trask in 11-on-11 drills. 
 Veteran offensive lineman Brady Christensen took some tackle reps on Monday after spending most of the summer at guard. 
 Rookie safety Zakee Wheatley picked off starting QB Bryce Young in 7-on-7 work. 
 Cornerback Corey Thornton ended practice on a diving pick off a throw from backup QB Kenny Pickett . 
 

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 19 
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- As Jaguars tight ends Brenton Strange and Nate Boerkircher made life difficult for the Panthers' defense Wednesday in joint practice, quarterback Bryce Young and wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan had some fun of their own on the opposite field.
 Young and McMillan were nearly automatic in foreign territory outside of EverBank Stadium. The quarterback heaved the ball down the field for his top target and McMillan routinely made him look good.

 The fireworks started with Young tossing a beautiful strike to McMillan as he beat cornerback Jabbar Muhammad to the end zone in 11-on-11 drills. A little while later, Young hit McMillan on a crossing route in front of defenders at the tip of the goal line for a contested touchdown grab.

 Finally, Young lifted a ball toward the end zone, about 25 yards, for McMillan, who jumped up to snag the ball over two defensive backs for a third touchdown.

 

 More observations: 

 
 The following players were sidelined during the joint practice: RB  Chuba Hubbard  (hamstring), NT Cam Jackson (concussion protocol), WR Ja'seem Reed (calf), CB Akayleb Evans (undisclosed), QB Haynes King (hamstring), CB  Will Lee III  (groin) and TE Darren Waller (onboarding). 
 Outside linebacker Jaelan Phillips and wide receiver Xavier Legette were pulled early from drills as a precaution due to minor injuries, according to coach Dave Canales. Phillips told the staff he was fine after hurting his wrist, while the team's medical staff cleared Legette after he got rolled up on in team drills. 
 Tight ends Feleipe Franks and Mitchell Evans both produced touchdowns in team drills. Franks caught an early touchdown off a throw from third-string quarterback Kyle Trask and then mocked the Jaguars fans in attendance with a celebration after the score. Young found Evans streaking wide open to the end zone on a roughly 50-yard completion for a touchdown. 
 It was a mixed bag for the Panthers' defense against quarterback Trevor Lawrence and the Jacksonville offense. But in the red zone drills, the Jaguars scored five consecutive touchdowns, including three completions in the end zone to tight ends. 
 Returning linebacker Devin Lloyd had a couple of nice moments with a stop against the run and a pass breakup that led to some jawing between both sides. Phillips had an early tackle for loss on running back Ameer Abdullah , which featured the free agent addition tossing the veteran to the ground. 
 Safety Nick Scott picked off Lawrence during team drills and cornerback Mike Jackson made an impressive two-handed pass breakup on wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr . in 11-on-11 work. 
 
 

 Monday, Aug. 17 
 New Panthers tight end Darren Waller 's free agency waiting game ended last Wednesday. He said his agent called him about the opportunity that morning right before he was heading out to a training session.

 Waller, who will turn 34 in September, didn't practice on Monday after officially signing with his fifth NFL team. Instead, he watched the workout, chatting with coaches and new teammates throughout the session.

 In Carolina, he is reunited with safety Tre'von Moehrig , whom he played with previously in Las Vegas, and outside linebacker Jaelan Phillips and associate head coach Darrell Bevell, whom he worked with in Miami last season.

 According to coach Dave Canales, Waller isn't likely to mix it up with the Jaguars in joint practices on Wednesday in Jacksonville. But the veteran playmaker might be able to suit up in his newly issued No. 35 jersey and get some individual work with starting quarterback Bryce Young .

 

 More observations: 

 
 Ja'seem Reed , a training camp wide receiver-turned-summer standout, sustained a calf injury against the Buffalo Bills on Saturday, according to Canales. He was set to undergo imaging on the ailment Monday after practice. 
 Outside linebacker Cam Gill played through a shoulder injury against the Bills, posting a sack in the second preseason game. He was held out of the first workout of the week due to increased soreness, according to Canales. 
 Rookie cornerback Will Lee III played through a groin injury against Buffalo but was sidelined Monday during practice. 
 The Panthers cross-trained offensive linemen during the workout. Rookie Albert Reese IV , who was signed as an offensive tackle, played second-team right guard, while veteran Jake Curhan worked with the second-team line as a left guard. Chandler Zavala , who had an underwhelming outing against Buffalo as the starting left guard, played second-team center. Backup center Nick Samac took his turn as the third-string right guard for the third time this summer. 
 The highlight of the hottest practice session to date was an intermediate sideline toss from Young to wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan over cornerback Akayleb Evans , who was wearing a red non-contact jersey. Young fit the ball perfectly in front of McMillan to grab it right before heading out of bounds. 
 Third-string QB Kyle Trask , who was signed last week, fired an excellent deep ball shot to depth wide receiver Casey Washington for a touchdown in 11-on-11 drills.

title: 2026 Carolina Panthers: Projecting final 53-man roster
summary: While tight end is still a position of discussion for Carolina, questions remain at inside linebacker and O-line.
full_text:
CHARLOTTE, N.C. -- The Carolina Panthers open the 2026 NFL regular season against the Chicago Bears on Sept. 13 (1 p.m. ET, Fox) at Bank of America Stadium. But first, they play one more preseason game Friday against the Houston Texans (7 p.m. ET) and then must cut their roster to 53 players by 6 p.m. ET on Sunday.

 Who will make the team? Which positions have tough decisions on deck? And where might the lineup be deepest and thinnest this season?

 Darren Waller , a late-summer arrival, has shaken up the discussion at tight end. A competition for the second inside linebacker spot, between Trevin Wallace and Claudin Cherelus , still seems unsettled heading into the final week of the preseason. Plus, undrafted rookie quarterback Haynes King , who earned rave reviews for his performance in Canton, Ohio, earlier this month, is sidelined with a hamstring injury , and his recovery timeline could factor heavily into the roster math on cut-down day.

 Here is our projection for the 53-man roster for the Panthers.

 

 Quarterbacks (3) 
 Bryce Young , Kenny Pickett , Haynes King 

 

 Young is entering an all-important campaign with a potential contract extension riding on his success (or lack thereof). Pickett was signed to be Young's experienced backup, and while his passing prowess won't "wow" onlookers, he knows what he's doing when called upon.

 King had an explosive debut in the Hall of Fame game earlier this month, but his roster status depends on his hamstring injury sustained during the same outing. For now, though, he's a guy they shouldn't risk to waivers.

 
 Running backs (4) 
 Chuba Hubbard , Jonathon Brooks , Trevor Etienne , AJ Dillon 

 The Panthers will have a top rotation of Hubbard and Brooks with Etienne backing them up. However, Hubbard's recent hamstring injury and Brooks' history of ACL injuries might force the team to keep four running backs. Dillon has been featured heavily on special teams this summer.

 
 Wide receivers (6) 
 Tetairoa McMillan , Jalen Coker , Xavier Legette , Brycen Tremayne , Ja'seem Reed , Jimmy Horn Jr . 

 The top trio of McMillan, Coker and Legette was solidified when third-round rookie Chris Brazzell II underwent season-ending knee surgery earlier this month. Reed has flashed regularly during the summer, and Horn has had a nice preseason. Tremayne can play all three wide receiver spots and is among Carolina's top special teams players, so David Moore might need to settle for a practice squad spot.

 
 Tight ends (4) 
 Tommy Tremble , Mitchell Evans , Ja'Tavion Sanders , Feleipe Franks 

 The addition of Darren Waller raised eyebrows, but the lack of interest in him before his signing and his lack of workload before cuts could make him more of a practice-squad option, barring a trade of an incumbent tight end. Waller isn't subject to waivers so the Panthers can be strategic with the vested veteran's inclusion in and around the cut-down deadline. Tremble and Evans are likely to serve as the top two inline options at the position, while Sanders works in the slot in two tight end sets if he sticks around. Franks is a special teams standout and the offense made a concerted effort to get him involved in the passing game this summer.

 
 Offensive linemen (8) 
 Rasheed Walker , Damien Lewis , Luke Fortner , Rob Hunt , Monroe Freeling , Brady Christensen , Sam Hecht , Jake Curhan 

 

 With Taylor Moton (blood clot) set to miss time on the non-football illness (NFI) list and Ickey Ekwonu likely to follow suit on the physically unable to perform (PUP) list, the Panthers will rely on Walker and Freeling, the team's 2026 first-round pick, at left and right tackle, respectively. Hunt (back) and Lewis (calf) battled injuries this summer as well, but they'll be in the lineup in Week 1. Fortner is the new starting center, while Hecht, a 2026 fifth-round pick, will back him up. Christensen and Curhan are versatile deep reserves in theory. Center Nick Samac and offensive tackle Albert Reese IV should be prioritized for the practice squad if unclaimed on waivers.

 
 Defensive linemen (5) 
 Derrick Brown , Bobby Brown III , Cam Jackson , Lee Hunter , Aaron Hall 

 Defensive end Turk Wharton (neck) is likely to start the season on the PUP list. The Panthers will lean on Derrick and Bobby Brown and Jackson in the starting lineup. Hunter, the team's second-round pick this year, and Hall, an undrafted rookie, will fill out the rotation until Wharton returns, though Elijah Garcia and Jared Harrison-Hunte could be options for a potential sixth spot.

 
 Outside linebackers (5) 
 Jaelan Phillips , Patrick Jones II , Princely Umanmielen , Thomas Incoom , Trevis Gipson 

 With Nic Scourton set to spend the entire season on injured reserve, the Panthers will need to rely on Jones opposite Phillips in the starting lineup. Umanmielen, last year's third-round pick, should factor heavily into the rotation as well. Incoom and Gipson provide proven special teams value with the ability to rotate into the front seven.

 
 Inside linebackers (5) 
 Devin Lloyd , Trevin Wallace , Claudin Cherelus , Bam Martin-Scott , Jackson Kuwatch 

 The Panthers might be looking for an upgrade opposite Lloyd over the next few days. Wallace and Cherelus are still competing for the other starting job this summer and neither option has run away with the gig. Martin-Scott is a promising 2025 holdover, who has been a productive special teams player. Kuwatch, the team's 2026 seventh-round pick, is a long-term development keeper.

 
 Cornerbacks (5) 
 Jaycee Horn , Mike Jackson , Will Lee III , Chau Smith-Wade , Akayleb Evans 

 Horn and Jackson form one of the league's better cornerback tandems. Lee, the team's 2026 fourth-round pick, showed encouraging signs in coverage this summer. Smith-Wade and Corey Thornton competed for the starting nickel job in camp and the former has outperformed the latter throughout the summer. Evans is a quality gunner on special teams with experience on defense.

 
 Safeties (5) 
 Tre'von Moehrig , Nick Scott , Lathan Ransom , Zakee Wheatley , Isaiah Simmons 

 Moehrig is a Swiss Army knife within the back end of the defense, and Scott is a veteran who the staff appreciates for his communication skills and leadership. Ransom will factor into the "big nickel" package, and he can hold his own as a starter if needed. Wheatley has been an excellent open-field tackler throughout the preseason, and he has the makings of a future starter, while Simmons is going to be a special teams mainstay.

 
 Special teams (3) 
 JJ Jansen (LS), Sam Martin (P), Ryan Fitzgerald (K) 

 This trio has been established since Week 1 of last season. Jansen and Martin are as sturdy as they come at their positions, and Fitzgerald had an encouraging rookie campaign.

title: 2026 Chicago Bears: Projecting final 53-man roster
summary: Will Kyler Gordon start Chicago's season on reserve/PUP and miss the first four games? What then?
full_text:
LAKE FOREST, Ill. -- The Chicago Bears open the 2026 NFL regular season at the Carolina Panthers on Sept. 13 at Bank of America Stadium. But first, they play one more preseason game Saturday at the  Tennessee Titans  and then must cut their roster to 53 players by 6 p.m. ET on Sunday.

 Who will make the team? Which positions have tough decisions on deck? And where might the lineup be deepest and thinnest this season?

 The Bears entered training camp in search of a starting left tackle and had hoped to settle this position by now. Braxton Jones was the front-runner before missing more than a week because of injury while the Bears tried to see if Kiran Amegadjie or  Jedrick Wills Jr . could offer consistency.

 

 Entering the fourth week of camp, coach Ben Johnson delivered a plot twist ahead of practice No. 14. Jones and Theo Benedet will now battle it out at left tackle. Amegadjie and Wills have since moved over to right tackle with the backup offensive line units.

 Here is our projection for the 53-man roster for the Bears.

 

 Quarterbacks (3) 
 Caleb Williams , Tyson Bagent , Case Keenum 

 Williams' training camp experience is a night-and-day difference from his first under Johnson. The quarterback has taken control of what the Bears are trying to accomplish while stacking strong practices. The offense has consistently been the strongest unit on the field, which is a testament to Williams' command.

 

 Running backs (3) 
 D'Andre Swift , Kyle Monangai , Salvon Ahmed 

 Swift had arguably the best training camp of any offensive skill player. He and Monangai will continue to power a rushing attack that ranked third in 2025. Ahmed edges out former fourth-round pick  Roschon Johnson  for the role of RB3.

 
 Wide receivers (6) 
 Rome Odunze , Luther Burden III , Kalif Raymond , Jahdae Walker , Zavion Thomas , Kaden Davis 

 Like Walker did last year, Davis has made a compelling case for a roster spot if the Bears opt to keep six wide receivers. He has routinely made big plays in practice and snags the final spot over veterans Scotty Miller and Maurice Alexander .

 
 Tight ends (3) 
 Colston Loveland , Cole Kmet , Sam Roush 

 The Bears play multiple tight ends more than most NFL teams. Loveland led the team in receiving as a rookie and looks like he's primed for a breakout season after a dominant showing in camp.

 
 Offensive linemen (10) 
 Braxton Jones , Joe Thuney , Garrett Bradbury , Jonah Jackson , Darnell Wright , Ozzy Trapilo , Theo Benedet , Logan Jones , Luke Newman , Jordan McFadden 

 It took Trapilo seven months to get back on the field after rupturing a patella tendon, which is way ahead of where the Bears thought he would be before Week 1. He'll be on his own timeline to get up to speed, according to Johnson, but this news means a couple of things: Trapilo will account for a roster spot and not start the year on the physically unable to perform list. And when ready, the Bears get their left tackle back. Chicago can move interior lineman Caden Barnett , who received a sizable undrafted free agent contract, on the practice squad and part ways with Amegadjie and Wills.

 

 

 Defensive linemen (10) 

 Montez Sweat , Grady Jarrett , Gervon Dexter Sr ., Dayo Odeyingbo , Austin Booker , Daniel Hardy , Neville Gallimore , Kentavius Street , Jordan van den Berg , Marcus Davenport 

 Odeyingbo has had a solid camp eight months removed from rupturing an Achillies, and the Bears appear to have a plan for him at defensive end in their base structure before kicking him inside on passing downs. Booker is primed to take his next step in Dennis Allen's system, while Davenport, who played for the Bears' defensive coordinator in New Orleans, is inexpensive depth.  Shemar Turner  has missed all of training camp while recovering from an ACL tear. If the Bears believe Turner's return is not too far off, they can use one of two injured reserve spots at cut-down with a designation to return.

 
 Linebackers (5) 
 T.J. Edwards , Devin Bush , D'Marco Jackson , Jack Sanborn , Ruben Hyppolite II 

 Rookie Keyshaun Elliott started camp on PUP and hasn't been seen since. It's possible he stays there when cuts are made, paving the way for Hyppolite to be the fifth linebacker. The former fourth-round pick has bounced back nicely in training camp after an underwhelming rookie season.

 
 Cornerbacks (6) 
 Jaylon Johnson , Tyrique Stevenson , Malik Muhammad , Josh Blackwell , Jaylon Jones , Dontae Manning 

 Given the lack of a timeline for Kyler Gordon 's return from PUP, it's possible the Bears move him to reserve/PUP during cuts, where he must remain for the first four games. Muhammad has been the Bears' nickel in Gordon's absence. Manning snags the final spot over  Beanie Bishop Jr ., who will serve a suspension for the first three games, and Terell Smith , who continues to struggle to stay healthy.

 
 Safeties (4) 
 Cam Lewis , Dillon Thieneman , Xavier Woods , Skyler Thomas 

 With a four-to-six-month window to return from a knee injury, Coby Bryant likely lands on injured reserve and is simultaneously designated to return the day the roster is cut down. Lewis will take over in the meantime opposite rookie first-rounder Thieneman. The information the Bears have on top backup safety Elijah Hicks , who is on PUP, will determine whether he is healthy enough to return before cut-down day and take the fourth spot or pave the way for that opening to go to Thomas.

 
 Special teams (3) 
 Cairo Santos  (K), Tory Taylor  (P), Beau Gardner  (LS) 

 The kicking battery was solidified Aug. 9 when the Bears waived Luke Elkin, ending the long-snapper battle after two weeks of camp.
