title: 2026 Cincinnati Bengals: Projecting final 53-man roster
summary: There are some quality players who might end up getting squeezed on a strong Bengals roster.
full_text:
CINCINNATI -- The Cincinnati Bengals open the 2026 NFL regular season against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at 1 p.m. on Sept. 13. But first, they play one more preseason game (Friday against the Philadelphia Eagles ) and then must cut their roster to 53 players by 6 p.m. ET on Sunday.

 Who will make the team? Which positions have tough decisions on deck? And where might the lineup be deepest and thinnest this season?

 Former CFL standout Dohnte Meyers has made a strong impression this offseason and increased the competition among the wide receivers. Cincinnati will also have some tough decisions to make on the defensive line that features several new additions.

 Here is our projection for the 53-man roster for the Bengals.

 

 Quarterbacks (2) 
 Joe Burrow , Joe Flacco 

 The Bengals kept three quarterbacks late in the year, but with Burrow healthy to start the season, keeping two will give Cincinnati flexibility elsewhere on the roster. Josh Johnson is slated to be the QB3 while on the practice squad.

 
 Running backs (3) 
 Chase Brown , Samaje Perine , Tahj Brooks 

 This group will be one of the most important on the roster. Brown should have an elevated role in Cincinnati's new-look offense with Perine also seeing some usage on early downs. The coaching staff is high on Brooks as he enters his second season.

 
 Wide receivers (6) 
 Ja'Marr Chase , Tee Higgins , Andrei Iosivas , Mitchell Tinsley , Dohnte Meyers , Colbie Young 

 Meyers, the former CFL signee, was impressive throughout training camp and made a strong impression on everyone in the building. That gives him the edge over  Charlie Jones , who is one of the best returners in the NFL.

 
 

 Tight ends (5) 
 Mike Gesicki , Drew Sample , Tanner Hudson , Erick All Jr ., Jack Endries 

 Endries, a rookie who played the bulk of his career at Cal, looked good in the preseason opener. Those two factors could make  Cam Grandy  a practice squad option.

 
 Offensive linemen (9) 
 Orlando Brown Jr ., Dylan Fairchild , Ted Karras , Dalton Risner , Amarius Mims , Cody Ford , Jalen Rivers , Connor Lew , Brian Parker II 

 Swing tackle remains a big question. Jalen Rivers received some looks at that spot after Cody Ford had started out in that role at the beginning of training camp.

 

 Defensive linemen (10) 

 Boye Mafe , Cashius Howell , Shemar Stewart , Myles Murphy , Kris Jenkins Jr .,  B.J. Hill , Jonathan Allen , Landon Robinson , Dexter Lawrence II ,  T.J. Slaton Jr . 

 This was a tough call on the deepest group on the roster. Cedric Johnson , a sixth-round pick in 2024, had two sacks in nine games last season. But with five new defensive linemen (three tackles, two edge rushers), Johnson and fellow 2024 pick McKinnley Jackson are most likely to get squeezed here.

 
 

 Linebackers (4) 
 Barrett Carter , Demetrius Knight Jr ., Oren Burks , Swayze Bozeman 

 Bozeman quietly had a very strong camp and earned reps with the second-string defense. Cincinnati acquired him on waivers in May and he appears to be making the most of his opportunity.

 
 Cornerbacks (7) 
 DJ Turner II , Dax Hill , Jalen Davis , Josh Newton , Tacario Davis , DJ Ivey , Ja'Sir Taylor 

 Newton made a few splash plays throughout training camp, which put him in contention over other guys who were fighting to make the initial 53-man roster. That depth at cornerback is needed with the limited proven outside CB options behind Turner and Hill.

 
 Safeties (4) 
 Bryan Cook , Kyle Dugger , Jordan Battle , PJ Jules 

 Cook and Battle are the starters, with Duggar coming onto the field in heavier coverage packages. Jules has been solid on special teams over the years.

 
 Special teams (3) 
 Evan McPherson  (K), Ryan Rehkow  (P),  William Wagner  (LS) 

 Cincinnati has a stable operation between McPherson and Wagner, while Rehkow started to make strides toward the end of last season with his situational punting.

title: Browns turn to QB Watson with Sanders (and 2027 draft class) lurking
summary: The Browns' quest to answer the franchise's quarterback quandary brings them back to a 30-year-old who faces enormous pressure to succeed.
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns are taking another chance on  Deshaun Watson .

 Sixteen months after Browns owner Jimmy Haslam called his team's March 2022 trade for Watson -- which included three first-round picks and a fully guaranteed $230 million contract after more than two dozen women accused him of sexual assault and inappropriate conduct during massage sessions -- a " big swing-and-miss ," first-year coach Todd Monken named him Cleveland's Week 1 starting quarterback for the 2026 NFL season .

 Watson was named QB1 on Monday , concluding a competition with second-year quarterback Shedeur Sanders that began in April and stretched into the final weeks of training camp.

 "I have another shot. I have another chance. So I wanna make sure I take full responsibility of this opportunity," Watson told reporters on Monday.

 

 Over the past year-plus, the Browns have been in what general manager Andrew Berry called a "strategic pivot," parting ways with aging veterans and players with big contracts, and using their replenished draft stock to infuse the roster with young talent.

 However, Cleveland's quest to answer the franchise's quarterback quandary brings the team back to Watson, with not only Sanders but a highly touted 2027 draft class  of QB prospects lurking in the background.

 Does Watson, who has one year remaining on his contract, have a future with the Browns? As he made his return this spring and summer from a right Achilles tendon tear that required two surgeries and sidelined him for the entire 2025 season, the Browns' top decision-makers talked around the topic of Watson's place with the team long term.

 Cap considerations help explain why Watson, 30, is still on Cleveland's roster in 2026. After multiple contract restructures, releasing him now would result in an NFL-record $127 million dead salary cap charge. Wait until next offseason, and the Browns can cut Watson with a post-June 1 designation that splits a more palatable $86 million dead cap charge between the 2027 and 2028 seasons amid an ever-rising salary cap .

 Monken, one day before announcing his decision, said his starting QB choice would not be made with the future in mind but solely focused on giving his team the best opportunity in Week 1, when the Browns face the Jacksonville Jaguars on the road ( Sept. 13, 1 p.m. ET, CBS ). He also reiterated that, although he had conversations with Berry and team ownership, the decision at quarterback was his own.

 "I know what we think and what we see every day in our building and our players and the momentum we have. And we're 100% behind Deshaun," Monken said Monday.

 

 During Watson's stop-and-start tenure with the Browns, he has battled rust and injuries as he fights to recapture his former Pro Bowl form. In the 19 games he has played since joining Cleveland, his 33.1 Total QBR would rank last among active QBs if he had enough starts to qualify.

 His latest bout -- one he called a "mental battle" -- occurred Saturday in his own stadium, where he was met with boos in his first home game since tearing his Achilles in October 2024; then, the injury was met with cheers .

 Watson bemoaned the reaction Saturday, calling it "disrespectful." He also said that if he was named the starter, he might play what amounts to "17 away games," though Monken later said the QB's comments came from an emotional player who was frustrated with a lackluster second-half performance.

 For a franchise that has started 42 different quarterbacks since returning to Cleveland in 1999, the question for the Browns has rarely centered on who is under center but rather who is up next. In this case, it could be Sanders, the 2025 fifth-round pick who started the final seven games of his rookie season and went 3-4 in his starts. However, his 18.9 QBR would have ranked last among qualifying quarterbacks. 

 Though Sanders will begin his second season on the bench, Monken has consistently praised his growth in both pre-snap operation and post-snap execution. If Watson struggles, Monken could turn to a player he also touted as a viable starter when discussing his quarterback situation during OTAs in the spring.

 "We met this morning for a good long time and all he had was a smile on his face, because he understands what really is in front of him, not really a short-term, maybe long-term decision," Monken said of Sanders. "I mean, this is like a player: he's going to work his butt off to get better. And he has already."

 

 While the Browns' brass hasn't publicly acknowledged the notion of a rebuild, Cleveland will field one of the youngest rosters in the NFL in 2026. The team's trade  of two-time NFL Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett lowered external expectations for the upcoming season even further, but it was executed with the franchise's short- and long-term future in mind.

 The Browns' win total for 2026 is set at 5.5; however, the team has plenty of young talent to build around in the coming years. Haslam said his sights are on contending in 2027, when the team's young core, which includes linebacker Carson Schwesinger , running back Quinshon Judkins , tight end Harold Fannin Jr ., and rookie receivers KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston , begins to enter its prime.

 That could make Cleveland, which owns a pair of first-round picks in what is already becoming a hyped 2027 draft quarterback class, a prime destination for a passer to bring it all together.

 "Andrew and his team will be keeping a close eye on the quarterbacks," Haslam said at the league meetings in March. "Now if you'll remember, we thought this time last year, this was going to be a great quarterback class. Maybe it will be, but if it doesn't shapen up ... I think you just have to see how things [pan] out."

 Watson, starting Week 1, will get another chance to salvage his albatross contract. If he falters, Sanders will be next. And if Sanders doesn't show enough promise, the 2027 quarterback draft class will come into focus and QB No. 43 might be up.

title: Cowboys OL Shiyazh Pete, Schottenheimer reflect on viral postgame speech
summary: Shiyazh Pete, a member of the Navajo Nation, said the reaction from fans during the Cowboys game against the Cardinals was overwhelming to him.
full_text:
FRISCO, Texas -- When Brian Schottenheimer had undrafted rookie offensive lineman Shiyazh Pete break the team down after the Dallas Cowboys beat the Arizona Cardinals , the head coach had no idea the moment would go viral.

 "It's amazing that our social media team, the media in general, captured it because it was what this team and really the game of football is all about," Schottenheimer said. "It's a storyline where you have a guy who's fighting his butt off trying to make the team, but when you give him an opportunity, deservedly so, to address the group, it was very raw. It was very authentic."

 Pete became the first member of the Navajo Nation, which is the largest Native American reservation in the United States, to join an NFL team when he signed with the Cowboys. Playing in Arizona, home to a sizable Native American population, Pete had a large number of fans in the stadium.

 

 Because of the reaction, Schottenheimer invited Pete to talk to the team postgame.

 "Well, that was an incredible win," Pete told the team on a video released by the Cowboys. "I am very fortunate to be amongst you and to play in the same field and wear the same star holden on our chest. And I'm proud of us, proud of how far we've come. Man, this game, fate brought us here as strangers, but this game, this star, this team will make us brothers."

 

 The locker room erupted, just the way the fans reacted inside the stadium.

 "The standing ovation was incredible," Pete said. "I want to take the moment to thank all the fans, and the people who showed up to support me, and to celebrate my name and to wear my jersey. I lost count of how many Navajo Nation flags I saw. I saw a Salish Nation flag as well, which was awesome."

 Pete played just six snaps in the fourth quarter and is a long shot to make the roster, but the reaction from fans was overwhelming to him.

 "It's definitely etched in the history books, I'll tell you that. It was incredible," Pete said. "I'm trying to find the words of how special and impactful that really was. The fact that I am able to participate on the field and conduct my play to the best of my ability and fans support me for that, for who I am, it's incredible."

 Schottenheimer recalled that during a ride to the airport in the offseason, the driver told him of an interaction he'd had with Pete the day before.

 "He said, 'Man, I drove one of your players, and he was the most incredible human being I've ever been,'" Schottenheimer said. "He was talking about Pete, and it was really cool. And the players, they love one another, but he captured the moment.

 "He has a better track record than I do of speeches after wins. And his language is much cleaner, which is good too. But I thought it was awesome."

title: Dallas Cowboys: Projecting final 53-man roster
summary: Who will back up Dak Prescott, and how will the CB corps and RB room flesh out?
full_text:
OXNARD, Calif. -- The Dallas Cowboys open the 2026 NFL regular season at the New York Giants on Sept. 13 at MetLife Stadium. But first, they play one more preseason game (Friday against the New Orleans Saints ) and then must cut their roster to 53 players by 6 p.m. ET on Sunday.

 Who will make the team? Which positions have tough decisions on deck? And where might the lineup be deepest and thinnest this season?

 Despite a productive training camp, the Cowboys have some questions about depth at cornerback, linebacker and running back. The backup quarterback job between Sam Howell and Joe Milton III remains up for grabs, too, and might make them keep three quarterbacks on the 53-man roster.

 Here is our final projection for the 53-man roster for the Cowboys.

 

 

 Quarterbacks (3) 

 Dak Prescott ,  Sam Howell , Joe Milton III 

 Maybe in a perfect world the Cowboys would rather go with two quarterbacks, but Milton and Howell have fared well and if quarterback is the most important spot on the team, then maybe it's wise to keep three.

 

 Running backs (4) 

 Javonte Williams , Malik Davis , Jaydon Blue , Hunter Luepke 

 Davis didn't enter camp as the No. 2 running back despite his work last season, but he earned it this summer. Blue's playmaking gives him the final nod over  Phil Mafah and Israel Abinkanda , both of whom could be on the practice squad.

 

 Wide receivers (6) 

 CeeDee Lamb , George Pickens , Ryan Flournoy , KaVontae Turpin , Jonathan Mingo , Camden Brown 

 The top four have been a given. The last two have been in a state of flux. Brown, undrafted out of Georgia Southern, was able to take to the game what he did in practice. Mingo has earned his way into the mix with a solid summer performance.

 

 Tight ends (3) 

 Jake Ferguson , Brevyn Spann-Ford , Luke Schoonmaker 

 No movement in this group other than Spann-Ford being the backup to Ferguson over Schoonmaker, a 2023 second-round pick. But the Cowboys will use all three in games.

 

 Offensive linemen (9) 

 
 Tyler Guyton , Tyler Smith , Cooper Beebe , Tyler Booker , Terence Steele , T.J. Bass , Nate Thomas , Drew Shelton , Nick Leverett 

 Guyton has locked down the left tackle spot with a good camp. The depth beyond Bass is a question. Thomas looks like the swing tackle for now, but he has lacked consistency. Like a lot of teams, look for the Cowboys to be active in potentially filling their last couple of spots here.

 

 Defensive linemen (5) 

 Quinnen Williams , Kenny Clark , Otito Ogbonnia , Jonathan Bullard , LT Overton 

 This might be the deepest the Cowboys have been at defensive tackle in years. All five can play, but Bullard has been out of practice for a couple of weeks with a soft-tissue injury. Ogbonnia has been a pleasant surprise.

 

 Outside linebackers (6) 

 Rashan Gary , Donovan Ezeiruaku , Von Miller , Malachi Lawrence , Marist Liufau , James Houston 

 The arrival of Miller brought the last spot down to Liufau, Houston and Sam Williams . Liufau is the better special-teamer and has worked a lot with the first group. Houston has a knack for finding the quarterback, so he gets the edge over Williams.

 

 Inside linebackers (4) 

 DeMarvion Overshown , Dee Winters , Jaishawn Barham , Shemar James 

 Overshown won't be able to answer the durability question until he actually plays a lot, but he has seemed like a good fit in Christian Parker's scheme. Winters has come on late in camp. Barham's development was slowed a little by a groin injury, but they have a role for him. It was tough to leave Justin Barron off the list.

 

 Cornerbacks (5) 

 DaRon Bland , Cobie Durant , Shavon Revel Jr. , Veteran not on roster, Devin Moore 

 Depth is a worry beyond the top three. While Revel has had an excellent camp, he has to show he can do it in the regular season. The fourth corner might not be on the roster at the moment. Adding a veteran free agent or making a small trade for one is not out of the question.

 

 Safeties (5) 

 Jalen Thompson , Caleb Downs , Malik Hooker , P.J. Locke , Markquese Bell 

 Like defensive tackle, the Cowboys like their depth. Maybe a team needing safety help would swing a deal for Bell, but he can be a core special-teamer. Tough calls on Alijah Clark and Julius Wood .

 

 Special teams (3) 

 Brandon Aubrey  (K), Bryan Anger  (P), Trent Sieg  (LS) 

 The Cowboys believe they have one of the NFL's best trios.

title: Cowboys camp wrap-up: Trackman Dak, GM Von and hot dogs
summary: Takeaways from the Cowboys' month in California, including a good first impression from rookie Caleb Downs.
full_text:
FRISCO, Texas -- After 28 days away from home, the Dallas Cowboys are back in Texas.

 A lot happened in the 13 practices in California, including two joint workouts against the Los Angeles Rams and New Orleans Saints , and two preseason games at the Seattle Seahawks and Arizona Cardinals .

 The Cowboys will hold two practices this week inside Ford Center at The Star before closing the preseason against the Saints on Friday at AT&T Stadium (8:00 p.m. ET, ESPN Unlimited). Before you know it, the Sept. 13 opener against the New York Giants will be here.

 But before we talk about Giants coach John Harbaugh, quarterback  Jaxson Dart , linebacker  Abdul Carter and wide receiver  Malik Nabers , let's look at some picked-up pieces from the Cowboys' time in Oxnard.

 

 

 Trackman Dak 

 Dak Prescott has gotten into golf in a major way the past couple of years, but he has not used Trackman, a device that uses radar and cameras, to measure his swing. He does, however, use it on the football field.

 A staffer aligns the device behind the offensive huddle so Trackman can document and digest all of the readings from a Prescott pass. It can tell the velocity on throws to his left versus throws to his right, and whether one is stronger than the other.

 "I can go look back and see the velocity on certain balls. I can see the apex," Prescott said. "Something that truly interests me is they're trying to get a lot of go-ball throws or post throws or big plays thrown. You want to put air on it, but you also want to make sure you don't underthrow the guy, and just having that data to go back to and look at my apex.

 "There's a certain apex that I want to accomplish on certain passes. And when they're off, I can go back and I can look. And if it's not, I can easily say that's me versus the receiver's not running or doing this."

 

 Answering the call 

 No player was under more scrutiny when training camp started than left tackle Tyler Guyton .

 He held the key to the offense. If he performed well, the Cowboys could keep Tyler Smith at left guard, his preferred position. What was supposed to be a competition between Guyton and Nate Thomas never really materialized in part because Thomas had an inconsistent camp but also because of how well Guyton played.

 

 Guyton has been dealing with a right elbow issue that has knocked him out for a few plays here and there, and the proof of his growth will come when the games start for real.

 Offensive coordinator Klayton Adams does not want to jinx things.

 "I'm happy to be to the point that we're at in training camp and him being able to put practices back to back," Adams said. "They all haven't been perfect, but they haven't been for any of our guys.

 "Trying to find consistency and confidence in his play has been kind of a special journey watching him, because I'm proud of the work that he's put in and the mental toughness that he's developed and some of the maturity. The maturation process that he's gone through is off the charts."

 

 Good first impression 

 On defense, it's hard not to say first-round safety  Caleb Downs  has made the best first impression.

 "He has a streak on the field," defensive coordinator Christian Parker said. "Obviously, you don't know that until you're in those competitive environments with somebody, but he definitely has a fire to him and an edge."

 

 On offense, the answer is a little different because everybody who excelled in 2025 is back in 2026. Undrafted rookie receiver  Camden Brown , however, is the answer.

 Brown made plays in Oxnard and then scored two highlight-level touchdowns in the preseason opener against the Seahawks.

 "When the ball is in the air, it's mine," Brown said. "That's always been the mindset from Georgia Southern to Auburn. Just having that mentality because I feel like just playing football in general is having the right mentality."

 

 

 Future calling 
 When his playing career ends, Von Miller wants to continue with football.

 He is about to enter his 16th season in the NFL. He played for the Denver Broncos ,  Los Angeles Rams , Buffalo Bills and Washington Commanders before joining the Cowboys. He has had hundreds of teammates and watched thousands of hours of film, if not more.

 "I feel like the things that I've learned over time is how to build great teams," Miller said.

 He remembers seeing linebacker  James Houston , now a teammate in Dallas, have a two-sack game for the Detroit Lions in his NFL debut against Buffalo while Miller was playing for the Bills.

 "I'm a fan of football in general. My dream is to be a GM, front office exec, director of player personnel," Miller said. "When you have that dream, you've got to love football and you've got to love the players that make it happen. So even though some of these guys haven't been my teammates, I know a little bit about everybody."

 

 What do coaches dream of? 

 As offensive coordinator, there are lots of things that go through the mind of Adams, such as hot dogs.

 Miked up for a practice by the Cowboys' social media team, Adams joked that a coach would have to pay a $100 fine for the "hot dog fridge" for not telling other coaches he was miked up.

 So what is the "hot dog fridge?"

 

 "Well, it's something that I'm working on here, kind of in the back of my mind, is how can you really have a break room or a snack room if you don't have a hot dog fridge?" Adams said. "And if you're going to have a hot dog fridge, you've got to have high quality hot dogs in it. And if you're going to have high quality hot dogs in it, we've got to have brioche buns and maybe some pretzel buns.

 "So these are all things that we're working on. Maybe an industrial size 7-Eleven hot dog roller, I don't know. I don't know. But these are just things that roll around in the back of my mind."

 Adams said he had a hot dog epiphany when he visited Disneyland with his kids.

 "I was trying to steam the bun, I was trying to toast the bun, and the guy at Disneyland goes, 'No, man, put it in the bun and wrap it in foil and let the hot dog steam the bun.' It's been revolutionary."

 

 Family day 

 Players' families have long been training camp visitors, but in recent years, the Cowboys have started a family day in which all 91 players invite their spouses, partners, children, parents and siblings to camp for a special day.

 After practice, the entire group goes to a nearby beach to enjoy each other's company away from football. Bludso's BBQ caters the food. There's music and games, like cornhole, as everybody mingles for a couple hours.

 It's an important part of camp to Schottenheimer.

 "You can't preach brotherhood and family in your building with your team and not include the ones that you love that are not in the building," Schottenheimer said. "It's something that my wife, Gemmi, and I, we always said when we get our shot to do it, we were going to make sure the families were loved, the families were a part of it.

 "We work crazy hours. We all leave at some point, but we want the people that are outside of our four walls of The Star to feel very much a part of it."

title: Broncos QB Bo Nix hopes slowing down leads to improvement
summary: Nix's mobility and sack avoidance have led to success, but the Broncos think slowing him down and getting his footwork right could produce more big plays.
full_text:
ENGLEWOOD, Colo. -- The Denver Broncos believe they can do big things with their passing offense this season -- if quarterback Bo Nix can find a better rhythm from the ground up.

 Nix is coming off his second straight season with at least 25 touchdown passes, and he has brought Denver to the playoffs in both of his pro seasons -- including a 14-3 record and an AFC Championship Game trip in 2025. But coach Sean Payton and offensive coordinator Davis Webb have made it a priority to better sync Nix's footwork with the routes his receivers run on each play. And they think that could smooth out some rough spots in the quarterback's game, allowing him to reach the next level in Year 3. 

 "He's a real good foot athlete ... I think it's one of his gifts," Payton said of Nix, who spent the offseason recovering from two surgeries following a fractured right ankle in the divisional playoffs . But Payton also said there is work to be done "within the framework of each pass play, the definement of a three-[step drop], three no hitch, one big [step], five and a hitch, some of those specifics that put him exactly in time with the depth of the route."

 

 Tucked into Payton's description is the question of the pace at which Nix drops back from center or sets his feet from the shotgun to position himself to throw so it matches the cadence of his receivers' routes. The Broncos want Nix to continue to think fast, but their emphasis is getting his feet right and better timed with his progressions through his receivers' routes.

 "I think it's [about] understanding what we're doing, so we can attack defenses," Nix said.

 Despite the successful 2025 season, the Broncos found they didn't consistently challenge defenses down the field. And when they did, Nix wavered in accuracy more significantly than most of the league's top passers.

 Nix was 28th in the league in yards per attempt last season (6.4). He finished 26th in the league in completion percentage over expectation (minus-2.1 percentage points), per NFL Next Gen Stats, and was 12th in completions of 20 or more yards. Nix completed only 44.1% of his pass attempts of 10 or more air yards, along with 36.1% of attempts of 20 or more air yards.

 Some of those troublesome numbers stem from Nix being one of the NFL's quicker thinkers, which helped Denver get 12 comeback victories a year ago. But they also represent a quarterback who doesn't always have the correct timing when he sets up to throw, sometimes getting to the top of his designed dropback too quickly and making his progressions a bit too rapid.

 "He does a very good job of avoiding [a] sack -- the minus play -- and because of that he's very good with his progression." Payton said. "He's not someone who's slow to progress and slow to process, it's the other way ... but I'd rather deal with that than a slow processor who's getting sacked."

 Chase Daniel, who spent five seasons as the  New Orleans Saints ' backup quarterback when Payton coached there, has studied Nix's play extensively, occasionally attending Broncos quarterback meetings over Nix's first two seasons. He sees what Payton described and said it will require Nix to realize that not all dropbacks are created equal in Payton's playbook.

 

 "Sean's offense is very much timing and rhythm," said Daniel, who now works with ESPN as an analyst. "So, there could be three different five-step drops, for example -- a slow-rhythmic one, a normal one and a really quick one. And [Nix], from what I saw, he hadn't mastered that in terms of timing with the play because there's different routes.

 "At times, Bo sped up his feet so he's already at the top of his drop and no receiver is out of his break, so ... he started to get to the checkdown too quick. 
 
"I don't think that's not him seeing it, I think it's the footwork didn't match up with the routes," he added.

 In those situations, Nix is faced with either trying to squeeze a pass to a receiver who hasn't arrived at the point in the route where the play was designed or just moving to the next progression. And a quarterback who has been drilled not to put the ball in harm's way -- like Nix -- will likely go to the next read.

 This causes a chain effect in which Nix gets to each progression prematurely, forcing him to arrive at his checkdown options or move out of the pocket before it's necessary. As a result, 395 of Nix's league-leading 612 attempts (64.5%) were within 10 yards of the line of scrimmage, with 121 (19.7%) thrown behind the line. Compare that with MVP Matthew Stafford , who threw 59 of his 597 attempts behind the line of scrimmage last season.

 Payton believes that Nix's footwork mechanics are sound and that he has the necessary decision-making ability. Nix's next step is to find the pacing and rhythm of each play yet still know when to use his mobility.

 It was part of an extensive offseason review of Nix and the offense by the coaching staff. And Webb said Nix has shown progress in training camp.

 "It's noticeable the strides he's taken, hanging on [the first read], getting to two, to three, then using his legs," Webb said.

 Webb has also said the Broncos have to be cognizant of how they "marry'' Nix's first reads to the second and third reads, and to how Webb is sequencing playcalls.

 Payton has been steadfast that Nix has the arm strength to punish defenses down the field if everything else is right. The arrival of wide receiver Jaylen Waddle -- who Nix called an "explosive playmaker" -- changes the dynamic, and Courtland Sutton said he has already seen the effects of the work his QB has put in.

 

 "He's in this spot where he's understanding the game at such a different level," Sutton said. 
 
"He's seen what defenses do, seeing what leverages are getting thrown at him ... and [the big plays] are in there, we've seen them out here more already, and our defense is hard to get."

 Nix said he believes it's all linked to simply understanding the position and the team's playbook.

 "When you have a second-nature thought process and you know the play and you're not thinking about operation, or emotion or a route concept or a handoff point, you can attack the defense in a little bit more of a strategic way," Nix said. "So my eyes are up a little bit more. I just feel comfortable.

 "I'm excited about the growth and know that there's plenty left, but also I feel strongly where I'm at."

title: 2026 Denver Broncos: Projecting final 53-man roster
summary: The Broncos have mostly run it back with last season's AFC Championship Game roster, but there are a couple positions worth watching.
full_text:
ENGLEWOOD, Colo. -- The Denver Broncos open the 2026 NFL regular season at the Kansas City Chiefs on Sept. 14 at 8:15 p.m. ET . in the season's "Monday Night Football" opener. But first, they play one more preseason game ( Friday against the Minnesota Vikings ) and then must cut their roster to 53 players by 6 p.m. ET on Sunday.

 Who will make the team? Which positions have tough decisions on deck? And where might the lineup be deepest and thinnest this season?

 These questions are difficult for a team with very few landing spots for new arrivals. Wide receiver Jaylen Waddle was the big-ticket acquisition , but 20 of the 22 starters on offense and defense from January's AFC Championship Game were on the training camp roster. Denver re-signed 17 of the 21 of its players who had been scheduled to be unrestricted, restricted or exclusive rights free agents. So, the Broncos will have multiple choices for the final spots on the depth chart in each position group as coach Sean Payton tries to avoid the cut-down nightmare.

 Here is our projection for the 53-man roster for the Broncos.

 

 Quarterbacks (3) 
 Bo Nix , Sam Ehlinger , Jarrett Stidham 

 The Broncos rostered two QBs in 2025, as Ehlinger opened the season on the practice squad. Payton said Ehlinger turned down offers last August for an active roster spot to stay on Denver's practice squad and turned down a late-season offer for a roster spot from the Colts to remain with the Broncos. He has looked like the No. 2 in camp practices this summer, so it's hard to believe they let him go now. Stidham could draw some trade interest if there are injuries across the league.

 
 Running backs (4) 
 J.K. Dobbins , Jonah Coleman , RJ Harvey , Jaleel McLaughlin 

 The fourth spot will likely be McLaughlin or Tyler Badie . McLaughlin is a more explosive player, but Payton has consistently used Badie in a variety of situations. Coleman, a rookie fourth-rounder, showed plenty of potential throughout the preseason and already projects to get some early-down touches.

 
 Fullbacks (1) 
 Adam Prentice 

 Payton likes having a fullback in his offense and says he'll always want to have a player in that role. He has had tight ends lined up there at times in the past, but Prentice's portfolio fits exactly what his coach wants from the position.

 
 Wide receivers (5) 
 Jaylen Waddle , Courtland Sutton , Marvin Mims Jr ., Troy Franklin , Pat Bryant 

 If a quarterback is released and the Broncos keep only two passers, perhaps there's room for a sixth player here. They have had a clear top five throughout camp, but Lil'Jordan Humphrey is a long-time Payton favorite, and players such as undrafted rookie Cameron Ross and Michael Bandy have flashed plenty in the preseason.

 
 Tight ends (4) 
 Evan Engram , Adam Trautman , Nate Adkins , Justin Joly 

 Caleb Lohner , who has missed the preseason with a foot injury, could alter this calculus if the Broncos believe he is close to a return for the start of the regular season. Besides Lohner, the final spot could well come down to two rookies -- fifth-rounder Joly, a more refined pass catcher, or seventh-rounder Dallen Bentley , a more polished in-line option.

 
 

 Offensive linemen (9) 
 Garett Bolles , Ben Powers , Luke Wattenberg , Quinn Meinerz , Mike McGlinchey , Alex Palczewski , Calvin Throckmorton , Frank Crum , Kage Casey 

 Casey, a fourth-round rookie, is a multi-positional player who likely wouldn't make it through waivers if the Broncos tried to get him to the practice squad. Throckmorton has shown his versatility, as well, with a start at center in the preseason opener adding to his work at guard. There's a numbers crunch here overall, as the Broncos have at least 10 linemen capable of making the roster, with  Alex Forsyth and Matt Peart  under consideration.

 
 Defensive linemen (6) 
 Zach Allen , D.J. Jones , Malcolm Roach , Eyioma Uwazurike , Tyler Onyedim , Jordan Jackson 

 In this scenario, Jackson edges out Sai'vion Jones , last year's third-round pick, for the sixth spot. There is always potential for them to keep seven here, but the entire depth chart is tight, making for squeaky tight fits throughout. Uwazurike has shown far more point-of-attack strength in camp and is in line for an increased workload.

 
 Edge rushers (4) 
 Nik Bonitto , Jonah Elliss , Que Robinson , Jonathon Cooper 

 The Broncos have allowed Cooper to practice throughout training camp and play in the preseason after his two arrests on domestic violence charges in a seven-day span in June. While his roster spot might have looked shakier in the spring given the tone of the team's statements at the time, he's on track to be on the 53 unless he is suspended by the NFL before Week 1 under the personal conduct policy. In that scenario, Dondrea Tillman likely earns the fourth spot.

 
 Linebackers (4) 
 Alex Singleton , Justin Strnad , Red Murdock , Jordan Turner 

 Undrafted rookie Taurean York certainly did enough to earn a spot, but it's just a matter of whether the Broncos think two rookies (Murdock being the other) are ready to be the primary backups behind the two starters. Drew Sanders ' injury in the preseason opener is a factor, but the Broncos have liked Turner's progress and physicality. He has also gained momentum since returning from the PUP (physically unable to perform) list to open camp.

 
 

 Cornerbacks (5) 
 Pat Surtain II , Riley Moss , Ja'Quan McMillian , Jahdae Barron , Kris Abrams-Draine 

 This is perhaps the league's deepest cornerback room and was likely the most difficult roster spot for anyone else to break into. Other teams have looked at this group with interest, but the Broncos continue to keep it intact.

 
 Safeties (5) 
 Talanoa Hufanga , Brandon Jones , Devon Key ,  Taylor Rapp , JL Skinner 

 With concerns about defensive depth, the Broncos added Rapp before their second preseason game, which tightens up the depth chart even more. Key was an All-Pro special teamer last season. On another team, rookie Miles Scott 's work in training camp would have been enough for a roster spot, but Skinner's special teams ability might be the difference.

 
 Special teams (3) 
 Wil Lutz (K), Jeremy Crawshaw (P), Mitchell Fraboni (LS) 

 The Broncos brought in rookie long-snapper Luke Basso to share some of Fraboni's workload in the offseason program and camp, but this group returns every player.

title: 2026 Detroit Lions: Projecting final 53-man roster
summary: Who will make the team? Which positions have tough decisions on deck? Lions reporter Eric Woodyard makes his predictions.
full_text:
DETROIT -- The  Lions  open the 2026 NFL regular season against the  New Orleans Saints  on Sept. Sept. 13 at Ford Field. But first, they play one more preseason game (Saturday against the Indianapolis Colts ) and then must cut their roster to 53 players by 6 p.m. ET on Sunday.

 Who will make the team? Which positions have tough decisions on deck? And where might the lineup be deepest and thinnest this season?

 Despite a down season in which Detroit missed the playoffs for the first time since 2022, the Lions (9-8) still finished with a winning record for the fourth consecutive campaign in 2025. But for coach Dan Campbell and an organization with championship aspirations, that wasn't good enough.

 One of the biggest questions coming out of training camp is who will begin the season as Detroit's starting center after veteran Cade Mays suffered a wrist injury. There are also some lingering concerns within the secondary, as safeties Kerby Joseph (knee) and Brian Branch (Achilles) are unlikely to be back ahead of Week 1. However, the offense still has the potential to be one of the most explosive units in the league under first-year coordinator Drew Petzing.

 Here is our projection for the 53-man roster for the Lions.

 

 

 Quarterbacks   (2) 

 Jared Goff , Joshua Dobbs 

 After veteran Teddy Bridgewater unexpectedly retired during training camp, the Lions had to pivot by signing Dobbs to play behind Goff. Undrafted rookie Luke Altmyer was having a solid camp, but the Lions will likely keep him around for the practice squad.

 

 Running backs (4) 

 Jahmyr Gibbs , Isiah Pacheco , Sione Vaki , Jacob Saylors 

 Gibbs is gearing up for a big season in which he is projected to take the bulk of the snaps as the team's unquestioned RB1, but he will have no shortage of talent around him. Former All-UFL performer Saylors has also turned heads throughout the preseason and training camp.

 

 Wide receivers (5) 

 Amon-Ra St. Brown , Jameson Williams , Isaac TeSlaa , Greg Dortch , Dominic Lovett 

 Injured reserve: WR Kendrick Law 

 To no surprise, St. Brown and Williams have made big plays throughout training camp, but the veteran Dortch has been impressive on offense and special teams. Campbell has been pleased with watching him and said he has been "even better than I thought" while reuniting with new OC Petzing, after their days with the Arizona Cardinals .

 

 Tight ends (3) 

 Sam LaPorta , Brock Wright , Tyler Conklin 

 Following a season-ending back injury, LaPorta has returned to full strength as he enters Year 4, which will undoubtedly boost the offense. However, Wright has also earned the trust of Petzing and could benefit from more opportunities behind LaPorta. Petzing described Wright as "arguably one of the most reliable pros in this organization just in terms of the role he has for us as an offense."

 

 Offensive linemen (9) 

 

 Penei Sewell , Blake Miller , Larry Borom , Seth McLaughlin , Tate Ratledge , Christian Mahogany , Miles Frazier , Ben Bartch , Juice Scruggs 

 Non-Football Injury list: Giovanni Manu 

 Former Panthers center Mays is expected to miss 8 eight to 10 weeks and will likely start the season on injured reserve. Mays was targeted by Detroit this offseason as an unrestricted free agent to help the unit after the Lions' offensive line struggled in 2025. Without Mays, the Lions continued to experimented with Scruggs, McLaughlin and Michael Niese at center as they search for the best fit at the position.

 

 Defensive linemen/Edge rushers   (10) 

 Alim McNeill , Tyler Lacy , Tyleik Williams , Skyler Gill-Howard , Levi Onwuzurike , Chris Smith ,  Aidan Hutchinson , Derrick Moore , DJ Wonnum , Ahmed Hassanein 

 Lacy is entering his second season with the Lions. He has emerged as a standout throughout training camp and is projected to be a starter. Campbell described Lacy and Onwuzurike as "two of our most powerful D-linemen that we have."

 "You talk about 'knock back and they are hard to move," Campbell said on Aug. 16.

 

 Linebackers   (6) 

 Jack Campbell , Malcolm Rodriguez , Derrick Barnes , Trevor Nowaske , Devin White , Damone Clark 

 Jimmy Rolder , a fourth-round selection out of Michigan, was off to a promising start throughout the offseason training program but will likely begin the season on injured reserve after suffering a leg injury early in training camp. The Lions signed free agent linebacker White to add depth after Rolder's injury and White has pushed hard for a starting spot.

 

 Cornerbacks   (8) 

 D.J. Reed , Nick Whiteside , Rock Ya-Sin , Ennis Rakestraw Jr ., Roger McCreary , Khalil Dorsey , Keith Abney II , Christian Izien 

 The Lions released Terrion Arnold , a first-round pick in 2024, after he was arrested on felony charges of armed robbery and kidnapping in June. Detroit will now be counting on Reed and Ya-Sin to anchor the secondary after Arnold's release, which left the Lions thin at the cornerback spot.

 

 Safeties (3) 

 Avonte Maddox , Chuck Clark , Thomas Harper 

 Both Joseph and Branch will likely begin the 2026 season on injured reserve, while Clark and Maddox are expected to start in Week 1 after getting the bulk of the first-team reps throughout camp. The Lions won't rush back Joseph and Branch until they're fully healthy, but there is a chance that they could return for practices later in training camp or possibly early September.

 

 Special teams   (3) 

 Jake Bates  (K), Jack Fox  (P), Hogan Hatten  (LS) 

 This trio has become a mainstay in Detroit for three straight seasons. No one should be surprised by this unit. Fox received First-Team AP All-Pro honors in 2024.

title: Keisean Nixon fights his way back to top cornerback spot in camp
summary: Rob Demovsky reports on Keisean Nixon's push to reclaim the top cornerback role.

title: 2026 Green Bay Packers training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Catch up on our daily updates from Packers training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. Packers reporter Rob Demovsky has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Packers camp. Will the revamped WR corps help QB Jordan Love and the offense take another step? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Catch up on all the updates, including the Packers' top camp performer and biggest lingering question as preseason games begin.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news out of Packers camp 
 
 Matt LaFleur, Mike LaFleur ready for Packers-Cardinals work 
 CB Keisean Nixon not guaranteed starting role with Packers 
 Aaron Rodgers wishes game at Lambeau, discusses retirement return 
 Packers QB Love expected to play in first preseason game 
 Micah Parsons: Playing vs. Cowboys in Week 6 'realistic' 
 Packers RT changes last name to Bako-Bewele to honor heritage 
 Packers star TE Tucker Kraft activated off PUP after ACL recovery 
 Packers CEO: Team needs financial bump to stay competitive 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 24 

 Enter the names Matthew Golden and Barryn Sorrell into a search engine and you'll find a picture of them fishing together, a congratulatory social media post from Golden to Sorrell during the 2025 draft, a video on the Packers' website of the two of them engaged in a toy boxing match. 

 
The former teammates at the University of Texas even have lockers right next to each other at Lambeau Field.

 
None of that stopped them from getting into it during Monday's practice.

 
They started what was the closest thing to a training camp fight we've seen here this summer. Golden appeared to take exception to something Sorrell did at the end of a play, and tempers flared. Players came off the sideline and at least one player, linebacker Zaire Franklin , appeared to take a swing at someone.

 
"You know how it is when you've got a brother-type thing," Sorrell said, glancing at Golden's empty locker. "Me and Matt are always getting into it. It's just how our relationship is. Today it got out on the football a little bit and everybody thought we were like so serious. The whole time we were joking around a little bit. Like I said, it's football. It's how it gets. It's fun."

 
This on a day when Packers coach Matt LaFleur warned that there will be consequences if anyone fights during Wednesday's joint practice with the Cardinals.

 
Golden was not in the locker room after practice, but Sorrell said they made up quickly after a practice that was dominated by the defense.

 
"When [LaFleur] called us all up, we were dapping it up, we were joking about it and stuff and everything," Sorrell said. "It's just part of the game."

 More observations: 

 
 Running back Josh Jacobs took part in his first 11-on-11 work since his Aug. 6 groin injury. Jacobs had returned to practice last week on a limited basis but did not do any team periods until Monday. 
 Keisean Nixon , who appears to be in a fight for a starting cornerback job, made one of his biggest plays of camp with a leaping interception of  Jordan Love to score a win for the defense in the two-minute drill. Nixon and Brandon Cisse were the No. 1 cornerbacks Monday. Carrington Valentine and Domani Jackson worked with the second unit. Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring) did not practice. 
 Speaking of interceptions, Kitan Oladapo also went up in the air to pick off a Kyle McCord pass near the sideline. Oladapo and Kamal Hadden have been splitting time in the slot position that is normally manned by Javon Bullard (bruised foot). 
 The Packers got a scare when starting right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele was slow to get up after a play midway through practice. He appeared to get knocked over by edge rusher Lukas Van Ness . After getting shaken up, Bako-Bewele finished the drill and afterward said he did not know what happened but felt OK. He's coming off patella tendon surgery on his right knee this offseason. 
 Rookie kicker Trey Smack has been perfect in two preseason games, including a 59-yard field goal against the Broncos last week, but he has had his struggles in practice. On Monday, he made his longest kick of camp, a 60-yarder. He did, however, miss wide left from 40 yards and went 3-for-4 on the day. 
 

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 19 

 Now we know why edge rusher Dani Dennis-Sutton had not practiced for more than a week. He experienced a heat-related illness and while the rookie said he wasn't overly concerned about it, the team wasn't taking any chances.

 
"He overheated at practice, so obviously you take that very seriously," coach Matt LaFleur said. "He's kind of working through the protocol to come back."

 
The fourth-round pick had been out since Aug. 10 before he was back on the field Wednesday but was limited to only a few individual drills early in practice.

 
While he wouldn't say whether he had to go to the hospital, Dennis-Sutton said he was treated with IVs and drank fluids. In fact, after his session with reporters in the locker room Wednesday, he drank from a giant jug.

 
Dennis-Sutton was off to a productive start to training camp and had even gotten some rotational work with the No. 1 defense. The Packers are going to need all the pass-rush help they can get early in the season with Micah Parsons expected to start the season on physically unable to perform list while he continues his ACL rehab.

 
"I feel as though I had a really good camp so far, and I just can't wait to get back out there," Dennis-Sutton said. "Right now, I'm just doing what I can, but yeah, feel great, plan to get back."

 

 Other observations: 

 
 Kamal Hadden has taken reps with the No. 1 defense as the slot defensive back in the nickel package this week, and on Wednesday he picked off a Kyle McCord pass. At the end of the play, Hadden got bumped by an offensive player and reacted by spiking the ball after the play. The ball then drilled offensive lineman Dillon Wade . Hadden apologized, saying he had a "PTSD moment" about his gruesome ankle injury from last season. "I just kind of get sensitive running to the left on my ankle and turning back right," Hadden said. "It just gets me in the mode where I'm like, you know, it's kind of unnecessary, but that was all on me, and it shouldn't happen." In fact, he said he and Wade actually sit next to each other in team meetings. "That's my boy," Hadden said, "and I apologize to him for doing that, losing my cool." 
 Despite the interception, McCord has been backing up his strong showing in the preseason opener with some big plays in practice this week. On Wednesday, he had another highlight play when he connected with J. Michael Sturdivant on a deep ball down the right sideline. When asked what the next step for McCord is, LaFleur said: "You've got to repeat that performance each and every week." The Packers might not keep three quarterbacks on the roster, but at the very least, they would like to retain McCord on the practice squad as a developmental prospect. 
 LaFleur said quarterback Jordan Love and the healthy starters will play in Friday's preseason game against the Broncos. Love played one series last week against the Steelers. LaFleur said if all goes according to plan, the starters would not play in the preseason finale against Arizona in part because he expected them to get enough work in next week's joint practice with the Cardinals. 
 All of the players who returned to practice/team drills after extended absences (see Tuesday's practice report) were on the field again Wednesday. That included left guard Aaron Banks (knee), who took some 11-on-11 snaps early in the practice but appeared to have his reps cut short by the end. Running back Josh Jacobs (groin) once…

title: Green Bay Packers: Projecting final 53-man roster
summary: Will the Packers trade or release CB Keisean Nixon? Will rookie kicker Trey Smack make the cut?
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. -- The Packers open the 2026 NFL regular season at the Minnesota Vikings on Sept. 13 at U.S. Bank Stadium. But first, they play one more preseason game (Friday against the Arizona Cardinals ) and then must cut their roster to 53 players by 6 p.m. ET on Sunday.

 Who will make the team? Which positions have tough decisions on deck? And where might the lineup be deepest and thinnest this season?

 The Packers have been the NFL's youngest team for three years running, but they might finally shed that label. They've added veterans in defensive tackle Javon Hargrave (33), linebacker Zaire Franklin (30) and quarterback Tyrod Taylor (37) among others. But this is still a draft-and-develop organization, and there will be plenty of young players on the roster.

 Here is our projection for the 53-man roster for the Packers.

 

 Quarterbacks (2) 

 Jordan Love , Tyrod Taylor 

 The Packers had one of the league's best backups the past two seasons in Malik Willis , who is now in Miami. Now they'll have one of the most experienced in Taylor, who is entering his 16th season. Look for them to try to keep Kyle McCord on the practice squad as a developmental backup.

 

 Running backs (3) 

 Josh Jacobs , MarShawn Lloyd , Chris Brooks 

 The Packers might be holding their breath that Jacobs doesn't get suspended because of his arrest earlier this year and that Lloyd can stay healthy after playing one game in his first two NFL seasons. If not, then they'll need help here.

 

 Wide receivers (6) 

 Christian Watson , Jayden Reed , Matthew Golden , Skyy Moore , Savion Williams , Bo Melton 

 The Packers are deep at this spot even after losing Romeo Doubs and Dontayvion Wicks  during the offseason. Isaiah Neyor and J. Michael Sturdivant had strong camps and would be under consideration if they keep a seventh guy here.

 

 Tight ends (3) 

 Tucker Kraft , Josh Whyle , Drake Dabney (or a player or two to be named later) 

 Kraft looks like he's healthy enough to be ready for Week 1 after last year's torn ACL, but there's not a lot of proven production behind him. Luke Musgrave will likely stay on the physically unable to perform list because of a neck injury. This is the No. 1 spot for general manager Brian Gutekunst to upgrade via trade or waivers. Gutekunst kept four tight ends on his initial 53 last year.

 

 Offensive linemen (10) 

 Jordan Morgan , Aaron Banks , Sean Rhyan , Jacob Monk , Zach Bako-Bewele , Anthony Belton , Jager Burton , John Williams , Darian Kinnard , Donovan Jennings 

 Gutekunst kept only nine here after the initial cuts last season, but perhaps all the injuries up front in 2025 will convince him to keep an extra lineman.

 

 Defensive tackles (6) 

 Javon Hargrave , Devonte Wyatt , Karl Brooks , Warren Brinson , Chris McClellan , Jonathan Ford 

 New defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon wants bigger bodies up front, and this group should give him that. Ford appears to have moved ahead of Nazir Stackhouse , who made last year's roster as an undrafted rookie.

 

 Edge rushers (5) 

 Lukas Van Ness , Barryn Sorrell , Brenton Cox Jr ., Dani Dennis-Sutton , Collin Oliver 

 There's pressure on this group to generate pass rush until the return of Micah Parsons , who will start the season on PUP while recovering from the torn ACL suffered last season.

 

 Linebackers (5) 

 Zaire Franklin , Edgerrin Cooper , Isaiah McDuffie , Ty'Ron Hopper , Nick Niemann 

 The switch to having only two off-ball linebackers in Gannon's scheme means McDuffie likely loses snaps, but the Packers feel great about the duo of Franklin and Cooper. It's either Niemann or Kristian Welch for special teams purposes.

 

 

 Cornerbacks (6) 

 Keisean Nixon , Brandon Cisse , Benjamin St-Juste , Carrington Valentine , Kamal Hadden , Domani Jackson 

 If there is going to be a high-profile move on cutdown day, it would be Nixon . Perhaps the Packers will try to trade him or release him. They have another corner, Jaylin Simpson , whom they like.

 

 Safeties (4) 

 Xavier McKinney , Evan Williams , Javon Bullard , Kitan Oladapo 

 The Packers are light here since they usually keep five. If that's the case, Mark Perry is the best option.

 

 Special teams (3) 

 Trey Smack  (K), Daniel Whelan  (P), Matt Orzech  (LS) 

 Barring a collapse, it appears the they are going with a rookie kicker .

title: 2026 Houston Texans: Projecting final 53-man roster
summary: As the cut-down deadline approaches, Houston hones in on depth with most spots already locked up. Who will make the Texans' roster?
full_text:
HOUSTON -- The Houston Texans open the 2026 NFL regular season against the Buffalo Bills on Sept. 13 at Reliant Stadium. But first, they play one more preseason game Friday at Carolina and then must cut their roster to 53 players by 6 p.m. ET on Sunday.

 Who will make the team? Which positions have tough decisions on deck? And where might the lineup be deepest and thinnest this season?

 Houston's developed its roster into a Super Bowl contender, so most position battles at this point have been centered around bubble players. All but a couple starting slots were truly open coming into camp, which was center and right tackle.

 Here is our projection for the 53-man roster for the Texans.

 

 Quarterbacks (2) 
 C.J. Stroud , Davis Mills 

 Mills' only competition for the No. 2 spot was 2025 sixth-round pick Graham Mertz . Granted, the chances of Mertz winning the job were slim, but Mertz tore an ACL.

 
 Running backs (4) 
 David Montgomery , Woody Marks , Noah Whittington , British Brooks 

 Brooks has been hurt throughout camp, but he provides special teams value, which the Texans weigh heavily.

 

 Wide receivers (6) 
 Nico Collins ,  Tank Dell , Xavier Hutchinson , Jaylin Noel , Lewis Bond , Justin Watson 

 The wideout room took a major hit after  Jayden Higgins  suffered a season-ending torn ACL  last week, and now they will have to find a way to replace him. Dell hasn't practiced a lot with the starting offense as he works his way back from a serious knee injury that caused him to miss last season. But Ryans has made it clear they're riding with the former 2023 third-round pick through the end. This room could also make some additions with Houston signing veterans Sterling Shepard and Zay Jones  on Friday, according to Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo. 

 

 

 Tight ends (4) 

 Dalton Schultz , Cade Stover , Marlin Klein , Foster Moreau 

 Brevin Jordan was originally on the pre-training camp list. But he's off it now because he's been dealing with camp injuries and has missed weeks of practice. That's usually a recipe for not making the roster and Houston can save a million in cap space.

 

 Offensive linemen (9) 
 

 Aireontae Ersery , Braden Smith , Trent Brown , Blake Fisher , Wyatt Teller , Ed Ingram , Febechi Nwaiwu , Keylan Rutledge , Evan Brown 

 Brown sneaks onto this list because he's shown the ability to play guard and center. Rutledge winning the center job made Jake Andrews , who mainly plays center, expendable because of Brown's versatility. Ryans overemphasizes the value of versatility when you're not a starter.

 

 Defensive linemen (9) 

 Will Anderson Jr ., Danielle Hunter , Dylan Horton , Jadeveon Clowney , Logan Hall , Sheldon Rankins , Tommy Togiai , Kayden McDonald , Naquan Jones 

 The biggest change here is the inclusion of Clowney, who Houston added after a week of training camp practices. The No. 3 defensive line spot appeared shaky, but Clowney in that role should strengthen that unit.

 

 Linebackers (6) 

 Azeez Al-Shaair ,  Henry To'oTo'o , Jamal Hill , Aiden Fisher , Wade Woodaz ,  Jake Hansen 

 Woodaz brings a physicality to the defense that fits in despite penalties being a slight issue. Hill makes the roster because of his athletic ability for special teams.

 

 Cornerbacks (5) 
 Derek Stingley Jr ., Kamari Lassiter , Jaylin Smith , Tremon Smith ,  Collin Wright 

 Wright is from Houston so his homecoming as an undrafted free agent worked out in fairy tale fashion. He's had reps with the starting defense throughout camp and has recieved praise from players and coaches throughout camp.

 

 Safeties (5) 

 Calen Bullock , Reed Blankenship , Jaylen Reed , Kamari Ramsey , Jalen Pitre 

 Blankenship is one of Houston's biggest offseason additions, and Ramsey has flashed the ability to take the ball away as he caught an interception during Houston's first preseason game.

 

 Special teams (3) 

 Ka'imi Fairbairn  (K),  Kai Kroeger  (P), Austin Brinkman (LS) 

 The Texans released punter Jack Stonehouse earlier this month, leaving Kroeger as the lone punter on the roster.

title: 2026 Indianapolis Colts: Projecting final 53-man roster
summary: Look for plenty of rookies to fill out the Colts' roster, including as starters, but what will the team do about all the defensive linemen?
full_text:
INDIANAPOLIS -- The Indianapolis Colts open the 2026 NFL regular season against the Baltimore Ravens on Sept. 13. But first, they play one more preseason game Saturday against the Detroit Lions and then must cut their roster to 53 players by 6 p.m. ET on Sunday.

 Who will make the team? Which positions have tough decisions on deck? And where might the lineup be deepest and thinnest this season?

 Areas with questions to be addressed include the quarterback unit, where the Colts seem inclined to keep former No. 4 overall pick Anthony Richardson Sr . But they also must find space for what they think is a long list of defensive linemen who deserve roster spots. Finally, the rookie class figures prominently here, with several in line to start and all eight selections in contention to make the roster.

 Here is our projection for the 53-man roster for the Colts.

 

 Quarterbacks (3) 
 Daniel Jones , Anthony Richardson Sr ., Riley Leonard 

 The Colts have emphasized multiple times the need for quarterback depth in the wake of last year's desperate move to pull Philip Rivers out of retirement after nearly five seasons away from the game. Richardson had previously requested a trade but now seems destined to stick around.

 
 Running backs (3) 
 Jonathan Taylor , Seth McGowan , Ulysses Bentley IV 

 The odd man out here is 2025 draft pick DJ Giddens , who has been slowed by injury in the preseason and is not as versatile as McGowan or Bentley. McGowan looks like a candidate to offer some real relief in the backfield after Taylor's heavy workloads the past two seasons.

 

 Wide receivers (6) 
 Alec Pierce , Josh Downs , Keenan Allen , Nick Westbrook-Ikhine , Ashton Dulin , Coleman Owen 

 Allen's recent signing bolsters the depth and adds a critical option for Jones on third down. Owen grabs the final spot because of his role in the return game, getting the nod over Anthony Gould and rookie Deion Burks .

 
 Tight ends (4) 
 Tyler Warren , Mo Alie-Cox , Drew Ogletree , Will Mallory 

 There's good balance in this unit with Warren and Mallory offering options in the passing game and Alie-Cox and Ogletree mainly asked to be blockers. Warren led the Colts in targets last season.

 
 Offensive linemen (9) 
 Bernhard Raimann , Quenton Nelson , Tanor Bortolini , Matt Goncalves , Jalen Travis , Blake Freeland , Dalton Tucker , Jalen Farmer , Luke Tenuta 

 Travis slides into the lineup at right tackle, making him the lone new starter here. Farmer, a fourth-round pick, had a strong camp and will be the first guard off the bench. But the depth at center and offensive tackle is questionable.

 
 Defensive linemen (10) 
 Arden Key , DeForest Buckner , Grover Stewart , Laiatu Latu , Micheal Clemons , Jaylahn Tuimoloau , George Gumbs Jr ., Colby Wooden , Adetomiwa Adebawore , Caden Curry 

 GM Chris Ballard will always lean toward keeping extra bodies at defensive line, and that philosophy is reflected here. The balance between edge players and interior players is a bit skewed, but the versatility of a couple players to play inside and outside could make up for that.

 
 Linebackers (5) 
 CJ Allen , Akeem Davis-Gaither , Bryce Boettcher , Austin Ajiake , Jaylon Carlies 

 This unit arguably has the least proven talent on the entire roster. Talented rookies Allen and Boettcher should play important roles, which might include the customary growing pains.

 
 Cornerbacks (6) 
 Sauce Gardner , Charvarius Ward , Justin Walley , Cam Taylor-Britt , Johnathan Edwards , Mekhi Blackmon 

 This position will be fluid. Taylor-Britt won't technically count on the final roster because he'll be serving a one-game suspension in Week 1, but there could be adjustments beyond that. A waiver claim after final cuts could be in play to address the bottom of the depth chart here.

 
 Safeties (4) 
 Cam Bynum , A.J. Haulcy , Jonathan Owens , Hunter Wohler 

 Bynum was a great addition in free agency in 2025 and should be further settled in for Year 2. Haulcy has big play-making potential and should start as a rookie.

 
 Special teams (3) 
 Spencer Shrader (K),  Rigoberto Sanchez (P), Luke Rhodes (LS) 

 Sanchez and Rhodes are longtime holdovers, but Shrader sticks around at kicker after a tough offseason position battle with  Blake Grupe . Both seem likely to wind up on rosters, whatever happens here.

title: 2026 Jacksonville Jaguars: Projecting final 53-man roster
summary: While there are injuries along the O-line and at linebacker to consider, much of the Jaguars' roster is set ahead of Sunday's cut-down deadline.
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars open the 2026 NFL regular season against the Cleveland Browns on Sept. 13 at EverBank Stadium. But first, they play one more preseason game (Friday against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers ) and then must cut their roster to 53 players by 6 p.m. ET on Sunday.

 Who will make the team? Which positions have tough decisions on deck? And where might the lineup be deepest and thinnest this season?

 The offensive line and linebacker unit have been battered by injuries this summer, but few are expected to linger long enough to impact the start of the regular season. Receiver and defensive line are two of the team's strongest position groups, especially with the emergence of one young pass rusher. While there are still a few things to figure out, there aren't expected to be any surprise releases by the Jaguars.

 Here is our projection for the 53-man roster for the Jaguars.

 

 Quarterbacks (2) 
 Trevor Lawrence , Nick Mullens 

 Mullens is in the final year of his contract. Carter Bradley , son of former head coach Gus Bradley, likely heads to practice squad and might get a chance to compete to be Lawrence's backup in 2027.

 
 Running backs (3) 
 Chris Rodriguez Jr ., Bhayshul Tuten , LeQuint Allen Jr . 

 Allen is dealing with a soft tissue injury and will miss the rest of camp, but there's no indication at this point that he's going to begin the season on injured reserve. If that does become the case, undrafted rookie  J'Mari Taylor  (who ran for 78 yards and a TD in the first preseason game) or veteran Ameer Abdullah could take his spot.

 
 Tight ends (3) 
 Brenton Strange , Nate Boerkircher , Tanner Koziol 

 Boerkircher (second round) and Koziol (fifth round) are both 2026 draft picks, so this will be a group short on experience behind Strange. The Jaguars love Boerkircher as a blocker, and using him in 12 personnel could open things up in the pass game for Strange.

 
 Wide receivers (5) 
 Jakobi Meyers , Parker Washington , Brian Thomas Jr ., Josh Cameron ,  CJ Williams 

 This is arguably the best position group on the roster, especially when you add Travis Hunter to the mix. If the Jaguars no longer want Washington returning punts, the job will go to Cameron. And Thomas is healthy (he dealt with wrist, ankle and shoulder injuries in 2025), improved his hand strength and is more physical than he was in his first two seasons. 

 
 Offensive linemen (10) 
 Cole Van Lanen , Ezra Cleveland , Robert Hainsey , Patrick Mekari , Anton Harrison , Jonah Monheim , Wyatt Milum , Walker Little , Emmanuel Pregnon , Chuma Edoga 

 This is a banged-up group. Mekari had back surgery, and the Jaguars have not yet made a decision on whether he'll start the season on IR. Little, Pregnon and Edoga also have dealt with injuries in camp. Van Lanen (knee) just came off the physically unable to preform list. That's why the Jaguars have cross-trained almost everyone but Hainsey (center), and there could be as many as four players starting in different spots than expected in Week 1.

 
 Defensive linemen (11) 
 Josh Hines-Allen , Travon Walker , B.J. Green II , Danny Striggow , Wesley Williams , Zach Durfee , DaVon Hamilton , Arik Armstead , Matt Dickerson , Albert Regis , Ruke Orhorhoro 

 Green, an undrafted rookie in 2025, is having a great camp and has ascended to the No. 3 pass rusher role behind Hines-Allen and Walker. Dickerson is the top interior backup behind Hamilton and Armstead. There are a lot of new faces: Williams, Durfee and Regis are draft picks, and Orhorhoro was acquired in an offseason trade with Atlanta.

 
 Linebackers (6) 
 Foyesade Oluokun ,  Dennis Gardeck , Branson Combs , Ventrell Miller , Yasir Abdullah , Jahlani Tavai 

 Combs and Miller have been battling at strongside linebacker. Injuries have battered this group, too, which led the team to bring in eight-year veteran Tavai on Aug. 6. Abdullah played only two snaps on defense last season, but he is a good special teams player.

 
 Cornerbacks (5) 
 Travis Hunter , Montaric Brown , Jourdan Lewis , Jarrian Jones , Jabbar Muhammad 

 Hunter is the team's top corner and will primarily play defense, but he will also have a role on offense. Jones has lined up inside and outside and likely will take Hunter's spot outside if he's not on the field. Coach Liam Coen called Muhammad one of the team's most improved players, and he broke up a pass in the end zone to secure the Jaguars' preseason victory over New Orleans.

 
 Safeties (5) 
 Eric Murray , Antonio Johnson , Caleb Ransaw , Rayuan Lane III , Jalen Huskey 

 Murray is a steady veteran leader who is still a good player at 32 years old. Johnson went from a part-time player at the start of last season to one of the defense's most important players. Ransaw missed his rookie season with a foot injury, and that impacted his transition from corner to safety. Huskey, a sixth-round pick, has flashed and might end up as the third safety.

 
 Special teams (3) 
 Cam Little  (K), Logan Cooke  (P), Ross Matiscik  (LS) 

The only question about this group is whether Little will get a chance to break the NFL record for longest field goal (68 yards), which he set last season against Las Vegas.
