title: 2026 Kansas City Chiefs: Projecting final 53-man roster
summary: Who will make the team? Which positions have tough decisions on deck? Chiefs reporter Nate Taylor makes his predictions.
full_text:
KANSAS CITY, Mo. -- The Kansas City Chiefs open the 2026 NFL regular season against the Denver Broncos on Sept. 14 at Arrowhead Stadium. But first, they play one more preseason game Friday against the Seattle Seahawks  and then must cut their roster to 53 players by 6 p.m. ET on Sunday.

 Who will make the team? Which positions have tough decisions on deck? And where might the lineup be deepest and thinnest?

 One of the biggest differences this season is that the Chiefs are a younger team, especially considering they had three rookies selected in the top 50 draft picks. The defense will be a young group hoping to support pass rusher Chris Jones , defensive end George Karlaftis and linebacker Nick Bolton . The offense received the biggest acquisition in the offseason: running back Kenneth Walker III . And although the Chiefs' passing game struggled last season, the team didn't add any veterans to the position.

 Here is our projection for the 53-man roster for the Chiefs.

 

 Quarterbacks (3) 

 Patrick Mahomes , Justin Fields , Garrett Nussmeier 

 Much of the season comes down to how well Mahomes performs after the most significant injury of his career, the torn ACL and LCL he had surgically repaired in December. Fields is an adequate backup if needed. The Chiefs should spend this year developing Nussmeier to be the long-term backup for the rest of Mahomes' prime.

 

 Running backs (4) 

 Kenneth Walker III , Emari Demercado , Emmett Johnson , Brashard Smith 

 Walker has been exceptional during training camp. The Chiefs are optimistic that Walker and Johnson can provide explosive gains on the ground. Smith appears ready to be a kickoff returner, and Demercado provides the best option for a third-down back with quality pass-protection skills.

 

 Wide receivers (7) 

 Rashee Rice , Xavier Worthy , Tyquan Thornton , Cyrus Allen , Nikko Remigio , Andrew Armstrong , Jalen Royals 

 With no true No. 1 receiver, the Chiefs need plenty of depth at the position, especially since Rice and Worthy are returning from injuries. The biggest surprise in camp has been the emergence of Allen as a pure route runner.

 

 Tight ends (4) 

 Travis Kelce , Noah Gray , Jared Wiley , Jake Briningstool 

 If the Chiefs are serious about running the ball more often with Walker, adding more tight ends not named Kelce is a requirement. Kelce led the Chiefs in receiving last year and looks to be in better shape in camp than a year ago. Gray and Wiley need to demonstrate they can be positive when it comes to blocking. Briningstool offers the most potential as a pass catcher in the future.

 

 Offensive linemen (9) 

 Josh Simmons , Kingsley Suamataia , Creed Humphrey , Trey Smith , Jaylon Moore , Kahlil Benson , Esa Pole , Hunter Nourzad , Mike Caliendo 

 A strong starting group, but the Chiefs lack depth here. Look for them to add an interior player through waivers if the opportunity is there. The Chiefs still don't know who their right tackle is, whether it's five-year veteran Moore or undrafted rookie Benson.

 

 Defensive linemen (9) 

 George Karlaftis , Chris Jones , Khyiris Tonga , Ashton Gillotte , R Mason Thomas , Peter Woods , Omarr Norman-Lott , Felix Anudike-Uzomah , Emmanuel Ogbah 

 An argument can be made that the biggest improvement on the roster is here. The Chiefs have better depth than they had a year ago after acquiring rookies such as Woods and Thomas. The Chiefs are hoping for a bounce-back performance from Jones and Karlaftis, the pair combining for just 13 sacks a year ago.

 

 Linebackers (5) 

 Nick Bolton , Drue Tranquill , Jeffrey Bassa , Jack Cochrane , Cooper McDonald 

 The strength in the defense will rely on the veteran experience of Bolton and Tranquill. Bassa, a second-year player, needs to make a huge leap, perhaps in the second half of the season, for the defense to reach its full potential.

 

 Cornerbacks (6) 

 Mansoor Delane , Nohl Williams , Chris Roland-Wallace , L'Jarius Sneed , Kristian Fulton , Jadon Canady 

 In one offseason, the Chiefs swapped out Trent McDuffie and  Jaylen Watson  for Delane, a rookie, and Williams, a second-year player. Sneed is an intriguing option if he can stay healthy, and Roland-Wallace should receive the bulk of the snaps at nickel. If a team needs a veteran cornerback later this season, a trade option for them could be Fulton, who was steady late last season.

 

 Safeties (3) 

 Alohi Gilman , Chamarri Conner , Jaden Hicks 

 Longtime defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo needs all three players to stay healthy and productive for him to be his most creative with his dime personnel. The Chiefs will have to find out if Gilman can be a true free safety that can prevent long completions. Hicks has a chance to be a breakout star.

 

 Special teams (3) 

 Harrison Butker  (K), Matt Araiza  (P), James Winchester  (LS) 

 The unit remains the same from last year. The Chiefs will need Butker to return to form after he missed a career-high nine kicks -- five field goals and four extra-point attempts -- a year ago.

title: 2026 Los Angeles Chargers: Projecting final 53-man roster
summary: Coach Jim Harbaugh and GM Joe Hortiz have difficult decisions to make at outside linebacker, safety and offensive line.
full_text:
LOS ANGELES -- The Los Angeles Chargers open the 2026 NFL regular season against the Arizona Cardinals on Sept. 13 at SoFi Stadium. But first, they play one more preseason game on Thursday against the  Los Angeles Rams  and then must cut their roster to 53 players by 6 p.m. ET on Sunday.

 Who will make the team? Which positions have tough decisions on deck? And where might the lineup be deepest and thinnest this season?

 Coach Jim Harbaugh and general manager Joe Hortiz have difficult decisions to make across the board, particularly at positions including outside linebacker, safety and offensive line. Outside linebacker Nadame Tucker  and cornerbacks Rodney Shelley and Avery Smith are three undrafted players who have had standout performances in camp and will make decisions difficult on cut down day.

 Here is our projection for the 53-man roster for the Bolts.

 

 Quarterbacks (2) 
 Justin Herbert , Trey Lance 

 DJ Uiagalelei was an improved player throughout the offseason, pushing Lance for this backup job. Ultimately, Lance's mobility gives him the edge over Uiagalelei, whom the Chargers will probably want back for their practice squad.

 

 

 Running backs (3) 

 Omarion Hampton , Keaton Mitchell , Kimani Vidal 

 Amar Johnson and Jaret Patterson would be neck and neck if the Chargers keep four running backs, but it seems more likely they will go with this group. All three are players new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel has raved about.

 

 Fullbacks (1) 

 Alec Ingold 

 Ingold is familiar with McDaniel's system after playing for him for four seasons in Miami and gives the Chargers versatility with an ability to also move to tight end.

 

 Wide receivers (6) 

 Ladd McConkey , Tre' Harris , Quentin Johnston , Brenen Thompson , Derius Davis , KeAndre Lambert-Smith 

 This group may benefit the most from McDaniel, who said to expect career highs across the board. Dalevon Campbell could push for this sixth spot, but Lambert-Smith seems to have the upper hand.

 

 Tight ends (3) 

 David Njoku , Oronde Gadsden , Charlie Kolar 

 This is one of the deepest positions on the Chargers' roster. This group has a mix of blocking and receiving prowess needed for McDaniel's offense. There has never been much of a competition here.

 

 Offensive linemen (9) 

 Joe Alt , Trey Pipkins III , Rashawn Slater , Cole Strange , Jacob Spomer , Kayode Awosika , Jake Slaughter , Travis Burke , Branson Taylor 

 This may be the toughest roster battle. Trevor Penning , who began camp in the mix to start at left guard, misses the cut, as do the Chargers' two sixth-round rookies, Alex Harkey and Logan Taylor . With Tyler Biadasz suffering a season-ending ACL injury in his left knee undrafted rookie center Jacob Spomer makes the team.

 

 Defensive linemen (5) 

 Teair Tart , Jamaree Caldwell , Justin Eboigbe , Nick Barrett , Dalvin Tomlinson 

 TeRah Edwards  would be the next man up in this scenario, but five make the roster in this case. This is a group that should have increased pass-rush opportunities under new defensive coordinator Chris O'Leary.

 

 

 Linebackers (10) 

 Denzel Perryman , Daiyan Henley , Troy Dye , Del'Shawn Phillips , Marlowe Wax , Khalil Mack , Bud Dupree , Tuli Tuipulotu , Akheem Mesidor , Kyle Kennard 

 Another one of the toughest battles here. Former third-round pick Junior Colson , Kennard and  Nadame Tucker  are all in the mix for the final spot. Here Kennard gets that last spot. He's a 2025 fourth-round pick whom the Chargers hope will reach his potential.

 

 Cornerbacks (6) 

 Donte Jackson , Tarheeb Still , Cam Hart , Deane Leonard , Nikko Reed , Avery Smith 

 Smith has stood out since training camp began, earning the final roster spot in this projection. The battle will likely come down to Smith, Eric Rogers (one of last year's camp stars) and undrafted free agent  Rodney Shelley .

 

 Safeties (5) 

 Derwin James Jr ., Elijah Molden , RJ Mickens , Genesis Smith , Tony Jefferson 

 Another tough roster crunch here. In this scenario, Kendall Williamson , who was on the 53-man roster all of last season, misses the cut. The fourth-round rookie Smith takes his place.

 

 Special teams (3) 

 Cameron Dicker (K), JK Scott (P), Josh Harris (LS) 

 No battles here. The Chargers run it back with a group they've had since 2022.

title: 2026 Los Angeles Rams: Projecting final 53-man roster
summary: Coach Sean McVay and GM Les Snead have difficult decisions to make on the Rams' 2026 roster.
full_text:
LOS ANGELES -- The Rams open the 2026 NFL regular season against the San Francisco 49ers on Sept. 10 at Melbourne Cricket Ground. But first, they play one more preseason game Thursday against the  Los Angeles Chargers  and then must cut their roster to 53 players by 6 p.m. ET on Sunday.

 Who will make the team? Which positions have tough decisions on deck? And where might the lineup be deepest and thinnest this season?

 This roster projection doesn't include Aaron Donald , who is currently going through a "regimented" process to determine whether he wants to come out of retirement. This is an offensive-heavy projection, in part because it includes six receivers, five tight ends and 10 offensive linemen.

 Here is our projection for the 53-man roster for the Rams.

 

 Quarterbacks (3) 
 Matthew Stafford ,  Stetson Bennett IV , Ty Simpson 

 After the Rams drafted Simpson with the No. 13 pick in April, coach Sean McVay said the rookie and Bennett would compete to back up Stafford. After two preseason games, McVay has not announced who has won that job. This projection includes all three quarterbacks, as Bennett has taken the majority of the second-team reps during training camp.

 

 Running backs (4) 
 Kyren Williams , Blake Corum , Ronnie Rivers , Jarquez Hunter 

 Williams and Corum had about a 65-35 percent split in carries last season, with Williams rushing for 1,252 yards and 10 touchdowns on 259 carries. That could look closer to a 50-50 split this season if both running backs can stay healthy.

 

 Wide receivers (6) 
 Davante Adams , Puka Nacua , Jordan Whittington , Konata Mumpfield , Xavier Smith , CJ Daniels 

 Last season, Adams led the league in touchdown receptions (14) and Nacua led the NFL with 129 catches. Whittington and Mumpfield are likely competing for the No. 3 receiver spot behind that pair.

 

 Tight ends (5) 
 Tyler Higbee , Terrance Ferguson , Colby Parkinson , Davis Allen , Max Klare 

 Five tight ends on a 53-man roster would be unheard of for most teams -- and the Rams before last season -- but it seems the most likely scenario going into training camp. Los Angeles had 331 plays in 13 personnel last season , more than twice as many as any other team, according to ESPN Research.

 

 

 Offensive linemen (10) 
 Alaric Jackson , Steve Avila , Coleman Shelton , Kevin Dotson , Warren McClendon Jr ., David Quessenberry , Beaux Limmer , Keagen Trost , Dylan McMahon , Justin Dedich 

 The Rams have several uncertain spots on the offensive line given Jackson's legal situation and possible suspension. Trost, a rookie third-round pick, injured his hamstring in the Rams' preseason opener and could miss several weeks. Dedich missed all of training camp on the NFI list after injuring his hand in early July.

 

 Defensive linemen (5) 
 Kobie Turner , Poona Ford , Braden Fiske , Tyler Davis , Tim Keenan III 

 If Donald decides to return, that would shake up this group. Donald, a future Hall of Fame defensive tackle, retired in March 2024. Turner, a third-round pick in 2023, is going into the final season of his rookie contract and is a candidate for a contract extension.

 

 Linebackers (8) 
 Myles Garrett , Byron Young , Josaiah Stewart , Desjuan Johnson , Nate Landman , Omar Speights , Shaun Dolac , Grant Stuard 

 The biggest offseason addition for the Rams came on June 1, when they traded for Garrett , the reigning NFL Defensive Player of the Year. Young, who is coming off a 12-sack season for Los Angeles, is also entering the final season of his rookie deal.

 

 Cornerbacks (5) 
 Trent McDuffie , Jaylen Watson , Josh Wallace , Emmanuel Forbes Jr ., Cam Lampkin 

 The Rams revamped this room after last season , trading for McDuffie and signing Watson to a three-year, $51 million deal. Lampkin, who has spent most of the past two seasons on the Rams' practice squad, impressed during training camp.

 

 Safeties (4) 
 Quentin Lake , Kam Curl , Kamren Kinchens , Jaylen McCollough 

 The Rams have continuity in their safety room after signing Lake to a contract extension during the 2025 season and re-signing Curl before the start of free agency. Kinchens, a third-round pick in 2024, could be a breakout candidate for the group.

 

 Special teams (3) 
 Harrison Mevis  (K),  Ethan Evans  (P), Joe Cardona  (LS) 

 Special teams was a weakness for the Rams last season, forcing an in-season change at kicker and long-snapper. Mevis, who took over in mid-November, missed just one kick in nine regular-season games and was perfect during the playoffs.

title: 2026 Las Vegas Raiders: Projecting final 53-man roster
summary: Coach Klint Kubiak and GM John Spytek have difficult decisions to make at quarterback, wide receiver and cornerback.
full_text:
Editor's note: This was updated after the Noah Brown was cut by the Raiders on Monday.  

 HENDERSON, Nev. -- The Las Vegas Raiders open the 2026 NFL regular season against the Miami Dolphins on Sept. 13 at Allegiant Stadium. But first, they play one more preseason game Thursday against the San Francisco 49ers and then must cut their roster to 53 players by 6 p.m. ET on Sunday.

 Who will make the team? Which positions have tough decisions on deck? And where might the lineup be deepest and thinnest this season?

 No matter how roster cut-down day shakes out, coach Klint Kubiak will rely on a fairly young team in his first season in Las Vegas. The team's trust in their wide receivers and cornerbacks will be tested, as both position groups could very well add more help at some point during the season. But one of the biggest questions facing the Raiders is whether they should keep three quarterbacks on the roster.

 Here is our projection of the Raiders' 53-man roster.

 

 Quarterbacks (2) 
 Kirk Cousins , Fernando Mendoza 

 In this exercise, the Raiders decided to stick with two quarterbacks. Kubiak said during training camp that he had three NFL-ready quarterbacks on the roster. Mendoza has shown enough that if the Raiders needed him to step in sooner than expected, the team is confident the No. 1 pick will be ready to go. As for  Aidan O'Connell , he could be a good trade candidate for a team that's looking to add a quarterback with starter experience.

 

 

 Running backs (4) 

 Ashton Jeanty , Mike Washington Jr ., Roman Hemby , Dylan Laube 

 The Raiders went into training camp with the expectation that Jeanty would be the undisputed No. 1 at running back. But Washington, the team's 2026 fourth-round pick, has shown he could make a serious impact. Las Vegas has had the worst rushing attacks in the league over the past two seasons. The Raiders have the potential to put together better numbers with the one-two punch of Jeanty and Washington.

 

 Fullbacks (1) 

 Connor Heyward 

 The fullback position matters a ton to Kubiak. He hopes Heyward can add valuable support in the run game and pass protection. Expect the Raiders to utilize 21 and 22 personnel quite a bit during the regular season.

 

 Tight ends (3) 

 Brock Bowers , Michael Mayer , Ian Thomas 

 If Bowers is healthy, he should put up big numbers, no matter which quarterback is under center. But what about Mayer? The Raiders have been waiting for him to break out since he was selected in the second round of the 2023 draft. There's a good chance that he can in Kubiak's system as well as playing alongside Cousins, who likes to rely on his tight ends.

 

 Wide receivers (5) 

 Tre Tucker , Jalen Nailor , Jack Bech , Malik Benson , Dareke Young 

 It will be interesting to see which player emerges as the WR3. Bech didn't have the best rookie season, and his performance during training camp has been underwhelming for the most part. But he can be a big-body target in the slot, and his physicality will be useful in the run game as a blocker. Benson, on the other hand, has been a better pass catcher. He has consistently made plays during practice, emerging as a go-to target for Mendoza.

 

 Offensive linemen (8) 

 Kolton Miller , Spencer Burford , Tyler Linderbaum , Jackson Powers-Johnson , DJ Glaze , Charles Grant , Trey Zuhn III , Caleb Rogers 

 Guard and right tackle are still the biggest question marks. Glaze has maintained his role as the starting right tackle, but will he fair well against tough competition? Powers-Johnson alternated starting reps with Rogers. Still, he should be the team's starting right guard to begin the season.

 

 Defensive linemen (6) 

 Thomas Booker IV , Adam Butler , Folorunso Fatukasi , Tonka Hemingway , Jonah Laulu , JJ Pegues 

 Hemingway has emerged as a starter on the team's defensive front. The unit's overall ability in slowing down the run is a bit worrisome. Las Vegas gave up 4.3 yards per rush in its preseason opener against the Arizona Cardinals .

 

 Edge rushers (5) 

 Maxx Crosby , Kwity Paye , Malcolm Koonce , Keyron Crawford , Cian Slone 

 Crosby is expected to maintain his status as one of the league's best pass rushers. He has been dominant throughout training camp. But in the offseason, general manager John Spytek briefly mentioned the possibility of managing Crosby's snap count during the regular season to help the longevity of his career. With that said, the Raiders will need consistency from Koonce and Paye. 

 

 Linebackers (5) 

 Quay Walker , Nakobe Dean , Cody Lindenberg , Tommy Eichenberg , Segun Olubi 

 Dean has already established himself as a vocal leader on defense. Walker's versatility should provide additional pass rush support.

 

 

 Cornerbacks (6) 

 Eric Stokes , Taron Johnson , Darien Porter , Jermod McCoy , Hezekiah Masses , Decamerion Richardson 

 The Raiders' young cornerbacks certainly have upside. However, will that be enough this season? Porter is entering Year 2 but is still learning to play the position. McCoy hasn't played football for more than a year due to injury and it looked that way in the preseason. The group could be solid in a season or two. But asking them to provide consistent pass coverage in 2026 might be a tall task.

 

 Safeties (5) 

 Jeremy Chinn , Treydan Stukes , Isaiah Pola-Mao , Dalton Johnson ,  Tristin McCollum 

 The thought was that Stukes could beat out Pola-Mao as the starting deep safety. But Pola-Mao will walk away from training camp maintaining his position. Stukes has improved as camp progressed and could very well be in a rotation with Pola Mao, or line up alongside the veteran safety while Chinn plays closer to the line of scrimmage in certain packages. Stukes will also alternate with Johnson at nickel.

 

 Special teams (3) 

 Matt Gay  (K),  AJ Cole (P),  Tyler Duzansky  (LS) 

 Gay might not be a better option than former kicker Daniel Carlson , but he is the team's best and only option at the moment.

title: 2026 Miami Dolphins: Projecting final 53-man roster
summary: Who sticks at wide receiver? Which cornerbacks make the cut? Dolphins reporter Marcel Louis-Jacques makes his predictions.
full_text:
MIAMI GARDENS, Fla. -- The Miami Dolphins open the 2026 NFL regular season at the Las Vegas Raiders on Sept. 13 at 4:25 p.m. ET at Allegiant Stadium. But first, they play one more preseason game Friday against the  Atlanta Falcons . The roster will be cut to 53 players by 6 p.m. ET on Sunday.

 Who will make the team? Which positions have tough decisions on deck? And where might the lineup be deepest and thinnest this season?

 The youngest team in the NFL will eat a league-record $180 million in dead cap this season, as first-year general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan made deliberate attempts to get "younger and cheaper" in 2026. The Dolphins also drafted a league-high 13 rookies this year, many of whom project to not only make the initial roster, but have legitimate roles early in their careers.

 Here is our projection for the 53-man roster for the Dolphins.

 

 Quarterbacks (2) 
 Malik Willis , Quinn Ewers 

 The gap between Ewers and Cam Miller is a lot closer than the one between Ewers and Willis. Neither backup was particularly impressive in their preseason debut, and it's a position that might require attention after cut day.

 

 Running backs (4) 
 De'Von Achane , Ollie Gordon II , Jaylen Wright , Carlos Washington Jr . 

 No major surprises in the Dolphins' running backs room. The team didn't bring in much veteran competition this offseason and the top three are firmly established. Achane will be the focal point of Miami's offense, with Wright and Gordon spelling him. Washington makes the team after consistent playmaking throughout camp.

 
 Wide receivers (6) 
 Malik Washington , Jalen Tolbert , AJ Henning , Caleb Douglas , Chris Bell , Kevin Coleman Jr . 

 Douglas emerged as a potential lead receiver this summer, while Henning consistently made plays throughout camp -- enough to earn his place on the roster over veteran Tutu Atwell . Washington could be in line for a career season in Year 3, and Bell's return from an ACL tear midway through training camp sets up an intriguing rookie trio with Douglas and Coleman.

 
 Tight ends (4) 
 Greg Dulcich , Will Kacmarek , Seydou Traore , Ben Sims 

 Dulcich is a candidate to lead the Dolphins in targets this season, and Kacmarek has proven to be an upper-tier blocker at the position. Traore is a rookie who offers upside, particularly as a receiver, and Sims offers flexibility as both a tight end and fullback.

 
 Offensive linemen (8) 
 Patrick Paul , Kadyn Proctor , Aaron Brewer , Jonah Savaiinaea , Austin Jackson , Caedan Wallace , DJ Campbell , Andrew Meyer 

 The Dolphins bring back four starters from last season's offensive line, switching Savaiinaea to right guard and adding first-round pick Proctor at left guard. Free agent signee Jamaree Salyer will miss the entire season after being placed on injured reserve this summer, and Miami will likely add to this group after cut day.

 
 Defensive linemen (9) 
 Chop Robinson ,  Josh Uche ,  David Ojabo ,  Cameron Goode , Max Llewellyn , Zach Sieler , Kenneth Grant , Jordan Phillips , Zeek Biggers 

 Robinson turned in the best training camp of his career and the Dolphins will need him to lead this group. Miami is excited about its front seven, and it starts with its interior defensive line of Sieler, Phillips, Grant and Biggers.

 
 Linebackers (7) 
 Jordyn Brooks , Tyrel Dodson , Jacob Rodriguez , Kyle Louis , Willie Gay Jr ., Trey Moore , Ronnie Harrison Jr . 

 Brooks leads arguably the Dolphins' strongest position group, and second-round pick Rodriguez has made plays throughout the summer and could open the season with a starting job. Fellow rookies Louis and Moore provide position flexibility and are part of the team's future plans on defense.

 
 Cornerbacks (6) 
 Chris Johnson ,  JuJu Brents , Jason Marshall Jr ., Ethan Bonner , Marco Wilson , AJ. Green III 

 The Dolphins re-work their cornerbacks room for the second consecutive season but bring back Brents, Marshall and Bonner. Storm Duck has yet to make his return from an ACL injury he suffered last season, and is a PUP candidate. First-round pick Johnson is capable of playing multiple positions and has come along nicely this summer.

 
 Safeties (4) 
 Dante Trader Jr ., Lonnie Johnson Jr ., Michael Taaffe , Zayne Anderson 

 Trader has taken on a leadership role in his second NFL season, but this room still projects an air of uncertainty. UDFA Louis Moore is a name to keep an eye on here as a bubble player.

 
 Special teams (3) 
 Riley Patterson  (K), Bradley Pinion  (P), Tucker Addington  (LS) 

 Patterson wins the Dolphins kicker competition after an injury to Zane Gonzalez , while Pinion replaces last year's starter Jake Bailey .

title: Minnesota Vikings: Projecting final 53-man roster
summary: At least four rookies are poised to contribute out of the gate on both sides of the ball. Who are they?
full_text:
EAGAN, Minn. -- The Minnesota Vikings open the 2026 NFL regular season against the Green Bay Packers on Sept. 13 at U.S. Bank Stadium. But first, they play one more preseason game (Friday at the Denver Broncos ) and then must cut their roster to 53 players by 6 p.m. ET on Sunday. 

 Who will make the team? Which positions have tough decisions on deck? And where might the lineup be deepest and thinnest this season? 

 While most eyes were on the Vikings' quarterback competition, won to no surprise by veteran Kyler Murray , competition was playing out across the roster. What emerged, most notably, is the potential for immediate offensive or defensive contributions from at least four and possibly five members of the 2026 draft class. 

 Here is our projection for the 53-man roster for the Vikings.

 

 Quarterbacks (3) 

 Kyler Murray , J.J. McCarthy , Carson Wentz 

 It's possible the Vikings will look to put No. 4 quarterback Max Brosmer on the practice squad. Otherwise, the only question was deciding whether McCarthy or Wentz will be No. 2 on gamedays behind Murray. It appears that McCarthy will open the season there, with Wentz as the emergency No. 3, but that is always subject to change.

 

 Running backs (5) 

 Aaron Jones Sr ., Jordan Mason , Demond Claiborne , Zavier Scott , Max Bredeson (FB)  

 Two veterans in the final year of their contracts (Jones, Mason) and two members of the 2026 draft class (Claiborne, Bredeson) make up the crux of this position. Jones and Mason will be the primary ball carriers, but Claiborne has a burst that neither of them possess. Based on usage in training camp and the preseason, Bredeson figures to play a prominent blocking role. 

 

 Wide receivers (5) 

 Justin Jefferson , Jordan Addison , Jauan Jennings , Tai Felton , Myles Price 

 Jefferson, Addison and Jennings will comprise the Vikings' three-receiver sets, which Jennings has compared to the  Golden State Warriors ' championship trio of Kevin Durant , Stephen Curry and Klay Thompson . Felton and Price were both impressive during training camp but will play limited roles unless there are injuries.

 

 Tight ends (3) 

 T.J. Hockenson , Josh Oliver , Gavin Bartholomew 

 Could this position get a makeover next spring under new general manager Nolan Teasley? Hockenson's contract expires after the season. Oliver has been an elite blocker over the past three seasons but has been used minimally in the passing game, catching 59 passes while earning $22 million. Bartholomew emerged as a smooth pass-catcher after missing his rookie season because of a back injury.

 

 Offensive linemen (10) 

 Christian Darrisaw , Donovan Jackson , Blake Brandel , Will Fries , Brian O'Neill , Ryan Van Demark , Michael Jurgens , Joe Huber , Caleb Tiernan , Walter Rouse 

 Four starters return from 2025, while Brandel completes the transition from guard/tackle to center following the retirement of Ryan Kelly . The Vikings hope they have upgraded their depth at all positions, particularly after prying Van Demark away from the Buffalo Bills via restricted free agency.

 

 

 Defensive linemen (6) 

 Jalen Redmond , Levi Drake Rodriguez , Caleb Banks , Domonique Orange , Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins ,  Elijah Williams 

 The Vikings have infused this position with young talent, and they should have five players in their rotation with no more than three years of experience. That includes two rookies in Banks and Orange, both of whom received first-team work during training camp as defensive coordinator Brian Flores tested various packages.

 

 Linebackers (8) 

 Andrew Van Ginkel , Dallas Turner , Eric Wilson , Blake Cashman , Jake Golday , Ivan Pace Jr ., Bo Richter , Tyler Batty 

 Camp did not reveal obvious depth at edge pass rusher, where Turner has taken over the spot vacated by the trade of Jonathan Greenard to the Philadelphia Eagles . But Ingram-Dawkins has shown some position flexibility, and Golday got work at the off-ball position and edge. 

 

 Cornerbacks (4) 

 Byron Murphy Jr ., Isaiah Rodgers , James Pierre , Charles Demmings 

 It's possible the Vikings will add to this position during the flurry of cuts, but for now they were encouraged to see Demmings -- a fifth-round draft pick from FCS Stephen F. Austin -- challenge some of their top receivers and push Pierre for the No. 3 cornerback job. In some cases, however, Flores will use a safety as his nickel.

 

 Safeties (6) 
 Joshua Metellus , Jay Ward , Theo Jackson , Jakobe Thomas , Tavierre Thomas , Jacob Thomas 

 The Vikings didn't backfill Harrison Smith 's starting role as if they were certain he would retire. (He hasn't made any announcements one way or the other.) Following Jamal Adams ' season-ending torn right quadriceps in the first preseason game, two rookies with nearly identical names -- Jakobe Thomas was a third-rounder, Jacob Thomas was an undrafted free agent -- are on track to make the roster. 

 

 Special teams (3) 

 Will Reichard  (K), Johnny Hekker  (P), Andrew DePaola  (LS) 

 Rookie punter Brett Thorson has had a strong camp, but Hekker is the more reliable option for a veteran team hoping to make a playoff push.

title: 2026 New England Patriots training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Catch up on our daily updates from Patriots training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. Patriots reporter Mike Reiss has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Patriots camp. Will Drake Maye  start another MVP-like campaign in Year 3? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Patriots camp 
 
 Vrabel says starters sitting in order to develop depth 
 Patriots TE Hunter Henry signs extension worth up to $20M 
 Has Patriots CB Christian Gonzalez found his voice? 
 A.J. Brown on injury: 'Thumb out of place, you keep going' 
 Patriots' Brown knows Vrabel's rip comes from 'great place' 
 Kraft: Patriots' Gonzalez has offer to be 'highest-paid' CB ever 
 Too many receivers? A look at the Patriots' crowded WR room 
 
 

 Monday, Aug. 24 
 Cornerback Christian Gonzalez , who had been sidelined since landing hard at the end of practice Aug. 10, returned to the field Monday and his presence was noted by teammates.

 Gonzalez's agent remains engaged in contract extension negotiations with the team.

 "He's a ballplayer, first and foremost. He loves football. He loves being around the team. He loves lining up and playing against the best," linebacker Christian Elliss said. "It doesn't matter what he has going on, he's going to line up and play and he locks people down."

 Gonzalez was a full participant in his return to practice.

 "It's always special to have one of the better corners in this league, and have him out there with us. Obviously as we start to ramp up getting into the season, for him to be able to go out there and start practice fully, it was pretty cool," starting safety  Kevin Byard  said.

 Earlier in the day, coach Mike Vrabel was asked about the status of contract talks with Gonzalez.

 "We're working hard to try to get him; we want him [to be] a part of our team for as long as certainly I'm here, for as long as he can possibly here," he said on sports radio WEEI.

 

 More observations: 

 
 RB TreVeyon Henderson slipped while making a cut, had his right ankle/foot area looked at, and left practice about midway through. The team practiced on its lower field and multiple players noted the slippery natural-grass surface when asked by reporters. 
 Safety John Saunders Jr . stepped in front of a Tommy DeVito sideline pass for an interception, which was his team-leading fifth of training camp. 
 RB Rhamondre Stevenson had a beautiful touchdown catch in the end zone from QB Drake Maye , beating LB Robert Spillane on a longer-developing pass route from the high red zone. 
 After punter Bryce Baringer sustained an undisclosed injury in Saturday's preseason game, the team signed veteran Matt Haack , who showed up midway through practice and donned No. 19. 
 Patriots signed former Boston College OL Jack Conley , who spent time with the team in 2025. He wore No. 67 and practiced at right guard with the third unit. 
 

 

 

 Thursday, Aug. 20 
 Quarterback Drake Maye has said that wide receiver A.J. Brown is "open even when he's covered," and Thursday's practice with the Eagles highlighted the fine line Maye walks with that thought.

 Maye was intercepted twice when targeting Brown, the first of which came in front of the right pylon in red zone work as cornerback Riq Woolen stepped in front of the pass and returned it for a would-be pick-six.

 "I was just late with the football. You can't be late in the red zone," Maye explained. "It's tight, and it's a concept that we probably need to get some more work on and just find some timing."

 The second pick came closer to midfield, with Maye firing a pass to Brown on an in-breaking route. It was unclear in real-time if Brown caught the ball and had it jarred loose from his grasp by Woolen, or if the ball simply popped up in the air. Nonetheless, outside linebacker Jalyx Hunt showed impressive awareness and quickness to dive and haul it in.

 Overall, Maye was pleased with the two days of practices with the Eagles. The teams play Saturday night but it's possible Maye won't see any action based on the extensive reps he received in practice.

 "I think we had a lot of great work," he said. "You got to string some plays together in a row, and I felt like we did that more [Wednesday] than we did today."

 More observations: 

 
 CB Marcus Jones had two interceptions. That gave the Patriots a total of seven INTs over the two days of practice with the Eagles. 
 With starting right tackle Morgan Moses having his reps managed, first-round pick Caleb Lomu elevated to the top unit in his place. 
 In one-on-one red zone work, Brown had what looked like a highlight-reel catch in the back left corner of the end zone on CB Quinyon Mitchell , but the official ruled him out of bounds. If there was instant replay, it might have been overturned. 
 Former teammates Brown and Jalen Hurts shared time together after practice, as did Drake Maye and Hurts. 
 More than an hour after the final open-to-the-public practice ended, two players remained signing autographs for fans -- WRs Efton Chism III and Mack Hollins . 
 

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 19 
 On the first snap the Patriots and Eagles were on the field together, wide receiver A.J. Brown ran a go route against cornerback Quinyon Mitchell and had a chance to electrify the estimated crowd of 12,000-plus.

 Brown created separation, fought through a potential penalty, but then failed to secure the catch.

 It was the only blemish on a productive day in which Brown totaled six receptions against his former team.

 "Q got away with a little holding," Brown said with a laugh, when asked to describe the play against Mitchell. "I won, he pulled himself back into the play, and I just have to finish the play. My right hand didn't get to the ball quick enough. My left hand got on the ball. That's on me. Attention to detail -- catching the ball high, not letting it get low.

 "... It's never about who I'm going against, it's the little things; that could have been a 40-yard bomb, but now it's a long foul ball. Those are the things I'm focusing on."

 Brown met with reporters after practice and upon his arrival he took note of seeing "old friends" in the media from spending four seasons in Philadelphia. He said he hasn't spoken with Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts since the trade, but he had "all love" for his time in Philadelphia.

 As for how he feels things are going learning to work with a new quarterback in Drake Maye , he said: "There have definitely been some challenges but he's very special. He makes my job a lot easier. There's a learning curve and we'll continue to keep working at it."

 

 More observations: 

 
 One area of improvement from last week's practice with the Colts came in the two-minute drill. The Patriots' top offense rushed Andy Borregales on for a successful field goal, while the top defense held the Eagles without points. The backup units also were successful, with the D capping off a turnover-laden day as CB Kindle Vildor registered an INT. 
 The Patriots totaled five interceptions from safeties Craig Woodson (2) and John Saunders Jr ., and CBs Vildor and Marcus Jones . 
 Although not facing a pass rush that can tackle him, Maye was accurate and in rhythm for the most part. One charting of his day had him 16-of-19 in 11-on-11 work. 
 Rookie OLB Gabe Jacas was elevated to the first unit on punt protection, and said after practice he has never executed those responsibilities prior to coming to New England. Coach Mike Vrabel has been spending one-on-one time with him.

title: 2026 New Orleans Saints: Projecting final 53-man roster
summary: Injuries have hit New Orleans hard, so some tough decisions will be made at wide receiver and running back.
full_text:
NEW ORLEANS -- The Saints open the 2026 NFL regular season at the Detroit Lions on Sept. 13 ( 1 p.m. ET, Fox ) at Ford Field. But first, they play one more preseason game, Friday at the Dallas Cowboys ( 8 p.m. ET, ESPN Unlimited ), and then must cut their roster to 53 players by 6 p.m. ET on Sunday.

 Who will make the team? Which positions have tough decisions on deck? And where might the lineup be deepest and thinnest this season?

 The Saints have had major injuries lately to key players such as defensive end Cameron Jordan , wide receiver Jordyn Tyson , running back Alvin Kamara , guard Dillion Radunz (season-ending) and defensive tackle Bryan Bresee (season-ending). With Kamara, Jordan and Tyson expected to return, the Saints will have to do some roster maneuvering to shore up depth until each returns.

 Here is our projection for the 53-man roster for the Saints.

 

 Quarterbacks (3) 
 Tyler Shough , Zach Wilson , Spencer Rattler 

 Wilson had a better performance than Rattler in the first preseason game, but neither player has locked down the backup position after a lackluster performance by both quarterbacks against the Rams on Saturday. Rattler has gotten more time with the second-team offense in practice, but the Saints might want to keep all three quarterbacks unless one backup seals the deal in the preseason finale.

 
 

 Running backs (5) 
 Alvin Kamara , Travis Etienne Jr ., Zamir White , Audric Estime , Kendre Miller 

 Miller wasn't going to initially make this roster due to his limited availability after being injured in camp, but this running back room has seen injuries all over and he has performed well now that he's healthy again. Kamara is out at least a month with a sprained MCL, and Neal and Estime are also injured.

 The Saints traded for White on Sunday, indicating they're concerned about depth. With Devin Neal recently suffering a hamstring injury, assume he (or Estime) ends up on injured reserve to start the season, with White adding depth until the room gets healthy.

 
 Wide receivers (5) 
 Chris Olave , Devaughn Vele , Barion Brown , Bryce Lance , Bub Means 

 Tyson's injury and Ja'Lynn Polk's retirement opened up a roster spot for another player, and it was a toss-up between Kevin Austin Jr . and Means. Both have had solid camps and will likely stick around in some capacity, but Means gets the nod here.

 
 Tight ends (3) 
 Juwan Johnson , Noah Fant , Oscar Delp 

 Johnson and Fant are locks due to their production, and Delp gets a spot due to his third-round draft status. Moliki Matavao doesn't make the roster for now due to numbers needed at running back.

 
 Offensive linemen (9) 
 Erik McCoy , Kelvin Banks Jr ., Cesar Ruiz , Taliese Fuaga , David Edwards , Jeremiah Wright , Asim Richards , William Sherman , Torricelli Simpkins III 

 Radunz tore his ACL and is out for the season, which leaves a spot open for Simpkins as the backup center. Sherman has played multiple positions in camp, which proves valuable as a backup.

 
 

 Defensive linemen (10) 
 Cameron Jordan , Chase Young , Carl Granderson , Tyree Wilson , Anfernee Jennings , Nathan Shepherd , Vernon Broughton , John Ridgeway III , Christen Miller , Davon Godchaux 

 Bryan Bresee tore his ACL and is out for the season. Godchaux has been hurt, but he'll make the roster with the spot opened up by Bresee. The Saints might have been tempted to put undrafted free agent edge rusher Mike Heldman here after a strong camp by him, but he'll be a practice squad candidate for now.

 
 Linebackers (5) 
 Kaden Elliss , Pete Werner , Danny Stutsman , Jaylan Ford , Isaiah Stalbird 

 There aren't any changes here for now. Chris Rumph II switched to this position but he has missed several weeks with an ankle injury. While the severity is unknown, if he begins the season on IR, then this position stays the same as it was pre-camp.

 
 Cornerbacks (5) 
 Kool-Aid McKinstry , Martin Emerson Jr. , Isaac Yiadom , Quincy Riley , Jayden Price 

 Price, a 2024 undrafted rookie who spent time on the Saints' practice squad last season, played his way onto the roster with a consistently good camp, including an interception in the first preseason game. He has backed up Jonas Sanker at the Star position.

 
 Safeties (5) 
 Julian Blackmon , Justin Reid , Jordan Howden , Jonas Sanker , Terrell Burgess 

 Lorenzo Styles Jr. becomes the odd man out here with veteran Burgess making the roster again. Styles, a fifth-round draft pick, can stick around on the practice squad.

 
 Special teams (3) 
 Zach Wood (LS), Ryan Wright (P), Tanner Brown (K) 

 Does either kicker want this job? Charlie Smyth entered with the edge due to his time with the team, but a couple of three-miss days in practice were concerning. Brown looked like he could be taking the lead because of that, but his only kick in Saturday's game was a miss. The kicker might not even be in the roster right now, and this position is certainly up for grabs.

title: 2026 New York Giants: Projecting final 53-man roster
summary: Tough calls will have to happen at wide receiver (keep Odell Beckham Jr.?) and at running back (roster four guys?).
full_text:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- The New York Giants open the 2026 NFL regular season against the Dallas Cowboys on Sept. 13 ( 8:20 p.m. ET, NBC ) at MetLife Stadium. But first, they play one more preseason game Friday against the New York Jets ( 7:30 p.m. ET ) and then must cut their roster to 53 players by 6 p.m. ET on Sunday.

 Who will make the team? Which positions have tough decisions on deck? And where might the lineup be deepest and thinnest this season?

 Wide receiver will be the source of the most difficult decisions for new Giants coach John Harbaugh, with big names Odell Beckham Jr . and Braxton Berrios among them. Beckham has proved this summer that he's a capable receiver, but is it worth keeping a sixth or seventh wide receiver who doesn't play special teams? One can argue that the much lesser-known Dalen Cambre makes more sense. The other tough calls will come at running back and whether the Giants should keep all four backs in  Cam Skattebo , Tyrone Tracy Jr ., Devin Singletary and Najee Harris , and at cornerback where they remain on the prowl for outside options.

 Here is our projection for the 53-man roster for the Giants.

 

 Quarterbacks (2) 
 Jaxson Dart , Jameis Winston 

 Dart is the starter and Winston is the backup. It was never going to be anything else.

 
 Running backs (4) 
 Cam Skattebo , Tyrone Tracy Jr ., Devin Singletary , Najee Harris 

 It's a deep room after the addition of Harris last week. All four will fight for playing time, with Skattebo and Tracy still the front-runners.

 
 Fullbacks (1) 
 Patrick Ricard 

 Harbaugh brought him to New York for a reason. He's a big addition to the running game and will have a massive role.

 
 Tight ends (3) 
 Isaiah Likely , Theo Johnson , Chris Manhertz 

 A thin group, but Ricard also plays the tight end position.

 
 Wide receivers (7) 
 Malik Nabers , Malachi Fields , Darnell Mooney , Darius Slayton , Calvin Austin III , Braxton Berrios , Odell Beckham Jr . 

 Beckham barely snuck onto the roster, and it wouldn't be surprising if he somehow lands on the practice squad as they finagle the roster. Berrios is safer because he is the team's returner.

 
 Offensive linemen (9) 
 Andrew Thomas , Jermaine Eluemunor ,  Jon Runyan , Francis Mauigoa ,  John Michael Schmitz Jr ., Marcus Mbow , J.C. Davis , Bryan Hudson ,  Aaron Stinnie 

 This leaves off Evan Neal , Josh Ezeudu  and Jake Kubas . It's a new era under Harbaugh. Hudson also sticks over Lucas Patrick , who is tough to keep because of his "old-man" knee.

 
 

 Defensive linemen (4) 
 DJ Reader , Shelby Harris , Darius Alexander ,  Leki Fotu 

 The Giants will be looking outside for interior defensive line help after final cuts and into the season. Also, Chauncey Golston and several other outside linebackers are considered part of the defensive line because of their ability to play inside. Meanwhile, sixth-round rookie Bobby Jamison-Travis  (he's raw) lands on the practice squad. 

 
 Outside linebackers (4) 
 Brian Burns , Abdul Carter , Kayvon Thibodeaux ,  Chauncey Golston 

 This might be the strongest position group on the roster, and they know it. "We already say this team goes as far as we go," Carter said recently. "So, we already put that chip on our shoulder."

 
 Inside linebackers (5) 
 Tremaine Edmunds , Arvell Reese , Jack Kelly , Micah McFadden , Zaire Barnes 

 This became a deep group when they drafted Reese at No. 5 this year. McFadden is a starter in a backup role. Barnes makes it for his special teams play, which is especially important to Harbaugh.

 
 Cornerbacks (6) 
 Greg Newsome II , Deonte Banks , Paulson Adebo , Colton Hood , Dru Phillips , Korie Black 

 This could get shaken up if the Giants find an upgrade. It's a group filled with questions from top to bottom. Might be the weakest position group on the roster.

 
 Safeties (5) 
 Jevon Holland , Tyler Nubin , Jason Pinnock , Ar'Darius Washington , Elijah Campbell 

 The starter opposite Holland isn't set. Nubin, Pinnock and Washington are in the mix. Campbell brings special teams value.

 
 Special teams (3) 
 Dominic Zvada (K), Jordan Stout (P), Ben Mann (LS) 

 Zvada wins the kicking job despite Ben Sauls having a strong summer. And the Giants are going with the undrafted rookie Mann as their long-snapper. That's a lot of trust in rookies.

title: Did Aaron Glenn, Geno Smith change? 10 notes from Jets camp
summary: As New York heads toward the regular season, we look back at training camp, including the high-end promise of rookie linebacker David Bailey﻿.
full_text:
FLORHAM PARK, N.J. -- The New York Jets were 0-2, on their way to 0-7 and eventually 3-14, when Aaron Glenn delivered a line that still resonates. "Big ships turn slow," the coach said last September.

 Translation: Don't expect an overnight miracle after more than a decade of losing and dysfunction.

 Glenn inherited a team that seemed lost at sea -- a league-low .311 winning percentage from 2016 to 2024 -- but now he's had more than a year to implement his program, and there's no reason why it shouldn't look better in 2026.

 "We're still turning that ship -- we're still turning it -- but I like exactly where we are," Glenn said last week.

 Training camp ends Tuesday, the preseason culminates Friday against the New York Giants  (7:30 p.m. ET) and soon Season 2 of the Glenn era will be underway.

 Here's a look at 10 things we learned in training camp:

 

 1. Glenn has changed 

 He seems more at ease than last year, not as edgy. Maybe it's because he's back in his comfort zone, calling the defense -- his "super power," as he noted in the offseason. Maybe it's because his revamped coaching staff is more experienced than last year, particularly with offensive coordinator Frank Reich on board -- a departure from first-timer Tanner Engstrand.

 Maybe it's simply his natural evolution as a head coach. It's probably all of the above.

 Glenn said his rookie year taught him the importance of being able to "pivot" -- changing on the fly if something (or someone) isn't working.

 

 2. Speaking of a pivot ... 

 Subscribing to load management, Glenn dialed back training camp in the interest of preserving players for the regular season. An extreme example: Linebacker Kiko Mauigoa received a veterans' rest day because his practice rep count was soaring, according to Glenn. Mind you, Mauigoa is only 23 years old. Typically, the rest days are reserved for the guys in the 30-and-older club.

 Glenn, who last year made such a big deal out of having live tackling in practice, eliminated the drills from this year's script while claiming, "I want to be the best tackling team in the NFL." He believes "thud" tackling (hitting and wrapping up but not going to the ground) promotes better technique.

 In his soul, Glenn is an old-school coach, but he is embracing new-school concepts such as sports science and artificial intelligence.

 

 

 3. Geno Smith hasn't changed 

 At 35, Smith still throws a gorgeous ball -- his upper-body mechanics are pristine, Reich said -- but he's still prone to interceptions, based on what he showed in camp. He threw a league-high 17 interceptions last season for the Las Vegas Raiders , and it'll be up to Reich and quarterbacks coach Bill Musgrave to coach that out of him. He was sharp in his preseason debut Friday night against the Steelers, illustrating how good he can be when he's on.

 In practice, Smith displayed a penchant for pushing the ball downfield, a tendency that played well with his receivers. They loved his aggressiveness, his willingness to take chances.

 

 4. The organization believes in Cade Klubnik  -- more than we thought 

 You knew there was an affinity for the former Clemson star when they traded up 18 spots to draft him in the fourth round, but they doubled down by not bringing in a seasoned quarterback for the No. 2 job. They made it Klubnik's job to lose ... and he hasn't. Not in emphatic fashion, though.

 Klubnik was up and down in camp, and his performance against the Steelers wasn't as crisp as the previous week, but the organization apparently has seen enough maturity and intelligence to make him the backup.

 "He's kind of got a little bit of a swagger to him," guard Joe Tippmann said.

 The decision to go with a middle-round rookie for such an important job carries a lot of risk, especially for a head coach who needs to win games in a potential make-or-break season.

 

 

 5. David Bailey will be the Jets' most compelling defensive rookie since Sauce Gardner (2022) 

 You can't take your eyes off him when he lines up on the edge, usually over the right tackle, because his speed creates possibilities.

 "I see him in the backfield all the time, my gosh," defensive tackle Harrison Phillips said.

 The No. 2 draft pick still is polishing his craft, but the raw tools -- notably, an elite get-off -- were evident on most days in camp. So was his confidence. During a joint practice with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , he did some trash talking, telling veteran tackle Luke Goedeke that he was eager to beat him in a one-on-one drill. And he did, sparking a melee. Against the Steelers, he used a power rush to beat veteran tackle Broderick Jones for a sack.

 

 6. Beyond Bailey, the most impactful rookie was -- surprise! 

 It wasn't a great camp for the draft class, as tight end Kenyon Sadiq , cornerback D'Angelo Ponds and safety VJ Payne missed significant time because of injuries. Wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr . was OK, nothing spectacular.

 The unsung standout was fourth-round defensive lineman Darrell Jackson Jr ., a 6-foot-5, 315-pounder with knock-back ability and surprisingly quick feet. With T'Vondre Sweat nursing a hamstring for the first three weeks, Jackson capitalized on his extra reps. Because he can play multiple spots, including 5-technique end, he could crack the early-season rotation.

 

 7. Minkah Fitzpatrick will be everywhere 

 On the first play of the first preseason game, the former All-Pro safety set up on the line of scrimmage and blitzed from the front side. Get used to it. The plan is to deploy Fitzpatrick in a Kyle Hamilton -like role, which means multiple positions.

 

 Publicly and privately, Fitzpatrick has expressed a desire to be a chess piece in Glenn's defense. He doesn't want to be a traditional safety. His wish will be granted.

 

 8. The competition fell short 

 One of the objectives in camp was to increase the competition on both sides of the ball, but it didn't materialize, in part, because of injuries. Cornerback got hit the hardest, as Ponds and Nahshon Wright missed time. The only true positional battle is safety ( Andre Cisco versus Dane Belton ), along with kicker ( Jason Sanders versus Cade York ).

 

 9. Glenn's defense will be aggressive 

 He outlined a four-point plan for his defense: Disrupt the quarterback. Disrupt the receivers. Attack the ball. Limit explosive plays.

 In other words, look for pressure schemes and a lot of man-to-man coverage. When he called plays for the Detroit Lions , his "man" percentage in 2024 was the highest in the league, per NFL Next Gen Stats. His blitz rate was No. 2.

 

 10. And, finally: Most Improved Player 

 It is wide receiver Isaiah Williams . Can the team MVP be the most improved? In this case, yes, because he was voted the MVP last season by his teammates because of his success as a kick returner. This summer, he made his impact as a receiver, improving in all areas and impressing with his leadership.

 Receivers coach Shawn Jefferson said Williams is so reliable that, "If I was in a burning building -- Jefferson pretended to dial a phone -- 'Hey, you need to come get me.' And he's on the way.

 "Just to put it bluntly, he's a heartbeat on offense."

title: 2026 New York Jets: Projecting final 53-man roster
summary: New York looking to solidify starters at key positions, including settling on a kicker. Who will make the final roster?
full_text:
FLORHAM PARK, N.J. -- The New York Jets open the 2026 NFL regular season at the Tennessee Titans on Sept. 13 at Nissan Stadium. But first, they play one more preseason game Friday against the New York Giants and then must cut their roster to 53 players by 6 p.m. ET on Sunday.

 Who will make the team? Which positions have tough decisions on deck? And where might the lineup be deepest and thinnest this season?

 As a rebuilding team, the Jets could look to churn the bottom of the roster on the final cutdown. Darren Mougey is an aggressive general manager, having made 13 player trades in the last 12 months. They could use depth upgrades on the offensive line, linebacker and safety.

 Here is our projection for the 53-man roster for the Jets:

 

 Quarterbacks (2) 
 Geno Smith , Cade Klubnik 

 This is a transition year for the quarterback position. Smith, 35, coming off a down year with the Las Vegas Raiders , is a one-year stop gap. They probably will draft a quarterback in 2027. In the meantime, they're eager to see what they have in Klubnik, a fourth-round pick -- so eager that it was decided not to bring in legitimate competition for the No. 2 job. Will Mougey and coach Aaron Glenn regret not having an experienced backup?

 
 Running backs (4) 
 Breece Hall , Braelon Allen , Isaiah Davis , Kene Nwangwu 

 This is the Jets' deepest position. They expect big things out of Hall, whom they re-signed for $43.5 million over three years this offseason. This is a pivotal year for Allen, who tantalizes with his size and speed but hasn't put it all together yet. Fullback Andrew Beck could be the odd-man out.

 

 Wide receivers (6) 

 Garrett Wilson , Adonai Mitchell , Isaiah Williams , Omar Cooper Jr ., Arian Smith , Tim Patrick 

 Wilson is the only proven commodity. Mitchell, Williams and Cooper are intriguing players at different stages of development. The key is Mitchell, who must validate the organization's belief in him. Cooper, a first-round pick in April, is battling Williams for the WR3 spot. Smith has drop issues but probably will stick because of special teams. Patrick, the OG, isn't a roster lock.

 

 Tight ends (4) 

 Mason Taylor , Kenyon Sadiq , Jeremy Ruckert , Jelani Woods 

 This is a young, talented group that still hasn't reached its ceiling. It hinges on Taylor improving as a receiver and the rookie first-rounder in Sadiq ... well, staying healthy. Offensive coordinator Frank Reich is planning to use Sadiq as a Swiss Army knife. Woods is a bubble player.

 

 Offensive linemen (9) 

 Olu Fashanu , Dylan Parham , Josh Myers , Joe Tippmann , Armand Membou , Max Mitchell , Xavier Newman , Chukwuma Okorafor , Anez Cooper 

 The starting five is solid, especially the right side with Membou and Tippmann. The concern is depth, particularly the interior. The Jets were the only team to start the same five in every game last season. What are the odds of that happening again?

 

 Defensive linemen (5) 

 Harrison Phillips , David Onyemata ,  T'Vondre Sweat , Jowon Briggs , Darrell Jackson Jr . 

 Phillips, Onyemata and Sweat will be the starting three in the base 3-4 front. They're good run defenders, but where's the interior pass rush? The 366-pound Sweat can be special if he stays in shape and motivated. Former Dallas Cowboys first-round pick Mazi Smith , acquired in the Quinnen Williams trade, is injured and will be hard-pressed to make the roster. 

 

 Edge rushers (4) 

 David Bailey , Joseph Ossai , Will McDonald IV , Kingsley Enagbare 

 Next to Hall and Wilson, Bailey might be the most exciting player on the team. This year's No. 2 overall pick oozes pass-rushing talent but needs to get stronger versus the run. Ossai and Enagbare bring toughness to the group. McDonald, no longer an every-down player, will be used mainly on passing downs. Braiden McGregor is lurking.

 

 Linebackers (5) 

 Demario Davis , Jamien Sherwood , Kiko Mauigoa , Marcelino McCrary-Ball , Mykal Walker 

 Davis, known for his vocal leadership, will raise the energy level of the defense. At 37, he's still an effective run stuffer, but his pass coverage bears watching -- an area where Sherwood has struggled. Depth is a big concern.

 

 Cornerbacks (6) 

 Brandon Stephens ,  Azareye'h Thomas , Jarvis Brownlee Jr .,  D'Angelo Ponds , Nahshon Wright ,  Qwan'tez Stiggers 

 The anticipated battles at CB2 (Thomas versus Wright) and nickel back (Brownlee versus Ponds) haven't materialized because of injuries to Wright and the rookie Ponds, a second-round pick. Ponds figures to play his way into the mix once he's up to speed after a calf injury. Jordan Clark , having a sneaky good camp, is bidding for a spot.

 

 Safeties (5) 

 Minkah Fitzpatrick , Dane Belton , Andre Cisco , Malachi Moore , VJ Payne 

 It's Fitzpatrick and everybody else. Next to quarterback, this probably is the most suspect position on the team. Cisco is an incumbent, but it wouldn't surprise anyone if he loses his starting job to Belton. You will see some three-safety looks throughout the season. They're still waiting for Moore to make a leap.

 

 Special teams (3) 

 Cade York  (K), Austin McNamara  (P), Thomas Hennessy  (LS) 

 The York- Jason Sanders battle is too close to call, but it's clear that York has the stronger leg. McNamara, coming off a breakout year, has added new wrinkles to his punting repertoire.

title: 2026 Philadelphia Eagles: Projecting final 53-man roster
summary: Coach Nick Sirianni and GM Howie Roseman have difficult decisions to make at quarterback and wide receiver.
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA -- The  Philadelphia Eagles  open the 2026 NFL regular season against the Washington Commanders on Sept. 13 at Lincoln Financial Field. But first, they play one more preseason game Friday versus the Cincinnati Bengals and then must cut their roster to 53 players by 6 p.m. ET on Sunday.

 Who will make the team? Which positions have tough decisions on deck? And where might the lineup be deepest and thinnest this season?

 There's intrigue at wide receiver with a number of players vying for the final spot or two. Quarterback is interesting as well, given the No. 2 role is still seemingly up for grabs. Whoever loses out could be on the move.

 Here is our projection for the 53-man roster for the Eagles.

 

 Quarterbacks (3) 

 

 Jalen Hurts , Andy Dalton , Cole Payton 

 Dalton and Tanner McKee have been competing for the backup role all offseason, and there's been no clear separation between the two. General manager Howie Roseman has said he'd be comfortable carrying four QBs on the roster, but it would be no surprise if either Dalton or McKee got dealt before the start of the season.

 

 Running backs (3) 

 Saquon Barkley , Tank Bigsby , Will Shipley 

 Dameon Pierce looked good early in camp, but a hamstring injury slowed his momentum. If they want a fullback on the roster, it could open the door for Carson Steele .

 

 Wide receivers (6) 

 DeVonta Smith , Makai Lemon , Dontayvion Wicks , Hollywood Brown , Darius Cooper , Elijah Moore 

 This becomes especially tough if the Eagles decide to carry five receivers, given both Cooper and Moore have developed a good connection with Hurts. The 6-foot-6 Johnny Wilson and return specialist Britain Covey both bring unique skill sets to the table.

 

 

 Tight ends (4) 

 Dallas Goedert , Eli Stowers , Johnny Mundt , Grant Calcaterra 

 Stowers, the team's 2026 second-round pick, still needs some seasoning -- particularly as a blocker. With Mundt as the only true blocking tight end on the roster, this feels like a position Roseman could look to tweak for a team that wants to be run-heavy.

 

 Offensive linemen (10) 

 Lane Johnson , Jordan Mailata , Landon Dickerson , Tyler Steen , Cam Jurgens , Markel Bell , Fred Johnson , Willie Lampkin , Micah Morris , Drew Kendall 

 Bell, a potential replacement at right tackle when 36-year-old Lane Johnson calls it a career, has been the best Eagles rookie this offseason by a good margin. The undersized Lampkin (5-foot-11, 290 pounds) has acquitted himself well at both center and guard during the preseason and has earned a spot.

 

 Defensive linemen (6) 

 Jalen Carter , Jordan Davis , Moro Ojomo , Ty Robinson , Uar Bernard , Byron Young 

 Robinson had a quiet rookie season but has flashed in recent weeks. Bernard, a member of the International Player Pathway program from Nigeria, hasn't played football at any level. He has a ton of ability, and the coaching staff is invested in him.

 

 Linebackers (9) 

 Zack Baun , Jihaad Campbell , Jeremiah Trotter Jr ., Jonathan Greenard , Jalyx Hunt , Nolan Smith Jr ., AJ Epenesa , Smael Mondon Jr ., Arnold Ebiketie 

 Greenard has been sidelined with a pec injury for weeks. Smith and Hunt will be leaned on should it take some time for Greenard to get back up to speed.

 

 

 Cornerbacks (6) 

 Quinyon Mitchell , Cooper DeJean , Riq Woolen , Jonathan Jones , Mac McWilliams , Kelee Ringo 

 The combo of Mitchell, DeJean and Woolen has the potential to be the league's best. McWilliams, who was selected in the fifth round of the 2025 draft, needs more consistency to his game but has had some strong moments.

 

 Safeties (3) 

 Andrew Mukuba , Marcus Epps , Michael Carter II 

 DeJean will move from nickel to safety in base packages. That allows Philadelphia to go a little light at this position if need be.

 

 Special teams (3) 

 Jake Elliott  (K), Braden Mann  (P), Rocco Underwood  (LS) 

 Elliott is coming off a down season by his standards and needs to bounce back. Mann, meanwhile, has emerged as one of the top punters in the game.

title: 2026 Pittsburgh Steelers: Projecting final 53-man roster
summary: The toughest decision facing Pittsburgh comes behind QB Aaron Rodgers and the deliberation between keeping two or three backups.
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Steelers open the 2026 NFL regular season against the Atlanta Falcons on Sept. 13 ( 1 p.m. ET, Fox ) at Acrisure Stadium. But first they play one more preseason game Thursday at the Buffalo Bills  ( 7 p.m. ET, NFL Network ) and then must cut their roster to 53 players by 6 p.m. ET on Sunday.

 Who will make the team? Which positions have tough decisions on deck? And where might the lineup be deepest and thinnest this season?

 The toughest decision facing the Steelers comes behind Aaron Rodgers and the deliberation between keeping two or three backup quarterbacks. Will Howard and Drew Allar are young and unproven, but their preseason performances show they're progressing well under coach Mike McCarthy and could handle filling in for Rodgers in case of emergency. Beyond quarterback, the depth on the defensive line made that position a difficult one to reduce.

 Here is our projection for the 53-man roster for the Steelers.

 

 Quarterbacks (4) 
 

 Aaron Rodgers , Mason Rudolph ,  Will Howard , Drew Allar 

 McCarthy has never had four quarterbacks on his Week 1 roster, but that changes this season. While keeping four signal-callers takes away another roster spot, the decision is necessary because the gulf between Rudolph and the pair of young quarterbacks is sizable.

 That much was noticeable in the second preseason game when Howard threw a pair of interceptions and couldn't replicate the success he had in his first outing. Allar's arm talent is evident, but he is still too green to be a legitimate safety net for a 42-year-old quarterback. Keeping Rudolph along with Allar and Howard gives the Steelers an insurance policy for Rodgers and McCarthy more time to evaluate and develop potential future options.

 
 Running backs (3) 
 Jaylen Warren , Rico Dowdle , Travis Homer 

 Lew Nichols turned heads in training camp, but ultimately, Homer's special teams prowess gives him the edge over the undrafted free agent. Nichols, though, is a good practice squad candidate. Kaleb Johnson , a 2025 third-round pick, was buried in the running back rotation throughout training camp and struggled to stand out in a crowded backfield.

 
 Wide receivers (6) 
 DK Metcalf , Michael Pittman Jr ., Germie Bernard , Roman Wilson , Ben Skowronek , Kaden Wetjen 

 No change here from the pre-training camp prediction. This group has been solidified throughout camp.

 
 Tight ends (3) 
 Pat Freiermuth , Darnell Washington , Robert Tonyan 

 Tonyan emerged as Howard's go-to target in the first preseason game, and he's a savvy veteran with a good rapport with Rodgers from their Green Bay days. He rounds out a solid tight end group.

 
 Fullbacks (1) 
 Riley Nowakowski 

 The rookie is a true fullback, something the Steelers haven't had since Roosevelt Nix in 2019.

 

 

 Offensive linemen (9) 

 Troy Fautanu , Zach Frazier , Mason McCormick , Spencer Anderson , Dylan Cook , Max Iheanachor , Gennings Dunker , Brock Hoffman , Broderick Jones 

 Jones' health to start training camp was a pleasant surprise after a long recovery from season-ending neck surgery . He still hasn't regained his strength or technique, but Iheanachor's early camp injury means that the Steelers need as much veteran depth as they can get at tackle.

 
 Defensive linemen (6) 
 Cameron Heyward , Keeanu Benton , Derrick Harmon , Yahya Black , Sebastian Joseph-Day , Gabriel Rubio 

 One of the biggest surprises of training camp is sixth-round rookie Rubio, who even missed the last six games of his final season at Notre Dame with an elbow injury. Rubio performed well in his preseason debut, and because of that, he edges out veterans Dean Lowry and Esezi Otomewo .

 
 Linebackers (9) 
 T.J. Watt , Alex Highsmith , Nick Herbig , Jack Sawyer , Patrick Queen , Payton Wilson , Cole Holcomb , Carson Bruener , Elandon Roberts 

 Roberts' late addition infused a shot of energy into training camp, and he'll be a key player in the Steelers' run defense. Veteran Malik Harrison was unnoticeable during camp, leading to Roberts taking his spot.

 
 Cornerbacks (6) 
 Jalen Ramsey , Joey Porter Jr , Jamel Dean , Asante Samuel Jr ., Daylen Everette , Brandin Echols 

 Half of this group missed significant parts of training camp either on PUP (Ramsey and Porter) or with an injury (Echols). But the Steelers unearthed quality depth in their absence thanks to a standout camp from Samuel. Everette, a rookie, had some growing pains in camp but largely held up against tough competition.

 
 Safeties (3) 
 DeShon Elliott , Jaquan Brisker , Rayshawn Jenkins 

 Keeping the fourth quarterback means making cuts somewhere else on the roster, and with the position flexibility of Ramsey, that spot is safety. Seventh-round pick  Robert Spears-Jennings  benefited from extra snaps in training camp with Elliott slowly working back from last season's knee injury, but the numbers just don't work in his favor. He's a great candidate for the practice squad and could get some gameday elevations to prove his value.

 
 Special teams (3) 
 Chris Boswell  (K), Cameron Johnston  (P), Christian Kuntz  (LS) 

 No changes here. The standard is the standard.

title: 2026 Seattle Seahawks: Projecting final 53-man roster
summary: Let's predict how many wide receivers and cornerbacks Seattle will keep on its roster as Sunday's cut-down day looms.
full_text:
RENTON, Wash. -- The Seattle Seahawks open the 2026 NFL regular season against the New England Patriots on Sept. 9 at Lumen Field. But first, they play one more preseason game Friday against the Kansas City Chiefs and then must cut their roster to 53 players by 6 p.m. ET on Sunday.

 Who will make the team? Which positions have tough decisions on deck? And where might the lineup be deepest and thinnest this season?

 Cornerback is the position with the most current intrigue. The Seahawks recently signed Trevon Diggs and have agreed to a deal with Terrion Arnold . But with the NFL expected to place Arnold on the NFL commissioner exempt list amid an ongoing legal case that could lead to a suspension, he won't be available anytime soon. Arnold, 23, was released by the  Detroit Lions  in June as he faces eight felony charges stemming from a kidnapping and robbery in Tampa, Florida, in February.

 Here is our projection for the 53-man roster for the Seahawks.

 

 Quarterbacks (3) 
 Sam Darnold , Drew Lock , Jalen Milroe 

 Milroe has made improvements from his rookie season, but he doesn't appear ready to overtake Lock for the No. 2 job. That would be his best path to seeing the field in specialty packages that take advantage of his athleticism.

 
 Running backs (3) 
 Jadarian Price , George Holani , Emanuel Wilson 

 It doesn't seem out of the question that Zach Charbonnet could come off the physically unable to perform list before the season opener and play sometime before Week 5. But in this projection, he stays on PUP and misses the first four games. Wilson's status for Week 1 also seems a bit iffy. The Seahawks can't afford for Price to get hurt, which is why they might be content to not play their top pick in the preseason even though he could use the reps as he prepares to lead Seattle's backfield until Charbonnet is ready. With Robbie Ouzts (neck) out for the season, Russell is the next man up at fullback.

 
 Fullbacks (1) 
 Brady Russell 

 With Robbie Ouzts (neck) out for the season, Russell is the next man up at fullback.

 
 Tight ends (4) 
 AJ Barner , Eric Saubert , Elijah Arroyo , Nick Kallerup 

 New coordinator Brian Fleury likes to use a fullback, but he has said that doesn't necessarily have to be a traditional fullback. Blocking specialists Saubert and Kallerup look like options in that regard.

 
 

 Wide receivers (5) 
 Jaxon Smith-Njigba , Cooper Kupp , Rashid Shaheed , Tory Horton , Montorie Foster Jr . 

 Jake Bobo 's season-ending knee injury opens up a spot, and in this projection, Foster wins it while Cody White begins the season on the practice squad. Horton was having an excellent camp before suffering an injury that has kept him out for over a week. It does not appear serious, but his durability remains a big question mark. The guess here is that rookie sixth-round pick Emmanuel Henderson Jr . starts the season on the practice squad and gets called up for gamedays early on.

 
 Offensive linemen (9) 
 Charles Cross , Grey Zabel , Jalen Sundell , Anthony Bradford ,  Abraham Lucas , Josh Jones , Olu Oluwatimi , Beau Stephens ,  Bryce Cabeldue 

 Oluwatimi has been a candidate to be traded, but the Seahawks may not want to further weaken their O-line depth after Mason Richman suffered a serious injury Sunday in their preseason game against the Tennessee Titans . Stephens, a sixth-round pick, is not yet ready to challenge Bradford for the starting job at right guard.

 
 Defensive linemen (6) 
 Leonard Williams , Byron Murphy II , Jarran Reed , Rylie Mills , Mike Morris , Brandon Pili 

 The Seahawks are hoping that Mills can break out in Year 2. Neither seventh-round pick Deven Eastern nor undrafted rookie Uso Seumalo appear to have done enough to earn a spot on the 53-man roster.

 
 Outside linebackers (5) 
 Uchenna Nwosu , DeMarcus Lawrence , Derick Hall , Dante Fowler Jr .,  Connor O'Toole 

 O'Toole and Jared Ivey both made the team as undrafted rookies last season but were regularly inactive as healthy scratches. Clearly, the Seahawks were afraid to lose them on waivers. They might have a similar fear this summer with O'Toole after his 1.5-sack performance against the Titans.

 
 Inside linebackers (4) 
 Ernest Jones IV , Drake Thomas , Tyrice Knight , Chazz Surratt 

 Knight is making a push for playing time after losing his starting job to Thomas last season. Just like he did a year ago, Patrick O'Connell is making a strong case for a roster spot.

 
 Cornerbacks (5) 
 Devon Witherspoon , Josh Jobe , Julian Neal , Nehemiah Pritchett , Trevon Diggs 

 Diggs might not be an immediate, surefire upgrade over Noah Igbinoghene or Pritchett, who are battling for the CB3 job. But he can at least reinforce the depth, as Neal, a rookie third-round pick, has likely fallen behind due to an undisclosed injury that has sidelined him for much of camp.

 As a vested veteran, Igbinoghene would not be subject to waivers if he's released, meaning the Seahawks could get him onto their practice squad and call him up if needed -- thereby saving a roster spot for someone else -- without fear of another team claiming him. The No. 3 cornerback spot looks like it will be a question mark regardless of who wins the job.

 
 Safeties (5) 
 Julian Love , Ty Okada , Nick Emmanwori , D'Anthony Bell ,  AJ Finley 

 Immediately after Emmanwori had ankle surgery in July, the Seahawks believed he would be ready for the opener. That now seems uncertain, as Emmanwori is off the PUP list but has yet to begin practicing. Bell is his backup as the third safety in their big nickel package. Rookie second-round pick Bud Clark broke his ankle against Tennessee and will be out for multiple months, according to Mike Macdonald.

 
 Special teams (3) 
 Jason Myers  (PK), Michael Dickson  (P), Chris Stoll  (LS) 

 The Seahawks ranked first in ESPN's Football Power Index special teams rankings last season. Stoll, their long-snapper, was an underrated part of that, which is why he got a new two-year contract over the offseason.
