title: 2026 San Francisco 49ers: Projecting final 53-man roster
summary: How will injuries impact the 49ers' final lineup? How will their WR and LB rooms shake out? We made roster projections before the Niners' last preseason game.
full_text:
SANTA CLARA, Calif. -- The San Francisco 49ers open the 2026 NFL regular season  against the Los Angeles Rams on Sept. 10 at 8:35 p.m. ET in Melbourne, Australia. But first, the 49ers play one more preseason game ( Thursday at the Raiders ) and then must cut their roster to 53 players by 6 p.m. ET on Sunday.

 Who will make the team and where might the lineup be deepest and thinnest this season?

 The 49ers have tough decisions at a few key positions, such as wide receiver, linebacker and offensive line. But injuries have also muddled the picture at running back and defensive line, leading to questions about who will fill out those spots.

 Here is our projection for the 53-man roster for the 49ers.

 

 Quarterbacks (2) 
 Brock Purdy , Mac Jones 

 The question here is whether Kurtis Rourke has done enough to convince the 49ers to keep three signal-callers. He played well in his preseason debut but suffered an injury that prevented him from building more of a case, which means the team could look to do some roster juggling to get him to injured reserve without using an extra roster spot.

 
 Running backs (4) 
 Christian McCaffrey ,  Kyle Juszczyk , Jordan James , Kaelon Black 

 Injuries to McCaffrey, James, Black and Isaac Guerendo have made this one of the most difficult groups to project because it's unclear who will be available once the season starts. Guerendo could begin the season on the physically unable to perform (PUP) list if the Niners want to hold onto him.

 
 Wide receivers (7) 
 Mike Evans , De'Zhaun Stribling ,  Deebo Samuel Sr ., Demarcus Robinson , Jordan Watkins , Christian Kirk ,  Jacob Cowing 

 There's a lot to sort out here after Ricky Pearsall 's season-ending knee surgery. Kirk has barely practiced because of a calf injury, which means his status is a big question. Cowing is the most reliable returner on the roster and had an 83-yard return for a score against the Chargers, which probably lands him a spot. We'll keep all three of Watkins, Cowing and Kirk for now but this seems like a good spot for some roster gymnastics where a vested veteran like Kirk could go and be brought back later.

 
 Tight ends (3) 
 George Kittle , Luke Farrell , Jake Tonges 

 These three are in with Kittle's return from the PUP list on Sunday. Brayden Willis has had a good camp but could probably sneak through to the practice squad.

 
 

 Offensive linemen (9) 
 Trent Williams , Jake Brendel , Colton McKivitz , Dominick Puni , Robert Jones , Brett Toth , Carver Willis , Vederian Lowe ,  Connor Colby 

 This is another tricky spot to project because of injuries. Willis and Toth have missed time with concussions, and the 49ers have three, maybe four players vying to be the starting left guard. Jones and Colby have been the frontrunners, but Willis looks like he's the current leader. Lowe has missed almost all of camp, but signed to be the swing tackle while Austen Pleasants was in a good spot before a knee injury that could land him on injured reserve. Rookie Enrique Cruz Jr . likely needs too much work to land on the initial 53, but he would make sense on the practice squad.

 
 Defensive linemen (9) 
 Nick Bosa , Osa Odighizuwa , C.J. West , Alfred Collins , Sam Okuayinonu , Romello Height , Keion White , Gracen Halton , James Thompson Jr . 

 Mykel Williams has been doing a lot of work on side fields as he recovers from a torn ACL , but we'll project him to begin the year on PUP and miss the first four games. From there, it's a lot of guesswork as Bosa, West, Collins, White and Halton have all dealt with injuries this preseason. Thompson is the surprise here after getting some run with the starters when West and/or Collins have missed practice time.

 
 Linebackers (7) 
 Fred Warner , Dre Greenlaw , Jaden Dugger , Tatum Bethune , Luke Gifford , Nick Martin , Garret Wallow 

 The Niners don't usually go this heavy at linebacker, but this might be the deepest group on the roster -- and also could be a logical spot for a possible trade. It's worth noting that with new coordinator Raheem Morris in charge of the defense, there are some names here who can fill multiple roles. Dugger heads that list, and he seems to have a good shot to be the " fever backer ." Bethune, Martin, Gifford and Wallow have jockeyed for roles on special teams. Rookie Larry Worth III is tough to leave off here, too.

 
 Cornerbacks (5) 
 Deommodore Lenoir , Renardo Green , Upton Stout , Jack Jones , Ephesians Prysock 

 A groin injury for Nate Hobbs likely means he lands on injured reserve, or the Niners release him with the chance to return when he's healthy. Darrell Luter Jr . has stuck around repeatedly, but Prysock's emergence allows them to get a bit younger here while keeping Jones as a versatile backup.

 
 Safeties (4) 
 Ji'Ayir Brown , Malik Mustapha , Marques Sigle , Siran Neal 

 Safety is another position where the Niners could look to add more help via trade or the waiver wire. The real drama here is whether Mustapha or Sigle will start next to Brown, and whether it's Neal or Ashtyn Davis (or neither) for a fourth spot. Neal gets the nod for his special teams excellence.

 
 Special teams (3) 
 Jon Weeks (LS), Corliss Waitman (P),  Eddy Pineiro  (K) 

 The Niners seem to have made their decision at punter, going with Waitman over rookie Jack Bouwmeester and locking in these three spots.

title: 2026 Tampa Bay Buccaneers: Projecting final 53-man roster
summary: Tampa Bay has some decisions to make on defense.
full_text:
TAMPA, Fla. -- The Tampa Bay Buccaneers open the 2026 NFL regular season at the Cincinnati Bengals  on Sept. 13. But first, they play one more preseason game Friday at the Jacksonville Jaguars , and then must cut their roster to 53 players by 6 p.m. ET on Sunday.

 Who will make the team? Which positions have tough decisions on deck? And where might the lineup be deepest and thinnest this season?

 This projection looks surprisingly close to what we had heading into camp. That includes outside linebacker Chris Braswell -- the Bucs' 2024 second-round draft pick -- among the cuts. Cornerback Josh Hayes , a 2023 sixth-round draft pick is also out too, with the addition of special teams Pro Bowler Miles Killebrew following Danny Smith from Pittsburgh. He was also outperformed by rookie undrafted free agent Ayden Garnes and Damarion "Pepe" Williams at outside cornerback.

 You'll also notice the Bucs have three quarterbacks in this projection. Many would argue Jalon Daniels played his way into the No. 2 role, but Jake Browning affords them some experience, which is a benefit to Mayfield.

 Here is our projection for the final 53-man roster for the Bucs.

 

 Quarterbacks (3) 
 Baker Mayfield ,  Jalon Daniels ,  Jake Browning 

 Daniels has proven to be a fast study going from a college wristband system to having his offensive coordinator in his helmet, and he gave the offense a jolt every time he entered the game, with his greatest attributes being his ability to throw on the run and thrive out of structure. Is he quite ready to step in if Mayfield goes down tomorrow though? That's where Browning comes in.

 
 Running backs (3) 
 Bucky Irving ,  Kenny Gainwell , Sean Tucker 

 Irving remains the starter while Gainwell handles third down duties while also offering a change of pace and contributions to the return game. Tucker, despite inconsistent opportunities over the last two years, has shown he's very capable (seven touchdowns last year) and beats out Josh Williams and Barika Kpeenu . 

 

 Wide receivers (6) 
  Chris Godwin Jr ., Emeka Egbuka , Jalen McMillan , Tez Johnson , Ted Hurst III ,  Kameron Johnson 
 Johnson wins the sixth receiver role due to his performance in the second preseason game, which saw him lining up in multiple spots and included a 22-yard reception off Jake Browning , and we saw him line up at punt and kick returner -- a role in which he started all last year. Garrett Greene was the only other receiver in the mix whom we saw on kick returns this preseason. Neither Dennis Houston nor Dean Patterson played special teams in the preseason, while David Sills V served as a gunner on punts.

 

 Tight ends (4) 

 Cade Otton , Payne Durham , Ko Kieft , Bauer Sharp 

 Sharp, a rookie sixth-round pick out of LSU, beats out third-year tight end Devin Culp because of his positional versatility to line up in different spots and blocking abilities. Kieft continues to be a big contributor on special teams.

 

 Offensive linemen (9) 

 

 Tristan Wirfs , Ben Bredeson , Graham Barton , Cody Mauch , Luke Goedeke , Justin Skule ,  Benjamin Chukwuma , Dan Feeney , Billy Schrauth 

 Chukwuma got a ton of opportunities with Wirfs dealing with injuries in camp, and he showed a lot of improvement. He and Skule will serve as backup tackles. Schrauth, a 2026 fifth-round pick, missed time with a knee injury. If he needs to miss more time, Luke Haggard gives them another backup who can play inside and outside, or there is Elijah Klein , who can play guard or center. Paul Rubelt can be the 17th member of the practice as part of the International Pathway Player Program, allowing for an extra roster spot.

 

 Defensive linemen (6) 

 Vita Vea , Calijah Kancey ,  A'Shawn Robinson ,  Rakeem Nunez-Roches , Elijah Roberts , DeMonte Capehart 

 Vea, Kancey and Robinson will start with Nuñez-Roches, Roberts and Capehart serving as backups. Capehart, the Bucs' other fifth-round pick this year, beats out Jayson Jones , Josiah Green  and  Elijah Simmons for the final spot.

 

 Outside linebackers (5) 

 Yaya Diaby , Al-Quadin Muhammad , Rueben Bain Jr ., Anthony Nelson , David Walker 

 Diaby and Bain will start, with Muhammad moving all across the line and Walker and Nelson serving in rotational capacities.  Mohamed Kamara  makes the practice squad.

 

 Inside linebackers (4) 
  Alex Anzalone , Josiah Trotter , Christian Rozeboom , SirVocea Dennis 

 Anzalone and Trotter will start, with Rozeboom (who had 122 tackles in 15 games for the Carolina Panthers last year) and Dennis serving as backups and contributing on special teams. Those two beat out John Bullock , Caden Fordham and Nick Jackson .

 

 Cornerbacks (6) 
 

 Zyon McCollum , Benjamin Morrison , Jacob Parrish , Keionte Scott , Ayden Garnes ,  Damarion Williams 

 McCollum and Parrish should be Week 1 starters, especially with Morrison coming back from a hamstring injury. Garnes and Williams beat out Hayes, a core special teams performer who showed some improvement in his coverage in camp but did not match that duo's consistent playmaking. Scott provides value as a nickelback, backup safety and he played outside corner in college.

 

 Safeties (4) 
 

 Antoine Winfield Jr ., Tykee Smith , Miles Killebrew , Rashad Wisdom 

 Wisdom, who had an interception in the first preseason game, plays free safety, while Killebrew can play strong safety. JJ Roberts who had a solid camp last year before suffering a torn ACL, is still working his way back from the injury.

 

 Special teams (3) 

 Chase McLaughlin  (K), Evan Deckers  (LS), Riley Dixon  (P) 

 The trio of specialists return, but it should be noted that Dixon did have some struggles this preseason.

title: 2026 Tennessee Titans: Projecting final 53-man roster
summary: Does QB Will Levis make the team? Tennessee has key decisions to make ahead of Sunday's roster cuts.
full_text:
NASHVILLE, Tenn. -- The Tennessee Titans open the 2026 NFL regular season against the New York Jets on Sept. 13 at Nissan Stadium. But first, they play the final game of the preseason Saturday ( 6 p.m. ET, NFL Network ) against the Chicago Bears and then must cut their roster to 53 players by 6 p.m. ET on Sunday.

 So who will make the team? Which positions have tough decisions on deck? And where might the lineup be deepest and thinnest this season?

 General manager Mike Borgonzi wanted to add talent to help aide second-year quarterback Cam Ward . They added receivers  Wan'Dale Robinson  (four years, $70 million) and Carnell Tate (No. 4 overall pick), and they have performed well at times during camp and could be vital parts of the passing game. The defense starts with the front where 2025 All-Pro  Jeffery Simmons pairs with newly signed free agent  John Franklin-Myers . But what was supposed to be an improved back end has raised question marks instead, especially with high-priced free agent additions in  Cor'Dale Flott  and Alontae Taylor .

 Here is our projection for the 53-man roster for the Titans.

 

 Quarterbacks (2) 
 Cam Ward , Mitchell Trubisky 

 Ward should benefit from playing under offensive coordinator Brian Daboll. Having Trubisky, who has played in the scheme before and knows what it's like to be charged with carrying an organization's hope for the future will provide a good source of experience. Carrying two quarterbacks will most likely signal the end for Will Levis ' time in Nashville.

 
 Running backs (4) 
 Tony Pollard , Tyjae Spears , Nicholas Singleton , Kalel Mullings 

 Spears and Pollard are in contract years as they gear up to split the bulk of the carries. Singleton had a solid start to camp and could claim a feature role in the future. The fourth spot came down to Mullings or Julius Chestnut with youth giving Mullings the edge.

 

 Wide receivers (6) 
 Calvin Ridley , Wan'Dale Robinson , Carnell Tate , Chimere Dike , Elic Ayomanor , Bryce Oliver 

 Tate is a future No.1 receiver while Robinson works the slot. Ayomanor has had the best camp for the receivers. Oliver and veteran  K.J. Osborn  jockeyed for the final spot, but Oliver's special teams value is too great to leave off the roster.

 

 Tight ends (4) 
 Gunnar Helm , Daniel Bellinger , David Martin-Robinson ,  Kylen Granson 

 Helm ascended to TE1 in only his second NFL season. Bellinger presents another option in the passing game. Robinson and Granson are more athletic options that can play H-back and contribute on special teams.

 
 

 Offensive linemen (10) 
 Dan Moore Jr ., Peter Skoronski , Austin Schlottmann , Fernando Carmona , JC Latham , Brandon Crenshaw-Dickson , Jackson Slater , Pat Coogan , Austin Deculus , Cordell Volson 

 This group had the most question marks heading into camp. Center and guard are still questionable after Schlottmann and Carmona are looking to prove themselves after earning the starting center and right guard spots. Crenshaw-Dickson is the swing tackle.

 

 Defensive linemen (10) 
 Jeffery Simmons ,  John Franklin-Myers , Jermaine Johnson II , Jordan Elliott , Keldric Faulk , Oluwafemi Oladejo , Solomon Thomas , Jackie Marshall , Jacob Martin , Khalen Saunders 

 The front line is the best unit on the team. Saleh wants a deep rotation along the line, so they keep 10 defensive linemen. Johnson and Martin lead a young group of outside pass rushers.

 

 Linebackers (4) 
 Cedric Gray , Cody Barton , Anthony Hill Jr ., James Williams Sr . 

 Any of these four are capable of starting. Both Hill and Williams were camp standouts.

 

 Cornerbacks (6) 

   Cor'Dale Flott , Alontae Taylor , Marcus Harris , Joshua Williams , Micah Robinson ,  Mario Goodrich III   

 The cornerback room has been remade with Flott and Taylor leading the way. Goodrich was a late addition, but he edged out Keydrain Calligan  for the final cornerback slot.

 

 Safeties (4) 
 Amani Hooker , Kevin Winston Jr .,  Tony Adams ,  Jerrick Reed II 

 Winston could blossom into a playmaker as he heads into Year 2, and Reed edged out  Erick Hallett II  for the fourth safety role.

 

 Special teams (3) 

 Joey Slye (K),  Tommy Townsend (P),  Morgan Cox (LS) 

 Cox is back for his 17th season. Townsend takes over the punter role after coming over from the Chiefs.

title: Commanders still searching for answers at center
summary: John Keim lays out why there's so much uncertainty surrounding the Commanders' starting center position.

title: 2026 Washington Commanders: Projecting final 53-man roster
summary: Who sticks from a deep WR room? How many QBs will be kept? Commanders reporter John Keim makes his predictions.
full_text:
ASHBURN, Va. -- The Washington Commanders open the 2026 NFL regular season at the Philadelphia Eagles on Sept. 13 at Lincoln Financial Field. But first, they play one more preseason game Friday against the Baltimore Ravens and then must cut their roster to 53 players by 6 p.m. ET on Sunday.

 Who will make the team? Which positions have tough decisions on deck? And where might the lineup be deepest and thinnest this season?

 The Commanders will have tough decisions at receiver, where they have eight players worthy of a roster spot. That could result in a possible trade -- potentially for a pick or, perhaps, more interior offensive line depth.

 The secondary will be interesting to watch as well, in part because corner Trey Amos has barely practiced this summer and last year's starting safeties, Will Harris and Quan Martin , could both be fighting for a roster spot this year. It will be interesting to see how they handle players such as left tackle  Laremy Tunsil (out with a torn triceps) and defensive lineman Jer'Zhan Newton (torn pec). Both will miss significant time, but if there's a chance they can return, both could be placed on injured reserve prior to final cuts -- with a return designation.

 Here is our projection for the 53-man roster for the Commanders.

 

 

 Quarterbacks (3) 
 Jayden Daniels , Marcus Mariota , Athan Kaliakmanis 

 With so many tough calls on offense, keeping three quarterbacks is somewhat difficult. But they drafted Kaliakmanis in the sixth round and he had a good enough preseason debut to warrant a spot. With Daniels missing 10 full games and parts of three others in 2025, quarterback depth is a necessity. Mariota also is nursing a sprained right medial collateral ligament.

 
 Running backs (4) 
 Rachaad White , Jacory Croskey-Merritt ,  Robert Henry Jr ., Kaytron Allen 

 Allen offers a different type of runner, able to get tough yards inside. Fellow rookie Henry Jr. is a possibility if they keep four at the position -- veterans Jeremy McNichols (quad) and Jerome Ford (hamstring) are hurt -- but a tough second preseason game didn't help. Washington wants to emphasize the run game more, but it likely will be by committee with White in particular on third downs while Croskey-Merritt offers more explosiveness in the run game.

 
 Wide receivers (7) 
 Terry McLaurin , Stefon Diggs , Antonio Williams , Treylon Burks , Jaylin Lane , Luke McCaffrey , Dyami Brown 

 This is easily the toughest call on offense as eight players warrant a spot, as well as veteran Van Jefferson . But others are ahead in part because of their special teams ability -- notably Lane and McCaffrey. The latter needs to prove more as a receiver and that's where Jefferson could edge him out. Washington has far more depth here than in 2025.

 
 Tight ends (4) 
 Chig Okonkwo , John Bates , Ben Sinnott , Colson Yankoff 

 It's a deeper group with the addition of Okonkwo and the development of Yankoff. The Commanders are expected to use their tight ends more in the pass game, whereas in the past they featured just Zach Ertz . Bates remains one of the best blocking tight ends in the NFL while Okonkwo provides explosive play potential. Lawrence Cager  falls prey to numbers at this position.

 
 

 Offensive line (8) 
 Brandon Coleman , Chris Paul , Nick Allegretti , Sam Cosmi ,  Josh Conerly Jr ., Andrew Wylie , Matt Gulbin , Trent Scott 

 Eight is not enough and the depth remains a question, particularly inside. With so many tough calls elsewhere, veteran Julian Good-Jones  could stick as a backup center but an inability to also play guard limits him and he could end up on the practice squad. Regardless, the Commanders should be on the lookout for more help after final cuts -- this number should get to nine before the opener. This list, of course, includes Tunsil opening on injured reserve.

 
 Defensive line (6) 
 Daron Payne , Tim Settle , Javon Kinlaw , Charles Omenihu ,  Byron Cowart , Shy Tuttle 

 Washington will play a base 3-4 front and Settle will be their nose tackle, but because he's coming off a Lis Franc injury, Tuttle can provide depth. Jer'Zhan Newton is out for a significant time because of a torn pectoral, paving the way for someone else; we'll pick Cowart though Ricky Barber could be another option. Payne, Kinlaw and Omenihu have had good summers while Newton, a 2024 second-round pick, adds quickness -- but he needs to become more consistent.

 
 Linebackers (9) 
 K'Lavon Chaisson , Odafe Oweh , Sonny Styles , Frankie Luvu , Leo Chenal , Jordan Magee ,  Kain Medrano ,  Javontae Jean-Baptiste , Joshua Josephs 

 There's one glaring absence: Dorance Armstrong , who is suspended and won't count against the 53-man roster until Week 2, so he'll soon be on the roster. Medrano or Ale Kaho will get a final spot as an inside linebacker and special teamer. It's possible both make the cut. This is a faster, more athletic group than they've had in a long, long time.

 
 Cornerbacks (4) 
 Trey Amos , Mike Sainristil , Amik Robertson , Rasul Douglas 

 With questions about Amos' health -- he's practiced one day this camp -- a fifth corner becomes necessary (coordinator Daronte Jones doesn't always rely on three-corner nickel packages).  Antonio Hamilton  and Darius Rush can be kept on the practice squad for special teams depth. The question will be who else plays outside when Amos is healthy: Douglas excels in zone while both Sainristil and Robertson can play in the slot or outside.

 
 Safeties (5) 
 Nick Cross , Jeremy Reaves ,  Quan Martin , Percy Butler , Tyler Owens 

 Four spots are easy to call: Cross and Reaves have worked as the starters while Butler and Owens are special teams standouts. Jones likes using three safety sets and he prizes versatility, which gives Martin an edge over veteran  Will Harris . Washington also could try to trade Martin and keep Harris; it's a tight call.

 
 Special teams (3) 
 Tress Way  (P), Drew Stevens  (K), Tyler Ott  (LS) 

 Stevens has been more consistent kicking field goals than veteran Jake Moody and has a stronger leg. The main issue: Stevens has never kicked in an NFL game so he's unproven. It's also possible another kicker comes free and Washington takes a look. But Stevens did have a solid summer. Way and Ott were locks.
